text:
浙江鄉試錄序
天地生物厚於人而賢則人之秀
者也自昔君臨天下克承
上天休命任人理物以保乂家邦未始
不由賢才衆多然後治功有成而
丕基永固也書曰天惟純佑命則
商實詩曰王國克生惟周之楨是
===
已仰惟
皇明統一寰區
聖聖御極歷百餘年多賢彙征布列中
外而庶績咸熈華夷綏服皆由
天眷純至錫賚賢俊而教養之有素選
舉之有法也乃成化丁酉值大比
興賢之秋浙江觀風臺憲暨藩臬
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

天地生物，厚於人，而賢則人之秀者也。自昔君臨天下，克承上天休命，任人理物，以保乂家邦，未始不由賢才衆多，然後治功有成，而丕基永固也。《書》曰：「天惟純佑命，則商實。」《詩》曰：「王國克生，惟周之楨。」是已。

仰惟皇明統一寰區，聖聖御極，歷百餘年，多賢彙征，布列中外，而庶績咸熈，華夷綏服，皆由天眷純至，錫賚賢俊，而教養之有素，選舉之有法也。乃成化丁酉，值大比興賢之秋，浙江觀風臺憲暨藩臬
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In bringing forth living things, Heaven and Earth bestow their richest gifts upon human beings, and the worthy are the finest among them. From antiquity, those who ruled all under Heaven and duly received Heaven’s gracious mandate appointed men and ordered affairs to safeguard and govern their realms. Their success in government and the enduring security of their great foundations invariably depended upon an abundance of worthy talent. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven bestowed its full favor and mandate, and Shang was filled with worthy men.” The Book of Odes says: “The royal realm could bring them forth; they were the pillars of Zhou.” This is precisely the point.

We reverently reflect that the august Ming unified the world, and sage sovereign after sage sovereign has occupied the throne for more than a hundred years. Many worthy men have come forward together and taken their places in office at court and throughout the provinces. Every undertaking has flourished, and Chinese and non-Chinese alike have submitted peacefully. All this is because Heaven’s favor is complete and profound, bestowing worthy and outstanding men, and because their education and nurture are long established, while their selection and recruitment follow proper procedures. Now, in the dingyou year of Chenghua [1477], when autumn brought the triennial examination for advancing the worthy, Zhejiang’s censorial officials charged with inspecting local conditions, together with the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
重臣前期走幣聘教授劉祥為考
試官而華亦與焉學正胡淵教諭
楚綸何覲陳震單暠闗銓訓導顧
宗義先楷為同考官主司文衡至期
合十一郡髦士抱藝操觚皷勇文
塲者二千有竒循例三試焉先其
未試也提督學校副使胡榮詢察
士之學行于庠序既而巡按監察
御史佀鍾復覈實之然後藩司具
名進諸棘院所以杜僥倖而禁奸
弊者嚴且密矣于時
欽差鎮守司設監太監李義巡塩監察
御史李介他若工部員外郎韓紳
亦有事於斯境相與勸勉振作以
punctuated: 重臣前期走幣，聘教授劉祥為考試官，而華亦與焉。學正胡淵，教諭楚綸、何覲、陳震、單暠、闗銓，訓導顧宗義、先楷為同考官，主司文衡。至期，合十一郡髦士抱藝操觚、皷勇文塲者二千有竒，循例三試焉。先其未試也，提督學校副使胡榮詢察士之學行于庠序，既而巡按監察御史佀鍾復覈實之，然後藩司具名進諸棘院，所以杜僥倖而禁奸弊者嚴且密矣。于時，欽差鎮守司設監太監李義、巡塩監察御史李介，他若工部員外郎韓紳，亦有事於斯境，相與勸勉振作，以
translation_en:
…the senior officials sent gifts ahead of time to engage Liu Xiang, a prefectural school instructor, as Examiner; Hua also participated. Hu Yuan, a subprefectural school instructor; Chu Lun, He Jin, Chen Zhen, Shan Gao, and Guan Quan, county school instructors; and Gu Zongyi and Xian Kai, assistant instructors, served as Associate Examiners, responsible for judging the written compositions. When the appointed time arrived, more than two thousand outstanding scholars from the eleven prefectures gathered, bringing their learning and taking up their writing tablets, eager to prove themselves in the literary arena. They underwent three examination sessions according to established practice.
Before the examination, Hu Rong, the surveillance vice commissioner supervising education, had investigated the scholars’ learning and conduct in their schools. Subsequently, Si Zhong, the regional investigating censor, verified these findings once more. Only then did the Provincial Administration Commission draw up the list of names and submit it to the examination compound. The measures for preventing undeserved success and prohibiting fraud were thus both strict and thorough.
At this time, Li Yi, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Imperial Furnishings, imperially commissioned to serve as resident defender, and Li Jie, the censor inspecting the salt administration, as well as others such as Han Shen, a vice director in the Ministry of Works, were also carrying out duties in this territory. Together they offered encouragement and spurred everyone to action, in order to…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
圖贊襄
當宁求賢盛典内而提調則右布政使
杜謙右叅議張敷華監試則按察使
戴珙僉事魏富外而綱維防範則
左叅政李田右叅政張寕李嗣副
使楊瑄端宏王齊左叅議盧雍右
叅議吳森僉事劉餘慶李瓛林倓吳
瑼梁昉潘珪錢山以及凡百執事
靡不簡任得人恪恭厥職而御史
佀鐘寔監臨焉華等躬勤考校積
日逾旬披卷閱辭黜鄙倍抑恠詭
汰浮冗取其言之成文純雅中式
者九十名所以鑑别妍媸評品高
下者公且明矣故事列在院官屬
punctuated: 圖贊襄當宁求賢盛典。内而提調，則右布政使杜謙、右叅議張敷華；監試，則按察使戴珙、僉事魏富；外而綱維防範，則左叅政李田、右叅政張寕、李嗣、副使楊瑄、端宏、王齊、左叅議盧雍、右叅議吳森、僉事劉餘慶、李瓛、林倓、吳瑼、梁昉、潘珪、錢山，以及凡百執事，靡不簡任得人，恪恭厥職。而御史佀鐘寔監臨焉。華等躬勤考校，積日逾旬，披卷閱辭，黜鄙倍，抑恠詭，汰浮冗，取其言之成文、純雅中式者九十名。所以鑑别妍媸、評品高下者，公且明矣。故事，列在院官屬，
translation_en:
…with the aim of assisting the reigning emperor’s grand undertaking of seeking worthy men. Within the examination compound, the Proctors were Du Qian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Zhang Fuhua, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; oversight of the examination was entrusted to Dai Gong, Surveillance Commissioner, and Wei Fu, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner. Outside, responsibility for maintaining order and taking preventive measures fell to Li Tian, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Zhang Ning and Li Si, Right Administration Vice Commissioners; Yang Xuan, Duan Hong, and Wang Qi, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Lu Yong, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Wu Sen, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; and Liu Yuqing, Li Huan, Lin Tan, Wu Zhuan, Liang Fang, Pan Gui, and Qian Shan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. These and all the other functionaries were suitably selected for their appointments and discharged their duties with scrupulous respect. Censor Si Zhong served as the Supervising Official.

Hua and his colleagues personally applied themselves diligently to examining and assessing the papers for more than ten days. They opened the scripts and read their compositions, rejecting the vulgar and perverse, excluding the bizarre and eccentric, and eliminating the superficial and verbose. They selected ninety candidates whose writings formed accomplished compositions, pure and elegant, and met the prescribed standards. Their discrimination between excellence and inferiority, and their assessment of higher and lower quality, were impartial and discerning.

Following established practice, the officials serving in the examination compound are listed…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第舉人氏名并刻文之粹者為小
錄以獻諸
御覽傳播四方焉華謹拜手稽首為
國家得賢賀用序諸首曰惟江浙東南
文物大藩湖山清峙海陸環衍士
生其間孕秀鍾靈接武賢科視他
邦尤勝茲逢
===
昭代亨嘉之運爾諸士子居養學校衣
冠絃誦服禮樂而泳詩書講明大
學之道固濟濟衆盛稱凡民之俊
秀矣一旦舒英吐秀刊名賢書觀
其典則條暢之為經義嚴整淵奧
之為表誥鋪張發越之為論策精
彩煥郁又言之秀而文者足以動
punctuated: 第舉人氏名，并刻文之粹者為小錄，以獻諸御覽，傳播四方焉。華謹拜手稽首，為國家得賢賀，用序諸首曰：惟江浙，東南文物大藩，湖山清峙，海陸環衍。士生其間，孕秀鍾靈，接武賢科，視他邦尤勝。茲逢昭代亨嘉之運，爾諸士子居養學校，衣冠絃誦，服禮樂而泳詩書，講明大學之道，固濟濟衆盛，稱凡民之俊秀矣。一旦舒英吐秀，刊名賢書，觀其典則條暢之為經義，嚴整淵奧之為表誥，鋪張發越之為論策，精彩煥郁，又言之秀而文者，足以動
translation_en:
… arrange the names of the provincial graduates in order and have the finest essays printed as a small record, to be presented for imperial inspection and circulated throughout the realm. I, Hua, respectfully bow with clasped hands and knock my head to the ground, offering congratulations on the state's acquisition of worthy men. Accordingly, I place this preface at the beginning:

Jiangsu and Zhejiang constitute a great southeastern region of cultural accomplishment. Their lakes and mountains stand clear and lofty; sea and land extend all around. Scholars born here are endowed with exceptional refinement and spiritual vitality, following one another into the ranks of successful examination candidates in numbers surpassing those of other regions. Now, in this flourishing age of our illustrious dynasty, you scholars have been housed and nurtured in the schools. Properly attired, you have played the strings and recited, devoted yourselves to ritual and music, immersed yourselves in the Poetry and Documents, and studied and elucidated the Way of the Great Learning. Truly, you form a distinguished and numerous company, worthy to be called the outstanding talents of the common people.

Once you unfold your brilliance and display your gifts, your names are inscribed in the register of the worthy. Consider your expositions of the Classics, correct in form and lucid in development; your memorials and proclamations, rigorously ordered and profound; and your discourses and policy essays, expansive and forceful. Their brilliance is radiant and abundant: these, too, are words of refinement and literary accomplishment, sufficient to stir …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人耳目振耀一時矣然秀而不實
聖師所歎行將會試禮闈進對
大廷荐躋祿位可不思所以充其實乎
必曰吾之進身敷奏以言耳言者
心之聲行之表言外也心内也言
末也行本也急於外而遺其内競
其末而棄其本豈務實乎盍反求
===
諸心主敬以存之寡欲以養之知
性以盡之使廣大髙明廓然而大
公致謹其行非仁無為非義無行
非禮不動而動容周旋循蹈乎規
矩由是宅此心以明德則内能成
已推此心以新民則外能成物至
於調元賛化寅亮天工皆此心之
punctuated: 人耳目，振耀一時矣。然秀而不實，聖師所歎。行將會試禮闈，進對大廷，荐躋祿位，可不思所以充其實乎？必曰：吾之進身，敷奏以言耳。言者，心之聲，行之表。言外也，心内也；言末也，行本也。急於外而遺其内，競其末而棄其本，豈務實乎？盍反求諸心，主敬以存之，寡欲以養之，知性以盡之，使廣大髙明，廓然而大公；致謹其行，非仁無為，非義無行，非禮不動，而動容周旋，循蹈乎規矩。由是宅此心以明德，則内能成已；推此心以新民，則外能成物。至於調元賛化，寅亮天工，皆此心之
translation_en:
…people’s eyes and ears, and shine brilliantly for a time. Yet flowering without bearing fruit was what the sage teacher lamented. Soon you will sit the Metropolitan Examination in the examination compound of the Ministry of Rites, present your answers at the imperial court, and advance to salaried office. Can you fail to consider how to give substance to your accomplishments? You will surely say: “My advancement and my reports to the throne depend only on words.” Words are the voice of the heart and the outward expression of conduct. Words are external; the heart is internal. Words are the branches; conduct is the root. If you attend urgently to the external while neglecting the internal, and compete over the branches while abandoning the root, are you truly pursuing substance?

Why not seek it within your own heart? Make reverent attentiveness your guiding principle to preserve it, reduce desires to nourish it, and understand your nature to develop it fully, making it broad and lofty, open and wholly impartial. Exercise the utmost care in your conduct: undertake nothing that is not benevolent, pursue nothing that is not righteous, and make no movement contrary to ritual propriety. Let every gesture and movement conform to the compass and square. By thus grounding yourselves in this heart and making virtue manifest, you can perfect yourselves inwardly; by extending this heart to renew the people, you can bring others to fulfillment outwardly. As for harmonizing the primordial forces, assisting the transforming processes of creation, and reverently aiding Heaven’s work, these are all this heart’s…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
實用行成乎邇則親和而家正行
孚乎遠則君正而國定民康乂而
天下平皆此行之實效天之厚我
以靈秀而同類蚩蚩同生芸芸皆
於我而使各遂其性實心普實行
順匪直虛言虛文而已秀之充實
有如是夫允哉其為有德之賢也
===
斯可無負上天生賢輔治之心
聖明養賢及民之意臺省諸臣舉賢報
國之忠而德業建于當時聲光垂于
永世
皇朝億萬年承保無疆佑命弼寧無疆
宗社亦將咸有賴焉名動一時奚足多
歟華忝預校文之末敢以是為諸
punctuated:
實用。行成乎邇，則親和而家正；行孚乎遠，則君正而國定，民康乂而天下平，皆此行之實效。天之厚我以靈秀，而同類蚩蚩，同生芸芸，皆於我而使各遂其性。實心普，實行順，匪直虛言虛文而已。秀之充實有如是夫！允哉，其為有德之賢也！
斯可無負上天生賢輔治之心、聖明養賢及民之意、臺省諸臣舉賢報國之忠，而德業建于當時，聲光垂于永世。皇朝億萬年承保無疆佑命，弼寧無疆宗社，亦將咸有賴焉。名動一時，奚足多歟？華忝預校文之末，敢以是為諸
translation_en:
…practical application. When one's conduct is perfected close at hand, one's kin live in harmony and one's household is rightly ordered; when one's conduct wins trust afar, the ruler is upright and the state stable, the people enjoy well-being and good order, and all under Heaven is at peace. These are all the tangible results of such conduct. Heaven has generously endowed us with spiritual excellence; the untutored multitude of our fellow humans and the teeming beings that share life with us all depend upon us [?] to enable each to fulfill its nature. A sincere heart extends everywhere, and genuine conduct accords with what is right [?]: these are not merely empty words and hollow literary embellishments. Such is the fullness of excellence! Truly, such a person is a worthy possessed of virtue!
Only thus can one avoid disappointing Heaven's intention in bringing forth worthies to assist in government, the sage sovereign's purpose in nurturing worthies so that their benefits reach the people, and the loyalty of the officials of the Censorate and central administration who recommend worthies to repay the state. Their virtuous achievements will be established in their own age, and their renown will endure forever. The imperial dynasty, in receiving and preserving Heaven's boundless favor and mandate for countless millions of years, and in sustaining and securing its ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain without end, will likewise depend upon them all. What is so worthy of praise in merely winning fame for a time? I, Hua, have undeservedly occupied a humble place among those assessing the examination essays, and venture to offer these words to the assembled…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
賢勸循名責實尚願有徵於茲云
賜進士江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教
諭莆田鄭華謹序
punctuated:
賢勸，循名責實，尚願有徵於茲云。
賜進士、江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭、莆田鄭華謹序。
translation_en:
…as encouragement to you worthy men. In holding you to the substance your reputation implies, I hope that these words will find fulfillment in you.
Respectfully prefaced by Zheng Hua of Putian, conferred metropolitan graduate (jinshi), Instructor of the Confucian School of Luling County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
成化十三年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史侶鍾〔大器山東鄆城縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使杜謙〔益之直隸昌黎縣人甲戌進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參議張敷華〔公實江西安福縣人甲申進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司按察使戴珙〔廷璧河南沔池縣人甲戌進士〕
===
浙江等處提刑按察司僉事魏富〔仲禮福建龍溪縣人丙戌進士〕
考試官
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭鄭華〔思賢福建莆田縣人甲戌進士〕
廣東肇慶府儒學教授劉祥〔公瑞江西安福縣人癸酉貢士〕
同考試官
山西太原府岢嵐州儒學學正胡淵〔仲深江西南城縣人乙酉貢士〕
山西平陽府解州聞喜縣儒學教諭蔡綸〔大經河南祥符縣人庚午貢士〕
直隸安慶府宿松縣儒學教諭何覲〔觀光廣東南海縣人癸酉貢士〕
punctuated:
成化十三年浙江鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按浙江監察御史侶鍾〔大器，山東鄆城縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官：
浙江等處承宣布政使司右布政使杜謙〔益之，直隸昌黎縣人，甲戌進士〕。
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參議張敷華〔公實，江西安福縣人，甲申進士〕。

監試官：
浙江等處提刑按察司按察使戴珙〔廷璧，河南沔池縣人，甲戌進士〕。
浙江等處提刑按察司僉事魏富〔仲禮，福建龍溪縣人，丙戌進士〕。

考試官：
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭鄭華〔思賢，福建莆田縣人，甲戌進士〕。
廣東肇慶府儒學教授劉祥〔公瑞，江西安福縣人，癸酉貢士〕。

同考試官：
山西太原府岢嵐州儒學學正胡淵〔仲深，江西南城縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
山西平陽府解州聞喜縣儒學教諭蔡綸〔大經，河南祥符縣人，庚午貢士〕。
直隸安慶府宿松縣儒學教諭何覲〔觀光，廣東南海縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination, thirteenth year of Chenghua (1477).

Supervising Official:
Lü Zhong, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor, courtesy name Daqi, was from Yuncheng County, Shandong. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the bingxu year.

Proctors:
Du Qian, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Yizhi, was from Changli County in the Metropolitan Region (Zhili). He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Zhang Fuhua, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission, courtesy name Gongshi, was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiashen year.

Examination Monitors:
Dai Gong, Surveillance Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Surveillance Commission, courtesy name Tingbi, was from Mianchi County, Henan (written 沔池 [?]). He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
顏淵喟然歎曰仰之彌高鑽之彌堅瞻之
在前忽焉在後夫子循循然善誘人博
我以文約我以禮欲罷不能既竭吾才
如有所立卓爾雖欲從之末由也已
悠遠則博厚博厚則高明博厚所以載物
也高明所以覆物也悠久所以成物也
===
孔子聖之時者也孔子之謂集大成集大
成也者金聲而玉振之也金聲也者始
條理也玉振之也者終條理也始條理
者智之事也終條理者聖之事也智譬
則巧也聖譬則力也由射於百步之外
也其至爾力也其中非爾力也
易
聖人久於其道而天下化成
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

顏淵喟然歎曰：「仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅；瞻之在前，忽焉在後。夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。欲罷不能，既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。雖欲從之，末由也已。」

悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。

孔子，聖之時者也。孔子之謂集大成。集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。金聲也者，始條理也；玉振之也者，終條理也。始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。

易

聖人久於其道，而天下化成。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: “The more I look up to it, the higher it becomes; the more I bore into it, the harder it becomes. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind me. The Master skillfully guides people onward, step by step. He broadens me through learning and restrains me through ritual propriety. Even if I wished to stop, I could not. Having exhausted all my abilities, I seem to see something standing loftily before me. Though I wish to follow it, I have no way to do so.”

Far-reaching endurance leads to breadth and depth; breadth and depth lead to height and brightness. Breadth and depth are the means by which things are borne; height and brightness are the means by which things are covered; enduring constancy is the means by which things are brought to completion.

Kongzi was the sage who acted according to the time. Kongzi is said to have gathered together the great accomplishment. Gathering together the great accomplishment is like sounding the bronze bell and concluding with the jade chime. Sounding the bronze bell begins the ordered sequence; sounding the jade chime completes it. Beginning the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; completing it is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength. It is like shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away: that the arrow reaches it is due to your strength; that it hits the mark is not due to your strength.

Book of Changes (Yi)

The sage perseveres long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed and brought to fulfillment.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
父父子子兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正
正家而天下定矣象曰風自火出家人
君子以言有物而行有恒
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢聖人以此洗心退藏於密
吉凶與民同患神以知來知以藏往其
孰能與於此哉古之聰明叡知神武而
不殺者夫是以明於天之道而察於民
===
之故是興神物以前民用聖人以此齋
戒以神明其德夫是故闔戶謂之坤闢
戶謂之乾一闔一闢謂之變往來不窮
謂之通見乃謂之象形乃謂之器制而
用之謂之法利用出入民咸用之謂之
神
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
punctuated:
父父子子，兄兄弟弟，夫夫婦婦，而家道正。正家而天下定矣。象曰：「風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恒。」

是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明叡知、神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齋戒，以神明其德夫！是故闔戶謂之坤，闢戶謂之乾，一闔一闢謂之變，往來不窮謂之通，見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此
translation_en:
When fathers act as fathers, sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, younger brothers as younger brothers, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives, the way of the family is set right. Set the family right, and all under Heaven will be settled. The Commentary on the Images says: “Wind issues from fire: this is the hexagram The Family (Jiaren). Accordingly, the noble man gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.”

Thus the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; and the meanings of the six lines are expressed through change. By these the sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into hidden secrecy, sharing the people’s concern over good and ill fortune. Through numinous insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores up what has passed. Who could attain this? Surely those of antiquity who were perceptive, discerning, sagacious, and wise, whose martial power was numinous yet did not kill! Thus they understood the Way of Heaven and discerned the circumstances of the people, and so brought forth these numinous objects to guide the people’s use of them. Through these the sage purifies himself and observes abstinence, making his virtue numinous and luminous. Thus closing the door is called Kun, the Receptive; opening the door is called Qian, the Creative. One closing and one opening is called change; coming and going without exhaustion is called continuity. What becomes visible is called an image; what takes form is called an implement. Making things and putting them to use is called a method; making their use beneficial in going out and coming in, so that all the people use them, is called numinous efficacy.

Li, the Clinging, means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the hexagram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven and turns toward the light to govern, taking his model, presumably, from this…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也坤也者地也萬物皆致養焉故曰致
役乎坤兌正秋也萬物之所說也故曰
說言乎兌
書
惟動丕應傒志
往盡乃心無康好逸豫乃其乂民
欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
予不允惟若茲誥予惟曰襄我二人汝有
===
合哉言曰在時二人天休滋至惟時二
人弗戡其汝克敬德明我俊民在讓後
人于丕時嗚呼篤棐時二人我式克至
于今日休我咸成文王功于不怠丕冒
海隅出日罔不率俾公曰君予不惠若
茲多誥予惟用閔于天越民
詩
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播□
punctuated:
也。坤也者，地也，萬物皆致養焉，故曰：「致役乎坤。」兌，正秋也，萬物之所說也，故曰：「說言乎兌。」

書

惟動丕應傒志。
往盡乃心，無康好逸豫，乃其乂民。
欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。
予不允惟若茲誥，予惟曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉！」言曰：「在時二人，天休滋至，惟時二人弗戡。其汝克敬德，明我俊民，在讓後人于丕時。嗚呼！篤棐時二人，我式克至于今日休。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。」公曰：「君，予不惠若茲多誥，予惟用閔于天越民。」

詩

晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播□
translation_en:
… Kun is the earth: all things receive their nourishment from it. Hence the saying, “They render service in Kun.” Dui is the height of autumn, in which all things rejoice. Hence the saying, “They rejoice in Dui.”

Book of Documents

Let your actions fully answer the hopes awaiting their fulfillment.
Go and devote your whole heart to your task. Do not settle into a love of ease and pleasure; then you will govern the people well.
If this is to endure for ten thousand years, the king’s sons and grandsons must forever protect the people.
It is not merely with such admonitions that I demonstrate my sincerity [?]. I say only: “Assist us two; may you work in accord!” It is said: “With these two men, Heaven’s blessings came in abundance; yet these two men could not bear the burden alone. If you can reverently cultivate virtue and bring our worthy men to light, you can bequeath this great prosperity to those who come after. Ah! Give these two men steadfast support, so that we may attain the blessings of this day. Let us together complete King Wen’s work without flagging, extending its protection even to the shores of the sea where the sun rises, so that none fail to follow and obey.” The duke said: “My lord, it is not that I delight in giving so many admonitions of this kind. I do so only out of concern for Heaven and the people.”

Book of Odes

By day, go gather thatching grass; by night, twist rope. Hurry up onto the roofs to thatch them; then begin sowing □ [illegible] …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌陰
四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭
保茲天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
假以溢我我其收之駿惠我文王曾孫篤
===
之
有駜有駜駜彼乘黃夙夜在公在公明明
振振鷺鷺于下鼓咽咽醉言舞于胥樂
兮有駜有駜駜彼乘牡夙夜在公在公
飲酒振振鷺鷺于飛鼓咽咽醉言歸于
胥樂兮有駜有駜駜彼乘駽夙夜在公
在公載燕自今以始歲其有君子有穀
詒孫子于胥樂兮
punctuated:
穀。二之日，鑿冰冲冲；三之日，納于凌陰。四之日，其蚤，獻羔祭韭。

保茲天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則。令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力。天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫：「式是百辟，纘戎祖考。王躬是保，出納王命。王之喉舌，賦政于外，四方爰發。」

假以溢我，我其收之。駿惠我文王，曾孫篤之。

有駜有駜，駜彼乘黃。夙夜在公，在公明明。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言舞，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘牡。夙夜在公，在公飲酒。振振鷺，鷺于飛。鼓咽咽，醉言歸，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘駽。夙夜在公，在公載燕。自今以始，歲其有，君子有穀，詒孫子，于胥樂兮！
translation_en:
…grain. In the days of the second month, they hew the ice with resounding blows; in the days of the third month, they store it in the icehouse. In the days of the fourth month, early in the season, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives.

To protect this Son of Heaven, Heaven brought forth Zhong Shanfu. Zhong Shanfu’s virtue takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing and expression are admirable; he is cautious and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and strives for dignified conduct. He obeys the Son of Heaven, whose clear command charges him with distributing government duties. The king commands Zhong Shanfu: “Be a model for the many lords; continue the work of your forefathers. Protect the king’s person; convey the king’s commands within and without. Be the king’s throat and tongue; administer government abroad, so that the four quarters respond.”

He has bestowed abundance upon us; we shall receive it. Deeply follow our King Wen; may his great-grandson firmly uphold his way.

Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four yellow horses! Morning and night they attend to public service, performing it diligently. Egrets gather in flocks; the egrets descend. The drums resound; flushed with wine, they dance. Together they rejoice! Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four stallions! Morning and night they attend to public service; there they drink wine. Egrets gather in flocks; the egrets take flight. The drums resound; flushed with wine, they return home. Together they rejoice! Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four dark gray horses! Morning and night they attend to public service; there they hold a feast. From this time forward, may the years bring abundance [?]; may the noble men possess goodness and bequeath it to their descendants. Together they rejoice!

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛
侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城秋楚人圍許諸
侯遂救許〔僖公六年〕
諸侯會于扈〔文公十七年〕楚子鄭人侵陳遂侵宋
晉人宋人伐鄭〔並宣公元年〕宋華元帥師及
鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘晉人宋
人衛人陳人侵鄭〔並宣公二年〕晉侯使士匄
来聘杞伯来朝邾子来朝〔並成公十八年〕
公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯莒子邾
子齊世子光己未同盟于雞澤陳侯
使袁僑如會〔襄公三年〕
季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥
師會晉郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊
侯戰于鞌齊師敗績〔成公二年〕
陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮
punctuated:
春秋

盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕。夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。秋，楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許〔僖公六年〕。

諸侯會于扈〔文公十七年〕。楚子、鄭人侵陳，遂侵宋。晉人、宋人伐鄭〔並宣公元年〕。宋華元帥師及鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘。晉人、宋人、衛人、陳人侵鄭〔並宣公二年〕。晉侯使士匄来聘。杞伯来朝。邾子来朝〔並成公十八年〕。

公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光，己未，同盟于雞澤。陳侯使袁僑如會〔襄公三年〕。

季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌，齊師敗績〔成公二年〕。

陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕。鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

A covenant was concluded at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In summer, the Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. In autumn, the men of Chu besieged Xu; the assembled lords thereupon went to Xu’s rescue. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi.〕

The lords met at Hu. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Wen.〕 The Viscount of Chu and the men of Zheng invaded Chen, then proceeded to invade Song. The men of Jin and Song attacked Zheng. 〔Both entries: first year of Duke Xuan.〕 Hua Yuan of Song, commanding an army, fought at Daji against Prince Guisheng of Zheng, who also commanded an army. The men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng. 〔Both entries: second year of Duke Xuan.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a diplomatic visit to Lu. The Earl of Qi came to pay court. The Viscount of Zhu came to pay court. 〔All three entries: eighteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕

The Duke of Lu met with the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi. On the jiwei day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Jize. The Marquis of Chen sent Yuan Qiao to attend the meeting. 〔Third year of Duke Xiang.〕

Jisun Hangfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi led an army and joined Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao in fighting the Marquis of Qi at An. The army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕

The Marquis of Chen fled home. 〔Seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 The men of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Prince Xie of Cai…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
〔襄公五年〕冬楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕晉侯
使士匄来聘〔襄公八年〕冬公會晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小
邾子齊世子光伐鄭十有二月己亥同
盟于戲〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥師伐吳〔昭公六年〕
秋公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子
于平丘〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕齊侯
===
伐徐〔昭公十六年〕秋齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕
禮記
土工金工石工木工獸工草工典制六材
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳凰降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
punctuated:
〔襄公五年〕冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭。〔襄公八年〕晉侯使士匄来聘。〔襄公八年〕冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥師伐吳。〔昭公六年〕秋，公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘。〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来。〔昭公十三年〕齊侯伐徐。〔昭公十六年〕秋，齊高發帥師伐莒。〔昭公十九年〕

禮記

土工、金工、石工、木工、獸工、草工，典制六材。

是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳凰降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南
translation_en:
…〔Fifth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In winter, Prince Zhen of Chu led an army against Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a courtesy mission to Lu. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In winter, the Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the dukes of Song and Wei, the Earl of Cao, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, the Viscount of Xiao Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 Wei Pi of Chu led an army against Wu. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, the Duke met the Viscount of Liu, the marquises of Jin and Qi, the dukes of Song and Wei, the earls of Zheng and Cao, the viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Xiao Zhu at Pingqiu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 Wu destroyed Zhoulai. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The Marquis of Qi attacked Xu. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, Gao Fa of Qi led an army against Ju. 〔Nineteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

Workers in earth, metal, stone, wood, animal materials, and plant materials oversee the fashioning of these six kinds of material.

Thus, in antiquity, the former kings esteemed those possessed of virtue, honored those possessed of the Way, employed the capable, raised up worthy men and appointed them to office, and assembled the multitude and bound them by solemn charges. Thus they relied on Heaven to serve Heaven and on Earth to serve Earth; they used renowned mountains to present reports of their accomplishments to Heaven, and auspicious ground to make offerings to the Supreme Lord at the suburban sacrifice. When they presented their accomplishments to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they made offerings to the Supreme Lord at the suburban sacrifice, wind and rain were regulated, and cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Thus the sage, facing south…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
面而立而天下大治
王者功成作樂治定制禮其功大者其樂
備其治辯者其禮具干戚之舞非備樂
也孰亨而祀非達禮也五帝殊時不相
沿樂三王異世不相襲禮樂極則憂禮
粗則偏矣及夫敦樂而無憂禮備而不
偏者其唯大聖乎
賓再拜受主人般還曰辟主人阼階上拜
===
送賓般還曰辟
第貳場
論
明王以孝治天下
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表
punctuated:
面而立，而天下大治。
王者功成作樂，治定制禮。其功大者，其樂備；其治辯者，其禮具。干戚之舞，非備樂也；孰亨而祀，非達禮也。五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異世，不相襲禮。樂極則憂，禮粗則偏矣。及夫敦樂而無憂，禮備而不偏者，其唯大聖乎！
賓再拜受，主人般還曰辟。主人阼階上拜送，賓般還曰辟。
第貳場
論
明王以孝治天下。
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔。
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥。
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表。
translation_en:
…stands facing south, and all under Heaven is well governed.
When a king’s achievements are complete, he creates music; when his government is settled, he establishes rites. The greater his achievements, the more fully developed his music; the more differentiated his government, the more comprehensive his rites. Dancing with shields and battle-axes does not constitute music in its completeness; offering cooked food in sacrifice does not constitute a full understanding of ritual. The Five Emperors lived at different times and did not perpetuate one another’s music; the Three Kings lived in different ages and did not copy one another’s rites. Music carried to excess produces sorrow; rites that are crude become one-sided. As for making music rich without producing sorrow, and rites complete without becoming one-sided—surely only a great sage can accomplish this!
The guest bows twice and receives the offering; the host turns aside, a movement called “withdrawing.” The host bows to send off the offering from the top of the eastern steps; the guest turns aside, likewise called “withdrawing.”
Second Session
Discourse
The enlightened king governs all under Heaven through filial piety.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to seek out worthy men who have been overlooked.
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Han Yu as Vice Minister of Personnel.
Compose a memorial of thanks in which the Libationer of the Directorate of Education leads the students in expressing gratitude for an increase in the bamboo and wooden offering vessels and the ranks of dancers used in sacrifices to Confucius.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
判語五條
隱匿費用稅粮課物
公差人員欺陵長官
公使人等索借馬疋
監守自盜倉庫錢粮
有司官吏不住公廨
第叄塲
策五道
===
問自古帝王之治天下必有洪謨大訓以
昭鑒萬世如我
太祖高皇帝之大誥
太宗文皇帝之為善陰隲以及
列聖垂統頒煥典章光同日月其與仲尼所纘
述易書詩春秋禮樂之言果有同歟否
歟夫讀典謨而潜思堯舜之聖德頌
制書而逺想
punctuated:
判語五條：隱匿費用稅粮課物；公差人員欺陵長官；公使人等索借馬疋；監守自盜倉庫錢粮；有司官吏不住公廨。

第叄塲
策五道

問：自古帝王之治天下，必有洪謨大訓，以昭鑒萬世。如我太祖高皇帝之大誥、太宗文皇帝之為善陰隲，以及列聖垂統，頒煥典章，光同日月，其與仲尼所纘述易、書、詩、春秋、禮、樂之言，果有同歟？否歟？夫讀典謨而潜思堯舜之聖德，頌制書而逺想
translation_en:
Five legal judgments: Concealing and misappropriating tax grain and goods collected as levies; personnel on official assignments bullying their superior officials; persons on official missions demanding horses on loan; custodians stealing money and grain from the storehouses under their charge; officials and clerks of the competent authorities failing to reside in their official quarters.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings governing the realm have invariably provided great plans and weighty instructions to serve as a shining mirror for all ages. Consider our Emperor Taizu Gao’s Grand Pronouncements (Da gao), Emperor Taizong Wen’s Doing Good and Hidden Merit (Weishan yinzhi), and the successive sage emperors’ transmission of the imperial legacy and promulgation of resplendent statutes and institutions, whose brilliance equals that of the sun and moon. Are these indeed in accord with the words of the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites, and Music compiled and transmitted by Zhongni (Confucius), or are they not? Reading the Canons and Counsels, one meditates deeply upon the sagely virtue of Yao and Shun; reciting imperial decrees, one calls to mind the distant …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之神功亦臣子之所當講也且如延曆數
所以紀年如漢如唐或遇災祥而輒改
今則紀一元而終始創廟宇所以祀神
如宋如元或加美號而過諂今則立木
主以正名至於前代宫室多施繪畫今
乃命侍臣以大學衍義書於兩廡者其
意果安在歟自古人君多好馳騁今乃
命畫工以經歷艱難繪於圖冊者其心
===
果何為歟他如定歷代名臣從祀帝王
廟庭所去者誰氏所增者何官俱可得
而詳言之歟爾諸士子沐浴
聖化亦有年矣今應賓興而来宜鋪張萬世之
宏規揚厲無前之偉績庶使後生晚學
有如親覩焉幸毋讓
問治道隆替風化醇漓係乎賢才之進退
而賢才之進其要在乎抑奔競獎恬退
punctuated:
祖宗之神功，亦臣子之所當講也。且如延曆數，所以紀年，如漢如唐，或遇災祥而輒改；今則紀一元而終始。創廟宇，所以祀神，如宋如元，或加美號而過諂；今則立木主以正名。至於前代宫室多施繪畫，今乃命侍臣以《大學衍義》書於兩廡者，其意果安在歟？自古人君多好馳騁，今乃命畫工以經歷艱難繪於圖冊者，其心果何為歟？他如定歷代名臣從祀帝王廟庭，所去者誰氏？所增者何官？俱可得而詳言之歟？爾諸士子沐浴聖化，亦有年矣。今應賓興而来，宜鋪張萬世之宏規，揚厲無前之偉績，庶使後生晚學有如親覩焉。幸毋讓！

問：治道隆替，風化醇漓，係乎賢才之進退。而賢才之進，其要在乎抑奔競、獎恬退
translation_en:
…the wondrous achievements of the imperial ancestors are also matters that subjects ought to study and discuss. Consider, for example, the extension of calendrical reckoning [?] to mark the years: under the Han and Tang, an era name might be changed whenever a calamity or auspicious portent occurred; now a single era name is used from the beginning of a reign to its end. Temples are established to worship spirits: under the Song and Yuan, flattering titles were sometimes added to excess; now wooden spirit tablets are erected to rectify their designations. Whereas palace buildings in earlier dynasties were often adorned with paintings, attendants were now ordered to inscribe the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) on the two side galleries. What, precisely, was the intention behind this? From antiquity, rulers have often delighted in galloping about; yet painters were now ordered to depict hardships experienced in an illustrated album. What, precisely, was the purpose behind this?

Further, when the famous ministers of successive dynasties were designated to receive accompanying sacrifices in the temple precincts of past emperors, who was removed, and which officials were added? Can you explain all these matters in detail? You scholars have enjoyed the influence of sagely instruction for many years. Now that you have come in response to the summons for the selection and ceremonial reception of worthy men, you should expound the grand plans enduring for ten thousand generations and extol the unprecedented achievements, so that younger students and later learners may feel as though they had witnessed them in person. Please do not hold back!

Question: The flourishing or decline of government, and the purity or corruption of customs, depend upon the advancement or withdrawal of worthy and talented men. The key to advancing such men lies in restraining those who scramble competitively for office and encouraging those who remain contentedly withdrawn…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而已考之於古若玉堂獻記不入翰苑
河平獻頌不留蘭臺兩及相門則却以
素定一謁大資則却以不求所以抑奔
競也然以名世大儒而甘有美新之作
後學山斗而三上宰相之書豈奔競不
足鄙歟不以私書至京師則擢之御史
不以私事干朝廷則處之諫諍有不就
廷試者遷除監學有不肯自陳者薦充
===
館職所以奬恬退也然以首陽逸民無
裨於邦家之治桐江高節有乖於君臣
之倫豈恬退不足尚歟方今
朝廷治理清明登用賢俊選舉有方考察有
法所以杜僥倖防請謁至矣盡矣然而
望塵奔趨者猶未息鎮靜恬退者或未
見不知其故安在兹欲使士大夫盡尚
廉恥甘事恬退絕夫奔競之跡藹然禮
punctuated: 而已。考之於古，若玉堂獻記，不入翰苑；河平獻頌，不留蘭臺；兩及相門，則却以素定；一謁大資，則却以不求，所以抑奔競也。然以名世大儒，而甘有美新之作；後學山斗，而三上宰相之書，豈奔競不足鄙歟？不以私書至京師，則擢之御史；不以私事干朝廷，則處之諫諍；有不就廷試者，遷除監學；有不肯自陳者，薦充館職，所以奬恬退也。然以首陽逸民，無裨於邦家之治；桐江高節，有乖於君臣之倫，豈恬退不足尚歟？方今朝廷治理清明，登用賢俊，選舉有方，考察有法，所以杜僥倖、防請謁，至矣，盡矣。然而望塵奔趨者猶未息，鎮靜恬退者或未見，不知其故安在？兹欲使士大夫盡尚廉恥，甘事恬退，絕夫奔競之跡，藹然禮
translation_en:
…and nothing more. Examining antiquity, we find such cases as the presentation of a record concerning the Jade Hall without admission to the Hanlin Academy, and the presentation of a eulogy during the Heping era without being retained at the Orchid Terrace. Someone who twice visited a chief councillor’s gate was rebuffed with “It was settled beforehand”; someone who once called upon a Grand Academician was rebuffed with “I did not seek it.” These were ways of restraining competitive pursuit of advancement. Yet a great Confucian scholar renowned in his age willingly composed In Praise of Xin, while a scholar revered by later students as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper submitted letters to a chief councillor three times. Could competitive pursuit of advancement, then, be unworthy of contempt?

One who sent no private letters to the capital was promoted to censor; one who did not trouble the court with private affairs was appointed to a remonstrance post. Someone who declined to attend the Palace Examination was appointed to an educational office; someone unwilling to submit a statement of his own merits was recommended for an academy post. These were ways of rewarding quiet restraint and withdrawal. Yet the recluses of Shouyang contributed nothing to the governance of the state, while the lofty integrity displayed at Tongjiang departed from the proper relationship between ruler and subject. Could quiet restraint and withdrawal, then, be unworthy of esteem?

Today the court’s government is clear and enlightened. It advances and employs worthy and talented men; selection has its proper procedures, and assessment its established rules. Its measures to block advancement through undeserved good fortune and guard against solicitation could scarcely be more thorough or complete. Nevertheless, those who rush forward at the sight of the dust raised by the powerful have not yet ceased, while those who remain composed, quietly restrained, and withdrawn are perhaps still nowhere to be seen. Where does the reason lie? We now wish to make all scholar-officials prize integrity and a sense of shame, willingly practise quiet restraint and withdrawal, and eliminate every trace of competitive pursuit of advancement, so that a flourishing spirit of ritual propriety…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讓之風以驗
聖明治道之隆風化之醇不知何道而可爾諸
士子涵薰有年抱負而來必有其說願
著于篇
問自孔子刪詩三百篇之後即為楚辭視
風雅已一變矣又下而為漢魏之五言
則詩再變矣然三百篇經聖人所筆削
善惡昭彰以示勸懲楚辭則經朱子所
===
校錄亦取其發於性情為人臣子不得
於君父者讀之亦可以發其抑鬱無聊
之態厥後劉坦之輯選詩補註謂其可
以羽翼風雅焉夫楚辭作於屈原雖曰
南國宗之為辭賦之祖然其跌蕩怪神
怨懟激發醇儒莊士或羞稱之朱子果
何為之集註耶又欲掇經史韻語及文
選古詞附于詩楚辭之後果何旨耶其
punctuated:
讓之風，以驗聖明治道之隆、風化之醇，不知何道而可？爾諸士子涵薰有年，抱負而來，必有其說，願著于篇。

問：自孔子刪詩三百篇之後，即為楚辭，視風雅已一變矣；又下而為漢魏之五言，則詩再變矣。然三百篇經聖人所筆削，善惡昭彰，以示勸懲。楚辭則經朱子所校錄，亦取其發於性情，為人臣子不得於君父者，讀之亦可以發其抑鬱無聊之態。厥後劉坦之輯《選詩補註》，謂其可以羽翼風雅焉。夫楚辭作於屈原，雖曰南國宗之，為辭賦之祖，然其跌蕩怪神、怨懟激發，醇儒莊士或羞稱之，朱子果何為之集註耶？又欲掇經史韻語及文選古詞，附于詩、楚辭之後，果何旨耶？其
translation_en:
…a spirit of deference, thereby demonstrating the excellence of our sagely and enlightened ruler’s governance and the purity of moral transformation. By what means can this be achieved? You candidates have been nurtured by this influence for years and have come with learning and aspirations of your own. You must have something to say; please set it down in writing.

Question: After Confucius edited the three hundred poems of the Book of Odes, there followed the Songs of Chu, already representing a transformation from the Airs and Elegantiae. Later came the five-character verse of the Han and Wei, marking a second transformation of poetry. Yet the three hundred poems underwent the Sage’s revision and deletion, making good and evil manifest so as to offer encouragement and admonition. The Songs of Chu, in turn, were collated and recorded by Master Zhu, who likewise valued their expression of human nature and feelings. Those serving as subjects or sons who fail to find favor with their rulers or fathers can also, by reading them, give expression to their pent-up sorrow and desolation. Subsequently, Liu Tanzhi compiled Supplementary Annotations to Selected Poems, saying that it could serve as an aid to the Airs and Elegantiae.

Now, the Songs of Chu originated with Qu Yuan. Although it is said that the southern lands revered him as the progenitor of lyrical poetry and rhapsodies, their unrestrained manner, strange spirits, and impassioned expressions of resentment were such that orthodox Confucian scholars and dignified gentlemen sometimes felt ashamed to speak of them. Why, then, did Master Zhu compile collected annotations to them? He also wished to gather rhymed passages from the classics and histories, together with ancient verses from the Selections of Refined Literature, and append them to the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu. What precisely was his intention? As for his…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
續楚辭也始之於成相終之以鞠歌擬
招其意何在至於補註也其立法之意
亦有得於朱子註詩及楚辭之意歟其
補遺也抑又有得於朱子抄經史韻語
文選古詩附于詩楚□之後之意歟他
如續編集之始終其與楚辭後語成相
擬招之意同歟否歟不學詩無以言聖
人之訓也爾多士必有能言之者幸明
===
以告我毋多讓焉
問兵凶器也聖人不得已而用之然有文
事者必有武備亦君子之所當講焉姑
舉一二已往者論其成敗且以見今日
之事亦有可憂者焉昔韓信之破趙而
李左車說陳餘曰信下井陘其勢粮食
必在後假竒兵三萬絶其輜重此取勝
之策也千載悔其謀之不用若然則拔
punctuated:
續楚辭也，始之於成相，終之以鞠歌、擬招，其意何在？至於補註也，其立法之意，亦有得於朱子註詩及楚辭之意歟？其補遺也，抑又有得於朱子抄經史韻語、文選古詩，附于詩、楚□之後之意歟？他如續編集之始終，其與楚辭後語成相、擬招之意同歟否歟？不學詩，無以言，聖人之訓也。爾多士必有能言之者，幸明以告我，毋多讓焉。
問：兵，凶器也，聖人不得已而用之。然有文事者必有武備，亦君子之所當講焉。姑舉一二已往者，論其成敗，且以見今日之事亦有可憂者焉。昔韓信之破趙，而李左車說陳餘曰：「信下井陘，其勢粮食必在後。假竒兵三萬，絶其輜重，此取勝之策也。」千載悔其謀之不用。若然，則拔
translation_en:
…As for his continuation of the Songs of Chu, what was his intention in beginning with Chengxiang (Accompanying the Pestle) and ending with Ju ge (Ball Song) and Ni zhao (Imitation Summons)? As for the supplementary commentary, did the principles he established likewise derive from an understanding of Zhu Xi’s intentions in annotating the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu? And in supplying omissions, did he also grasp Zhu Xi’s intention in copying rhymed passages from the classics and histories and ancient poems from the Selections of Refined Literature, and appending them to the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu [one character illegible]? In other matters, such as the choice of opening and closing pieces in the continuation collection, was his intention the same as that behind placing Chengxiang and Ni zhao in the Further Discourses on the Songs of Chu, or was it different? “Without studying the Odes, one has no means of speaking”: this is the Sage’s teaching. Among you, the assembled candidates, there must be those able to discuss these matters. Please explain them clearly to me, without undue modesty.
Question: Weapons are instruments of ill omen; the sage uses them only when compelled. Yet those engaged in civil affairs must also maintain military preparedness: this, too, is something a gentleman should study. Let us take one or two examples from the past and discuss their successes and failures, thereby also showing that present affairs contain grounds for concern. When Han Xin was defeating Zhao, Li Zuoche advised Chen Yu: “When Xin descends through Jingxing, his provisions must, given the terrain, be in the rear. Give me thirty thousand troops for a surprise operation to cut off his baggage train: this is the strategy for victory.” For a thousand years, people have regretted that his plan was not adopted. If that is so, then pulling out …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
赤幟於趙壁背綿水而為陣豈必賴井
陘而後可以成功耶是必有一說也諸
葛亮之伐魏而司馬懿謂諸將曰亮若
出武功依山而東誠為可憂若西上五
丈原諸將可以無事也當時信其說而
不疑若然則遺巾幗而必怒知食簡而
不喜豈必在出武功而後可以威敵耶
是必有一論也方今浙江東北沿海延
===
袤數千里海賊出没
朝廷深以為慮既設武臣以總督之又設憲
臣以監臨之然巡司弓兵僉自均徭守
倭軍士太半餘丁兼以邊海倉廒多半
空虛萬一有警敵之既無人守之又無
粮若何而可也爾諸士俱負窮經致用
之學可酌古準今條陳長治久安之策
以俟
punctuated: 赤幟於趙壁，背綿水而為陣，豈必賴井陘而後可以成功耶？是必有一說也。諸葛亮之伐魏，而司馬懿謂諸將曰：「亮若出武功，依山而東，誠為可憂；若西上五丈原，諸將可以無事也。」當時信其說而不疑。若然，則遺巾幗而必怒，知食簡而不喜，豈必在出武功而後可以威敵耶？是必有一論也。方今浙江東北沿海延袤數千里，海賊出没，朝廷深以為慮。既設武臣以總督之，又設憲臣以監臨之。然巡司弓兵僉自均徭，守倭軍士太半餘丁，兼以邊海倉廒多半空虛。萬一有警，敵之既無人，守之又無粮，若何而可也？爾諸士俱負窮經致用之學，可酌古準今，條陳長治久安之策，以俟
translation_en:
…red banners at Zhao’s ramparts and drawing up an army with its back to the Mian River—was success necessarily dependent on Jingxing? There must be an explanation for this.

When Zhuge Liang attacked Wei, Sima Yi told his generals: “If Liang advances through Wugong and proceeds eastward along the mountains, there will indeed be cause for concern. If he goes west up to Wuzhangyuan, you generals may remain untroubled.” At the time, his statement was believed without question. If so, then sending women’s headgear would surely provoke anger, while learning that he ate little brought no rejoicing [?]. Was advancing through Wugong necessarily the only way to overawe the enemy? There must be an argument to explain this.

At present, Zhejiang’s northeastern coastline stretches for several thousand li, and maritime bandits appear and disappear along it. The imperial court is deeply concerned. It has appointed a military official to exercise overall command and a censorial official to supervise. Yet the archers of the Police Offices are conscripted through the equitable corvée levy, and more than half the soldiers defending against Japanese pirates are surplus males from military households. Moreover, most coastal granaries stand empty. Should an alarm arise, there would be no men to meet the enemy and no grain to sustain the defense. How can this be remedied? You candidates all possess learning that thoroughly investigates the Classics and applies them to practical affairs. Weigh the precedents of antiquity against present circumstances and set out, point by point, policies for enduring order and lasting peace, in readiness for…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上問而發焉
問旱澇之災雖堯湯之世所不免也說者
謂彼災自災耳於堯湯之民無損焉書
曰有備無患傳曰凡事豫則立此之謂
歟浙為東南大藩民素富庶地瀕江海
比年以來陰陽愆伏水旱相仍浹旬淫
雨海水泛溢而一河兩岸民居之壞於
蕩析者在在有之經月不雨旱魃為虐
===
而東疇西畝禾稼之傷於枯槁者比比皆
是將欲委諸氣化歟則所司坐視之咎
有所歸將欲變置壇壝歟則
朝廷擅易之禁無敢任於斯二者日展轉往
來於心思焉此救災禦患所宜講也矧
備災易救災難攷之成周有救荒之政
可詳其目歟亦有治水之制可悉其實
歟他如後世或發廩减直以濟貧或聽
punctuated:
上問而發焉。

問：旱澇之災，雖堯湯之世所不免也。說者謂彼災自災耳，於堯湯之民無損焉。《書》曰：「有備無患。」《傳》曰：「凡事豫則立。」此之謂歟？浙為東南大藩，民素富庶，地瀕江海。比年以來，陰陽愆伏，水旱相仍。浹旬淫雨，海水泛溢，而一河兩岸，民居之壞於蕩析者，在在有之；經月不雨，旱魃為虐，而東疇西畝，禾稼之傷於枯槁者，比比皆是。將欲委諸氣化歟？則所司坐視之咎有所歸。將欲變置壇壝歟？則朝廷擅易之禁，無敢任。於斯二者，日展轉往來於心思焉。此救災禦患所宜講也。矧備災易，救災難。攷之成周，有救荒之政，可詳其目歟？亦有治水之制，可悉其實歟？他如後世，或發廩减直以濟貧，或聽
translation_en:
…to set them forth when His Majesty asks.

Question: Even in the ages of Yao and Tang, droughts and floods could not be avoided. Commentators say that those calamities remained merely calamities, doing no harm to the people of Yao and Tang. The Book of Documents says, “With preparation, there is no calamity.” The Record says, “In all affairs, advance preparation ensures success.” Is this what these sayings mean? Zhejiang is a great province of the southeast. Its population has long been prosperous and numerous, and its lands border rivers and the sea. In recent years, yin and yang have fallen out of their proper seasonal order, and floods and droughts have followed one another. When excessive rain continues for ten days, seawater overflows, and everywhere along both banks of a river people's dwellings are swept away and destroyed. When no rain falls for a month, the drought demon wreaks havoc, and crops wither and die in fields everywhere, east and west. Should we leave this to the transformations of nature? Then the responsible authorities would bear the blame for standing idly by. Should we alter the arrangement of altar enclosures [?]? Yet, faced with the court's prohibition on unauthorized alterations, no one dares undertake this. These two alternatives turn over and over in our minds each day. These are matters that must be considered in relieving disasters and warding off calamities. Moreover, preparing for disaster is easy; providing relief once it strikes is difficult. Looking back to the established Zhou order, there were policies for famine relief: can you explain their provisions in detail? There were also institutions for water management: can you give a full account of how they worked? As for later ages, some opened granaries and reduced grain prices to aid the poor, while others permitted…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
民興造以取給均有惠於浙者參之古
果有合歟或作石堤以防江潮或浚二
河以免市淘均有功於杭者行於今抑
克濟歟夫事不師古無以善於今徒便
諸今無以合於古諸生齎所蘊而来其
參酌古今務宜民情以合土俗我将採
其可行者轉而語之所司
punctuated: 民興造以取給，均有惠於浙者，參之古，果有合歟？或作石堤以防江潮，或浚二河以免市淘，均有功於杭者，行於今，抑克濟歟？夫事不師古，無以善於今；徒便諸今，無以合於古。諸生齎所蘊而来，其參酌古今，務宜民情，以合土俗。我将採其可行者，轉而語之所司。
translation_en:
…the people to undertake construction to earn their livelihood. These measures all benefited Zhejiang; compared with ancient practice, did they indeed accord with it? Some built stone embankments to guard against river tides; others dredged the two waterways to prevent scouring in the city [?]. These measures all benefited Hangzhou; if implemented today, could they prove effective?

In undertaking affairs, without taking antiquity as a model, one cannot achieve good results today; merely pursuing present convenience offers no means of according with antiquity. You students have come bearing your accumulated learning. Weigh ancient and present practices together, making every effort to suit the circumstances of the people and accord with local customs. I shall select those proposals that can be put into practice and convey them to the responsible officials.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十名
第一名 孫昇 餘姚縣學生 禮記
第二名 潘温 新昌縣學增廣生 書
第三名 姜森 慈谿縣學增廣生 詩
第四名 邵誠 太平縣學生 易
第五名 劉湜 山陰縣學增廣生 春秋
第六名 戴豪 太平縣學增廣生 書
===
第七名 陳邦直 紹興府學生 詩
第八名 莫立之 錢塘縣學生 易
第九名 丁養浩 仁和縣儒士 禮記
第十名 錢鏞 仁和縣學生 詩
第十一名 王宗積 紹興府學生 書
第十二名 姜鳳 天台縣學生 詩
第十三名 朱顯 紹興府學生 春秋
第十四名 許𡆠 開化縣學生 易
punctuated:
中式舉人九十名。

第一名，孫昇，餘姚縣學生，禮記。
第二名，潘温，新昌縣學增廣生，書。
第三名，姜森，慈谿縣學增廣生，詩。
第四名，邵誠，太平縣學生，易。
第五名，劉湜，山陰縣學增廣生，春秋。
第六名，戴豪，太平縣學增廣生，書。
第七名，陳邦直，紹興府學生，詩。

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
四書
顏淵喟然嘆曰仰之彌高鑽之彌堅瞻之在前
忽焉在後夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約
我以禮欲罷不能既竭吾才如有所立卓爾
雖欲從之末由也已
潘温
同考試官教諭單批場中作此題者多牽率一中字講甚不
快人此篇發明顏子學聖人處不馳不驟有學有見佳作也
同考試官訓導顧批行文條暢命意光明一結尤見學力可取
===
考試官教授劉批說顏子歸功聖人處三復讀之旨意焠然
考試官教諭鄭批此作周旋曲折殆繪畫然可謂之善作者也
大賢嘆聖道之高妙必述其教之有序與學之所
至也盖聖道高妙未易學也大賢因其教之有序
而學之有得是宜發嘆而歸功於聖人也歟昔顏
子學既有得無上事而喟然嘆曰我游夫子之門
學夫子之道以為高而可及耶則仰彌高而不可
及以為堅而可入耶則鑽彌堅而不可入何無窮
盡也從容以求之瞻之若在吾前勇猛以進之忽
punctuated:
四書

顏淵喟然嘆曰：「仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅；瞻之在前，忽焉在後。夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。欲罷不能，既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。雖欲從之，末由也已。」

潘温

同考試官教諭單批：「場中作此題者，多牽率一中字，講甚不快人。此篇發明顏子學聖人處，不馳不驟，有學有見，佳作也。」

同考試官訓導顧批：「行文條暢，命意光明，一結尤見學力，可取。」

考試官教授劉批：「說顏子歸功聖人處，三復讀之，旨意焠然。」

考試官教諭鄭批：「此作周旋曲折，殆繪畫然，可謂之善作者也。」

大賢嘆聖道之高妙，必述其教之有序與學之所至也。盖聖道高妙，未易學也。大賢因其教之有序，而學之有得，是宜發嘆而歸功於聖人也歟！昔顏子學既有得，無上事，而喟然嘆曰：「我游夫子之門，學夫子之道，以為高而可及耶？則仰彌高而不可及；以為堅而可入耶？則鑽彌堅而不可入。何無窮盡也！從容以求之，瞻之若在吾前；勇猛以進之，忽
translation_en:
Four Books

Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: “The more I look up to it, the higher it grows; the more I bore into it, the harder it becomes. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind me. The Master skillfully guides people step by step. He broadens me through learning and restrains me through ritual. Though I wish to stop, I cannot. When I have exhausted my abilities, something seems to stand loftily before me. Though I wish to follow it, I have no means of doing so.”

Pan Wen

Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: “Among those in the examination who wrote on this topic, many forced their interpretations around the single character zhong, ‘center’ [?], making their exposition quite unsatisfying. This essay elucidates how Master Yan learned from the sage, neither racing nor rushing. It displays learning and insight: an excellent work.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: “The writing is orderly and fluent, and its conception clear and luminous. The conclusion especially demonstrates the strength of his learning. Worthy of selection.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “On its explanation of Master Yan’s attributing his achievement to the sage, I have read it over three times: its purport is finely refined.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “This composition follows every turn and bend, almost as though painting a picture. Its author may be called an accomplished writer.”

When the great worthy marveled at the loftiness and subtlety of the sage’s Way, he necessarily described the orderly progression of the sage’s teaching and the point his own learning had reached. For the sage’s Way is lofty and subtle, and not readily learned. Through the orderly progression of that teaching, the great worthy attained something in his learning. Was it not fitting, then, that he should sigh in admiration and attribute his achievement to the sage?

In former times, Master Yan, having attained something in his learning, with ‘no higher undertaking’ [?], sighed deeply and said: “I have studied at the Master’s gate and learned the Master’s Way. Do I think it lofty yet within reach? The more I look up to it, the higher it grows, beyond my reach. Do I think it hard yet penetrable? The more I bore into it, the harder it becomes, beyond my power to penetrate. How inexhaustible it is! When I seek it calmly, I see it seemingly before me; when I advance toward it with courage and vigor, suddenly …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
焉又在吾後何無方體也夫子之道雖曰高妙其
教人也循循善誘先博我以文使我致知而為入
道之門然後約我以禮使我力行以為進道之路
教之有序如此故我從事於斯悅之之深自不容
已而吾才之既竭味之之至自不能止而吾力之
已盡由是向之高堅者今則如有卓立於吾前向
之前後者今則如見卓爾於吾目然見之雖親造
之尤難欲致知以從之歟夫子生而知也博文之
功將安施乎欲力行以從之歟夫子安而行也約
===
禮之功將安用乎吁顏子學既有得述其先難之
故後得之由而歸功於聖人如此其可謂深知聖
人而善學之者矣大抵顏子之知鄰於生知顏子
之行幾於安行其未至於卓爾之地者守之也非
化之也假之以年則不日而化矣何卓爾之不可
造乎奈何賢哉之稱方興喪予之嘆即繼惜哉
悠遠則博厚博厚則高明博厚所以載物也高
明所以覆物也悠久所以成物也
劉湜
punctuated:
焉又在吾後，何無方體也！夫子之道雖曰高妙，其教人也循循善誘。先博我以文，使我致知而為入道之門；然後約我以禮，使我力行以為進道之路。教之有序如此，故我從事於斯，悅之之深，自不容已，而吾才之既竭；味之之至，自不能止，而吾力之已盡。由是向之高堅者，今則如有卓立於吾前；向之前後者，今則如見卓爾於吾目。然見之雖親，造之尤難。欲致知以從之歟？夫子生而知也，博文之功將安施乎？欲力行以從之歟？夫子安而行也，約禮之功將安用乎？吁！顏子學既有得，述其先難之故、後得之由，而歸功於聖人如此，其可謂深知聖人而善學之者矣。大抵顏子之知鄰於生知，顏子之行幾於安行。其未至於卓爾之地者，守之也，非化之也。假之以年，則不日而化矣，何卓爾之不可造乎？奈何賢哉之稱方興，喪予之嘆即繼，惜哉！

悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。

劉湜
translation_en:
…suddenly it is again behind me. How it eludes any fixed position or form! Though the Master's Way is lofty and subtle, in teaching others he skillfully guides them step by step. First he broadens my learning through letters, enabling me to extend my knowledge and thereby providing a gateway into the Way; then he restrains me through ritual, enabling me to put it earnestly into practice and thereby providing a path for advancing in the Way. Such is the orderly sequence of his teaching. Thus, as I devote myself to it, my delight is so profound that I cannot desist, though I have already exhausted my abilities; my savoring of it is so complete that I cannot stop, though my strength is already spent. Consequently, what formerly seemed lofty and hard now seems to stand towering before me; what formerly appeared now ahead, now behind, now seems to rise distinctly before my eyes. Yet although I see it intimately, attaining it is all the harder. Would I extend my knowledge to follow him? The Master was born knowing: where, then, could the work of broadening my learning through letters be applied? Would I exert myself in practice to follow him? The Master acts with effortless ease: what use, then, could the work of restraining myself through ritual serve?

Ah! Having gained something through learning, Master Yan described the reasons for his initial difficulties and the means of his later attainment, attributing his achievement to the sage in this way. He may indeed be called one who deeply understood the sage and learned well from him. In general, Master Yan's knowledge approached that of one born knowing, and his conduct came close to effortless practice. That he had not yet reached that towering height was because he still held fast to the Way, rather than having been transformed by it. Had he been granted more years, he would before long have undergone that transformation. How could that towering height have remained beyond his reach? Alas, scarcely had the praise, “How worthy he is!” arisen when the lament, “Heaven has bereft me!” followed. How grievous!

Extending far and long, it becomes broad and substantial; broad and substantial, it becomes high and luminous. Through breadth and substance it bears all things; through height and luminosity it covers all things; through enduring constancy it brings all things to completion.

Liu Shi 劉湜.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導顧批此篇有鋪叙有發明場中似此不多見焉
同考試官教諭楚批中庸一題場中作者多拘拘如鶴處雞
籠局促不舒此作其氣奮騰其文暢達高薦無疑
考試官教授劉批體認真確不疾不徐佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批此作能發明聖人功業與天地同用可取
中庸論聖人功業極其盛故能與天地同其用也
盖功業之盛實德之著見也向非積久而益盛何
能與天地同其用也哉中庸二十六章發明天道
如此謂夫有至誠無息之盛德斯發而為至誠無
===
息之功業自其功業之悠遠者言之蕩蕩乎寬大
無促迫也穆穆乎廣遠無終窮也惟悠遠故其積
也漸仁摩義施及中國廣博而深厚焉惟博厚故
其發也巍乎成功煥乎文章高大而光明焉此實
德之著見積久而益盛也如此故其博厚之積也
奠群生於教養之區與地之所以載萬物者同其
用高明之發也囿萬類於畢照之下與天之所以
覆萬物者同其功至其博厚而悠久也無一物之
不得其所高明而悠久也無一物之不被其澤豈
punctuated:
同考試官訓導顧批：此篇有鋪叙，有發明，場中似此不多見焉。
同考試官教諭楚批：中庸一題，場中作者多拘拘，如鶴處雞籠，局促不舒。此作其氣奮騰，其文暢達，高薦無疑。
考試官教授劉批：體認真確，不疾不徐，佳作也。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作能發明聖人功業與天地同用，可取。
《中庸》論聖人功業極其盛，故能與天地同其用也。盖功業之盛，實德之著見也。向非積久而益盛，何能與天地同其用也哉？《中庸》二十六章發明天道如此，謂夫有至誠無息之盛德，斯發而為至誠無息之功業。自其功業之悠遠者言之，蕩蕩乎寬大無促迫也，穆穆乎廣遠無終窮也。惟悠遠，故其積也漸仁摩義，施及中國，廣博而深厚焉。惟博厚，故其發也巍乎成功，煥乎文章，高大而光明焉。此實德之著見，積久而益盛也如此。故其博厚之積也，奠群生於教養之區，與地之所以載萬物者同其用；高明之發也，囿萬類於畢照之下，與天之所以覆萬物者同其功。至其博厚而悠久也，無一物之不得其所；高明而悠久也，無一物之不被其澤。豈
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor, comments: This essay offers both ample exposition and illuminating explanation. Few essays like it are to be seen in this examination.
Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor, comments: On this topic from the Doctrine of the Mean, most candidates write with excessive constraint, like a crane confined in a chicken coop, cramped and unable to stretch out. This essay has soaring vigor and fluent expression. I have no hesitation in recommending it highly.
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: Its understanding is genuine and precise; its pace is neither hurried nor slow. An excellent essay.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: This essay illuminates how the sage’s achievements share the workings of Heaven and Earth. It merits acceptance.
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the supreme flourishing of the sage’s achievements, through which he can share the workings of Heaven and Earth. For the flourishing of his achievements is the visible manifestation of his true virtue. Had this not accumulated over time and grown ever more abundant, how could he share the workings of Heaven and Earth? Chapter twenty-six of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the Way of Heaven in this manner: where there is the abundant virtue of utmost sincerity without cease, it issues in achievements of utmost sincerity without cease. Speaking of the far-reaching endurance of these achievements, how vast they are—broad and capacious, without constraint! How august they are—extensive and far-reaching, without limit or end! Precisely because they endure and reach far, their accumulation, steeping people in benevolence and shaping them through righteousness, extends throughout the Central Kingdom, becoming broad and profound. Precisely because they are broad and profound, their manifestation is lofty in accomplishment and resplendent in cultural forms, elevated and bright. Such is the visible manifestation of true virtue, accumulating over time and growing ever more abundant. Thus, in the accumulation of his breadth and profundity, the sage establishes all living people within a realm of instruction and nurture, sharing the workings by which Earth bears the myriad things. In the manifestation of his loftiness and brightness, he encompasses all kinds of beings within an all-embracing illumination, sharing the accomplishment by which Heaven overspreads the myriad things. When his breadth and profundity are also enduring, there is not a single thing that fails to find its proper place; when his loftiness and brightness are also enduring, there is not a single thing that does not receive his beneficence. How could …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不與天地同一成物之妙乎是其本以悠遠致高
厚而高厚又悠久也聖人至誠功業何其盛哉大
抵誠之為道有以天而言者真實無妄自然而然
也有以人而言者未能真實無妄而欲其真實無
妄者也此章之論正以推明前章天道之意其所
積而成者乃其實德著見功效氣象之謂非謂在
己之德亦待積而後成也故章末引文王之事以
證之夫豈積累漸次之謂哉學者詳之
孔子聖之時者也孔子之謂集大成集大成也
===
者金聲而玉振之也金聲也者始條理也玉
振之也者終條理也始條理者智之事也終
條理者聖之事也智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
由射於百步之外也其至爾力也其中非爾
力也
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批孟子一題塲中俱能鋪叙求其能將樂之
始終射之巧力發明孔子聖之時中僅見此篇
同考試官教諭何批能以時字通貫一章深合題意
punctuated:
不與天地同一成物之妙乎？是其本以悠遠致高厚，而高厚又悠久也。聖人至誠功業何其盛哉！大抵誠之為道，有以天而言者，真實無妄，自然而然也；有以人而言者，未能真實無妄，而欲其真實無妄者也。此章之論，正以推明前章天道之意。其所積而成者，乃其實德著見功效氣象之謂，非謂在己之德亦待積而後成也。故章末引文王之事以證之，夫豈積累漸次之謂哉？學者詳之。
「孔子，聖之時者也。孔子之謂集大成。集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。金聲也者，始條理也；玉振之也者，終條理也。始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。」
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批：「孟子一題，塲中俱能鋪叙，求其能將樂之始終、射之巧力，發明孔子聖之時中，僅見此篇。」
同考試官教諭何批：「能以時字通貫一章，深合題意。」
translation_en:
…Does this not share with Heaven and Earth the same wondrous capacity to bring things to fulfillment? Thus, enduring far into time is the foundation by which he attains loftiness and breadth, and that loftiness and breadth in turn endure. How magnificent are the achievements of the sage’s utmost sincerity! Generally speaking, sincerity as a Way may be discussed in terms of Heaven: it is true and without falsity, spontaneously so. It may also be discussed in terms of human beings: they are not yet true and without falsity but seek to become so. The argument of this chapter precisely develops and clarifies the meaning of the Way of Heaven in the preceding chapter. What it describes as accumulating and reaching fulfillment refers to the effects and outward manifestations of the sage’s substantial virtue. It does not mean that the virtue within him must also await accumulation before becoming complete. Thus, the chapter concludes by citing King Wen’s deeds as evidence. How could this mean gradual accumulation through successive stages? Students should examine this carefully.
“Confucius was the sage who acted according to the time. Confucius is said to have gathered together the great culmination. Gathering together the great culmination is like sounding the bronze bell and concluding with the jade chime. Sounding the bronze bell begins the ordered sequence; concluding with the jade chime completes the ordered sequence. Beginning the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; completing the ordered sequence is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength. It is like shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away: reaching it is due to your strength, but hitting the mark is not due to your strength.”
Shao Cheng.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “On this question from the Mencius, all the candidates in the examination hall could provide an extended exposition. But when seeking an essay that could use the beginning and ending of music, and the skill and strength of archery, to illuminate how Confucius’s sagehood attained the mean appropriate to the time, I found only this one.”
Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “It succeeds in using the word ‘time’ to connect the entire chapter throughout, closely capturing the meaning of the topic.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授劉批融會傳註發明透徹真作手也
考試官敎諭鄭批此作不窘滯不放肆可采
大賢論聖人具時中之道既即樂以見其聖智之
全復即射以明夫聖智之義盖孔子之聖聖而時
中者也自非大賢即樂與射以著明之又何以見
其兼三子之聖而為一大聖也哉昔孟子之意謂
夫夷聖於清而不足於尹之任孔子可仕則仕可
止則止兼清與任而時出之焉尹聖於任而不足
於惠之和孔子可久則久可速則速兼任與和而
===
時出之焉夫孔子集三聖之事而為一大聖之事
如此不猶作樂者集衆音之小成而為一大成乎
集大成也者盖於其樂之未作而先擊鎛鐘以宣
其聲俟其樂之既闋而後擊特磬以收其韻金以
宣之則八音翕然並奏而脉絡不紊此始條理也
玉以收之則八音詘然皆止而脉絡通貫此終條
理也始條理者猶孔子知無不盡非智之事乎終
條理者猶孔子德無不全非聖之事乎然聖智之
事如此而聖智之義何如是故以智言之譬則射
punctuated:
考試官敎授劉批：融會傳註，發明透徹，真作手也。
考試官敎諭鄭批：此作不窘滯，不放肆，可采。
大賢論聖人具時中之道，既即樂以見其聖智之全，復即射以明夫聖智之義。盖孔子之聖，聖而時中者也。自非大賢即樂與射以著明之，又何以見其兼三子之聖而為一大聖也哉？昔孟子之意謂：夫夷聖於清，而不足於尹之任；孔子可仕則仕，可止則止，兼清與任而時出之焉。尹聖於任，而不足於惠之和；孔子可久則久，可速則速，兼任與和而時出之焉。夫孔子集三聖之事而為一大聖之事如此，不猶作樂者集衆音之小成而為一大成乎？集大成也者，盖於其樂之未作而先擊鎛鐘以宣其聲，俟其樂之既闋而後擊特磬以收其韻。金以宣之，則八音翕然並奏而脉絡不紊，此始條理也；玉以收之，則八音詘然皆止而脉絡通貫，此終條理也。始條理者，猶孔子知無不盡，非智之事乎？終條理者，猶孔子德無不全，非聖之事乎？然聖智之事如此，而聖智之義何如？是故以智言之，譬則射
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, an Instructor, comments: “He integrates the commentaries and annotations, elucidating their meaning thoroughly. Truly an accomplished writer.”
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: “This composition is neither constrained and labored nor unrestrained. It merits selection.”
In discussing how the sage possesses the Way of attaining the mean appropriate to the time, the great worthy first uses music to reveal the completeness of his sageliness and wisdom, then uses archery to clarify what sageliness and wisdom mean. For Confucius’s sageliness consists in being sage and attaining the mean appropriate to the time. Had the great worthy not made this manifest through music and archery, how could we see that Confucius combines the sageliness of the three masters and thus constitutes one great sage?
Mencius’s meaning was this: Bo Yi was sage in purity, yet fell short of Yi Yin’s sense of responsibility. Confucius took office when it was proper to take office and withdrew when it was proper to withdraw; he combined purity with responsibility, manifesting each as the time required. Yi Yin was sage in responsibility, yet fell short of Liuxia Hui’s harmony. Confucius remained long when it was proper to remain long and departed swiftly when it was proper to depart swiftly; he combined responsibility with harmony, manifesting each as the time required. Confucius thus gathered together the accomplishments of the three sages to constitute the accomplishments of one great sage. Is this not like a musician gathering the lesser completions of the many sounds into one grand completion?
As for gathering them into a grand completion: before the music begins, the large bell is struck to sound its opening; after the music has run its course, the single sounding stone is struck to gather in its resonance. When metal sounds the opening, the eight classes of instruments play together in concert, their interconnections undisturbed: this is bringing orderly articulation into being. When jade gathers in the close, the eight classes of instruments all cease together, their interconnections continuous throughout: this is bringing orderly articulation to completion. Bringing orderly articulation into being is like Confucius’s knowledge leaving nothing unfathomed—is this not the work of wisdom? Bringing orderly articulation to completion is like Confucius’s virtue lacking nothing—is this not the work of sageliness? Such, then, are the workings of sageliness and wisdom; but what do sageliness and wisdom mean? Thus, speaking of wisdom, it may be likened to archery …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之巧也以聖言之譬則射之力也由射於百歩之
外至其地者乃其力之所及非巧也中其的者乃
其巧之所致非力也由是觀之三子之力有餘而
巧不足孔子則巧力俱全聖智兼備此所以為聖
之時中也歟抑此章言三子之行各極其一偏孔
子之道兼全於衆理所以偏者由其蔽於始是以
缺於終所以全者由其知之至是以行之盡三子
猶春夏秋冬之各一其時孔子則太和元氣之流
行於四時也
===
易
父父子子兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正正家
而天下定矣象曰風自火出家人君子以言
有物而行有恒
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批家人一義求其簡明切當者僅見此篇
同考試官教諭何批此篇深得家人正倫理之義是宜錄出
考試官教授劉批易貴潔靜精微此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批發明家人之旨殆無餘蘊
punctuated:
之巧也。以聖言之，譬則射之力也。由射於百歩之外，至其地者，乃其力之所及，非巧也；中其的者，乃其巧之所致，非力也。由是觀之，三子之力有餘而巧不足，孔子則巧力俱全，聖智兼備，此所以為聖之時中也歟！抑此章言三子之行各極其一偏，孔子之道兼全於衆理。所以偏者，由其蔽於始，是以缺於終；所以全者，由其知之至，是以行之盡。三子猶春夏秋冬之各一其時，孔子則太和元氣之流行於四時也。

《易》

父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正。正家而天下定矣。《象》曰：「風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恒。」

邵誠

同考試官教諭陳批：「家人一義，求其簡明切當者，僅見此篇。」
同考試官教諭何批：「此篇深得家人正倫理之義，是宜錄出。」
考試官教授劉批：「易貴潔靜精微，此作得之。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「發明家人之旨，殆無餘蘊。」
translation_en:
…the skill of archery. As for sagehood, it may be compared to the strength used in archery. When shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away, reaching that distance is the effect of strength, not skill; hitting the target is the achievement of skill, not strength. Viewed in this light, the three masters had strength in abundance but insufficient skill. Kongzi possessed both skill and strength in full, combining sagehood and wisdom. Is this not why he was the sage who attained the mean appropriate to the time? Furthermore, this chapter explains that each of the three masters carried one particular aspect of conduct to its utmost, whereas Kongzi’s Way fully encompassed all principles. Their partiality arose from limitations in their understanding at the outset, resulting in deficiencies at the end. His completeness arose from the utmost understanding, resulting in the fullest realization in practice. The three masters were like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, each confined to its own season; Kongzi was like the primordial vital energy of supreme harmony circulating through all four seasons.

Book of Changes

When fathers act as fathers, sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, younger brothers as younger brothers, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives, the way of the family is rightly ordered. Set the family right, and all under Heaven will be settled. The Commentary on the Images says: “Wind issues from fire: the Family hexagram. Thus the gentleman gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.”

Shao Cheng

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Among essays on the meaning of the Family hexagram, this alone meets the requirements of concision, clarity, relevance, and aptness.”
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “This essay profoundly grasps the Family hexagram’s meaning of setting human relationships in proper order. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The Book of Changes prizes purity, stillness, precision, and subtlety. This composition achieves these qualities.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Its elucidation of the purport of the Family hexagram leaves scarcely any underlying meaning unexplored.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
推卦畫以見正家之化因卦象以著正家之本盖
天下之本在於家而家之本則在於身也彖象聖
人互言以示人其意至矣昔吾夫子傳家人之彖
而推之卦畫謂夫上焉為父初焉為子則父子之
分嚴五焉為兄三焉為弟則兄弟之倫序五三夫
也夫正位乎外四二婦也婦正位乎內如此家道
其有不正乎家道旣正殆見天下之大凡為父子
兄弟者莫不於焉是則是效各安其分焉四海之
廣凡為夫夫婦婦者莫不於焉是儀是刑各止其
===
所焉若然天下其有不定乎夫天下之定固本於
正家而家之正又本於脩身焉且家人之卦貞體
離也其象為火悔體巽也其象為風風自火出自
內及外有家人之象也君子體之言不虛言而言
皆切乎倫理則言為有物矣行非偽行而行必本
於倫理則行為有恒矣言行相顧則其身脩而家
豈有不治哉聖人以是傳家人之象厥旨微矣抑
論之言行者一身之樞機也一身之樞機一家之
規範也一家之規範天下之規範也能脩其身則
punctuated:
推卦畫以見正家之化，因卦象以著正家之本。盖天下之本在於家，而家之本則在於身也。彖象聖人互言以示人，其意至矣。昔吾夫子傳家人之彖，而推之卦畫，謂夫上焉為父，初焉為子，則父子之分嚴；五焉為兄，三焉為弟，則兄弟之倫序；五三夫也，夫正位乎外；四二婦也，婦正位乎內。如此，家道其有不正乎？家道旣正，殆見天下之大，凡為父子兄弟者，莫不於焉是則是效，各安其分焉；四海之廣，凡為夫夫婦婦者，莫不於焉是儀是刑，各止其所焉。若然，天下其有不定乎？

夫天下之定，固本於正家，而家之正，又本於脩身焉。且家人之卦，貞體離也，其象為火；悔體巽也，其象為風。風自火出，自內及外，有家人之象也。君子體之，言不虛言，而言皆切乎倫理，則言為有物矣；行非偽行，而行必本於倫理，則行為有恒矣。言行相顧，則其身脩，而家豈有不治哉？聖人以是傳家人之象，厥旨微矣。

抑論之，言行者，一身之樞機也；一身之樞機，一家之規範也；一家之規範，天下之規範也。能脩其身，則
translation_en:
By drawing out the meaning of the hexagram’s lines, one sees the transforming influence of setting the family right; through the hexagram’s images, one makes clear the foundation of setting the family right. For the foundation of all under Heaven lies in the family, and the foundation of the family lies in the self. In the Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Image, the sage presents complementary explanations to instruct people: his meaning is most complete. When our Master expounded the Judgment of the hexagram The Family (Jiaren), he drew out the meaning of its lines. The top line represents the father and the first line the son, so the distinction between father and son is strict. The fifth represents the elder brother and the third the younger brother, so the relationship between elder and younger brothers is properly ordered. The fifth and third represent husbands: the husband takes his proper place outside. The fourth and second represent wives: the wife takes her proper place within. With things thus arranged, how could the way of the family fail to be correct? Once the way of the family is correct, we may expect to see, throughout the vastness of all under Heaven, every father and son, elder and younger brother taking this as their standard and example, each content in his allotted role. Throughout the breadth of the Four Seas, all husbands and wives will take this as their pattern and model, each abiding in the proper place. If this is so, how could all under Heaven fail to be settled?

The settling of all under Heaven is indeed rooted in setting the family right, while setting the family right is in turn rooted in cultivating oneself. Now, in the hexagram The Family, the inner trigram is Li, whose image is fire; the outer trigram is Xun, whose image is wind. Wind issues from fire, proceeding from within to without: this presents the image of the family. The gentleman embodies this. His words are not empty words, but all bear directly upon the principles governing human relationships; thus his words have substance. His actions are not feigned actions, but necessarily rest upon those principles; thus his conduct has constancy. When words and actions accord with each other, he cultivates himself; how then could his family fail to be well governed? It is through this that the sage expounds the Image of The Family. Its purport is subtle indeed.

To discuss this further: words and actions are the pivotal workings of the self. The pivotal workings of the self constitute the standard for a family, and the standard for a family constitutes the standard for all under Heaven. If one can cultivate oneself, then…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家豈有不齊國豈有不治天下豈有不平乎不然
大學何以曰欲治其國先齊其家欲齊其家先脩
其身
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖人南
面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此也坤也者
地也萬物皆致養焉故曰致役乎坤兌正秋
也萬物之所說也故曰說言乎兌
莫立之
同考試官教諭陳批本德位象時而兼以物隨帝出入為言說
===
卦之義於斯備矣易卷如子者指不多屈
同考試官教諭何批此篇以德位象時立說深得本旨
考試官教授劉批講析明白非熟於易者不能允宜高薦
考試官教諭鄭批易義如此作詳明者不多見
聖人說後天之卦有舉德位而推其義者有舉象
時而申其義者甚矣後天易卦之妙也自非聖人
舉其德位象時而互言之其義何自而見哉昔吾
夫子說卦論後天之易謂夫離之為卦具中虛之
體有明照之德故萬物之隨帝出乎震者莫不煥
punctuated:
家豈有不齊，國豈有不治，天下豈有不平乎？不然，《大學》何以曰：「欲治其國，先齊其家；欲齊其家，先脩其身。」

離也者，明也，萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。坤也者，地也，萬物皆致養焉，故曰：「致役乎坤。」兌，正秋也，萬物之所說也，故曰：「說言乎兌。」

莫立之

同考試官教諭陳批：本德位象時，而兼以物隨帝出入為言，《說卦》之義於斯備矣。易卷如子者，指不多屈。

同考試官教諭何批：此篇以德位象時立說，深得本旨。

考試官教授劉批：講析明白，非熟於易者不能，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭鄭批：易義如此作詳明者，不多見。

聖人說後天之卦，有舉德位而推其義者，有舉象時而申其義者。甚矣，後天易卦之妙也！自非聖人舉其德位象時而互言之，其義何自而見哉？昔吾夫子《說卦》論後天之易，謂夫離之為卦，具中虛之體，有明照之德，故萬物之隨帝出乎震者，莫不煥
translation_en:
…how could the family fail to be put in order, the state fail to be governed, or all under Heaven fail to be brought to peace? Otherwise, why does the Great Learning say: “Those wishing to govern their states first put their families in order; those wishing to put their families in order first cultivate themselves”?

“Li means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the trigram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven, turning toward the light to govern: he presumably takes his pattern from this. Kun means earth. All things receive nourishment there; hence the saying, ‘He brings them to service in Kun.’ Dui is the height of autumn, when all things rejoice; hence the saying, ‘He gladdens them in Dui.’”

Mo Lizhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Taking the trigrams’ attributes, positions, images, and seasons as its basis, this essay also discusses how things follow the Lord on High in emerging and withdrawing. The meaning of the Explanation of the Trigrams is fully conveyed here. Papers on the Changes like yours can be counted on very few fingers.

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: This essay develops its argument through attributes, positions, images, and seasons, thoroughly grasping the original purport.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: The exposition and analysis are clear. Only someone thoroughly familiar with the Changes could achieve this. It certainly deserves recommendation at a high rank.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Essays on the meaning of the Changes as detailed and lucid as this are seldom seen.

In explaining the trigrams of the Later Heaven arrangement, the sage sometimes adduces their attributes and positions to draw out their meaning, and sometimes adduces their images and seasons to elaborate their meaning. How profound are the subtleties of the trigrams of the Changes in the Later Heaven arrangement! Had the sage not brought forward their attributes, positions, images, and seasons and discussed them in relation to one another, how could their meaning have become apparent? Long ago, our Master discussed the Changes in its Later Heaven arrangement in the Explanation of the Trigrams. His meaning was that Li, as a trigram, has a form empty at its center and the attribute of illuminating brightness. Thus all things that follow the Lord on High in emerging in Zhen invariably shine brilliantly…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
然昭明于焉而相見乃為南方之卦焉萬物之隨
帝齊乎巽者靡不藹然暢茂于焉而嘉會位乎正
南之方焉是以聖人端冕凝旒面乎正南而聽天
下者非有取於此乎明目達聰嚮乎離明而治萬
民者又非取於是乎然物固隨帝以相見於離矣
而致養則在於坤焉蓋坤之為卦三畫皆陰有地
之象也物之相見於離者今皆委之於厚載之中
而各遂其長養之天物之嘉會于離者今悉致之
於含弘之內而各遂其發育之性故曰致役乎坤
===
者此也夫物既隨帝以致役於坤矣而和悅則又
在於兌焉蓋兌之為卦居乎正西之位適乎正秋
之時故向焉物之長養於坤者今則各正性命不
相假借而自足也昔焉物之發育於坤者今則保
合大和不相凌奪而自適也故曰說言乎兌者此
也是知離以德位言固足以明坤兌之德位坤兌
以象時言亦足以明離之象時也聖人以是說後
天之卦寧復有餘蘊哉抑考大傳上章明先天之
學以著其對待之體也此章論後天之學以明其
punctuated: 然昭明，于焉而相見，乃為南方之卦焉。萬物之隨帝齊乎巽者，靡不藹然暢茂，于焉而嘉會，位乎正南之方焉。是以聖人端冕凝旒，面乎正南而聽天下者，非有取於此乎？明目達聰，嚮乎離明而治萬民者，又非取於是乎？然物固隨帝以相見於離矣，而致養則在於坤焉。蓋坤之為卦，三畫皆陰，有地之象也。物之相見於離者，今皆委之於厚載之中，而各遂其長養之天；物之嘉會于離者，今悉致之於含弘之內，而各遂其發育之性。故曰「致役乎坤」者，此也。夫物既隨帝以致役於坤矣，而和悅則又在於兌焉。蓋兌之為卦，居乎正西之位，適乎正秋之時。故向焉物之長養於坤者，今則各正性命，不相假借而自足也；昔焉物之發育於坤者，今則保合大和，不相凌奪而自適也。故曰「說言乎兌」者，此也。是知離以德位言，固足以明坤兌之德位；坤兌以象時言，亦足以明離之象時也。聖人以是說後天之卦，寧復有餘蘊哉？抑考大傳，上章明先天之學，以著其對待之體也；此章論後天之學，以明其
translation_en:
…shine brightly and become manifest to one another here: thus Li is the trigram of the south. The myriad things that follow the Lord on High and attain orderly completion in Xun all flourish luxuriantly and meet here in a splendid convergence; its position is due south. Thus, when the sage ruler, in ceremonial robes and cap, with its pendant strings of jade held still, faces due south to hear the affairs of the realm, does he not take his pattern from this? When he makes his sight clear and his hearing perceptive, facing the brightness of Li to govern the myriad people, does he not likewise take his pattern from this? Yet although things follow the Lord on High and become manifest to one another in Li, it is in Kun that they receive nourishment. For Kun is a trigram whose three lines are all yin, and it has the image of earth. The things that became manifest to one another in Li are now all entrusted to earth’s substantial support, each fulfilling its Heaven-given capacity for growth and nourishment. The things that met in splendid convergence in Li are now all brought within earth’s capacious embrace, each fulfilling its nature through development. This is what is meant by “He brings them to service in Kun.”

Once things have followed the Lord on High and been brought to service in Kun, their harmony and joy lie in Dui. For the trigram Dui occupies the position due west and corresponds to the season of mid-autumn. Thus the things formerly nourished in Kun now each attain their proper nature and allotted destiny, self-sufficient without borrowing from one another. The things that formerly developed in Kun now preserve and unite in supreme harmony, at ease without encroaching upon or taking from one another. This is what is meant by “He gives them joy in Dui.” We therefore know that explaining Li through its virtue and position is indeed sufficient to illuminate the virtues and positions of Kun and Dui; explaining Kun and Dui through their images and seasons is likewise sufficient to illuminate the image and season of Li. When the sage explains the trigrams of the Later Heaven in this way, can any meaning remain undisclosed? Moreover, examining the Great Commentary, the preceding chapter elucidates the learning of the Earlier Heaven to reveal its underlying configuration of paired opposites; this chapter discusses the learning of the Later Heaven to elucidate its…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
流行之用也至於下章則又合先天後天而言之
焉是則非先天無以為後天之體非後天無以為
先天之用此先天後天所以可相有而不可相無
者歟
書
欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
戴豪
同考試官訓導顧批此題本難於摸寫求其能說出有周大臣祈君永命之意僅見此篇非究心於本領者不能高薦奚疑
===
同考試官教諭單批人臣忠愛其君之意此作發明殆盡
考試官教授劉批理到詞充佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批能形容題意而且質實不浮可取
歷年遠而世保其民此大臣祈君永命之意也盖
永天命而世保民不易致也大臣祈君永命而言
及乎此其忠愛無窮之心為何如哉吾想有周大
臣祈君之意若曰我向告王以明德而懷諸侯用
德而和迷民豈有他哉盖將有所祈也祈之何如
惟曰我周之有天下自今至于後日不徒百斯年
punctuated:
流行之用也。至於下章，則又合先天後天而言之焉。是則非先天無以為後天之體，非後天無以為先天之用。此先天後天所以可相有而不可相無者歟？

書
欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
戴豪

同考試官訓導顧批：此題本難於摸寫，求其能說出有周大臣祈君永命之意，僅見此篇。非究心於本領者不能，高薦奚疑？
同考試官教諭單批：人臣忠愛其君之意，此作發明殆盡。
考試官教授劉批：理到詞充，佳作也。
考試官教諭鄭批：能形容題意，而且質實不浮，可取。

歷年遠而世保其民，此大臣祈君永命之意也。盖永天命而世保民，不易致也。大臣祈君永命而言及乎此，其忠愛無窮之心為何如哉！吾想有周大臣祈君之意，若曰：我向告王以明德而懷諸侯，用德而和迷民，豈有他哉？盖將有所祈也。祈之何如？惟曰：我周之有天下，自今至于後日，不徒百斯年
translation_en:
…its operation in ongoing circulation. In the following chapter, however, the Prior-to-Heaven and Subsequent-to-Heaven arrangements are discussed together. Thus, without the Prior-to-Heaven arrangement, there would be no underlying structure for the Subsequent-to-Heaven arrangement; without the Subsequent-to-Heaven arrangement, there would be no functioning of the Prior-to-Heaven arrangement. Is this why the two can coexist but cannot dispense with one another?

Book of Documents
“For it to endure for ten thousand years, may the king’s sons and grandsons forever protect the people.”
Dai Hao

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: “This topic is inherently difficult to portray. In seeking an essay capable of expressing the Zhou minister’s wish for his ruler’s enduring mandate, I have found only this one.
