Someone who had not devoted himself to the fundamentals could not achieve this. Why hesitate to recommend it highly?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: “This composition elucidates almost exhaustively the loyal affection a minister bears his ruler.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Its reasoning is sound and its expression full: an excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “It brings out the meaning of the topic and is substantial and grounded, without superficiality. It merits selection.”

That the years should extend far into the future and that successive generations should protect their people: this is what the great minister meant in wishing his ruler an enduring mandate. For perpetuating Heaven’s Mandate and protecting the people generation after generation are not easily achieved. When the great minister, wishing his ruler an enduring mandate, spoke of this, how boundless was his heart’s loyal affection! I imagine the intention of the great minister of Zhou in expressing this wish for his ruler as though he were saying: “Earlier I told the king to make his virtue bright and thereby win over the regional lords, and to employ virtue and thereby bring harmony to the misguided people. Could I have had any other purpose? I had a wish to express. What was that wish? Simply this: that our Zhou’s possession of All-under-Heaven, from now into the days to come, should last not merely a hundred years…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而已雖千斯年未多也不徒千斯年而已欲至于
萬斯年而後可焉殆必繼王而為子者穆穆皇皇
宜君宜王皆以明德而永安斯民非特一世為然
而世世之為子者莫不以嗣以續於無窮所謂天
子萬年者于是矣繼子而為孫者本支百世君臨
萬邦皆用明德而承保萬民非惟一代為爾而代
代之為孫者莫不勿替引之於悠久所謂無疆惟
休者于是矣吁古人於進戒之餘而不忘乎祈禱
之誠祈禱之中而猶存乎勸戒之意忠君愛國之
===
心一何至哉嘗觀此章有周人臣之祈君既曰欲
至于萬年者所以歆動之也又曰惟王子子孫孫
永保民者又所以規戒之也告之未幾而戒之隨
至如此惜乎全書不可見而忠愛猶可想厥後周
家卜世三十歷年八百其大臣祈君永命之明驗
歟
予不允惟若茲誥予惟曰襄我二人汝有合哉
言曰在時二人天休滋至惟時二人弗戡其
汝克敬德明我俊民在讓後人于丕時嗚呼
punctuated:
而已，雖千斯年未多也。不徒千斯年而已，欲至于萬斯年而後可焉。殆必繼王而為子者，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王，皆以明德而永安斯民，非特一世為然，而世世之為子者，莫不以嗣以續於無窮，所謂天子萬年者于是矣。繼子而為孫者，本支百世，君臨萬邦，皆用明德而承保萬民，非惟一代為爾，而代代之為孫者，莫不勿替引之於悠久，所謂無疆惟休者于是矣。吁！古人於進戒之餘，而不忘乎祈禱之誠；祈禱之中，而猶存乎勸戒之意。忠君愛國之心，一何至哉！嘗觀此章，有周人臣之祈君，既曰欲至于萬年者，所以歆動之也；又曰惟王子子孫孫永保民者，又所以規戒之也。告之未幾，而戒之隨至如此。惜乎全書不可見，而忠愛猶可想。厥後周家卜世三十，歷年八百，其大臣祈君永命之明驗歟？
予不允，惟若茲誥。予惟曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉？」言曰：「在時二人，天休滋至，惟時二人弗戡。其汝克敬德，明我俊民，在讓後人于丕時。嗚呼！
translation_en:
…alone; even a thousand years would not be many. Nor should it be merely a thousand years: only ten thousand years would suffice. Surely the sons who succeed the king must be reverent and illustrious, fit to be lords and kings, all using manifest virtue to bring lasting peace to this people. Nor should this hold for just one generation: successive generations of sons must all carry on the succession without end. Herein lies the meaning of “May the Son of Heaven live ten thousand years.” The grandsons who succeed those sons, perpetuating the main line and its branches for a hundred generations and ruling over the myriad states, must all employ manifest virtue to continue protecting the myriad people. Nor should this hold for just one generation: successive generations of grandsons must all sustain it without decline into the distant future. Herein lies the meaning of “May their glory be boundless.” Ah! Even after presenting admonitions, the ancients did not forget the sincerity of prayer; and even within their prayers, they retained the intention to exhort and admonish. How consummate was their devotion to their ruler and love for their state! I have considered this chapter: in praying for their ruler, the ministers of Zhou first spoke of wishing his reign to extend to ten thousand years, thereby inspiring him; then they spoke of the king’s sons and grandsons protecting the people forever, thereby admonishing him. Scarcely had they addressed him before admonition followed in this way. Alas, the complete document cannot be seen, yet their loyal affection can still be imagined. Thereafter, the house of Zhou endured for thirty generations, as foretold by divination, and lasted eight hundred years. Was this not clear evidence of the efficacy of its great ministers’ prayers for their ruler’s enduring mandate?
“I am not believed [?]; thus do I make this declaration. I say only: ‘Help us two: will you join with us?’ I say: ‘Upon these two men, Heaven’s blessings came ever more abundantly; yet these two men could not fully bear them. May you indeed revere virtue and bring our outstanding men to prominence, so as to hand on a great season of prosperity to those who come after. Ah! …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
篤棐時二人我式克至于今日休我咸成文
王功于不怠丕冒海隅出日罔不率俾公曰
君子不惠若茲多誥予惟用閔于天越民
潘温
同考試官訓導顧批此篇以天命民心立說深合本旨
同考試官教諭單批此題頭緒頗多難於包括是篇文法簡
勁而理致炳如槩視初場無出其右矣
考試官教授劉批長題貴斂繁就實此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批寫出周公留召公之深意可佳
===
大臣之留同列也既原已之致誥而欲共念乎天
民復申已之詳誥而惟用憂乎天民盖大臣一身
天命民心所繫也苟於求去而不反覆致誥以留
之又何以終天命而安民心哉昔召公告老而去
周公留之若曰商周群臣之輔君文武受命之惟
艱我嘗為公告矣豈不信於人而若此告語乎予
惟曰王業之成在我二人汝聞我言而有合哉亦
曰在是二人但天命我周休嘉滋至惟我二人將
不堪勝汝若以盈滿為懼則當勉自敬德益加寅
punctuated:
篤棐時二人，我式克至于今日休。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。公曰：「君子不惠若茲多誥，予惟用閔于天越民。」
潘温
同考試官訓導顧批：此篇以天命民心立說，深合本旨。
同考試官教諭單批：此題頭緒頗多，難於包括。是篇文法簡勁，而理致炳如，槩視初場，無出其右矣。
考試官教授劉批：長題貴斂繁就實，此作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批：寫出周公留召公之深意，可佳。
大臣之留同列也，既原已之致誥而欲共念乎天民，復申已之詳誥而惟用憂乎天民。盖大臣一身，天命民心所繫也。苟於求去而不反覆致誥以留之，又何以終天命而安民心哉？昔召公告老而去，周公留之，若曰：「商周群臣之輔君，文武受命之惟艱，我嘗為公告矣。豈不信於人而若此告語乎？予惟曰：王業之成，在我二人。汝聞我言而有合哉？亦曰：在是二人。但天命我周，休嘉滋至，惟我二人將不堪勝。汝若以盈滿為懼，則當勉自敬德，益加寅
translation_en:
…Through the devoted assistance of us two, we have thus been able to attain the blessings of this day. Let us together complete King Wen’s achievement without flagging, extending its protection broadly to the remotest shores where the sun rises, so that none fail to follow and obey. The Duke said: “You, sir, do not acquiesce in these repeated admonitions; I offer them only out of concern for Heaven and the people.”

Pan Wen 潘温

Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This essay grounds its argument in Heaven’s Mandate and the people’s hearts, closely matching the fundamental meaning.”

Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor, comments: “This topic has many strands, which are difficult to encompass. This essay’s composition is concise and vigorous, and its reasoning shines clearly. Surveying the first-session essays as a whole, none surpasses it.”

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “With a long topic, what matters is drawing its many strands together and getting to the substance. This composition achieves that.”

Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “It brings out the profound intention behind the Duke of Zhou’s efforts to retain the Duke of Shao. Admirable.”

When a great minister seeks to retain a colleague, he first explains his reasons for admonishing him, wishing that they should together keep Heaven and the people in mind; he then reiterates his detailed admonitions, solely out of concern for Heaven and the people. For Heaven’s Mandate and the people’s hearts depend upon the person of a great minister. If, when such a minister seeks to leave, one does not repeatedly admonish him in order to retain him, how can one bring Heaven’s Mandate to fulfillment and set the people’s hearts at ease?

Formerly, when the Duke of Shao sought retirement on grounds of age, the Duke of Zhou urged him to remain, saying in effect: “I have already spoken to you, Duke, about how the ministers of Shang and Zhou assisted their rulers, and how difficult it was for Kings Wen and Wu to receive the Mandate. Could it be that I speak to you in this way because I do not trust you? I say only that the completion of the royal enterprise rests with us two. Having heard my words, do you agree? You too say that it rests with these two men. Yet Heaven has bestowed its Mandate upon our Zhou, and blessings and favors arrive in increasing abundance; we two may prove unable to bear them. If you fear the fullness of our prosperity, you should exert yourself to honor virtue and become still more reverent …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
畏明揚俊民布列庶位以盡大臣之職業以答滋
至之天休他日推遜後人於盛大之時而去可也
今天休未答豈汝辭位之時乎夫天休固所當答
而民心尤所當圖故又嘆息而告之以為惟我二
人左右之功既篤于前時故政教之美式隆於今
日然未可以自足也尤當并力一心共成文王
未終之功而罔敢或怠仁覆天下使海隅日出之
地無不臣服可也今遠人未俾豈汝求退之時乎
然周公之言雖切恐召公之意未信於是又稱君
===
以尊之而申其意謂夫共答天命咸服民心我今
為公告矣豈不順于理而若茲多誥耶誠以乘茲
大命公之責也今而遽去則乘載無所托而天命
不終矣此我所為憂焉命作民極公之任也今而
不留則作極無其人而斯民無賴矣此我所為閔
焉吁始言若茲誥終言若茲多誥周公之告召公
其言語之際亦可悲矣大抵成功不居大臣之道
故洛邑既成周公告歸成王親政召公退休雖然
忠君憂國之心未嘗已也是以迪將之言一出而
punctuated: 畏，明揚俊民，布列庶位，以盡大臣之職業，以答滋至之天休。他日推遜後人，於盛大之時而去，可也。今天休未答，豈汝辭位之時乎？夫天休固所當答，而民心尤所當圖。故又嘆息而告之，以為惟我二人左右之功，既篤于前時，故政教之美，式隆於今日。然未可以自足也，尤當并力一心，共成文王未終之功，而罔敢或怠。仁覆天下，使海隅日出之地無不臣服，可也。今遠人未俾，豈汝求退之時乎？然周公之言雖切，恐召公之意未信，於是又稱君以尊之，而申其意，謂夫共答天命，咸服民心，我今為公告矣，豈不順于理而若茲多誥耶？誠以乘茲大命，公之責也。今而遽去，則乘載無所托，而天命不終矣，此我所為憂焉。命作民極，公之任也。今而不留，則作極無其人，而斯民無賴矣，此我所為閔焉。吁！始言若茲誥，終言若茲多誥，周公之告召公，其言語之際亦可悲矣！大抵成功不居，大臣之道。故洛邑既成，周公告歸；成王親政，召公退休。雖然，忠君憂國之心未嘗已也。是以迪將之言一出而
translation_en:
…in reverent awe, publicly promote outstanding men and array them in the various offices, thereby fulfilling the duties of a great minister and responding to Heaven’s blessings as they increasingly arrive. On some future day, you may yield to your successors and depart at a time of flourishing greatness. But now, when Heaven’s blessings have yet to be requited, how can this be the time for you to resign your office?

Heaven’s blessings must certainly be requited, but the people’s hearts deserve particular consideration. Thus the Duke of Zhou again sighed and addressed him: “The two of us rendered substantial service in assisting the ruler in earlier days; hence the excellence of government and instruction has attained its present eminence. Yet we must not be content with ourselves. We should especially unite our strength and purpose to complete King Wen’s unfinished work, never daring to slacken. Our benevolence should shelter all under Heaven, so that none, even in the coastal regions where the sun rises, fail to acknowledge our rule. Now, when distant peoples have not yet been brought to submission [?], how can this be the time for you to seek retirement?”

Although the Duke of Zhou’s words were earnest, he feared that the Duke of Shao was not yet persuaded. He therefore further honored him by addressing him as “lord” and reiterated his meaning: “I have now spoken to you, my lord, about jointly answering Heaven’s mandate and winning all the people’s hearts. Would I offer so many admonitions if they did not accord with reason? Truly, bearing this great mandate is your responsibility. If you leave abruptly now, there will be no one to whom its burden can be entrusted, and Heaven’s mandate will not be carried through to completion. This is what troubles me. Being charged to serve as the people’s standard is your duty. If you will not remain now, there will be no one to establish that standard, and these people will have no one to depend upon. This is what grieves me.”

Alas! At the beginning he says, “admonish you thus,” and at the end, “offer so many admonitions thus.” In the Duke of Zhou’s address to the Duke of Shao, the very words convey sorrow! In general, to accomplish one’s work without remaining in office is the way of a great minister. Thus, once Luoyi was completed, the Duke of Zhou requested leave to return home; when King Cheng assumed personal rule, the Duke of Shao retired. Nevertheless, their devotion to their ruler and concern for the state never ceased. Thus, once the words about guiding and supporting were uttered …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事畢矣居室之治其可緩乎彼茅所以補屋也則
晝往取茅以為覆蓋之需索所以編茅也則夜而
絞索以為束縛之用于以亟乗其屋而葺理之惟
勤于以急升其居而營繕之不懈所以然者豈好
勞哉盖以来歲將至吾民欲播穀於南畝而不暇
於此也来春將及吾民欲有事於西疇而不遑於
斯也夫農事固不可忘而君事尤所當備彼二陽
之月固陰沍寒氷可取也吾則趨事赴工而鑿之
冲冲焉三陽之月風未解凍氷可藏也吾則併力
===
齊心而納于氷室焉所以然者豈惡逸哉盖以四
陽司令蚤朝届期吾君將獻彼羔羊而司寒是祀
以行乎啟氷之禮矣可不及時而為之藏乎將取
彼新韭而司寒是祭以舉乎開氷之儀矣可不先
時而為之備乎邠民不待督責而自相勸戒如此
非先公風化之厚能若是哉大抵七月之詩一言
以蔽之曰豫而已大寒在冬而備之於秋收成在
秋而圖之於春蠶績未成而曰為公子裳狩獵未
舉而曰為公子裘嘉蔬以養老朋酒以獻君拳拳
punctuated: 事畢矣，居室之治，其可緩乎？彼茅所以補屋也，則晝往取茅，以為覆蓋之需；索所以編茅也，則夜而絞索，以為束縛之用。于以亟乗其屋，而葺理之惟勤；于以急升其居，而營繕之不懈。所以然者，豈好勞哉？盖以来歲將至，吾民欲播穀於南畝，而不暇於此也；来春將及，吾民欲有事於西疇，而不遑於斯也。夫農事固不可忘，而君事尤所當備。彼二陽之月，固陰沍寒，氷可取也，吾則趨事赴工而鑿之冲冲焉；三陽之月，風未解凍，氷可藏也，吾則併力齊心而納于氷室焉。所以然者，豈惡逸哉？盖以四陽司令，蚤朝届期，吾君將獻彼羔羊，而司寒是祀，以行乎啟氷之禮矣，可不及時而為之藏乎？將取彼新韭，而司寒是祭，以舉乎開氷之儀矣，可不先時而為之備乎？邠民不待督責，而自相勸戒如此，非先公風化之厚，能若是哉？大抵《七月》之詩，一言以蔽之，曰豫而已。大寒在冬，而備之於秋；收成在秋，而圖之於春；蠶績未成，而曰「為公子裳」；狩獵未舉，而曰「為公子裘」。嘉蔬以養老，朋酒以獻君，拳拳
translation_en:
…the work is finished. Can the repair of their dwellings be delayed? Thatch is used to mend roofs, so by day they go to gather it to provide the necessary covering; rope is used to bind the thatch, so at night they twist ropes for fastening it. They promptly climb onto their roofs and diligently repair them; they hasten up onto their dwellings and work tirelessly at their upkeep. Why do they do this? Is it because they delight in toil? It is because the coming year draws near: our people will want to sow grain in the southern fields and will have no time for this. The coming spring approaches: our people will want to work in the western fields and will have no leisure for these tasks.

Agricultural work certainly must not be forgotten, but preparations for service to the lord are especially necessary. In the month of the second yang, when the yin is firmly established and the cold freezes everything, ice can be harvested. We hurry to the task and set to work cutting it with resounding blows. In the month of the third yang, when the winds have not yet thawed the ice, it can be stored. We unite our strength and purpose to place it in the icehouse. Why do we do this? Is it because we dislike ease? It is because, when the fourth yang holds sway and the appointed early morning arrives, our lord will offer a lamb in worship to the Spirit of Cold, performing the rite of opening the icehouse. Can we fail to store the ice in good time for him? He will take fresh chives and sacrifice to the Spirit of Cold, conducting the ceremony of opening the icehouse. Can we fail to make preparations for him beforehand?

The people of Bin encourage and admonish one another in this way without waiting for supervision or reprimand. Could they be like this without the profound moral influence of the former dukes? Broadly speaking, the poem “Seventh Month” can be summed up in a single word: preparedness. The bitter cold comes in winter, yet they prepare for it in autumn; the harvest comes in autumn, yet they plan for it in spring. Before silkworm rearing and spinning are completed, they say, “Make robes for the lord’s sons”; before the hunt has begun, they say, “Make fur garments for the lord’s sons.” Fine vegetables nourish the elderly, and paired jars of wine are presented to the lord, with earnest devotion…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎憂勤之意惓惓乎忠愛之心邠俗之厚如是周
公舉以為成王告得無意乎
有駜有駜駜彼乘黃夙夜在公在公明明振振
鷺鷺于下鼓咽咽醉言舞于胥樂兮有駜有
駜駜彼乘牡夙夜在公在公飲酒振振鷺鷺
于下鼓咽咽醉言歸于胥樂兮有駜有駜駜
彼乘駽夙夜在公在公載燕自今以始嵗其
有君子有穀詒孫子于胥樂兮
陳邦直
===
同考試官訓導先批形容當時燕飲頌禱之意有餘味焉
同考試官教諭楚批題合三章欲觀士子講貫作者類
多失此得彼冗繁可厭是篇詞簡意盡故錄之
同考試官學正胡批詞氣舂容筆力老健宜置高選
考試官教授劉批詞不冗費理甚明白
考試官教諭鄭批頌義宜簡古此作得之
詩人屢託所乘以興君臣燕飲而頌禱以相樂也
夫君臣相樂治世之休詩人屢托興而歌頌其事
不亦宜乎此燕飲而頌禱之辭想其託興之意若
punctuated:
乎憂勤之意，惓惓乎忠愛之心。邠俗之厚如是，周公舉以為成王告，得無意乎？

有駜有駜，駜彼乘黃。夙夜在公，在公明明。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言舞，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘牡。夙夜在公，在公飲酒。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言歸，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘駽。夙夜在公，在公載燕。自今以始，嵗其有。君子有穀，詒孫子，于胥樂兮！

陳邦直

同考試官訓導先批：形容當時燕飲頌禱之意，有餘味焉。
同考試官教諭楚批：題合三章，欲觀士子講貫。作者類多失此得彼，冗繁可厭。是篇詞簡意盡，故錄之。
同考試官學正胡批：詞氣舂容，筆力老健，宜置高選。
考試官教授劉批：詞不冗費，理甚明白。
考試官教諭鄭批：頌義宜簡古，此作得之。

詩人屢託所乘以興君臣燕飲，而頌禱以相樂也。夫君臣相樂，治世之休。詩人屢托興而歌頌其事，不亦宜乎？此燕飲而頌禱之辭，想其託興之意若
translation_en:
…the spirit of anxious diligence, and the earnest heart of loyalty and affection. Such was the depth of goodness in the customs of Bin. Could the Duke of Zhou have had no purpose in presenting them as an admonition to King Cheng?

Stout and strong, stout and strong—
Stout and strong are those four yellow horses.
Morning and night at the lord’s court,
At court, diligent and discerning.
Egrets flutter;
The egrets descend.
The drums resound.
Drunk, they dance:
Ah, all rejoice together!
Stout and strong, stout and strong—
Stout and strong are those four stallions.
Morning and night at the lord’s court,
At court, drinking wine.
Egrets flutter;
The egrets descend.
The drums resound.
Drunk, they return home:
Ah, all rejoice together!
Stout and strong, stout and strong—
Stout and strong are those four iron-gray horses.
Morning and night at the lord’s court,
At court, they hold a feast.
From this time onward,
May each year bring abundance.
May the lord possess goodness
And bequeath it to his descendants:
Ah, all rejoice together!

Chen Bangzhi

Associate Examiner Xian, Assistant Instructor, comments: “His portrayal of the spirit of feasting, praise, and prayer on that occasion leaves a lingering savor.”
Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor, comments: “The topic combines three stanzas to test the candidates’ comprehensive understanding. Most writers grasp one part while missing another, becoming tediously verbose. This essay is concise in expression and complete in meaning; therefore it has been selected for inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Hu, School Instructor, comments: “The language and tone are unhurried and ample, and the writing is seasoned and vigorous. It deserves a high ranking.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The wording is free of needless elaboration, and the reasoning is very clear.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of a hymn of praise should be expressed with concision and antique simplicity. This composition achieves that.”

The poet repeatedly evokes the horses they drive to introduce the feasting of ruler and ministers, praising and praying for blessings so that they may rejoice together. Now, ruler and ministers rejoicing together is a blessing of an age of good government. Is it not fitting that the poet should repeatedly employ evocative imagery to sing in praise of this occasion? These are words of praise and prayer offered at a feast. We may imagine the intention behind their evocative imagery as though …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰有駜然而肥強者四馬皆黃矣我魯君臣夙夜
在公相與辨治豈無燕樂乎燕必有舞則或坐或
伏振振然如鷺之下也燕必有鼓則或疾或徐咽
咽然其聲之長也斯時也君臣胥慶勢位兩忘醉
而起舞以相樂焉詩人之意無窮託興之詞必再
又謂有駜然而肥強者四馬皆牡矣我魯君臣夙
夜在公相與燕飲豈無樂舞乎蹲蹲舞我則既抑
且揚振振然如鷺之飛也坎坎鼓我則既和且平
咽咽然其聲之遠也斯時也上下相懽情意交契
===
醉而言歸以相樂焉詩人之意未已託興之詞必
三又謂有駜有駜則駜彼乘駽矣夙夜在公則在
公載燕矣君燕其臣臣媚其君惟願自今以始樂
歲相仍以一人之慶而為千萬人之慶也君子有
穀詒厥孫子以一己之善而為千萬世之善也豈
不足以相樂乎吁罄懽洽於燕飲之餘竭忠愛於
頌禱之頃魯之君臣何相得之深哉大抵君臣之
分以嚴為主朝廷之禮以敬為主然一於嚴敬則
情或不通而無以盡其忠告之益故先王制為燕
punctuated: 曰：「有駜然而肥強者，四馬皆黃矣。我魯君臣夙夜在公，相與辨治，豈無燕樂乎？燕必有舞，則或坐或伏，振振然如鷺之下也；燕必有鼓，則或疾或徐，咽咽然其聲之長也。斯時也，君臣胥慶，勢位兩忘，醉而起舞以相樂焉。」詩人之意無窮，託興之詞必再，又謂：「有駜然而肥強者，四馬皆牡矣。我魯君臣夙夜在公，相與燕飲，豈無樂舞乎？蹲蹲舞我，則既抑且揚，振振然如鷺之飛也；坎坎鼓我，則既和且平，咽咽然其聲之遠也。斯時也，上下相懽，情意交契，醉而言歸以相樂焉。」詩人之意未已，託興之詞必三，又謂：「有駜有駜，則駜彼乘駽矣；夙夜在公，則在公載燕矣。君燕其臣，臣媚其君，惟願自今以始，樂歲相仍，以一人之慶而為千萬人之慶也。君子有穀，詒厥孫子，以一己之善而為千萬世之善也，豈不足以相樂乎？」吁！罄懽洽於燕飲之餘，竭忠愛於頌禱之頃，魯之君臣何相得之深哉！大抵君臣之分以嚴為主，朝廷之禮以敬為主。然一於嚴敬，則情或不通，而無以盡其忠告之益，故先王制為燕
translation_en: …saying: “Sleek and strong are the four horses, all yellow. We, the ruler and ministers of Lu, attend to public duties morning and night, working together to conduct government: could we lack the pleasures of a banquet? At a banquet there must be dancing: now crouching, now bowing low, the dancers move like egrets descending in a flock. At a banquet there must be drumming: now quick, now slow, its deep sounds linger on. At this moment ruler and ministers rejoice together, forgetting both power and rank; warmed by wine, they rise to dance and delight in one another’s company.” The poet’s meaning is inexhaustible, so his evocative imagery must appear a second time. He says further: “Sleek and strong are the four horses, all stallions. We, the ruler and ministers of Lu, attend to public duties morning and night and banquet together: could we lack music and dancing? They dance rhythmically for us, now lowering themselves, now rising, moving like egrets flying in a flock. They beat the drums resoundingly for us, in harmony and measured cadence, their deep sounds carrying far. At this moment those above and below delight in one another, their feelings in accord; having drunk their fill, they speak of returning home, sharing their pleasure.” The poet’s meaning is not yet exhausted, so his evocative imagery must appear a third time. He says further: “‘Sleek, sleek’—sleek is that team of four iron-gray horses. ‘Morning and night at the duke’s court’—at the court they now banquet. The ruler feasts his ministers, and the ministers show affection for their ruler. They wish only that, from this time onward, years of abundance may follow one another, making the good fortune of one man the good fortune of countless people. ‘The lord possesses goodness and bequeaths it to his descendants’: thus the goodness of one person becomes the goodness of countless generations. Is this not enough for them to rejoice together?” Ah! They give full expression to their shared delight in the course of banqueting and pour out their loyalty and affection in their praises and prayers. How profound was the mutual accord between the ruler and ministers of Lu! In general, the distinction between ruler and minister rests chiefly on strictness, and the rites of the court chiefly on reverence. Yet if strictness and reverence alone prevail, feelings may fail to pass between them, leaving no means to realize fully the benefits of loyal counsel. Thus the former kings instituted the rites of banqueting…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
飲之禮以通上下之情今魯之羣臣宴于公所願
其年穀常登為庶民之慮切矣願其子孫為善為
後世之慮深矣亦可謂善頌善禱而盡忠告之益
者歟
春秋
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹
伯伐鄭圍新城秋楚人圍許諸侯遂救許
〔僖公六年〕
劉湜
===
考試官教授劉批〔此篇析理詳明措辭簡捷足可以破塲中之失體認而尚浮詞以求勝者尤宜高薦〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔有斷制有發揮賢能薦書舍子其誰〕
伯功既成而能節其力以討罪竭其力以恤患此
見齊桓召陵服楚之後而伐鄭救許又得討罪恤
患之義也時而春秋荆楚天下莫強焉齊桓主伯
勢不兩立一旦爰整八國仗義南征屈完服辜盟
于召陵不血一刃而楚自却不遺一矢而敵自沮
是齊之功烈盛矣然齊自召陵之後兵服四夷威
punctuated:
飲之禮，以通上下之情。今魯之羣臣宴于公所，願其年穀常登，為庶民之慮切矣；願其子孫為善，為後世之慮深矣。亦可謂善頌善禱而盡忠告之益者歟！

春秋

盟于召陵。〔僖公四年〕夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。秋，楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許。〔僖公六年〕

劉湜

考試官教授劉批〔此篇析理詳明，措辭簡捷，足可以破塲中之失體認而尚浮詞以求勝者，尤宜高薦。〕

考試官教諭鄭批〔有斷制，有發揮，賢能薦書，舍子其誰？〕

伯功既成，而能節其力以討罪，竭其力以恤患。此見齊桓召陵服楚之後，而伐鄭救許，又得討罪恤患之義也。時而春秋，荆楚天下莫強焉。齊桓主伯，勢不兩立。一旦爰整八國，仗義南征，屈完服辜，盟于召陵。不血一刃而楚自却，不遺一矢而敵自沮，是齊之功烈盛矣。然齊自召陵之後，兵服四夷，威
translation_en:
…the rites of ceremonial drinking, to allow feelings to pass between those above and those below. Now the assembled ministers of Lu feast at their lord’s residence. In wishing that his grain harvests may always be abundant, they show earnest concern for the common people; in wishing that his descendants may practice goodness, they show profound concern for later generations. May they not indeed be said to offer fitting praise and prayers, and to realize fully the benefits of loyal counsel?

Spring and Autumn Annals

“They concluded a covenant at Shaoling.” 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 “In summer, the duke joined the marquises of Qi, Song, Chen, and Wei and the earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. In autumn, the men of Chu besieged Xu. The assembled lords thereupon went to Xu’s aid.” 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi.〕

Liu Shi

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: 〔This essay analyzes principles thoroughly and clearly, and its wording is concise and direct. It can thoroughly refute those in the examination hall who lack substantive understanding yet prize empty phrasing as a means to prevail. It particularly merits a high recommendation.〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔There is decisive judgment, and there is full development of the argument. In a written recommendation of the worthy and capable, whom could we choose but you?〕

Once his achievements as hegemon were established, he could restrain his strength when punishing wrongdoing and exert it fully when relieving distress. This is evident in how Duke Huan of Qi, after bringing Chu to submission at Shaoling, attacked Zheng and relieved Xu, once again fulfilling the proper principles of punishing wrongdoing and relieving distress. At that time, in the Spring and Autumn period [?], none under Heaven was stronger than Jing-Chu. Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony, and the two powers could not coexist. He then marshaled eight states and marched south in the cause of righteousness. Qu Wan acknowledged culpability, and a covenant was concluded at Shaoling. Without a single blade being bloodied, Chu withdrew of its own accord; without a single arrow being discharged, the enemy lost heart of its own accord. Thus the achievements of Qi were magnificent. Yet after Shaoling, Qi’s armies brought the barbarians of the four quarters to submission, and its might…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
動諸夏今而大合列辟問罪懿親之鄭環攻新造
之邑然以六國而伐鄭兵車雲集宜若振槁然而
公乃圍而不舉者意豈不曰好攻戰樂殺人者於
罪為大於是惟整兵以示之而不狃於速克惟寬
容以來之而不急於圖勝豈非伯主節其力以討
罪乎繼而楚欲救鄭廼攻大岳之裔計解鄭人之
圍然以強楚而陵弱許勢力弗敵不啻拉朽然而
公即移師以赴之者意豈不曰救患分災於禮為
急於是寧釋有罪之鄭亟拯無辜之許寧隳垂成
===
之功速慰引領之望又非伯主盡其力以恤患乎
吁討罪猶理亂繩不可急也救患猶解倒懸不可
緩也桓知其然故於召陵之後伐鄭救許寬猛適
宜如此春秋得不備書以美之歟抑又論之陳不
可陵猶鄭不可虐也桓公前乎伐鄭責陳甚備何
慈於鄭而忍於陳乎徐不可棄猶許不可忘也桓
公後乎救許緩徐不力何勤於許而怠於徐乎先
儒謂其功過相半信矣
陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮〔襄公八年〕
punctuated:
動諸夏。今而大合列辟，問罪懿親之鄭，環攻新造之邑。然以六國而伐鄭，兵車雲集，宜若振槁。然而公乃圍而不舉者，意豈不曰：「好攻戰、樂殺人者，於罪為大。」於是惟整兵以示之，而不狃於速克；惟寬容以來之，而不急於圖勝。豈非伯主節其力以討罪乎？繼而楚欲救鄭，廼攻大岳之裔，計解鄭人之圍。然以強楚而陵弱許，勢力弗敵，不啻拉朽。然而公即移師以赴之者，意豈不曰：「救患分災，於禮為急。」於是寧釋有罪之鄭，亟拯無辜之許；寧隳垂成之功，速慰引領之望。又非伯主盡其力以恤患乎？吁！討罪猶理亂繩，不可急也；救患猶解倒懸，不可緩也。桓知其然，故於召陵之後，伐鄭救許，寬猛適宜如此，《春秋》得不備書以美之歟？抑又論之，陳不可陵，猶鄭不可虐也。桓公前乎伐鄭，責陳甚備，何慈於鄭而忍於陳乎？徐不可棄，猶許不可忘也。桓公後乎救許，緩徐不力，何勤於許而怠於徐乎？先儒謂其功過相半，信矣！

陳侯逃歸。〔襄公七年〕鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮。〔襄公八年〕
translation_en:
…shook the states of the central realm. Now he assembled the rulers in great numbers, called Zheng—a state closely related to the royal house—to account for its offenses, and surrounded and attacked its newly built town. With six states campaigning against Zheng and their war chariots massed like clouds, it should have been as easy as shaking down withered leaves. Yet the duke merely besieged the town without taking it. Surely his thought was: “To delight in aggressive warfare and take pleasure in killing people is among the gravest offenses.” Thus he merely marshaled his troops to make a show of force, without becoming intent on a swift conquest; he exercised forbearance to induce submission, without rushing to secure victory. Was this not a hegemon restraining his strength when punishing wrongdoing?

Then Chu, wishing to rescue Zheng, attacked the descendants of Dayue—the state of Xu—with the aim of lifting the siege of Zheng. When mighty Chu assailed weak Xu, their strength was so unequal that it was as easy as breaking rotten wood. Yet the duke immediately moved his army to Xu’s aid. Surely his thought was: “To relieve distress and share the burden of calamity is an urgent obligation of ritual propriety.” Thus he preferred to release guilty Zheng in order to rescue innocent Xu at once, and to abandon an achievement nearly completed in order promptly to fulfill the hopes of those craning their necks for aid. Was this not also a hegemon exerting his strength to the utmost to relieve distress?

Ah! Punishing wrongdoing is like untangling knotted cords: it must not be rushed. Relieving distress is like releasing someone hanging upside down: it must not be delayed. Duke Huan understood this. Hence, after Shaoling, he attacked Zheng and rescued Xu, applying leniency and severity with such fitting judgment. How could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to record these events fully in praise of him?

Yet let us consider further. Chen ought not to have been oppressed, just as Zheng ought not to have been treated cruelly. Before campaigning against Zheng, Duke Huan had been exceedingly exacting in calling Chen to account. Why was he compassionate toward Zheng but harsh toward Chen? The state of Xu (徐) ought not to have been abandoned, just as the state of Xu (許) ought not to have been forgotten. After rescuing Xu (許), Duke Huan was slow and ineffectual in aiding Xu (徐) [?]. Why was he diligent on behalf of Xu (許), yet negligent toward Xu (徐)? Earlier Confucian scholars said that his merits and faults were evenly balanced. True indeed!

The Marquis of Chen fled home. 〔Seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 The men of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Xie, a son of the ruler of Cai. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
冬楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕晉侯使士匄
来聘〔襄公八年〕冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭
十有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥
師伐吳〔昭公六年〕秋公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕齊侯伐
徐〔昭公十六年〕秋齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕
朱顯
===
考試官教授劉批場中作此題紛紜無定見惟此義寫出二
公之賢否宛在目前所謂過屠門大嚼其知肉味者乎
考試官教諭鄭批此作詞嚴義正得春秋之旨宜錄出
勢有難為而伯主得善勝之道時有可為而伯嗣
無自強之志此晉悼所以克復舊業而齊景所以
終於無成也比事以觀賢否昭然矣且夫春秋之
中晉悼嗣伯去文襄之時未遠其餘澤猶有存者
若何而見其勢之難為耶是時陳嘗與晉同事者
也今則不思輔晉而棄于鄬之會鄭亦與晉同志
punctuated:
冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕。晉侯使士匄来聘〔襄公八年〕。冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕。楚薳罷帥師伐吳〔昭公六年〕。秋，公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕。齊侯伐徐〔昭公十六年〕。秋，齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕。

朱顯

考試官教授劉批：「場中作此題，紛紜無定見。惟此義寫出二公之賢否，宛在目前。所謂過屠門大嚼，其知肉味者乎？」

考試官教諭鄭批：「此作詞嚴義正，得春秋之旨，宜錄出。」

勢有難為，而伯主得善勝之道；時有可為，而伯嗣無自強之志。此晉悼所以克復舊業，而齊景所以終於無成也。比事以觀，賢否昭然矣。且夫春秋之中，晉悼嗣伯，去文襄之時未遠，其餘澤猶有存者，若何而見其勢之難為耶？是時，陳嘗與晉同事者也，今則不思輔晉，而棄于鄬之會；鄭亦與晉同志
translation_en:
In winter, Prince Zhen of Chu led an army against Zheng.〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a courtesy mission to our state.〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In winter, the Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi 齊, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi.〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 Wei Pi of Chu led an army against Wu.〔Sixth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, the Duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi 齊, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi 杞, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu.〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 Wu extinguished the state of Zhoulai.〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The Marquis of Qi attacked Xu.〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, Gao Fa of Qi led an army against Ju.〔Nineteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Zhu Xian

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The candidates who addressed this topic offered a welter of conflicting views, with no firm judgment. This essay alone portrays the worthiness and unworthiness of the two dukes as vividly as if they stood before our eyes. To invoke the saying about chewing heartily when passing a butcher’s doorway: is this not someone who knows the taste of meat?”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “This composition is rigorous in expression and correct in interpretation, capturing the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals. It deserves inclusion in the record.”

Circumstances may make action difficult, yet a hegemon may grasp the way to prevail effectively; the times may offer opportunities for action, yet an heir to the hegemony may lack the resolve to strengthen himself. This is why Duke Dao of Jin succeeded in restoring his predecessors’ achievements, whereas Duke Jing of Qi ultimately accomplished nothing. Compare the events, and their respective worthiness and unworthiness become unmistakable. Now, during the Spring and Autumn period, when Duke Dao of Jin succeeded to the hegemony, the age of Dukes Wen and Xiang was not far distant, and some of their beneficent legacy still remained. How, then, can we discern the difficulty of his circumstances? At that time, Chen had previously acted in concert with Jin; now, however, it gave no thought to supporting Jin and deserted it at the meeting at Wei 鄬. Zheng, too, had shared Jin’s aims…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者也今則無故侵蔡而召子真之伐晋方失陳國
中之勢未振鄭又侵蔡楚人之詞稍直巳而士匄
聘魯告將用師于鄭焉則諸侯皆不欲戰而人心
亦必有疑怠矣以勢而觀誠難為也使悼公一以
戰伐為威兵力為武思復先君之業不亦難乎幸
而違荀偃戰楚之言聽武子敝楚之策雖合列國
而興伐鄭之兵卒許鄭成而結于戲之盟脩德息
師竟收成功悼公得善勝之道如此非賢而能之
乎春秋所□善之也若夫春秋之季齊景代興去
===
桓公之時巳遠其餘澤亦巳斬矣若何而見其時
之易為耶于時楚實中國勍敵也今而欲雪舊忿
命薳罷以伐吳晋乃諸夏盟主也今而欲服列國
會平丘以示威楚方攻吳則無睥睨之計晋惟示
威則無駕馭之畧巳而吳倂州來又出楚之不意
焉則吳之爭雄亦不在於中國矣以時而論實易
為也使景公誠能尊事王室輯寧中夏桓公之業
獨不可復乎柰何不以德義懷人惟以威力脅人
今年既躬親甲冑以伐徐明年復爰整師旅以伐
punctuated:
者也，今則無故侵蔡，而召子真之伐。晋方失陳，國中之勢未振，鄭又侵蔡，楚人之詞稍直。巳而士匄聘魯，告將用師于鄭焉，則諸侯皆不欲戰，而人心亦必有疑怠矣。以勢而觀，誠難為也。使悼公一以戰伐為威、兵力為武，思復先君之業，不亦難乎？幸而違荀偃戰楚之言，聽武子敝楚之策，雖合列國而興伐鄭之兵，卒許鄭成，而結于戲之盟。脩德息師，竟收成功。悼公得善勝之道如此，非賢而能之乎？春秋所□善之也。
若夫春秋之季，齊景代興，去桓公之時巳遠，其餘澤亦巳斬矣。若何而見其時之易為耶？于時楚實中國勍敵也，今而欲雪舊忿，命薳罷以伐吳；晋乃諸夏盟主也，今而欲服列國，會平丘以示威。楚方攻吳，則無睥睨之計；晋惟示威，則無駕馭之畧。巳而吳倂州來，又出楚之不意焉，則吳之爭雄亦不在於中國矣。以時而論，實易為也。使景公誠能尊事王室，輯寧中夏，桓公之業獨不可復乎？柰何不以德義懷人，惟以威力脅人？今年既躬親甲冑以伐徐，明年復爰整師旅以伐
translation_en:
…was likewise one that shared Jin’s aims, yet now it invaded Cai without cause and brought on an attack by Zi Zhen. Jin had just lost Chen, and its strength at home had not yet recovered; Zheng then invaded Cai, giving Chu a somewhat stronger justification. Subsequently, Shi Gai went on a diplomatic mission to Lu and announced that troops would be sent against Zheng. The feudal lords were all unwilling to fight, and the people must also have harbored doubts and grown dispirited. Judged by the circumstances, action was indeed difficult. Had Duke Dao relied entirely on warfare to establish his authority and on military strength to display his martial prowess, would it not have been difficult to restore his predecessor’s achievements? Fortunately, he rejected Xun Yan’s advice to fight Chu and followed Wuzi’s strategy of wearing Chu down. Although he assembled the states and raised troops against Zheng, he ultimately permitted Zheng to make peace and concluded the covenant at Xi. By cultivating virtue and resting his troops, he finally achieved success. Such was Duke Dao’s grasp of the way to secure victory skillfully. Could anyone lacking worthiness have accomplished this? The Spring and Autumn Annals commends him for this [?; one character illegible].
As for the closing years of the Spring and Autumn period, when Duke Jing of Qi rose to prominence in his turn, Duke Huan’s time was already far distant, and the benefits of his legacy had also come to an end. How, then, can we see that the times made action easy? At that time Chu was indeed a formidable enemy of the central states, but now, seeking to avenge an old grievance, it ordered Wei Pi to attack Wu. Jin was the leader of the covenant among the states of Xia, but now, seeking to bring the various states into submission, it convened the meeting at Pingqiu to display its might. Since Chu was occupied with attacking Wu, it had no designs upon the central states; since Jin merely displayed its might, it had no strategy for directing them. Subsequently, Wu annexed Zhoulai, again taking Chu by surprise. Thus Wu’s struggle for supremacy was likewise not directed toward the central states. Judged by the times, action was indeed easy. Had Duke Jing truly been able to serve the royal house with reverence and bring harmony and peace to the central states, could Duke Huan’s achievements not have been restored? Why did he fail to win people over through virtue and righteousness, relying solely on coercive force to intimidate them? One year he personally donned armor and helmet to attack Xu; the next year he again put his armies in order to attack…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
莒其心既私其志亦卑景公失圖伯之策如此而
謂賢者為之乎春秋所以惜之也雖然悼公之復
伯固賢矣亦由用武子之策而然也景公之失伯
固庸矣亦由不用晏子之謀而爾也噫賢才之用
舍係乎政事之得失政事之得失關乎國家之盛
衰有國者不用賢才奚可哉
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢而置
之聚眾而誓之是故因天事天因地事地因
===
名山升中于天因吉土以饗帝于郊升中于
天而鳳凰降龜龍假饗帝于郊而風雨節寒
暑時是故聖人南面而立而天下大治
孫昪
同考試官教諭關批此題雖長實易場中作者多強辭
求其講貫精切運筆雄健無如此篇也是宜録出
考試官教授劉批其文達其氣昌窮理者固如是乎
考試官教諭鄭批據理遣詞明白通暢有識之士也
聖王擇人示戒而舉祀獲其應此所以享無為之
punctuated:
莒。其心既私，其志亦卑。景公失圖伯之策如此，而謂賢者為之乎？春秋所以惜之也。雖然，悼公之復伯固賢矣，亦由用武子之策而然也；景公之失伯固庸矣，亦由不用晏子之謀而爾也。噫！賢才之用舍，係乎政事之得失；政事之得失，關乎國家之盛衰。有國者不用賢才，奚可哉？
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚眾而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳凰降、龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節、寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立，而天下大治。
孫昪
同考試官教諭關批：此題雖長，實易。場中作者多強辭，求其講貫精切、運筆雄健，無如此篇也，是宜録出。
考試官教授劉批：其文達，其氣昌，窮理者固如是乎！
考試官教諭鄭批：據理遣詞，明白通暢，有識之士也。
聖王擇人示戒而舉祀，獲其應，此所以享無為之
translation_en:
…Ju. His motives were selfish, and his aspirations base. Duke Jing’s failure to devise a strategy for attaining hegemony was such as this: could one call it the conduct of a worthy ruler? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses regret over him. Nevertheless, Duke Dao’s restoration of hegemony certainly showed his worthiness, but it also resulted from his adoption of Wuzi’s strategy. Duke Jing’s failure to attain hegemony certainly showed his mediocrity, but it also resulted from his failure to adopt Yanzi’s counsel. Alas! Whether worthy and talented men are employed or set aside determines success or failure in government; success or failure in government bears upon the flourishing or decline of the state. How could a ruler of a state possibly dispense with worthy and talented men?
Record of Rites
“Thus, the former kings of old esteemed those possessed of virtue, honored those possessed of the Way, entrusted responsibilities to the capable, and selected worthy men and installed them in office. They assembled the multitude and admonished them by solemn charge. Thus, they drew upon Heaven to serve Heaven and upon Earth to serve Earth. At renowned mountains they reported their accomplishments to Heaven, and on auspicious ground they made offerings to the Lord on High at the suburban sacrifice. When they reported their accomplishments to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they made offerings to the Lord on High at the suburban sacrifice, wind and rain were duly regulated, and cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Thus, the sage stood facing south, and all under Heaven was well governed.”
Sun Bian
Comment by Associate Examiner Guan, Instructor: Although this topic is long, it is actually easy. Many candidates in the examination hall strained their language. For precise and penetrating exposition and vigorous writing, none equals this essay. It certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: His writing is expressive, and its vital force abundant. Surely this is what one expects of a man who investigates principles to the utmost!
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: He chooses his words according to principle; his writing is clear and fluent. He is a man of discernment.
The sage king selected men, issued admonitions, and performed sacrifices, receiving the corresponding auspicious responses. This was how he came to enjoy the rule of effortless action…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
治也盖祀禮有關於治化也大矣自非聖王克謹
祀禮而獲休瑞之應其何以能享無為之治哉記
禮器者謂夫昔聖王之有天下也知天地生成之
功而報本之禮不可以不舉但不能自任其事故
必擇人以任之焉是故德有諸己者則貴尚之而
不敢忽道積厥躬者則尊崇之而不敢慢才能可
使者又任用之而無疑焉于以舉衆賢而置於位
則小大之官莫不具其職于以聚衆賢而誓其心
則小大之官莫不謹其職由是因天之尊而制為
===
事天之禮郊以祀天于圜丘因地之卑而制為事
地之禮社以祭地于方澤因巡狩而至於方岳則
進此方諸侯治功平成之事以告于天因王都而
兆於南郊則於每歳冬至一陽始生之時以饗於
帝夫告平成之事于天則誠格乎天而天饗之故
鳳凰以降龜龍以假而瑞物臻焉饗郊祀之禮于
帝則誠格乎帝而帝饗之故風雨以節寒暑以時
而休徵應焉聖王於此夫何為哉但見正離位而
履至尊嚮離明而臨大寳端冕凝旒而已耳萬邦
punctuated: 治也。盖祀禮有關於治化也大矣！自非聖王克謹祀禮而獲休瑞之應，其何以能享無為之治哉？記《禮器》者謂夫昔聖王之有天下也，知天地生成之功，而報本之禮不可以不舉，但不能自任其事，故必擇人以任之焉。是故德有諸己者，則貴尚之而不敢忽；道積厥躬者，則尊崇之而不敢慢；才能可使者，又任用之而無疑焉。于以舉衆賢而置於位，則小大之官莫不具其職；于以聚衆賢而誓其心，則小大之官莫不謹其職。由是因天之尊而制為事天之禮，郊以祀天于圜丘；因地之卑而制為事地之禮，社以祭地于方澤。因巡狩而至於方岳，則進此方諸侯治功平成之事以告于天；因王都而兆於南郊，則於每歳冬至一陽始生之時以饗於帝。夫告平成之事于天，則誠格乎天而天饗之，故鳳凰以降，龜龍以假，而瑞物臻焉；饗郊祀之禮于帝，則誠格乎帝而帝饗之，故風雨以節，寒暑以時，而休徵應焉。聖王於此夫何為哉？但見正離位而履至尊，嚮離明而臨大寳，端冕凝旒而已耳，萬邦
translation_en:
…order. Indeed, sacrificial rites have a profound bearing on governance and moral transformation! Unless a sage king could reverently observe these rites and obtain auspicious responses, how could he enjoy order achieved through nonaction?

The author of “Ritual Vessels” (Liqi) explains that when the sage kings of old possessed all under Heaven, they understood Heaven and Earth’s work of generating and nurturing life, and knew that rites repaying these ultimate sources could not be neglected. Yet they could not undertake these affairs alone, so they necessarily selected people to take responsibility for them. Thus, those who possessed virtue were esteemed and never disregarded; those who had accumulated the Way within themselves were honored and never treated slightingly; and those whose talents and abilities fitted them for service were employed without hesitation. By promoting the many worthy men and placing them in office, they ensured that officials, great and small alike, fulfilled their duties. By assembling these worthy men and binding their hearts by solemn oaths, they ensured that officials, great and small alike, attended reverently to their duties.

Accordingly, in recognition of Heaven’s exalted position, they established rites for serving Heaven, performing the suburban sacrifice to Heaven at the Round Mound. In recognition of Earth’s lowly position, they established rites for serving Earth, performing the soil sacrifice to Earth at the Square Marsh. When their tours of inspection brought them to the sacred mountain of a region, they presented to Heaven the achievements of that region’s feudal lords in bringing order and peace. At the royal capital, they marked out a sacrificial precinct in the southern suburb and made offerings to the Lord on High each year at the winter solstice, when the first yang force began to arise.

When they reported achievements of order and peace to Heaven, their sincerity reached Heaven and Heaven accepted their offerings. Thus phoenixes descended, tortoises and dragons arrived, and auspicious creatures appeared. When they offered the suburban sacrifice to the Lord on High, their sincerity reached him and he accepted their offerings. Thus wind and rain came in due measure, cold and heat arrived in their proper seasons, and favorable signs appeared in response.

What, then, did the sage king need to do? One saw only that he took his proper place in the south, the position of the trigram Li, and occupied the highest station; facing the brightness of Li, he presided over the great throne. He merely sat upright in his ceremonial cap, its pendant beads motionless, and the myriad states…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
自爾其協和也垂紳正笏而已耳四方自爾其風
動也至誠格天之效有如此夫抑嘗因是而考之
書曰黍稷非馨明德惟馨鬼神無常享享于克誠
然先王既合上下之誠而奉天帝之祭故瑞物之
臻休徵之應亦幽明感通自然之理也彼後世不
脩誠敬以格神徒事封禪以希福者何其謬哉
王者功成作樂治定制禮其功大者其樂備其
治辯者其禮具干戚之舞非備樂也孰亨而
祀非達禮也五帝殊時不相沿樂三王異世
===
不相襲禮樂極則憂禮粗則偏矣及夫敦樂
而無憂禮備而不偏者其唯大聖乎
丁養浩
同考試官教諭闕批題本冠冕作者缺記問之功漫不知所主間
有得者而文又不足以發之此篇如大匠運斤而尺度自合佳作也
考試官教授劉批詞簡理明允宜高捷
考試官教諭鄭批文理渾融宜錄為學禮者式
禮樂本治功而帝王不相述禮樂有偏弊而聖人
為獨全蓋禮樂所以象功飭治也帝王隨時世而
punctuated:
自爾其協和也。垂紳正笏而已耳，四方自爾其風動也。至誠格天之效有如此夫！抑嘗因是而考之，《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」然先王既合上下之誠而奉天帝之祭，故瑞物之臻、休徵之應，亦幽明感通自然之理也。彼後世不脩誠敬以格神，徒事封禪以希福者，何其謬哉！
王者功成作樂，治定制禮。其功大者，其樂備；其治辯者，其禮具。干戚之舞，非備樂也；孰亨而祀，非達禮也。五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異世，不相襲禮。樂極則憂，禮粗則偏矣。及夫敦樂而無憂、禮備而不偏者，其唯大聖乎！
丁養浩
同考試官教諭闕批：題本冠冕，作者缺記問之功，漫不知所主，間有得者，而文又不足以發之。此篇如大匠運斤，而尺度自合，佳作也。
考試官教授劉批：詞簡理明，允宜高捷。
考試官教諭鄭批：文理渾融，宜錄為學禮者式。
禮樂本治功，而帝王不相述；禮樂有偏弊，而聖人為獨全。蓋禮樂所以象功飭治也，帝王隨時世而
translation_en:
…of themselves attain harmony. He need only let his ceremonial sash hang down and hold his audience tablet upright, and the four quarters are spontaneously stirred by his influence. Such is the efficacy of perfect sincerity in reaching Heaven! I have also examined this in light of the Documents, which says: “It is not millet that gives fragrance; luminous virtue alone gives fragrance. Spirits do not invariably accept offerings; they accept those of one capable of sincerity.” Since the former kings united the sincerity of those above and below in offering sacrifices to Heaven, the Supreme Lord, the arrival of auspicious creatures and the response of favorable portents likewise followed the natural principle of sympathetic communication between the unseen and visible realms. How mistaken were those of later ages who failed to cultivate sincerity and reverence to reach the spirits, but merely performed the feng and shan sacrifices in hopes of blessings!
“When a true king's achievements are complete, he creates music; when his government is settled, he establishes rites. The greater his achievements, the more complete his music; the better ordered his government, the more fully furnished his rites. Dancing with shields and axes does not constitute music in its completeness; cooking offerings and sacrificing them does not constitute a full understanding of ritual. The Five Emperors lived at different times and did not continue one another's music; the Three Kings lived in different ages and did not copy one another's rites. Music taken to excess brings sorrow; rites performed crudely become one-sided. As for one whose music is full and substantial yet brings no sorrow, and whose rites are complete yet free of partiality—surely only a great sage can achieve this!”
Ding Yanghao
Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: “The topic is inherently grand and dignified. The writers lack the grounding acquired through memorization and inquiry and are quite at a loss as to its main point. Occasionally some grasp it, but their writing is insufficient to express it. This essay is like a master craftsman wielding his adze: the dimensions conform of themselves. An excellent composition.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “Concise in wording and clear in reasoning; it truly deserves to pass with a high rank.”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Its writing and reasoning form a harmonious whole. It should be recorded as a model for students of ritual.”
Rites and music are rooted in ordered government and achievement, yet emperors and kings did not follow one another's practices. Rites and music are susceptible to partiality and defects, yet the sage alone possesses them in their completeness. For rites and music serve to represent achievement and give orderly form to government. Emperors and kings, in accordance with their times and ages, …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
制作固有異矣然非聖人孰能用之而無弊哉樂
記載以示人宜矣且王者受天明命為天下君彼
功成於天下而必作樂以象其功治定於天下而
必制禮以飾其治惟樂以象功其功之成者巍巍
而無外則所作之樂亦無不備惟禮以飾治其治
之定者蕩蕩而無遺則所制之禮亦無不具總持
干戚而舞不如韶樂之盡善盡美以征伐之功異
於揖遜故耳豈得為備樂哉孰烹牲體而薦不如
血腥之得乎禮意以後世之治異於隆古故耳豈
===
得為達禮哉故少皥顓頊帝嚳堯舜五帝之時殊
矣然各因其功而作樂不相沿焉禹湯文武三王
之世異矣然各因其治而制禮不相襲焉夫禮樂
本治功而制作如此若奏樂而欲極其聲音之娛
樂則樂極悲来矣能無憂乎行禮而不能詳審於
節文則偏失不舉矣能無偏乎及夫敦厚於樂而
無樂極悲来之憂禮儀備具而無偏粗不舉之失
者其惟備道德之全建中和之極功大而樂備治
辯而禮具之大聖能然耳是豈常人所能及哉禮
punctuated: 制作固有異矣，然非聖人，孰能用之而無弊哉？《樂記》載以示人，宜矣。且王者受天明命，為天下君，彼功成於天下，而必作樂以象其功；治定於天下，而必制禮以飾其治。惟樂以象功，其功之成者巍巍而無外，則所作之樂亦無不備；惟禮以飾治，其治之定者蕩蕩而無遺，則所制之禮亦無不具。總持干戚而舞，不如《韶》樂之盡善盡美，以征伐之功異於揖遜故耳，豈得為備樂哉？孰烹牲體而薦，不如血腥之得乎禮意，以後世之治異於隆古故耳，豈得為達禮哉？故少皥、顓頊、帝嚳、堯、舜，五帝之時殊矣，然各因其功而作樂，不相沿焉；禹、湯、文、武，三王之世異矣，然各因其治而制禮，不相襲焉。夫禮樂本治功，而制作如此。若奏樂而欲極其聲音之娛樂，則樂極悲来矣，能無憂乎？行禮而不能詳審於節文，則偏失不舉矣，能無偏乎？及夫敦厚於樂，而無樂極悲来之憂，禮儀備具，而無偏粗不舉之失者，其惟備道德之全、建中和之極、功大而樂備、治辯而禮具之大聖能然耳。是豈常人所能及哉？禮
translation_en:
…their institutions and compositions necessarily differed. Yet who other than a sage could employ them without harmful consequences? It is fitting that the Record of Music records this to instruct people. Moreover, a true king receives Heaven’s illustrious mandate and becomes ruler of all under Heaven. When his achievements throughout the realm are complete, he must compose music to represent them; when his governance of the realm is established, he must institute rites to adorn it. Since music represents achievement, if his completed achievements are lofty and all-embracing, the music he composes will likewise lack nothing. Since ritual adorns governance, if his established governance is expansive and leaves nothing out, the rites he institutes will likewise be fully provided.

Dancing while holding shields and battle-axes does not equal the Shao music in its perfect goodness and perfect beauty, simply because achievement through punitive conquest differs from achievement through deferential yielding of the throne. How could this count as complete music? Cooking the bodies of sacrificial animals and presenting them as offerings does not capture the meaning of ritual as well as offerings of blood and raw flesh, simply because the governance of later ages differs from that of high antiquity. How could this count as fully realizing ritual?

Thus Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diku, Yao, and Shun—the Five Emperors—lived in different times, yet each composed music according to his achievements, without following his predecessors. Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—the Three Kings—belonged to different ages, yet each instituted rites according to his governance, without copying his predecessors. Ritual and music are rooted in governance and achievement, and this is how they were instituted and composed.

If, in performing music, one seeks to exhaust the pleasures of its sounds, pleasure carried to its extreme will bring sorrow. Can there then be no cause for concern? If, in performing rites, one cannot carefully examine their prescribed forms and refinements, partiality and omissions will result. Can there then be no imbalance? As for being earnest and generous in music, without the concern that pleasure carried to its extreme will bring sorrow, and possessing a complete array of ritual observances, without the faults of imbalance, crudeness, and omission: only a great sage can accomplish this—one who possesses the fullness of the Way and virtue, establishes the highest standard of equilibrium and harmony, whose achievements are great and whose music is complete, whose governance is well ordered and whose rites are fully provided. How could an ordinary person attain this? Ritual …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
樂本治功而制作信然矣抑論聖人之制禮樂不
特象功飭治盖將資之以賛造化扶世教焉經曰
禮樂明備天地官矣是造化有資於禮樂也既曰
樂也者聖人之所樂也而可以善民心又曰安上
治民莫善於禮非世教有資於禮樂乎吁禮樂所
關甚大如此非有道德之盛而致治功之隆者烏
能當制作之柄哉
論
明王以孝治天下
===
劉湜
同考試官訓導顧批作論貴乎抑揚反覆通暢厥旨場中
好髙者失之險好竒者失之恠此作深得作論之旨可敬可敬
同考試官教諭楚批事有證據文有鋪叙歆羡歆羡
考試官教授劉批有源流有發揮允宜髙薦
考試官教諭鄭批沿經遣辭而文豐贍當是作手
論曰聖人有至德以履天位必有要道以順
天下盖聖人之德純乎天性而孝為天之經
德之本聖人之道順乎民心而孝為民之行
punctuated:
樂本治功而制作，信然矣。抑論聖人之制禮樂，不特象功飭治，盖將資之以賛造化、扶世教焉。經曰：「禮樂明備，天地官矣。」是造化有資於禮樂也。既曰：「樂也者，聖人之所樂也，而可以善民心。」又曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」非世教有資於禮樂乎？吁！禮樂所關甚大如此，非有道德之盛而致治功之隆者，烏能當制作之柄哉？

論
明王以孝治天下
劉湜

同考試官訓導顧批：作論貴乎抑揚反覆，通暢厥旨。場中好髙者失之險，好竒者失之恠。此作深得作論之旨，可敬，可敬。

同考試官教諭楚批：事有證據，文有鋪叙，歆羡，歆羡。

考試官教授劉批：有源流，有發揮，允宜髙薦。

考試官教諭鄭批：沿經遣辭，而文豐贍，當是作手。

論曰：聖人有至德以履天位，必有要道以順天下。盖聖人之德純乎天性，而孝為天之經、德之本；聖人之道順乎民心，而孝為民之行
translation_en:
…music is instituted on the basis of achievements in governance: this is indeed so. Yet, considering the sages’ institution of rites and music, these do more than represent achievements and bring order to government. The sages would also draw upon them to assist the transformations of nature and sustain moral teaching in the world. The classic says: “When rites and music are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth perform their offices.” Thus the transformations of nature receive assistance from rites and music. It also says: “Music is what the sages delight in, and it can make the people’s hearts good.” And again: “For securing those above and governing the people, nothing excels rites.” Does this not show that moral teaching in the world draws assistance from rites and music? Ah! Since rites and music have such far-reaching significance, how could anyone wield the authority to institute them unless possessed of abundant moral virtue and having brought achievements in governance to their height?

Discourse
“The Enlightened Kings Governed All under Heaven through Filial Piety”
By Liu Shi 劉湜

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: “What matters in composing a discourse is varying emphasis and examining the subject from different sides, so as to convey its meaning fully and clearly. Among candidates in the examination hall, those who strive for loftiness err toward obscurity, while those who strive for originality err toward eccentricity. This composition thoroughly grasps the essentials of writing a discourse. Admirable, admirable!”

Comment by Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor: “Its factual claims have supporting evidence, and its prose develops its subject fully. How enviable, how enviable!”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “It traces sources and develops their implications. It certainly deserves a high recommendation.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Its wording follows the classics, yet its prose is rich and ample. This must be an accomplished writer.”

The discourse reads: A sage who possesses the highest virtue and occupies the heavenly position must possess the essential Way by which to bring All under Heaven into accord. For the sage’s virtue is pure in its accord with the nature bestowed by Heaven, and filial piety is Heaven’s constant principle and the root of virtue. The sage’s Way accords with the people’s hearts, and filial piety is the conduct of the people…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
教之始明王以孝治天下所謂至德要道而
民用和睦上下無怨也歟宜孔子以是為教
而曾子述以為經也愚請敷暢其旨天高地
下萬物散殊而聖人則代天理物乾父坤母
民胞物與而大君則父母宗子古昔明王備
聖人之德居大君之位知天地之化則善述
其事窮天地之神則善繼其志固以事親之
孝盡事天之道矣然神化雖妙不可使民知
也立政以張為治之具制刑以為輔治之法
===
道民以政而不從又有刑以一之矣然刑政
雖善不能使民從也惟其首出庶物知生物
之本於父母者無二本卓冠羣倫知人倫之
先於父子者同一性而愛親之孝人之良知
也孝親之道人之本性也聖人因其良知而
導之因其本性而教之何不知不化之有彼
有國而為諸侯有家而為卿大夫列爵分職
如目隨綱皆王臣也林生而族處同類而異
形面內環觀如星拱極皆天民也明王以孝
punctuated: 教之始。明王以孝治天下，所謂至德要道，而民用和睦，上下無怨也歟？宜孔子以是為教，而曾子述以為經也。愚請敷暢其旨。天高地下，萬物散殊，而聖人則代天理物；乾父坤母，民胞物與，而大君則父母宗子。古昔明王備聖人之德，居大君之位，知天地之化，則善述其事；窮天地之神，則善繼其志。固以事親之孝，盡事天之道矣。然神化雖妙，不可使民知也。立政以張為治之具，制刑以為輔治之法，道民以政而不從，又有刑以一之矣。然刑政雖善，不能使民從也。惟其首出庶物，知生物之本於父母者無二本；卓冠羣倫，知人倫之先於父子者同一性。而愛親之孝，人之良知也；孝親之道，人之本性也。聖人因其良知而導之，因其本性而教之，何不知不化之有？彼有國而為諸侯，有家而為卿大夫，列爵分職，如目隨綱，皆王臣也。林生而族處，同類而異形，面內環觀，如星拱極，皆天民也。明王以孝
translation_en:
…the beginning of instruction. When an enlightened king governs all under Heaven through filial piety, is this not what is meant by consummate virtue and the essential Way, through which the people live in harmony and neither those above nor those below harbor resentment? It is fitting that Confucius made this his teaching and that Zengzi set it down as a classic. I venture to expound its meaning.

Heaven is high and Earth is low, and the myriad things are dispersed and distinct; the sage orders them on Heaven’s behalf. Qian is father and Kun is mother; the people are siblings and other creatures companions. The great ruler is their parent and the lineage’s principal heir. The enlightened kings of antiquity possessed the virtue of sages and occupied the position of great rulers. Understanding the transforming operations of Heaven and Earth, they skillfully carried forward their work; fathoming the spiritual potency of Heaven and Earth, they skillfully continued their purpose. Through the filial piety with which they served their parents, they thus fully realized the Way of serving Heaven. Yet, however wondrous these spiritual transformations, they cannot make the people understand. They establish government to set out the instruments of rule and institute punishments as methods to assist it. If the people do not follow when guided through government, punishments are also available to bring them into conformity. Yet, however good punishments and government may be, they cannot make the people follow.

Standing foremost among all beings, the sage knows that living beings originate in their parents and have no second source. Towering above his fellows, he knows that human relationships begin with that between father and son, and that all share the same nature. The filial love of one’s parents is part of people’s innate moral knowledge; the Way of being filial toward one’s parents is part of their original nature. The sage guides them through their innate moral knowledge and teaches them through their original nature. How could any fail to understand or to be transformed?

Those who possess states and serve as regional lords, and those who possess domains and serve as ministers and grand masters, are assigned ranks and duties, like the meshes of a net following its main cord: all are the king’s servants. Those who spring up in multitudes and dwell in clans, alike in kind yet different in form, turn inward and gaze toward the center, like stars surrounding the celestial pole: all are Heaven’s people. The enlightened king, through filial piety…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而率臣内焉隆是孝以篤於親則祇載共職
之是敬問安視膳之唯謹外焉舉斯心以加
諸彼則不敢遺小國之臣而尤懷諸侯有恩
以孝而化民則上老老而民興孝上有好而
下必甚教以六行則孝為首糾以八刑則不
孝為先制田里教樹畜使民遂養老之願立
學校明禮義使民知愛敬之道制禮以節是
孝則生事葬祭隆殺有等而敬親之禮通上
下而均行作樂以和是孝則八音克諧神人
===
以和而和親之樂合幽明而咸格親親而仁
民仁民而愛物推孝之序有順而無逆家齊
而國治國治而天下平成孝之教由近以及
遠殆見天下之臣雖萬國也萬國之心靡不
欣欣然歡洽天下之民雖萬姓也萬姓之心
罔不熙熙然和睦於焉繼志述事踐先王之
位而無愧禴祠烝嘗嚴先王之祀而無斁諸
侯法之以治國恭儉愛民不敢侮鰥寡故得
百姓之懽心以事其先君卿大夫效之以治
punctuated: 而率臣，内焉隆是孝以篤於親，則祇載共職之是敬，問安視膳之唯謹；外焉舉斯心以加諸彼，則不敢遺小國之臣，而尤懷諸侯有恩。以孝而化民，則上老老而民興孝，上有好而下必甚。教以六行，則孝為首；糾以八刑，則不孝為先。制田里，教樹畜，使民遂養老之願；立學校，明禮義，使民知愛敬之道。制禮以節是孝，則生事葬祭，隆殺有等，而敬親之禮通上下而均行；作樂以和是孝，則八音克諧，神人以和，而和親之樂合幽明而咸格。親親而仁民，仁民而愛物，推孝之序有順而無逆；家齊而國治，國治而天下平，成孝之教由近以及遠。殆見天下之臣，雖萬國也，萬國之心靡不欣欣然歡洽；天下之民，雖萬姓也，萬姓之心罔不熙熙然和睦。於焉繼志述事，踐先王之位而無愧；禴祠烝嘗，嚴先王之祀而無斁。諸侯法之以治國，恭儉愛民，不敢侮鰥寡，故得百姓之懽心以事其先君；卿大夫效之以治
translation_en:
…and leads his ministers. Within, he exalts this filial devotion to deepen his affection for his parents, reverently fulfilling his duties and attending diligently to their well-being and meals. Beyond, he extends this same heart to others: he dares not neglect even the minister of a small state, and especially cherishes the feudal lords with kindness. When he transforms the people through filial devotion, those above honor the aged, and the people are stirred to filial conduct; whatever those above favor, those below will pursue still more ardently. In teaching the six forms of virtuous conduct, filial devotion comes first; in correcting wrongdoing through the eight punishments, unfilial conduct takes precedence. He regulates fields and residential plots and teaches planting and animal husbandry, enabling the people to fulfill their wish to support the aged. He establishes schools and elucidates ritual propriety and righteousness, enabling the people to understand the way of love and reverence. He establishes rites to regulate this filial devotion: service to parents in life, burial, and sacrifice have graded degrees of elaborateness and simplicity, while the rites for revering parents extend through every rank and are practiced by all. He creates music to harmonize this filial devotion: the eight kinds of musical sound are brought into concord, spirits and human beings are harmonized, and the music that brings kin into harmony unites the unseen and visible realms, reaching them all.

From affection for one's kin one proceeds to benevolence toward the people, and from benevolence toward the people to care for all things: the sequence by which filial devotion is extended follows its proper course without reversal. When the family is ordered, the state is well governed; when the state is well governed, all under Heaven is at peace: the teaching that brings filial devotion to fulfillment proceeds from near to far. Thus one may behold the ministers of all under Heaven: although they belong to a myriad states, the hearts of all those states are joyfully united. Likewise, although the people of all under Heaven comprise a myriad families, their hearts are without exception contented and harmonious. Thereupon he carries forward the intentions and undertakings of the former kings, occupying their throne without shame; through the seasonal sacrifices—yue, ci, zheng, and chang—he solemnly maintains their worship without wearying. The feudal lords take him as their model in governing their states: reverent and frugal, they love the people and dare not mistreat widowers and widows. They thus gain the joyful allegiance of the common people with which to serve their departed rulers. Ministers and grandees emulate him in governing…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家刑于寡妻至於兄弟故得人之懽心以事
其親由是達諸天下人皆順其自然之性通
乎四海人皆遵乎脩道之教庶政惟和由有
孝以為根本五刑不用由有孝以為教化陰
陽和風雨時一至德之感也羣生和萬物遂
一要道之洽也論至於是則知明王之治雖
萬目畢張必能孝而後綱舉以父子人倫之
綱也雖庶事咸治必克孝而後本立以事親
事之本也稽之於古若親睦九族而黎民於
===
變瞽瞍底豫而天下化堯舜之治以孝而成
也為人子止於孝而萬民咸和善繼人之志
善述人之事而四方訓之文武之治亦以孝
而成也方今
聖人在上德堯舜之德道文武之道以天下養而
慈闈安其孝嚴
郊廟祀而鬼神享其祭是以百司庶府是矜是式
皆移孝為忠用遂顯揚之志群黎百姓是訓
是行皆謹身節用欲致孝養之誠和氣充乎
punctuated:
家，刑于寡妻，至於兄弟，故得人之懽心以事其親。由是達諸天下，人皆順其自然之性；通乎四海，人皆遵乎脩道之教。庶政惟和，由有孝以為根本；五刑不用，由有孝以為教化。陰陽和，風雨時，一至德之感也；羣生和，萬物遂，一要道之洽也。論至於是，則知明王之治，雖萬目畢張，必能孝而後綱舉，以父子人倫之綱也；雖庶事咸治，必克孝而後本立，以事親事之本也。稽之於古，若親睦九族而黎民於變，瞽瞍底豫而天下化，堯舜之治以孝而成也；為人子止於孝而萬民咸和，善繼人之志，善述人之事而四方訓之，文武之治亦以孝而成也。
方今聖人在上，德堯舜之德，道文武之道，以天下養而慈闈安其孝，嚴郊廟祀而鬼神享其祭。是以百司庶府是矜是式，皆移孝為忠，用遂顯揚之志；群黎百姓是訓是行，皆謹身節用，欲致孝養之誠。和氣充乎
translation_en:
…their households, setting an example for their wives and extending it to their brothers; thus they win others’ joyful affection and thereby serve their parents. From this, the influence reaches all under Heaven, and everyone follows their natural disposition; it spreads throughout the Four Seas, and everyone observes the teaching that cultivates the Way. The many affairs of government are harmonious because filial piety provides their foundation; the Five Punishments go unused because filial piety provides moral instruction. Yin and yang are harmonious, and winds and rains timely: all this is the response evoked by supreme virtue. Living beings dwell in harmony, and all things flourish: all this is the pervasive influence of the essential Way. Having carried the discussion this far, we see that, in an enlightened king’s government, although every mesh of the net is spread out, only through filial piety can its main cord be raised, for the bond between father and son is the main cord of human relationships. Although all affairs are well ordered, only through the fulfillment of filial piety can the foundation be established, for serving one’s parents is the foundation of all undertakings. Examining antiquity, we find that affection and harmony among the nine degrees of kinship brought transformation to the common people, and that Gusou’s being brought to contentment transformed all under Heaven: the government of Yao and Shun was accomplished through filial piety. Taking filial piety as the highest standard of conduct for a son brought harmony to all the people; skillfully carrying on one’s forebears’ purposes and continuing their undertakings caused the four quarters to follow their example: the government of Kings Wen and Wu was likewise accomplished through filial piety.
Now the sage occupies the throne, embodying the virtue of Yao and Shun and following the Way of Wen and Wu. He supports his mother with the resources of all under Heaven, so that she dwells at ease in the maternal palace through his filial devotion; he solemnly performs the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices, so that the spirits accept his offerings. Thus the officials of every bureau and office honor him and take him as their model. All turn filial piety into loyalty, thereby fulfilling their aspiration to bring honor to their parents. The common people all follow his instruction and put it into practice. All are circumspect in their conduct and frugal in their expenditure, wishing to express their sincerity in filial support. Harmonious influences fill…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兩間休徵應乎五事唐虞成周之治復見於
今日矣愚何幸躬逢其盛
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批初讀此論可驚可駭深潜涵泳如走下坂
車如縛白額虎不可以科場文字視之也置居前列允協輿情
同考試官教諭單批不險不恠有趣有味議論至此宜當起敬
考試官教授劉批此論意深辭古如不施控勒而騎生馬者
豈穉筆所能及耶允宜録出以範後學
考試官教諭鄭批命意淵深行文蒼古真有學之士也
===
土積而成山山之為山草木生焉禽獸居焉
是山之性也水積而成川川之為川萍藻出
焉魚鱉遊焉是川之性也以山而植萍藻置
魚鱉是反其山之性而所謂萍藻所謂魚鱉
者皆失其所焉以川而植草木養禽獸是反
其川之性而所謂草木所謂禽獸者亦失其
所焉故體物而不遺者天也雲行雨施品物
流形化化而無窮天何容心哉随物而厚生
者地也飛潜動植大造普施形形而不已地
punctuated:
兩間，休徵應乎五事，唐虞成周之治復見於今日矣。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

孫昇

同考試官教諭闕批：初讀此論，可驚可駭；深潜涵泳，如走下坂車，如縛白額虎，不可以科場文字視之也。置居前列，允協輿情。

同考試官教諭單批：不險不恠，有趣有味。議論至此，宜當起敬。

考試官教授劉批：此論意深辭古，如不施控勒而騎生馬者，豈穉筆所能及耶？允宜録出，以範後學。

考試官教諭鄭批：命意淵深，行文蒼古，真有學之士也。

土積而成山。山之為山，草木生焉，禽獸居焉，是山之性也。水積而成川。川之為川，萍藻出焉，魚鱉遊焉，是川之性也。以山而植萍藻、置魚鱉，是反其山之性，而所謂萍藻、所謂魚鱉者，皆失其所焉。以川而植草木、養禽獸，是反其川之性，而所謂草木、所謂禽獸者，亦失其所焉。故體物而不遺者，天也。雲行雨施，品物流形，化化而無窮，天何容心哉？随物而厚生者，地也。飛潜動植，大造普施，形形而不已，地
translation_en:
…between Heaven and Earth, and auspicious signs arise in response to the Five Activities. The good government of Tang and Yu and of the flourishing Zhou is seen again today. How fortunate I, in my humble capacity, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

Sun Sheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: On first reading, this discourse astonishes and startles. Immersing oneself deeply in it is like driving a cart downhill or binding a white-browed tiger. It cannot be regarded as merely an examination composition. Placing it among the foremost entries truly accords with the collective judgment.

Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: Neither abstruse nor eccentric, it has interest and savor. Argument of this caliber deserves our respect.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: This discourse is profound in conception and antique in diction, like riding an unbroken horse without applying the reins. How could an immature writer attain this? It certainly deserves to be copied out as a model for later students.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its conception is deep and far-reaching, and its prose mature and antique. He is truly a man of learning.

Earth accumulates to form a mountain. What makes a mountain a mountain is that grasses and trees grow upon it and birds and beasts dwell there: this is the mountain’s nature. Water accumulates to form a river. What makes a river a river is that duckweed and water plants emerge there and fish and turtles swim there: this is the river’s nature. To plant duckweed and water plants on a mountain and put fish and turtles there goes against the mountain’s nature, and these water plants, fish, and turtles all lose their proper place. To plant grasses and trees in a river and rear birds and beasts there goes against the river’s nature, and these grasses, trees, birds, and beasts likewise lose their proper place. Thus, it is Heaven that gives substance to all things without omitting any. Clouds move and rain falls; the myriad things flow into their forms. Transformation follows transformation without end: what deliberate intention does Heaven entertain? It is Earth that enriches life in accordance with the nature of each thing. To creatures that fly or swim, to animals and plants, its great creative power is universally extended. Form follows form without cease; Earth…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何容心哉故明王之以孝治天下乃因人之
所固有者而開導之即天之體物而不遺因
民之所自然者而誘引之即地之隨物以厚
生所謂不立異以求名不反道而敗德如山
也必植草木必居禽獸焉如川也必生萍藻
必遊魚鱉焉其性也如此人或有疑之者曰
富國強兵人君治天下之要道所以制侵陵
厚邦本如秦如漢當時陳之者莫先行之者
恐後求賢取士安天下之良法所以充庶位
===
理繁劇如唐如宋當時告之者諄諄用之者
亟亟而仲尼謂明王以孝治天下抑有說歟
蓋孝者天之經地之義民之行也明王乃則
天之經因地之義順民之行焉故愛敬盡於
事親德教刑於四海將見治國者不敢侮鰥
寡治家者不敢侮臣妾無有不得其懽心者
焉又豈止於如此而已哉大寶之位祖宗之
所授也不敢以富貴而驕天下四海之衆祖
宗之所遺也不敢以天下而奉一人于以保
punctuated: 何容心哉？故明王之以孝治天下，乃因人之所固有者而開導之，即天之體物而不遺；因民之所自然者而誘引之，即地之隨物以厚生。所謂不立異以求名，不反道而敗德。如山也，必植草木，必居禽獸焉；如川也，必生萍藻，必遊魚鱉焉。其性也如此。人或有疑之者曰：「富國強兵，人君治天下之要道，所以制侵陵、厚邦本。如秦如漢，當時陳之者莫先，行之者恐後。求賢取士，安天下之良法，所以充庶位、理繁劇。如唐如宋，當時告之者諄諄，用之者亟亟。而仲尼謂明王以孝治天下，抑有說歟？」蓋孝者，天之經、地之義、民之行也。明王乃則天之經，因地之義，順民之行焉。故愛敬盡於事親，德教刑於四海。將見治國者不敢侮鰥寡，治家者不敢侮臣妾，無有不得其懽心者焉。又豈止於如此而已哉？大寶之位，祖宗之所授也，不敢以富貴而驕天下；四海之衆，祖宗之所遺也，不敢以天下而奉一人。于以保
translation_en:
…what deliberate intention could Earth have? Thus, when an enlightened king governs All Under Heaven through filial piety, he guides people by drawing upon what they inherently possess, just as Heaven embodies all things without leaving anything out. He leads the people by drawing upon what comes naturally to them, just as Earth sustains life abundantly in accordance with the nature of each thing. This is what is meant by neither seeking fame through contrived departures from the ordinary nor ruining virtue by going against the Way. A mountain must grow grasses and trees and shelter birds and beasts; a river must produce duckweed and algae and have fish and turtles swimming in it. Such are their natures.

Someone might question this, saying: “Enriching the state and strengthening its armed forces are essential means by which a ruler governs All Under Heaven: they check encroachment and strengthen the foundations of the state. Under the Qin and Han, those who proposed such measures strove to be first, and those who implemented them feared falling behind. Seeking worthy men and recruiting scholars are excellent methods for bringing peace to All Under Heaven: they fill the various offices and enable the management of complex and demanding affairs. Under the Tang and Song, those who advocated these methods did so earnestly, and those who employed them did so urgently. Yet Zhongni says that an enlightened king governs All Under Heaven through filial piety. Is there an explanation for this?”

Filial piety is Heaven’s constant principle, Earth’s proper order, and the people’s rule of conduct. An enlightened king therefore models himself upon Heaven’s constant principle, follows Earth’s proper order, and accords with the people’s rule of conduct. Thus, he fully expresses love and reverence in serving his parents, and his moral teaching becomes a model throughout the Four Seas. We shall then see those who govern states not daring to mistreat widowers and widows, and those who govern households not daring to mistreat male and female servants. There will be none whose goodwill they fail to win.

But could the effects end there? The supremely precious throne was bestowed by his ancestors: he dares not use his wealth and exalted station to treat All Under Heaven arrogantly. The multitudes within the Four Seas were bequeathed by his ancestors: he dares not use All Under Heaven to serve a single person. By these means he preserves…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
社稷於靈長于以措斯民於樂業亦何莫而
非明王之以孝治天下也耶是以天下和平
而四靈畢至禍亂不作而萬國休寧矣古亦
有是君歟若虞舜之事瞽瞍夔夔齊慄乃以
身先天下而四方有風動之休武王之事文
王善繼善述亦以身先天下而四海有永清
之化則孝之根於人心之固有者可知也已
真如山之養草木禽獸川之蓄萍藻魚鱉有
不期然而然者焉或又疑之曰在人有上智
===
與下愚為政有刑驅與勢迫離母而居見罪
於孟軻怨親之詩乃形於小弁若曰明王以
孝治天下恐四海之廣億兆之衆亦有離母
而怨親者焉似未可深信也於乎有是我人
君以仁感天下天下以仁應之者堯舜是也
人君以義感天下天下以義應之者湯武是
也矧至愚而神者民心也至明而顯者孝道
也人君能以孝而自處則天下之人必曰是
吾君能孝也吾亦有親焉有親而不事吾亦
punctuated:
社稷於靈長，于以措斯民於樂業，亦何莫而非明王之以孝治天下也耶？是以天下和平，而四靈畢至；禍亂不作，而萬國休寧矣。古亦有是君歟？若虞舜之事瞽瞍，夔夔齊慄，乃以身先天下，而四方有風動之休；武王之事文王，善繼善述，亦以身先天下，而四海有永清之化。則孝之根於人心之固有者，可知也已。真如山之養草木禽獸，川之蓄萍藻魚鱉，有不期然而然者焉。
或又疑之曰：「在人有上智與下愚，為政有刑驅與勢迫。離母而居，見罪於孟軻；怨親之詩，乃形於小弁。若曰明王以孝治天下，恐四海之廣、億兆之衆，亦有離母而怨親者焉，似未可深信也。」於乎！有是我？人君以仁感天下，天下以仁應之者，堯舜是也；人君以義感天下，天下以義應之者，湯武是也。矧至愚而神者，民心也；至明而顯者，孝道也。人君能以孝而自處，則天下之人必曰：「是吾君能孝也！吾亦有親焉，有親而不事，吾亦
translation_en:
…the altars of soil and grain in enduring security, and thereby settle the people in contented pursuit of their livelihoods—how could any of this fail to exemplify an enlightened king’s governing all under Heaven through filial piety? Thus all under Heaven enjoys peace and harmony, and the four auspicious creatures all appear; calamity and disorder do not arise, and the myriad states enjoy repose and tranquility. Were there such rulers in antiquity? Yu Shun served his father Gusou with reverent vigilance and trembling awe, setting an example in his own person for all under Heaven, so that the four quarters were blessed with a response like grass stirred by the wind. King Wu served King Wen by ably carrying on his purposes and undertakings, likewise setting an example in his own person for all under Heaven, so that the lands within the four seas were transformed and enjoyed lasting peace. From this we can understand that filial piety is rooted in what is inherent in the human heart. It is truly like mountains nourishing plants, trees, birds, and beasts, or rivers sustaining duckweed, algae, fish, and turtles: these things happen without anyone intending that they should.
Someone might nevertheless raise a doubt, saying: “Among people there are those of the highest wisdom and those of the lowest stupidity; in government there are the compulsion of punishments and the pressure of authority. Living apart from one’s mother incurred Meng Ke’s condemnation, and resentment toward one’s parents found expression in the poem ‘Little Cap’ (Xiao Bian). If one says that enlightened kings govern all under Heaven through filial piety, I fear that, throughout the vast lands within the four seas and among their countless inhabitants, there will still be those who abandon their mothers and resent their parents. It seems that this claim cannot yet be fully credited.” Alas! Can this be so [?]? When rulers moved all under Heaven through benevolence, and all under Heaven responded with benevolence, these were Yao and Shun. When rulers moved all under Heaven through righteousness, and all under Heaven responded with righteousness, these were Tang and King Wu. Moreover, the hearts of the people, though utterly simple, possess a wondrous responsiveness; the way of filial piety is supremely clear and manifest. If a ruler can conduct himself with filial piety, the people throughout the realm will surely say: “Our ruler can indeed be filial! I too have parents. If I have parents yet fail to serve them, I too…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有子焉不欲子之不順於我則不敢以此事
吾親不樂子之不孝於我則不敢以此奉吾
親相師相法於治教休明之日相牽相引於
仁義道德之塲仲尼所謂得萬國之懽心以
事其先君而明王以孝治天下至此瞭然矣
復民之性導民之善更豈有過於此哉是即
草木鳥獸生養於山萍藻魚鱉浮遊於水各
奠其位各適其性也而明王以孝治天下之
功化又當與天之體物不遺地之隨物厚生
===
相參列而不相背馳也如此夫求諸今日
聖天子奉
聖母以孝治天下則其感化之效又與帝舜文王
同驅而並列也仲尼之言幾二千載而始驗
矣愚何幸身親見之謹論
表
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批表佳
punctuated:
有子焉，不欲子之不順於我，則不敢以此事吾親；不樂子之不孝於我，則不敢以此奉吾親。相師相法於治教休明之日，相牽相引於仁義道德之塲。仲尼所謂得萬國之懽心以事其先君，而明王以孝治天下，至此瞭然矣。復民之性，導民之善，更豈有過於此哉？是即草木鳥獸生養於山，萍藻魚鱉浮遊於水，各奠其位，各適其性也。而明王以孝治天下之功化，又當與天之體物不遺、地之隨物厚生，相參列而不相背馳也，如此夫！求諸今日，聖天子奉聖母，以孝治天下，則其感化之效，又與帝舜、文王同驅而並列也。仲尼之言幾二千載而始驗矣，愚何幸身親見之！謹論。

表

擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表

孫昇

同考試官教諭闕批：表佳。
translation_en:
…have children. Not wishing my children to disobey me, I would not dare treat my own parents in that way; not wanting my children to be unfilial toward me, I would not dare serve my own parents in that way.” People teach and emulate one another in an age of splendid government and enlightened instruction, drawing and guiding one another into the realm of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue. What Zhongni meant by “winning the joyful hearts of the myriad states in order to serve their former rulers,” and how enlightened kings govern all under Heaven through filial piety, now become perfectly clear. What could surpass this in restoring the people’s inherent nature and guiding their goodness? It is like plants, trees, birds, and beasts growing and being nurtured in the mountains, and duckweed, algae, fish, and turtles floating and swimming in the waters: each is settled in its proper place and finds fulfillment according to its nature. The transformative achievements of enlightened kings who govern all under Heaven through filial piety should likewise rank alongside Heaven, which embodies all things without omission, and Earth, which richly nurtures each according to its kind, proceeding together without divergence. Such indeed is their greatness!

Looking to the present day, our sagely Son of Heaven reverently serves his august mother and governs all under Heaven through filial piety. The effects of his inspiring and transforming influence thus keep pace with, and rank alongside, those of Emperor Shun and King Wen. Only now, nearly two thousand years later, have Zhongni’s words found their fulfillment. How fortunate I, in my humble ignorance, am to witness this personally! Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial

A hypothetical memorial of thanks, presented by the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education at the head of the students, for an increase in the bamboo and wooden sacrificial vessels and the ranks of ritual dancers used in the sacrifices to Kongzi.

By Sun Sheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: “A fine memorial.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭何批氣象寛洪可取
考試官教授劉批有典有則佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批得體
伏以先孔子而聖者非孔子無以明後孔子
而聖者非孔子無以法道冠古今刪六經而
垂訓德侔天地配大化以施功宰我有賢於
堯舜之稱曽參有潔於江漢之喻故過魯一
祀開漢家四百年之帝業入廟再拜啓唐室
三百載之王基聞之者喜見之者榮陳綱立
===
紀伊誰之功著德立言是誰之力邇者尊崇
盛禮闡
昭代之宏規增制鴻休恢太平之盛典景行實
超於前哲報功垂法於後人士類歡騰儒風
益振兹盖伏遇
〇〇〇〇
默運乾綱布道義以臨天下
靜含坤造廣仁恕以賴萬方
智本生知
punctuated:
同考試官教諭何批：氣象寛洪，可取。
考試官教授劉批：有典有則，佳作也。
考試官教諭鄭批：得體。
伏以先孔子而聖者，非孔子無以明；後孔子而聖者，非孔子無以法。道冠古今，刪六經而垂訓；德侔天地，配大化以施功。宰我有賢於堯舜之稱，曽參有潔於江漢之喻。故過魯一祀，開漢家四百年之帝業；入廟再拜，啓唐室三百載之王基。聞之者喜，見之者榮。陳綱立紀，伊誰之功？著德立言，是誰之力？邇者尊崇盛禮，闡昭代之宏規；增制鴻休，恢太平之盛典。景行實超於前哲，報功垂法於後人。士類歡騰，儒風益振。
兹盖伏遇〇〇〇〇，默運乾綱，布道義以臨天下；靜含坤造，廣仁恕以賴萬方。智本生知，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The composition has a broad and generous bearing; it merits acceptance.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “It has classical authority and proper form: a fine composition.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “Appropriate to the genre.”
We respectfully submit: without Confucius, the sages who preceded him could not have been made manifest; without Confucius, those who became sages after him would have had no model to follow. His Way surpasses all, ancient and modern: he edited the Six Classics to bequeath instruction. His virtue equals Heaven and Earth: he assisted the great transforming process in accomplishing its work. Zai Wo praised him as worthier than Yao and Shun; Zeng Shen likened his purity to that surpassing the Jiang and Han rivers. Thus, a single sacrifice when passing through Lu inaugurated the Han dynasty’s four hundred years of imperial achievement; a double bow upon entering his temple opened the Tang house’s three hundred years of royal rule. Those who hear of this rejoice; those who witness it feel honored. Whose achievement was it to establish the guiding principles and rules? Whose efforts made virtue manifest and established enduring teachings? Recently, magnificent rites of veneration have displayed the grand designs of this illustrious age; expanded ritual provisions and abundant blessings have enlarged the splendid ceremonies of an age of peace. This lofty conduct truly surpasses that of earlier worthies, repaying his achievements and bequeathing a model to posterity. Scholars rejoice, and the Confucian tradition flourishes still more.
This is because we have respectfully encountered [〇〇〇〇: imperial address unclear], who silently wields Heaven’s governing authority, spreading the Way and righteousness to preside over all under Heaven; who serenely embodies Earth’s creative power, extending benevolence and sympathetic understanding to benefit every region. Your wisdom is innate …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖由天縱
盛名兼配於三王丕績纘承乎
列聖崇儒重道制度考文籩豆加飾增高夫子
之門墻佾舞展容用饗天王之禮樂于以格
聖靈而厚風化于以補缺典而重彜倫春秋
祀事於廟庭中外頒行於庠序郁郁斯文於
今為盛巍巍洪制振古罕聞臣某等職忝司成
位登胄監目覩曠世所無之禮身親百代所
吝之儀謹率六館之書生敬望
===
九重而稽首趨蹌舞蹈惟思感激之深進退周
旋莫罄揄揚之妙伏願
宗社奠安世道與吾道而俱泰
皇圖鞏固
聖壽與
國壽以無疆臣某等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
punctuated: 聖由天縱，盛名兼配於三王，丕績纘承乎列聖。崇儒重道，制度考文，籩豆加飾，增高夫子之門墻；佾舞展容，用饗天王之禮樂。于以格聖靈而厚風化，于以補缺典而重彜倫。春秋祀事於廟庭，中外頒行於庠序。郁郁斯文，於今為盛；巍巍洪制，振古罕聞。臣某等職忝司成，位登胄監，目覩曠世所無之禮，身親百代所吝之儀。謹率六館之書生，敬望九重而稽首，趨蹌舞蹈，惟思感激之深；進退周旋，莫罄揄揚之妙。伏願宗社奠安，世道與吾道而俱泰；皇圖鞏固，聖壽與國壽以無疆。臣某等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以
translation_en:
…Your sageliness is Heaven-bestowed. Your illustrious renown equals that of the Three Kings, and your great achievements continue those of your sagely predecessors. You exalt Confucian learning and honor the Way, establish institutions and examine cultural forms. By further embellishing the bamboo and wooden sacrificial vessels, you raise still higher the walls and gates of the Master's school; by displaying the ordered ranks of ritual dancers, you offer him the rites and music of the Son of Heaven. Thus you bring the sage's spirit into attendance and deepen moral transformation; thus you supply what was lacking in the ritual canon and give greater weight to the enduring human relationships. Spring and autumn sacrifices are performed in the temple courts, and these provisions are promulgated for observance in schools both at the capital and throughout the realm. This flourishing cultural tradition has now reached its height; such lofty and magnificent institutions have seldom been heard of since antiquity.
We, your servants So-and-so and the others, unworthily entrusted with educational duties and holding posts in the Directorate of Education, have witnessed rites unparalleled through the ages and personally participated in ceremonies rarely accorded in a hundred generations. Respectfully leading the students of the six halls, we gaze toward the imperial palace and bow our heads to the ground. Hastening forward and dancing in homage, we think only of our profound gratitude; advancing, withdrawing, and turning in ceremonial order, we cannot fully express the wonders we would extol.
We humbly wish that the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temples may rest secure, and that the world's affairs and our Way may prosper together; that imperial rule may stand firm, and that Your Majesty's lifespan and the life of the state may alike be boundless. We, your servants So-and-so and the others, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty, overcome with fervent emotion and the utmost awe. We respectfully present this memorial to express our thanks and thereby…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聞
策
第一問
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批氣壯而文達有學之士也
同考試官教諭單批有鋪叙有事實至於揚示我
聖祖神功聖德處所謂日月之光筆莫能描此作頗彷彿其一二焉允宜充選
