考試官教諭鄭批讀此策如入武庫得觀天球河圖着乎可佳
===
日月麗於天而四海仰其光明江河行於地
而萬物資其灌溉故有一代之
聖君必有一代之
聖制光同日月利比江河而可以垂憲萬世統緒
後昆者也洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝以生知之資受
天明命取天下於群雄之手措四海於一統之盛
乃於萬機之暇條成大誥三編以昭示臣民
punctuated:
聞。

策。第一問。孫昇。

同考試官教諭闕批：「氣壯而文達，有學之士也。」

同考試官教諭單批：「有鋪叙，有事實。至於揚示我聖祖神功聖德處，所謂日月之光，筆莫能描，此作頗彷彿其一二焉，允宜充選。」

考試官教授劉批：「敷對無遺，歸美得體，空群騏驥，非子其誰？」

考試官教諭鄭批：「讀此策，如入武庫，得觀天球河圖，着乎可佳。」

日月麗於天，而四海仰其光明；江河行於地，而萬物資其灌溉。故有一代之聖君，必有一代之聖制，光同日月，利比江河，而可以垂憲萬世、統緒後昆者也。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，以生知之資，受天明命，取天下於群雄之手，措四海於一統之盛，乃於萬機之暇，條成大誥三編，以昭示臣民。
translation_en:
… to bring this to Your Majesty’s attention.

Policy Essay. First Question. Sun Sheng.

Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: “Vigorous in spirit and fluent in expression: he is a man of learning.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: “There is ample exposition and factual substance. Where it proclaims the divine achievements and sagely virtue of our Sagely Ancestor, these are, as the saying goes, like the radiance of sun and moon, which no brush can depict. This composition captures something of that radiance and assuredly deserves selection.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “His response leaves nothing unaddressed, and his attribution of praise is fitting. A thoroughbred that outclasses the entire herd—who could this be but you?”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Reading this policy essay is like entering an arsenal and being privileged to behold the celestial jade sphere and the River Chart. It is manifestly admirable [?].”

The sun and moon shine in heaven, and all within the four seas look up to their radiance; the rivers flow upon the earth, and all things depend upon their irrigation. Thus, whenever an age has a sagely ruler, it must also have that age’s sagely writings, whose radiance equals the sun and moon and whose benefits rival the rivers. These can bequeath models for ten thousand generations and transmit the dynastic succession to posterity. We reverently reflect that our dynasty’s Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed with innate understanding, received Heaven’s illustrious mandate, took the realm from the hands of contending warlords, and brought all within the four seas to the flourishing condition of unified rule. Then, in moments spared from the myriad affairs of government, he compiled the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) in three collections, setting them out in ordered articles to instruct his officials and people.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝甫靖內難一新王度譔述為善陰騭
以曉諭四方以及
宣宗章皇帝纂集五倫書
英宗睿皇帝脩述大一統志皆所以繼前聖之道
脉開後學之愚蒙其有功於斯世豈淺淺哉
易曰天地感而萬物化生聖人感人心而天
下和平書曰至治馨香感于神明黍稷非馨
明德惟馨他如詩所謂無競維人四方其訓
之有覺德行四國順之春秋穀梁所謂為天
===
下主者天也繼天者君也君之所存者命也
以至記禮者有云有國者彰善癉惡以示民
厚則民情不貳夫
列聖之所以垂洪謨大訓其與仲尼所纘述六經
如持符取信如造車合轍無往而不同也載
思我
聖祖之
神功聖德真可以超卓高光比方湯武且如紀元
所以統曆數也漢武帝得寶鼎而改元唐肅
punctuated:
太宗文皇帝甫靖內難，一新王度，譔述《為善陰騭》，以曉諭四方。以及宣宗章皇帝纂集《五倫書》，英宗睿皇帝脩述《大一統志》，皆所以繼前聖之道脉，開後學之愚蒙。其有功於斯世，豈淺淺哉？
《易》曰：「天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。」《書》曰：「至治馨香，感于神明。黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」他如《詩》所謂「無競維人，四方其訓之」，「有覺德行，四國順之」；《春秋穀梁》所謂「為天下主者，天也；繼天者，君也；君之所存者，命也」；以至記禮者有云：「有國者彰善癉惡，以示民厚，則民情不貳。」夫列聖之所以垂洪謨大訓，其與仲尼所纘述六經，如持符取信，如造車合轍，無往而不同也。
載思我聖祖之神功聖德，真可以超卓高光，比方湯武。且如紀元，所以統曆數也。漢武帝得寶鼎而改元，唐肅
translation_en:
Emperor Wen, Taizong, having just quelled the internal troubles, renewed the institutions of kingship in their entirety and composed Doing Good and Hidden Blessings (Weishan yinzhi) to instruct the people throughout the realm. Subsequently, Emperor Zhang, Xuanzong, compiled the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), and Emperor Rui, Yingzong, compiled the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Unity (Da Yitong zhi). All these works served to continue the transmission of the Way from the former sages and dispel the ignorance of later students. Could their contribution to this world possibly be slight?
The Book of Changes says: “Heaven and earth act upon one another, and the myriad things are transformed and born; the sage moves people’s hearts, and all under Heaven is peaceful and harmonious.” The Book of Documents says: “The fragrance of perfect government reaches the spirits. It is not millet that gives forth fragrance; enlightened virtue alone is fragrant.” Other examples include what the Book of Odes calls “None can rival these men; the four quarters take instruction from them,” and “Illustrious in virtuous conduct, they are obeyed by the states of the four quarters.” The Guliang Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals says: “The master of all under Heaven is Heaven; he who succeeds Heaven is the ruler; what the ruler preserves is the Mandate.” Even the recorders of ritual have said: “When those who possess a state exalt goodness and condemn evil, thereby showing generosity to the people, the people’s affections will not be divided.” The grand plans and great instructions bequeathed by our successive sage emperors accord with the Six Classics compiled and transmitted by Zhongni [Confucius], like presenting a tally to establish trust, or building a carriage to fit the wheel tracks. In every respect they agree.
Reflecting further upon the divine achievements and sagely virtue of our sagely founding ancestor, we find that he truly surpassed Gaozu and Guangwu of the Han and equaled Tang and Wu. Take, for example, the establishment of reign eras: its purpose is to bring calendrical reckoning under a unified system. Emperor Wu of the Han obtained a precious tripod and changed his reign era; Emperor Suzong of the Tang…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宗因時變而更號紀錄紛紜全無定規廟宇
所以祀神祇也宋徽宗加鴻號於玉皇元文
宗上美謚於天祀濁亂反覆絕非善政今則
紀一元而終始如造化週流則歲功一定而
萬物自榮矣立木主以正名如品位分明則
尊卑配列而神明自享矣惡宮室之華美則
以兩廡書寫大學衍義不事雕飾惟務質朴
其思慮之深也又何如知稼穡之艱難則命
畫工圖繪經歷艱苦不為浮名思存實跡其
===
洪圖之遠也又何若所以如斯者蓋欲
聖子神孫知正心誠意之學識治亂興亡之理有
如法家拂士日在左右焉鑒起軍歷農之苦
察化家成國之難有如耕圖織譜日張前後
焉至於創造歷代帝王之廟考配歷代有功
之臣去趙普以為有負藝祖為不忠罷安童
以為祀厥祖而難並增陳平馮異以為君臣
有同德之休進潘美以為節義有始終之善
於是定以風后力牧皐陶夔龍伯夷伯益伊
punctuated:
宗因時變而更號，紀錄紛紜，全無定規。廟宇所以祀神祇也，宋徽宗加鴻號於玉皇，元文宗上美謚於天，祀濁亂反覆，絕非善政。今則紀一元而終始，如造化週流，則歲功一定而萬物自榮矣；立木主以正名，如品位分明，則尊卑配列而神明自享矣。惡宮室之華美，則以兩廡書寫《大學衍義》，不事雕飾，惟務質朴，其思慮之深也又何如！知稼穡之艱難，則命畫工圖繪經歷艱苦，不為浮名，思存實跡，其洪圖之遠也又何若！所以如斯者，蓋欲聖子神孫知正心誠意之學，識治亂興亡之理，有如法家拂士日在左右焉；鑒起軍歷農之苦，察化家成國之難，有如耕圖織譜日張前後焉。
至於創造歷代帝王之廟，考配歷代有功之臣，去趙普，以為有負藝祖，為不忠；罷安童，以為祀厥祖而難並；增陳平、馮異，以為君臣有同德之休；進潘美，以為節義有始終之善。於是定以風后、力牧、皐陶、夔、龍、伯夷、伯益、伊
translation_en:
…[Tang Su]zong changed his reign designation in response to changing circumstances. The records were confused and multitudinous, with no fixed rule at all. Temples serve to offer sacrifices to the spirits. Emperor Huizong of Song bestowed a grand title upon the Jade Emperor, and Emperor Wenzong of Yuan conferred a laudatory posthumous title upon Heaven. Such confused and repeatedly altered sacrifices were certainly not good government. Now, however, a single reign designation is maintained from beginning to end. Like the continuous cycles of creation, this fixes the annual course, and all things flourish of themselves. Wooden spirit tablets are established to rectify designations: as ranks are clearly distinguished, the higher and lower are arranged in their proper places, and the spirits duly partake of the offerings. Disliking ornate palaces, he had the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) inscribed in the two side galleries, eschewing carved ornament and seeking only simplicity. How profound was his deliberation! Knowing the hardships of sowing and reaping, he ordered painters to depict the privations he had experienced, seeking no empty reputation but wishing to preserve the record of actual deeds. How far-reaching was his grand design! He did this so that his sagely sons and divine grandsons would understand the learning of rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere, and recognize the principles governing order and disorder, rise and fall—as though upholders of the law and admonitory gentlemen stood beside them every day. They would reflect upon the hardships of raising armies and working the fields [?], and perceive the difficulty of transforming a household into a state—as though pictures of plowing and illustrations of weaving were displayed before and behind them every day.
As for establishing the Temple of Emperors of Successive Dynasties, he examined which meritorious ministers of past dynasties should receive associated sacrifices. He removed Zhao Pu, judging him disloyal for having failed Emperor Taizu of Song. He excluded An Tong, considering that, since An Tong’s ancestor was receiving sacrifices, it was difficult to include him alongside that ancestor. He added Chen Ping and Feng Yi because they exemplified the excellence of ruler and minister sharing the same virtue. He admitted Pan Mei because his integrity and righteousness were commendable from beginning to end. Accordingly, he settled upon Feng Hou, Li Mu, Gao Yao, Kui, Long, Bo Yi 伯夷, Bo Yi 伯益, Yi…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
尹傅說周公旦召公奭太公望召虎方叔張
良蕭何曹參陳平周勃鄧禹馮異諸葛亮房
玄齡杜如晦李靖李晟郭子儀曹彬潘美韓
世忠岳飛張浚木華黎博爾忽博爾术赤老
温伯顏共三十有七人配饗焉嗟夫雖卧首
陽而猶當知周家之德雖釣桐江而亦當感
漢室之恩矧生於
聖明之時膏沐菁莪之化今應賓興而來乃承明
問所及恨襪線之才不足以鋪張萬世之宏
===
規管窺之見安足以揚厲無前之偉績聊舉
所聞進教是幸
第二問
姜森
同考試官訓導先批此策於斷制處儘明白
同考試官教諭楚批場中能記事實者無如兹作
同考試官學正胡批條荅詳明可取
考試官教授劉批此作如良馬歩康莊不驚不驟必佳士也
考試官教諭鄭批末以公明二字為獻其知本者乎
punctuated:
尹、傅說、周公旦、召公奭、太公望、召虎、方叔、張良、蕭何、曹參、陳平、周勃、鄧禹、馮異、諸葛亮、房玄齡、杜如晦、李靖、李晟、郭子儀、曹彬、潘美、韓世忠、岳飛、張浚、木華黎、博爾忽、博爾术、赤老温、伯顏，共三十有七人配饗焉。嗟夫！雖卧首陽，而猶當知周家之德；雖釣桐江，而亦當感漢室之恩。矧生於聖明之時，膏沐菁莪之化，今應賓興而來，乃承明問所及，恨襪線之才不足以鋪張萬世之宏規，管窺之見安足以揚厲無前之偉績？聊舉所聞，進教是幸。

第二問
姜森

同考試官訓導先批：此策於斷制處儘明白。
同考試官教諭楚批：場中能記事實者，無如兹作。
同考試官學正胡批：條荅詳明，可取。
考試官教授劉批：此作如良馬歩康莊，不驚不驟，必佳士也。
考試官教諭鄭批：末以公明二字為獻，其知本者乎？
translation_en:
…Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou Dan, the Duke of Shao Shi, Grand Duke Wang, Shao Hu, Fang Shu, Zhang Liang, Xiao He, Cao Can, Chen Ping, Zhou Bo, Deng Yu, Feng Yi, Zhuge Liang, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Li Jing, Li Sheng, Guo Ziyi, Cao Bin, Pan Mei, Han Shizhong, Yue Fei, Zhang Jun, Muhuali, Bo’erhu, Bo’ershu, Chilaowen, and Boyan—a total of thirty-seven men—were accorded associated sacrifices there. Ah! Even one who lay in retirement on Mount Shouyang ought still to acknowledge the virtue of the house of Zhou; even one who fished on the Tong River ought likewise to feel gratitude for the grace of the Han house. How much more should I, born in an age of sagely enlightenment and nurtured by the educational influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Southernwood”! Having now come in response to the call for the ceremonial recommendation of worthy men, I have received your illuminating questions. I regret that my talent, as meager as thread for stockings, is insufficient to set forth fully the grand designs that will endure for myriad generations. How could my narrow view, like a glimpse through a tube, adequately extol these unprecedented achievements? I have merely presented what I have heard and would count it a blessing to receive your instruction.

Second Policy Question
Jiang Sen

Associate Examiner Xian, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This policy essay is quite clear in the passages where it reaches judgments.”
Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor, comments: “Among the examination essays, none matches this one in its command of historical facts.”
Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The answers to the individual points are detailed and clear, and merit acceptance.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “This composition is like a fine horse walking along a broad highway, neither shying nor rushing. Its author must be an excellent scholar.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “At the end he offers the two words ‘impartiality’ and ‘discernment’ as his counsel. Surely he understands the essentials?”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夫賢才者治天下之本也盛衰所由係焉故
孔明有曰親賢臣遠小人此先漢所以興也
親小人遠賢臣此後漢所以傾也然其進退
之要又在於主司知之明而守之公耳盖知
之不明則惑於讒邪而賢否無定見守之不
公則狃於勢利而予奪無定法何以丕隆
聖明之治道益醇天下之風化者哉請因明問所
及而詳陳之井田法行學校政舉故人各安
分而尚恬靜之習井田法壞學校政廢故人
===
無定向而起僥倖之心是知人情之趨避因
時勢而轉移然其知所勸戒者亦由上之用
舍何如耳夷稽諸古范杲玉堂獻記上惡其
躁競終不得入於翰苑胡旦河平獻頌上覽
其率繆終不得留於蘭臺兩及相門却以素
定者王文正之拒張師德嚴矣一謁大資却
以不求者程伊川之語韓持國當矣抑之若
此則奔競之風俗自將渙然而消釋矣然執
事因楊雄韓愈之納交而遂疑奔競者之可
punctuated:
夫賢才者，治天下之本也，盛衰所由係焉。故孔明有曰：「親賢臣，遠小人，此先漢所以興也；親小人，遠賢臣，此後漢所以傾也。」然其進退之要，又在於主司知之明而守之公耳。盖知之不明，則惑於讒邪，而賢否無定見；守之不公，則狃於勢利，而予奪無定法。何以丕隆聖明之治道，益醇天下之風化者哉？請因明問所及而詳陳之。

井田法行，學校政舉，故人各安分而尚恬靜之習；井田法壞，學校政廢，故人無定向而起僥倖之心。是知人情之趨避，因時勢而轉移。然其知所勸戒者，亦由上之用舍何如耳。夷稽諸古，范杲玉堂獻記，上惡其躁競，終不得入於翰苑；胡旦河平獻頌，上覽其率繆，終不得留於蘭臺。兩及相門，却以素定者，王文正之拒張師德嚴矣；一謁大資，却以不求者，程伊川之語韓持國當矣。抑之若此，則奔競之風俗，自將渙然而消釋矣。然執事因楊雄、韓愈之納交，而遂疑奔競者之可
translation_en:
Worthy and talented men are the foundation of governing the realm; upon them depend its flourishing and decline. Thus Kongming said: “Drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men at a distance was how the Former Han flourished; drawing close to petty men and keeping worthy ministers at a distance was how the Later Han fell.” Yet the essential point in advancing or dismissing men lies in those responsible discerning clearly and maintaining impartiality. If their discernment is unclear, slanderous and wicked men will mislead them, and they will have no settled judgment of worthiness or unworthiness. If they do not maintain impartiality, they will succumb to power and profit, and have no consistent rule for granting or withholding appointments. How, then, could they greatly enhance the sagely and enlightened sovereign’s government and further purify the realm’s customs? Allow me to explain in detail the matters raised by your illuminating question.

When the well-field system operated and schooling was maintained, people were content with their allotted stations and valued habits of quiet composure. When the well-field system collapsed and schooling was abandoned, people lost their settled direction and began hoping for undeserved advancement. From this we know that what people pursue or avoid changes with the circumstances of the times. Yet their understanding of what to emulate and what to shun also depends upon how those above employ or reject men. Examining earlier precedents [?], Fan Gao presented an account of the Jade Hall; the emperor disliked his restless striving for advancement, and he ultimately failed to enter the Hanlin Academy. Hu Dan presented a eulogy on the river’s pacification; the emperor saw its carelessness and errors, and he ultimately failed to remain at the Orchid Terrace. Zhang Shide twice visited the chief minister’s gate, but was turned away on the grounds that the decision had already been settled [?]: stern indeed was Wang Wenzheng’s rejection of him. Cheng Yichuan once visited the Grand Academician, but rebuffed him by declaring that he sought nothing: fitting indeed were his words to Han Chiguo. If such conduct is restrained in this way, the custom of scrambling for advancement will naturally dissipate and disappear. Yet because Yang Xiong and Han Yu cultivated connections, you, sir, consequently entertain the thought that those who scramble for advancement might be …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宥殊不知揚雄專於媚世取寵特名教之罪
人也韓愈急於救時行道實天下之阿衡也
豈可以一例而論哉唐介不以私書至京師
則擢以御史之職王舉正不以私事干朝廷
則處以諫諍之司不通問訊者劉噐之也而
薦充舘職非溫公急於親賢而何不就廷試
者韓維也而乞加甄錄非溫公切於勸善而
何獎之若此則恬退之風俗自將勃然而興
起矣然執事曰伯夷子陵之制行而遂疑恬
===
退者之為庸殊不知伯夷逺引潔身其清奚
擬焉子陵高尚忘勢其節孰加焉豈可以一
槩而言哉方今
朝廷治理清明賢俊登用下之發身有由科目
嵗貢而明經術者有由賢勞報効而殫才力
者固非一方上之考察有三年朝覲而大明
黜陟者有諸道按治而細行糾繩者亦非一
法其所以杜僥倖防請謁誠如執事之所云
矣然而望塵奔走者猶未息鎮靜恬退者或
punctuated:
宥，殊不知揚雄專於媚世取寵，特名教之罪人也；韓愈急於救時行道，實天下之阿衡也。豈可以一例而論哉？唐介不以私書至京師，則擢以御史之職；王舉正不以私事干朝廷，則處以諫諍之司。不通問訊者，劉噐之也，而薦充舘職，非溫公急於親賢而何？不就廷試者，韓維也，而乞加甄錄，非溫公切於勸善而何？獎之若此，則恬退之風俗自將勃然而興起矣。然執事曰「伯夷、子陵之制行」，而遂疑恬退者之為庸，殊不知伯夷逺引潔身，其清奚擬焉？子陵高尚忘勢，其節孰加焉？豈可以一槩而言哉？
方今朝廷治理清明，賢俊登用。下之發身，有由科目嵗貢而明經術者，有由賢勞報効而殫才力者，固非一方。上之考察，有三年朝覲而大明黜陟者，有諸道按治而細行糾繩者，亦非一法。其所以杜僥倖、防請謁，誠如執事之所云矣。然而望塵奔走者猶未息，鎮靜恬退者或
translation_en:
…pardoned. You fail to recognize that Yang Xiong devoted himself to flattering his age and courting favor: he was simply an offender against the moral teaching. Han Yu, however, was intent on rescuing his age and putting the Way into practice: he was truly an Aheng—a minister like Yi Yin—for all under Heaven. How can the two be judged by the same standard? Tang Jie brought no private letters to the capital and was promoted to the post of censor; Wang Juzheng did not trouble the court with private affairs and was appointed to an office of remonstrance. Liu Qizhi did not exchange greetings and inquiries, yet Duke Wen recommended him for an appointment in the literary institutes. What was this if not Duke Wen’s eagerness to draw worthy men close? Han Wei did not attend the court examination, yet Duke Wen requested that he be considered for selection and appointment. What was this if not Duke Wen’s earnest desire to encourage goodness? With such rewards, a custom of quiet restraint and withdrawal from advancement would naturally flourish. Yet you speak of “the conduct of Bo Yi and Ziling” and consequently suspect that those who quietly withdraw are mediocre. You fail to recognize that Bo Yi withdrew far away to preserve his integrity: what could compare with his purity? Ziling held himself aloof and disregarded power: who could surpass his moral constancy? How can they be discussed in such sweeping terms?
At present, the court’s government is lucid and enlightened, and worthy and talented men are advanced to office. Among those below who enter official service, some demonstrate their mastery of the classics through the examinations and annual tribute recommendations; others devote their talents and strength to diligent service and effective work. There is certainly more than one avenue. Likewise, those above employ more than one method of evaluating officials: the triennial court audiences make decisions on dismissal and promotion abundantly clear, while inspections throughout the circuits apply detailed scrutiny and correction. The means used to prevent advancement through mere good fortune and to guard against solicitation are indeed as you have described. Nevertheless, those who rush about at the sight of the dust raised by the powerful have still not ceased, while those who remain composed and quietly refrain from seeking advancement may…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
未見盖由
聖德寬宏而趨利之徒未遭其懲創幾務叢脞而
守道之士未荷其顯揚耳今欲使士大夫盡
尚廉恥甘事恬退愚敢以明公二字為執事
獻焉盖明則克知厥若而賢否先見公則不
訖于威而取舍無私秉至明於未用之先持
至公於已用之後果奔競之妨賢者嚴法制
以屏斥之則左右前後莫非正人而朝無倖
位矣果恬退之有守者量才德而器使之則
===
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣而野無遺賢矣又何患
夫奔競之跡不絕禮讓之風不興治道不躋
於隆盛風化不趨於醇厚哉愚也以力捕風
以捷追影固知其無能也執事其教之乎
第三問
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批條達明白必曾用心於學詩者耶
同考試官教諭何批塲屋中有此崛強之文三復起敬
考試官教授劉批抑揚反覆足見作手
punctuated:
未見。盖由聖德寬宏，而趨利之徒未遭其懲創；幾務叢脞，而守道之士未荷其顯揚耳。今欲使士大夫盡尚廉恥，甘事恬退，愚敢以「明」「公」二字為執事獻焉。盖明則克知厥若，而賢否先見；公則不訖于威，而取舍無私。秉至明於未用之先，持至公於已用之後。果奔競之妨賢者，嚴法制以屏斥之，則左右前後莫非正人，而朝無倖位矣。果恬退之有守者，量才德而器使之，則萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣，而野無遺賢矣。又何患夫奔競之跡不絕，禮讓之風不興，治道不躋於隆盛，風化不趨於醇厚哉？愚也以力捕風，以捷追影，固知其無能也。執事其教之乎？

第三問
邵誠

同考試官教諭陳批：條達明白，必曾用心於學詩者耶？

同考試官教諭何批：塲屋中有此崛強之文，三復起敬。

考試官教授劉批：抑揚反覆，足見作手。
translation_en:
…have not been seen. This is simply because, while the imperial virtue is generous and magnanimous, those who pursue profit have not yet received punishment sufficient to deter them; and because, amid the confusion of affairs of state, men who uphold the Way have not yet been accorded recognition. If we now wish all scholar-officials to prize integrity and a sense of shame, and willingly remain tranquil and retiring, I venture to offer you two words: discernment and impartiality. With discernment, one can recognize what is appropriate and distinguish the worthy from the unworthy beforehand; with impartiality, one does not yield to power [?], and one's selections and rejections are free from private bias. Exercise the utmost discernment before appointing men, and maintain the utmost impartiality after appointing them. Where those who scramble for advancement truly obstruct the worthy, enforce strict laws to exclude them. Then those on every side will all be upright men, and no one at court will hold a position gained through undeserved favor. Where those who remain tranquil and retiring truly possess integrity, assess their abilities and virtue and employ them accordingly. Then the worthy men of all the lands will together be the emperor's servants, and no worthy man will remain overlooked outside office. Why, then, worry that the scramble for advancement will not cease, that a spirit of courtesy and deference will not arise, that government will not attain flourishing prosperity, or that moral influence and customs will not become pure and substantial? In my foolishness, I try to catch the wind by strength and chase shadows by speed; I certainly know that I lack the ability. Would you be so kind as to instruct me?

Third Question
Shao Cheng

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Well organized and clear: surely this is someone who has devoted himself to studying the Book of Poetry?”

Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “To find writing of such forceful independence in the examination hall! On reading it three times, I am moved to admiration.”

Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “Its shifts of emphasis and repeated examination of the subject amply reveal an accomplished writer.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭鄭批寫出三代漢魏政事風俗以見詩道升
降一篇古制掃盡陳言場中之作誰出其右
甞謂聲音與政通文章與時高下盖詩者有
韻之文也可以卜世道矣三代之時其政渾
渾其俗雅雅家詩書户禮樂雖婦人小子亦
能之焉故善有頌惡有懲一經孔子筆削昭
然如白日矣自三代之後周道不興王綱解
紐即分為戰國其政烈烈其俗乖乖重功利
輕死生則詩降而為之騷焉故氣傷之激詞
===
傷之放一經朱子校錄珍重如九鼎矣自戰
國而流於漢自漢而入於魏漢也其政逸逸
其俗魚魚魏也其政紛紛其俗靡靡故詩降
而為五言蘇李之作其五言之祖乎世道漸
降則聲文漸卑矣王通取漢魏之作以續詩
千載譏之則劉履何如人乃敢輯選詩以羽
翼風雅焉是必有所授歟姑以朱子之取屈
原者論之謂其行雖過於中庸謂其心皆本
於愛國則露才揚己怨懟激發乃戰國之士
punctuated:
考試官教諭鄭批：寫出三代漢魏政事風俗，以見詩道升降。一篇古制，掃盡陳言，場中之作誰出其右？

甞謂聲音與政通，文章與時高下。盖詩者，有韻之文也，可以卜世道矣。三代之時，其政渾渾，其俗雅雅，家詩書，户禮樂，雖婦人小子亦能之焉。故善有頌，惡有懲，一經孔子筆削，昭然如白日矣。自三代之後，周道不興，王綱解紐，即分為戰國。其政烈烈，其俗乖乖，重功利，輕死生，則詩降而為之騷焉。故氣傷之激，詞傷之放，一經朱子校錄，珍重如九鼎矣。自戰國而流於漢，自漢而入於魏。漢也，其政逸逸，其俗魚魚；魏也，其政紛紛，其俗靡靡。故詩降而為五言，蘇李之作，其五言之祖乎？世道漸降，則聲文漸卑矣。王通取漢魏之作以續詩，千載譏之，則劉履何如人，乃敢輯選詩以羽翼風雅焉？是必有所授歟？姑以朱子之取屈原者論之：謂其行雖過於中庸，謂其心皆本於愛國，則露才揚己，怨懟激發，乃戰國之士
translation_en:
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: He depicts the government and customs of the Three Dynasties, Han, and Wei to show the rise and decline of the poetic tradition. The whole composition follows an ancient form and sweeps away stale expressions. Among the works produced in the examination hall, whose could surpass it?

It has been said that sounds are connected with government, and that literary composition rises and falls with the times. Poetry is writing in rhyme; through it one can discern the condition of the age. During the Three Dynasties, government was simple and whole, and customs were refined. Every family cultivated the Poetry and Documents, and every household observed rites and music; even women and young children were versed in these things. Thus goodness received praise and evil received admonition. Once Confucius had edited and pruned these poems, their meaning shone as clearly as the sun.

After the Three Dynasties, the Way of Zhou ceased to flourish, the bonds of royal authority came undone, and the realm split into the Warring States. Government was harsh and customs discordant; people prized achievement and profit and held life and death cheap. Poetry consequently declined into the sao form. Its spirit suffered from excessive vehemence, and its language from excessive abandon. Yet once Master Zhu had collated and recorded these works, they were treasured like the Nine Tripods.

From the Warring States the tradition flowed into Han, and from Han it entered Wei. Under Han, government was easygoing and customs orderly; under Wei, government was confused and customs decadent. Poetry thus declined into five-character verse. Were not the works of Su and Li the forebears of five-character verse? As the condition of the age gradually declined, poetic sound and expression likewise became progressively lower. Wang Tong took works from Han and Wei to continue the Classic of Poetry, and for a thousand years people have criticized him. What sort of man, then, was Liu Lü, that he dared compile Selected Poems to support the Airs and Odes? Surely he must have had some authority for doing so?

Let us consider this provisionally in light of Master Zhu’s acceptance of Qu Yuan. He said that although Qu Yuan’s conduct went beyond the Mean, his heart was wholly rooted in love of his country. Thus his display of talent and self-promotion, his resentment and impassioned outbursts, were those of the men of the Warring States …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
故習耳雖集註有何不可焉至於其初志欲
附楚騷也則掇經史韻語採文選古詞所謂
根本既立枝葉敷榮人有所準則矣其續楚
騷也始於荀況之成相終於張橫渠呂與叔
之輈歌擬招所謂使游藝者反而求之則文
章有不足為矣若夫劉履之輯詩其補註也
不過竊取朱子註詩之法恊音聲疏字義有
比有興焉其補遺也不過因襲朱子附詩之
意採古詞掇史語自虞至晉焉他如續編始
===
於陳子昂之感遇終於朱子之感遇正如續
楚詞始成相而終擬招也嗟夫因人而成事
倣古以立言有志者不為矣今執事以劉履
之補註為問殆取其成前人未就之書闢後
輩學詩之徑雖然因集以觀人之用心因詩
以觀時之升降未必無補也謹對
第四問
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批讀此策至歸宿處足見有志有學之士也
punctuated:
故習耳，雖集註，有何不可焉？至於其初志欲附楚騷也，則掇經史韻語，採文選古詞，所謂根本既立，枝葉敷榮，人有所準則矣。其續楚騷也，始於荀況之成相，終於張橫渠、呂與叔之輈歌、擬招，所謂使游藝者反而求之，則文章有不足為矣。若夫劉履之輯詩，其補註也，不過竊取朱子註詩之法，恊音聲，疏字義，有比有興焉。其補遺也，不過因襲朱子附詩之意，採古詞，掇史語，自虞至晉焉。他如續編，始於陳子昂之感遇，終於朱子之感遇，正如續楚詞始成相而終擬招也。嗟夫！因人而成事，倣古以立言，有志者不為矣。今執事以劉履之補註為問，殆取其成前人未就之書，闢後輩學詩之徑。雖然，因集以觀人之用心，因詩以觀時之升降，未必無補也。謹對。

第四問
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批：讀此策至歸宿處，足見有志有學之士也。
translation_en:
…were merely the ingrained habits of men of the Warring States period. What objection, then, could there be to compiling and annotating his works? As for the original intention to append material to the Songs of Chu, rhymed passages were gathered from the classics and histories, and ancient poems selected from the Selections of Refined Literature (Wen xuan). This exemplifies the saying that, once the roots are established, the branches and leaves flourish: people thereby have a standard to follow. The sequel to the Songs of Chu begins with Xun Kuang’s Working Songs (Cheng xiang) and ends with Zhang Hengqu’s Shaft Song (Zhou ge) [?] and Lü Yushu’s Imitation of the Summons (Ni zhao). As the saying goes, if those who take their recreation in the arts are led to turn back and seek the source, literary composition alone will seem insufficient as a pursuit.

As for Liu Lü’s compilation of poetry, his Supplementary Annotations merely borrow Master Zhu’s method of annotating the Odes: harmonizing sounds, explaining the meanings of characters, and identifying comparison and evocative imagery. His Supplement of Omitted Pieces merely follows Master Zhu’s intention in appending poems: selecting ancient verses and gathering passages from the histories, from the age of Yu down to the Jin dynasty. His Sequel, likewise, begins with Chen Zi’ang’s Reflections on Encounters (Gan yu) and ends with Master Zhu’s Reflections on Encounters, just as the sequel to the Songs of Chu begins with Working Songs and ends with Imitation of the Summons.

Alas! Accomplishing something by relying on others and establishing one’s words by imitating the ancients are things a man of aspiration would not do. Now that you, honored examiners, have asked about Liu Lü’s Supplementary Annotations, you presumably value its completion of a book that earlier scholars left unfinished and its opening of a path for later students of poetry. Nevertheless, using the collection to discern the compiler’s intentions, and using its poems to discern the rise and decline of their times, may indeed be of some benefit. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Sun Sheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: Reading this policy essay through to its conclusion, one can clearly see that its author is a man of aspiration and learning.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭單批此策正欲觀學者見識二千人中知音
寥寥晚得此篇如獲拱璧千古之疑冰消雲散矣
考試官教授劉批破千古之疑明今日之務有許力量耶
考試官教諭鄭批有傾河倒峽之勢有揮金擲玉之才可重
嘗聞荀卿有曰齊之擊技不可以遇魏之武
卒魏之武卒不可以直秦之銳士秦之銳士
不可以當桓文之節制桓文之節制不可以
敵湯武之仁義仁義之師天下無敵焉今執
事將已往之成敗見問沿邊之海寇是憂愚
===
雖不敏敢不拾先正之緒餘以答萬一也蓋
兵者所以除殘暴掃不庭以建太平之基抑
强横守邊隅以保無疆之休真聖王之不得
已而用之也昔韓信自虜魏王豹以來請益
兵以擊趙威振天下燕趙膽落矣當時雖有
智者不能為之謀勇者不能為之敵而李左
車說趙王曰千里餽粮士有饑色樵蘇後爨
師不宿飽誠哉言爾既而曰井陘之道車不
得方軌騎不得成列行數百里粮食在後彼
punctuated:
同考試官教諭單批：此策正欲觀學者見識，二千人中知音寥寥，晚得此篇，如獲拱璧，千古之疑冰消雲散矣。
同考試官教諭鄭批有傾河倒峽之勢有揮金擲玉之才可重
translation_en: Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor, comments: “This policy question was intended precisely to reveal the candidates’ understanding and judgment. Among two thousand men, scarcely any grasped its meaning. Finding this essay late in the process was like obtaining a precious jade disc: doubts persisting through the ages dissolve like ice and disperse like clouds.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兵三萬絶其輜重可謂迂矣殊不知陷之死
地而後生置諸危地而後存此信之熟於兵
法也當其兩陣未交勝負未見乃令裨將傳
餐俟破趙會食則信之目中已無趙矣故信
拔趙幟背水陣皆所以陷死求生置亡求存
則陳餘烏得不斬趙王歇烏得不擒乎馬遷
輕信左車之策為之展轉發明遂令千載悔
不用其謀豈得謂之知兵乎若夫諸葛亮自
聞曹休之敗以來請出兵以擊魏漢賊不兩
===
立王業不偏安矣當時恩信行於中原威畧
震乎逺邇而魏平諷司馬懿曰公畏蜀如虎
柰天下笑何信哉言爾既而亮至郿懿乃曰
亮若出武功依山而東誠可為憂若西止五
丈原諸將則無事可謂譎矣殊不知出軍渭
南分兵屯田而亮為久駐之計也當時實畏
孔明出五丈原憚於逆擊乃為億料以安軍
士之心矣故亮統大軍入敵境皆所以圖成
討賊之功不復有退軍之志則懿安得不甘
punctuated:
兵三萬，絶其輜重，可謂迂矣。殊不知陷之死地而後生，置諸危地而後存，此信之熟於兵法也。當其兩陣未交，勝負未見，乃令裨將傳餐，俟破趙會食，則信之目中已無趙矣。故信拔趙幟、背水陣，皆所以陷死求生、置亡求存，則陳餘烏得不斬，趙王歇烏得不擒乎？馬遷輕信左車之策，為之展轉發明，遂令千載悔不用其謀，豈得謂之知兵乎？
若夫諸葛亮自聞曹休之敗以來，請出兵以擊魏，漢賊不兩立，王業不偏安矣。當時恩信行於中原，威畧震乎逺邇，而魏平諷司馬懿曰：「公畏蜀如虎，柰天下笑何？」信哉，言爾！既而亮至郿，懿乃曰：「亮若出武功，依山而東，誠可為憂；若西止五丈原，諸將則無事。」可謂譎矣！殊不知出軍渭南，分兵屯田，而亮為久駐之計也。當時實畏孔明出五丈原，憚於逆擊，乃為億料以安軍士之心矣。故亮統大軍入敵境，皆所以圖成討賊之功，不復有退軍之志，則懿安得不甘
translation_en:
… thirty thousand troops to cut off his baggage train: this may well be called an ill-conceived plan. It entirely overlooked the principle that men plunged into deadly ground will then find life, and those placed in peril will then survive. This was Han Xin’s mastery of military strategy. Before the two armies had engaged, when victory or defeat was still undecided, he ordered his subordinate generals to pass the word about the meal: they would dine together after defeating Zhao. Thus, in Xin’s eyes, Zhao already counted for nothing. Xin’s uprooting of Zhao’s banners and his deployment with his back to the river were all means of seeking life by plunging into death, and survival by courting destruction. How, then, could Chen Yu escape execution, or Xie, King of Zhao, escape capture? Ma Qian credulously accepted Li Zuoche’s strategy and elaborated its merits at length, thereby causing people for a thousand years to regret that the plan had not been used. Can he be called someone who understood warfare?
As for Zhuge Liang, after hearing of Cao Xiu’s defeat, he requested permission to send troops against Wei. The Han and the rebels could not coexist, nor could the imperial enterprise rest content with holding only part of the realm. At that time, his benevolence and trustworthiness prevailed throughout the Central Plain, and his military prestige and strategy awed people near and far. Wei Ping taunted Sima Yi, saying: “You fear Shu like a tiger. What will you do about the laughter of all under Heaven?” True indeed were those words! Later, when Liang reached Mei, Yi said: “If Liang advances through Wugong and moves east along the mountains, there will indeed be cause for concern. If he stops to the west at Wuzhangyuan, you generals will have nothing to attend to.” This may well be called disingenuous! It entirely overlooked Liang’s plan for a prolonged stay: he had moved his army south of the Wei River and assigned detachments to establish agricultural garrisons. In fact, Yi feared Kongming’s advance at Wuzhangyuan and shrank from meeting him in battle; he therefore offered conjectures to reassure his soldiers. Thus, Liang’s leading a great army into enemy territory was entirely directed toward accomplishing the defeat of the rebels; he no longer had any intention of withdrawing. How, then, could Yi fail to submit willingly …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
受巾幗之辱聞食簡而喜乎陳壽小児之見
以為短於將畧遂令當時信之而不疑豈得
謂之識兵乎方
今天下一家四海一人臣妾九夷梯航萬國浙江
沿海獨有海賊出沒可慮此亦螳蜋皷臂當
車蜉蝣奮力撼樹愚固知其無能為也但此
巡司弓兵有捍禦之責今乃僉自均徭是扶
鋤之農民當出沒之強横所謂不教而戰者
也守倭軍士有望瞭之勞今乃太半餘丁是
===
不賞之軍士臨不測之死地所謂救死不贍
者也二者既不得其理雖設武臣以總督之
憲臣以監臨之亦何為哉况屯田之法已廢
而軍士悉靠食於農存䘏之制不明而京儲
皆仰給於此民之所種之田有数天之所生
之財有限無恠其倉廒空虚而敵守可慮也
為今之計莫若舉古人截貢之典則倉廒實
而軍士有給矣行古人募役之法則捍禦熟
而海賊可守矣於乎世無韓信安可不慮其
punctuated:
受巾幗之辱，聞食簡而喜乎？陳壽小児之見，以為短於將畧，遂令當時信之而不疑，豈得謂之識兵乎？
方今天下一家，四海一人，臣妾九夷，梯航萬國。浙江沿海獨有海賊出沒可慮，此亦螳蜋皷臂當車，蜉蝣奮力撼樹，愚固知其無能為也。但此巡司弓兵有捍禦之責，今乃僉自均徭，是扶鋤之農民當出沒之強横，所謂不教而戰者也。守倭軍士有望瞭之勞，今乃太半餘丁，是不賞之軍士臨不測之死地，所謂救死不贍者也。二者既不得其理，雖設武臣以總督之，憲臣以監臨之，亦何為哉？况屯田之法已廢，而軍士悉靠食於農；存䘏之制不明，而京儲皆仰給於此。民之所種之田有数，天之所生之財有限，無恠其倉廒空虚而敵守可慮也。
為今之計，莫若舉古人截貢之典，則倉廒實而軍士有給矣；行古人募役之法，則捍禦熟而海賊可守矣。於乎！世無韓信，安可不慮其
translation_en:
…accept the humiliation of the women's headdress and rejoice on hearing that his opponent ate little? Chen Shou, with a child's understanding, judged him deficient in generalship, and thereby led people of his time to believe this without question. How could he be said to understand warfare?
Today, all under Heaven forms one family, and all within the Four Seas belongs to one ruler. The peoples of the Nine Yi submit as servants, and the myriad countries come by mountain paths and sea. Along the coast of Zhejiang alone, the appearance and disappearance of sea raiders gives cause for concern. Yet this is merely a mantis raising its forelegs to stop a carriage, or a mayfly exerting itself to shake a tree. In my humble view, I know well that they can accomplish nothing. Nevertheless, the archers of the Police Offices bear responsibility for defense, yet they are now conscripted through the equalized labor-service levy. This means setting farmers who wield hoes against violent men who appear and disappear at will: precisely what is meant by sending people into battle without training them. The soldiers defending against Japanese raiders bear the toil of keeping watch, yet more than half are now supplementary males from military households. This means placing unrewarded soldiers in situations where death may strike unpredictably: precisely what is meant by having insufficient means even to save oneself from death. Since neither arrangement accords with proper principles, what use is it to appoint military officials to command them and censorial officials to supervise them? Moreover, the system of military agricultural colonies has already been abandoned, and the soldiers depend entirely on farmers for their food. Provisions for relief and support are ill-defined, while the capital's reserves depend entirely on supplies from here. The land the people cultivate is finite, and the resources Heaven produces are limited. No wonder the granaries are empty and defense against the enemy gives cause for concern.
For present purposes, nothing would be better than reviving the ancient precedent of retaining tribute locally: the granaries would then be full and the soldiers supplied. Implement the ancient method of recruiting men for service, and the defenders would become proficient and the sea raiders could be held off. Alas! In an age without a Han Xin, how can we fail to worry about their …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
絕軍後之粮時無諸葛烏得不憂其乏久駐
之食愚生也晚頗有志於經綸得遇也遲慙
無補於世事惟進而教之
第五問
潘温
同考試官訓導顧批場中之作多為問目所窘及有善對者
而於事實又遺此作敷陳詳細鐵中錚錚非此子乎
同考試官教諭單批荅策貴使人讀之如親歷其事此作有焉
考試官教授劉批有斷制有收拾盖嘗用心於策學者乎
===
考試官教諭鄭批識時務者呼俊傑此策其庶幾乎
孟軻有曰禹思天下有溺者由已溺之也稷
思天下有飢者由已飢之也古之聖賢以身
任天下之重如此今執事以浙之旱澇下策
愚生是欲觀致用之學矣雖不敏安敢不罄
竭所抱負以對明問乎夫古者三年耕必有
一年之積九年耕必有三年之積以三十年
之通計則國用有餘旱澇不憂矣是以堯雖
有九年之水不能害堯之民湯雖有七年之
punctuated:
絕軍後之粮？時無諸葛，烏得不憂其乏久駐之食？愚生也晚，頗有志於經綸；得遇也遲，慙無補於世事。惟進而教之。

第五問
潘温

同考試官訓導顧批：場中之作，多為問目所窘；及有善對者，而於事實又遺。此作敷陳詳細，鐵中錚錚，非此子乎？

同考試官教諭單批：荅策貴使人讀之如親歷其事，此作有焉。

考試官教授劉批：有斷制，有收拾，盖嘗用心於策學者乎？

考試官教諭鄭批：識時務者呼俊傑，此策其庶幾乎？

孟軻有曰：「禹思天下有溺者，由已溺之也；稷思天下有飢者，由已飢之也。」古之聖賢，以身任天下之重如此。今執事以浙之旱澇下策愚生，是欲觀致用之學矣。雖不敏，安敢不罄竭所抱負，以對明問乎？夫古者三年耕，必有一年之積；九年耕，必有三年之積。以三十年之通計，則國用有餘，旱澇不憂矣。是以堯雖有九年之水，不能害堯之民；湯雖有七年之
translation_en:
…the cutting off of provisions at the army’s rear? With no Zhuge Liang in our time, how can we fail to worry about a shortage of food for a prolonged deployment? This humble student was born late, yet has some ambition to put the realm in order; my opportunity has come late, and I am ashamed to have contributed nothing to public affairs. I ask only that you encourage and instruct me.

Fifth Question
Pan Wen

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: Compositions in the examination hall are often constrained by the particulars of the question. Even those that answer well leave out factual details. This composition sets matters forth fully and precisely. Among pieces of iron, is this candidate not the one that rings clear?

Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: What is prized in answering a policy question is making readers feel as though they had personally experienced the matters discussed. This composition achieves that.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: It shows decisive judgment and brings its material to a coherent conclusion. Surely its author has devoted considerable attention to the study of policy essays?

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: One who understands the affairs of the time is called an outstanding talent [?]. Does this policy essay not come close to that standard?

Meng Ke said: “Yu thought that if anyone under Heaven drowned, it was as though he himself had drowned them; Ji thought that if anyone under Heaven went hungry, it was as though he himself had caused their hunger.” Such was the way the sages and worthies of antiquity personally shouldered responsibility for all under Heaven. Now you, honored examiners, have put a policy question concerning droughts and floods in Zhejiang to this humble student, wishing to examine my learning in its practical application. Though I am slow of understanding, how could I dare not set forth all that I hold within me in response to your illuminating question? In antiquity, three years of cultivation necessarily yielded one year’s reserves, and nine years of cultivation necessarily yielded three years’ reserves. Reckoned over thirty years as a whole, there was thus a surplus for the state’s needs, and droughts and floods gave no cause for anxiety. Thus, although Yao experienced nine years of flooding, it could not harm his people; and although Tang experienced seven years of…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
旱不能害湯之民信乎執事所謂書曰有備
無患傳曰凡事豫則立也且如浙江為東南
大藩
朝廷供需比之他處實為繁劇雖曰民素富庶
邀之者無窮地瀕江海生之者有限況比年
以来陰陽愆伏水旱相仍民居壞於海水泛
濫者比比皆是田禾枯於亢陽肆虐者往往
有之若以為感召而致歟則堯湯之聖必無
失德若以為氣化而然歟則人定之說可以
===
===
勝天故坐視民患不可專責於有司更置壇
壝亦不可輕違乎舊制況平日若無備灾之
蓄今日必無救灾之術盖備灾可以施於平
日救灾乃欲行於目前不亦難乎此所以不
能不勞執事之問也成周荒政具於典章若
散利薄征緩刑弛力之属舍禁去幾眚禮殺
哀之類莫非良策下此有恵於浙者陳堯佐
之發廩减直以濟貧范仲淹之聽民興造以
取給因時制宜何為不可行於今成周治水
punctuated:
旱，不能害湯之民。信乎，執事所謂《書》曰「有備無患」，《傳》曰「凡事豫則立」也。且如浙江為東南大藩，朝廷供需，比之他處，實為繁劇。雖曰民素富庶，邀之者無窮，地瀕江海，生之者有限。況比年以来，陰陽愆伏，水旱相仍，民居壞於海水泛濫者，比比皆是；田禾枯於亢陽肆虐者，往往有之。若以為感召而致歟，則堯湯之聖必無失德；若以為氣化而然歟，則人定之說可以勝天。故坐視民患，不可專責於有司；更置壇壝，亦不可輕違乎舊制。況平日若無備灾之蓄，今日必無救灾之術。盖備灾可以施於平日，救灾乃欲行於目前，不亦難乎？此所以不能不勞執事之問也。
成周荒政具於典章，若散利、薄征、緩刑、弛力之属，舍禁、去幾、眚禮、殺哀之類，莫非良策。下此有恵於浙者，陳堯佐之發廩减直以濟貧，范仲淹之聽民興造以取給，因時制宜，何為不可行於今？成周治水
translation_en:
…drought, yet it could not harm Tang’s people. True indeed are the sayings you cite: the Book of Documents says, “With preparation there is no calamity,” and the transmitted text says, “In all affairs, preparation ensures success.” Zhejiang is a great province of the southeast, and its obligations to supply the court are considerably more onerous and complex than those of other places. Although its people have long been prosperous and numerous, demands upon them are endless; although its lands border rivers and the sea, what they produce is limited. Moreover, in recent years yin and yang have fallen out of their proper seasonal order, and floods and droughts have followed one another. Homes destroyed by inundations of seawater are everywhere, and crops withered by the ravages of excessive heat are frequently seen. If these disasters are held to arise through moral influence calling forth a corresponding response, surely sages such as Yao and Tang could have had no failings in virtue. If they are held to result from transformations of vital forces, then there is the teaching that determined human effort can overcome Heaven. Thus, responsibility for standing by and watching the people suffer cannot be laid entirely upon the responsible officials; nor, in relocating altars and their precincts, may established regulations lightly be transgressed. Furthermore, if reserves against disaster have not been accumulated in ordinary times, there will surely be no means of relieving disaster today. Preparations against disaster can be made in ordinary times, but to seek to provide relief only when disaster is already upon us—is this not difficult? This is why you have been obliged to trouble yourself with this question.
The famine policies of the Zhou dynasty are fully recorded in its statutes and institutions. Such measures as distributing resources, reducing levies, relaxing punishments, and easing labor obligations, as well as lifting prohibitions, removing inspections, curtailing ritual observances, and reducing mourning requirements, are all excellent policies. In later times, among those who benefited Zhejiang were Chen Yaozuo, who opened the granaries and reduced grain prices to aid the poor, and Fan Zhongyan, who allowed the people to undertake construction so that they could obtain a livelihood. These measures adapted to circumstances and suited the needs of the time: why could they not be implemented today? As for water management under the Zhou dynasty…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
見於周官若營溝行水之法則職之匠人止
水蓄水之令則領之稻人罔非良政下此有
功於杭者則張夏作石堤以防江潮蘇軾浚
二河以免市淘臨機應變何為不可合於古
夫以今求古以古合今本人情宜土俗必為
長久之計可也比如浙東一帶地多高仰遇
旱則赤地千里束手待斃民患非細為今之
計貴乎預備賑卹而
朝廷固已行之久矣必欲民安其生何必他求
===
哉成周之荒政十二今可舉也陳堯佐范文
正之拳宜今可舉也兼是数者而施之於今
則雖遇旱而民不被其困矣浙西一帶地多
卑下遇澇則浸淫環数百里加以海濤吞吐
民患殊甚為今之計貴乎隄防浚治而
朝廷固已行之久矣必欲水無浸淫何必遠圖
哉成周治水之制今可行也張夏蘇軾之成
效今可行也兼是数者而師之於古則雖遇
澇而不能病吾民矣愚也學不足以稽古才
punctuated:
見於《周官》。若營溝行水之法，則職之匠人；止水蓄水之令，則領之稻人，罔非良政。下此有功於杭者，則張夏作石堤以防江潮，蘇軾浚二河以免市淘。臨機應變，何為不可合於古？夫以今求古，以古合今，本人情，宜土俗，必為長久之計可也。比如浙東一帶，地多高仰，遇旱則赤地千里，束手待斃，民患非細。為今之計，貴乎預備賑卹，而朝廷固已行之久矣。必欲民安其生，何必他求哉？成周之荒政十二，今可舉也；陳堯佐、范文正之拳宜，今可舉也。兼是数者而施之於今，則雖遇旱而民不被其困矣。

浙西一帶，地多卑下，遇澇則浸淫環数百里，加以海濤吞吐，民患殊甚。為今之計，貴乎隄防浚治，而朝廷固已行之久矣。必欲水無浸淫，何必遠圖哉？成周治水之制，今可行也；張夏、蘇軾之成效，今可行也。兼是数者而師之於古，則雖遇澇而不能病吾民矣。愚也，學不足以稽古，才
translation_en:
…is set out in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). Methods for laying out channels and conducting water were entrusted to the master craftsmen; orders for checking and storing water were administered by the rice-field officials. All were sound measures of government. In later times, those who rendered service to Hangzhou included Zhang Xia, who built stone embankments to ward off river tides, and Su Shi, who dredged two waterways to prevent the scouring of the city [?]. In responding to circumstances and adapting to change, why should we be unable to accord with antiquity? We should seek guidance from antiquity for the present and adapt ancient practices to present circumstances, grounding our measures in human needs and fitting them to local customs. We must devise plans that will endure.

For example, much of eastern Zhejiang lies on high ground. When drought strikes, the land lies barren for a thousand li, and people can only await death helplessly. Their suffering is no small matter. The essential measure today is to prepare relief in advance, and the court has indeed been doing this for a long time. If we wish the people to live securely, why seek elsewhere? The twelve famine-relief measures of the Zhou dynasty can be put into effect today; so too can the expedients [?] of Chen Yaozuo and Fan Wenzheng. By combining these measures and applying them today, we can ensure that even when drought strikes, the people will not suffer its hardships.

Much of western Zhejiang lies low. When flooding occurs, water spreads for several hundred li around; with the surging ebb and flow of the sea added to this, the people suffer exceedingly. The essential measures today are embankments and dredging, and the court has indeed been carrying these out for a long time. If we wish to prevent inundation, why seek plans far afield? The Zhou dynasty’s system of water management can be implemented today; the successful measures of Zhang Xia and Su Shi can likewise be implemented today. By combining these measures and taking antiquity as our guide, we can ensure that even when flooding occurs, it cannot afflict our people. My learning is insufficient to investigate antiquity, and my ability…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不足以通今管見如斯未知是否惟執事進而
教之幸甚
punctuated: 不足以通今。管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …my abilities are insufficient to comprehend present affairs. Such are my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. If you, honored examiners, would offer me further instruction, I would be most grateful.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
皇上登極十有三禩歲丁酉秋八月適
當大比浙之東西合十一郡就試
之士二千有奇先是巡按監察御
史佀鍾右布政使杜謙按察使戴
珙等合議以禮聘儒紳為考試官
至期鎖院圍棘三試之而得士九
===
十人焉遵定額也小錄既成僉謂
祥宜序其後於乎賢才者國之元
氣也元氣之運行天地間則日升
而月沉寒往而暑來與夫山峙川
流鳥飛獸走無不各奠其位各順
其性若或日月薄蝕寒暑失候山
濯而川洩胎殰而卵殈此乃元氣
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

皇上登極十有三禩，歲丁酉，秋八月，適當大比。浙之東西合十一郡，就試之士二千有奇。先是，巡按監察御史佀鍾、右布政使杜謙、按察使戴珙等，合議以禮聘儒紳為考試官。至期，鎖院圍棘，三試之而得士九十人焉，遵定額也。小錄既成，僉謂祥宜序其後。

於乎！賢才者，國之元氣也。元氣之運行天地間，則日升而月沉，寒往而暑來，與夫山峙川流、鳥飛獸走，無不各奠其位，各順其性。若或日月薄蝕，寒暑失候，山濯而川洩，胎殰而卵殈，此乃元氣
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the thirteenth year since His Majesty ascended the throne, the dingyou year [1477], in autumn, in the eighth month, the time came for the triennial examination. From the eleven prefectures of eastern and western Zhejiang combined, more than two thousand candidates presented themselves for examination. Before this, Regional Inspector Si Zhong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Du Qian, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Dai Gong, and others had jointly deliberated and formally invited Confucian scholars of the gentry to serve as Examiners. At the appointed time, the examination compound was locked and enclosed with thorn barriers. After three examination sessions, ninety men were selected, in accordance with the prescribed quota. Once this brief record was completed, all agreed that I, Xiang, should write its postface.

Ah! Worthy and talented men are the vital force of the state. When the vital force circulates between Heaven and Earth, the sun rises and the moon sinks, cold departs and heat arrives; mountains stand, rivers flow, birds fly, and beasts run. All are settled in their proper places and follow their respective natures. But should the sun and moon suffer eclipses, cold and heat lose their seasons, mountains become bare and rivers drain away, young die in the womb and eggs fail to hatch, this is the vital force…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之塞也人君用賢以理天下何以
異此故治教休明風俗淳美此即
賢才之進用如元氣之運而物各
得其所也若或政弛而令廢風偷
而俗薄此即賢才之未進如元氣
之塞而物各失其所也然上之求
賢以應用者固難而下之欲進以
匡時者亦難如成湯之舉伊尹文
===
王之舉呂望皆得於側微使二臣
之不遇亦終與草木同腐安能成
吊伐之功垂簡冊之譽故詩曰綿
綿之葛在於曠野良工得之以為
絺綌書曰萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣是
則有國家者不可不以求賢為先
punctuated: 之塞也。人君用賢以理天下，何以異此？故治教休明，風俗淳美，此即賢才之進用，如元氣之運而物各得其所也。若或政弛而令廢，風偷而俗薄，此即賢才之未進，如元氣之塞而物各失其所也。然上之求賢以應用者固難，而下之欲進以匡時者亦難。如成湯之舉伊尹，文王之舉呂望，皆得於側微。使二臣之不遇，亦終與草木同腐，安能成吊伐之功，垂簡冊之譽？故《詩》曰：「綿綿之葛，在於曠野。良工得之，以為絺綌。」《書》曰：「萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣。」是則有國家者，不可不以求賢為先。
translation_en:
…is the blockage of primordial vital energy. How is a ruler’s employment of worthy men to govern the realm any different? Thus, when government and moral instruction flourish brightly and customs are sincere and good, this results from the advancement and employment of worthy talent: it is like the circulation of primordial vital energy, through which all things find their proper place. If, however, government grows lax and commands fall into disuse, and customs become careless and shallow, this results from worthy talent not having been advanced: it is like the blockage of primordial vital energy, through which all things lose their proper place.

Yet while it is certainly difficult for those above to seek worthy men for service, it is also difficult for those below to gain advancement in order to set their age aright. When Cheng Tang raised Yi Yin to office and King Wen raised Lü Wang, both men were found in obscure and humble circumstances. Had these two ministers not met with recognition, they too would ultimately have rotted away with the grasses and trees. How could they have accomplished their work of comforting the afflicted and chastising the guilty, and left their renown in the historical records?

Thus the Book of Odes says: “The trailing kudzu vines grow in the open wilds. Skilled craftsmen obtain them and make fine and coarse cloth.” The Book of Documents says: “The many worthy men of the myriad states are all ministers of the sovereign.” Therefore, those who rule states and domains must make seeking worthy men their foremost concern.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
三皇之所以皇五帝之所以帝三
王之所以王悉由此道也故古者
諸侯貢士一適謂之好德再適謂
之賢賢三適謂之有功乃加九錫
不貢士一則黜爵再則黜地三則
黜爵地畢矣所以如斯者不過欲
求賢以培養其元氣賢才進而元
===
氣養則天下豈有不治也哉洪惟
我
朝滋培元氣長育賢才天地位而萬
物育百有餘年矣矧浙為東南大
藩名山巨川甲觀天下其賢才之
美亦復如是乃循例三年一大比
考其德行道藝而興賢者能者茍
punctuated:
三皇之所以皇，五帝之所以帝，三王之所以王，悉由此道也。故古者諸侯貢士，一適謂之好德，再適謂之賢賢，三適謂之有功，乃加九錫。不貢士，一則黜爵，再則黜地，三則黜爵地畢矣。所以如斯者，不過欲求賢以培養其元氣。賢才進而元氣養，則天下豈有不治也哉！
洪惟我朝滋培元氣，長育賢才，天地位而萬物育，百有餘年矣。矧浙為東南大藩，名山巨川甲觀天下，其賢才之美亦復如是。乃循例三年一大比，考其德行道藝，而興賢者能者。茍
translation_en:
The Three August Ones became august, the Five Emperors became emperors, and the Three Kings became kings—all through this way. Thus, in antiquity, when the feudal lords presented scholars, one suitable presentation was called “loving virtue”; a second suitable presentation was called “honoring the worthy”; and a third suitable presentation was called “rendering meritorious service,” whereupon the Nine Bestowals were conferred. For failing to present scholars, the first offense brought demotion in rank, the second a reduction of territory, and the third complete deprivation of rank and territory. The purpose of these measures was simply to seek worthy men and thereby nurture the realm’s vital force. When worthy talent advances and the vital force is nourished, how could All under Heaven fail to be well governed?
We reverently reflect that our dynasty has nurtured this vital force and fostered worthy talent: Heaven and Earth have occupied their proper places, and the myriad things have flourished, for more than a hundred years. Moreover, Zhejiang is a great province of the southeast. Its renowned mountains and mighty rivers offer sights foremost in the world, and its worthy talent is likewise outstanding. Accordingly, following established practice, a great examination is held every three years to assess men’s virtuous conduct and their learning in the Way and the arts, and to advance the worthy and capable. If …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
於取之之際而無姸媸之別則如
耳聞雷霆而稱為聰眼見日月而
稱為明是舉天下無有不聰明之
士也烏有是理哉况元氣有厚薄
萬物有散殊則賢才固自有高下
耳是以人之溫厚者其文必潤澤
人之剛愎者其文必峻厲人之侃
===
侃自處者其文必直而不迂人之
悻悻自是者其文必恠而不經傳
曰人之不良言之不祥也𠥼言而
求才𠥼才而致用𠥼用以覈名𠥼
名而責實則取賢之能事畢矣爾
諸士子登名是錄可不思所以自
盡也哉行將上春官對
punctuated:
於取之之際而無姸媸之別，則如耳聞雷霆而稱為聰，眼見日月而稱為明，是舉天下無有不聰明之士也，烏有是理哉？况元氣有厚薄，萬物有散殊，則賢才固自有高下耳。是以人之溫厚者，其文必潤澤；人之剛愎者，其文必峻厲；人之侃侃自處者，其文必直而不迂；人之悻悻自是者，其文必恠而不經。傳曰：「人之不良，言之不祥。」也𠥼言而求才，𠥼才而致用，𠥼用以覈名，𠥼名而責實，則取賢之能事畢矣。
爾諸士子登名是錄，可不思所以自盡也哉？行將上春官，對
translation_en:
…if no distinction between beauty and ugliness is made at the moment of selection, it is like calling someone keen of hearing because his ears hear thunder, or keen of sight because his eyes see the sun and moon. On that basis, there would be no scholar anywhere under Heaven who lacked keen hearing and sight. How could this be reasonable? Moreover, primordial vital energy varies in strength, and the myriad things differ from one another; worthy talents therefore naturally have their higher and lower grades. Thus, a person of gentle and generous disposition will inevitably write with richness and grace; a person who is headstrong and obstinate will inevitably write with severity and harshness; one who conducts himself with upright assurance will inevitably write directly, without circumlocution; and one who is resentful and self-righteous will inevitably write in a strange manner that departs from established norms. A transmitted text says: “When a person is not good, his words are inauspicious.” By words one seeks talent; by talent one brings people into service; by their service one tests their reputation; and by their reputation one demands actual achievement [?]. Then the work of selecting worthy men is fully accomplished.
You scholars whose names appear in this record—can you fail to consider how to exert yourselves to the utmost? Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites and respond …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大廷小者佐使弼治大者承宣輔理
期毋負有司貢士之意毋負主司
揀拔之心將見
國家之元氣愈厚而致治之德澤愈
深則天下謂某藩某科取士得人
而吾輩可以塞責矣
廣東肇慶府儒學教授安福劉秈
===
謹序
punctuated:
大廷，小者佐使弼治，大者承宣輔理，期毋負有司貢士之意，毋負主司揀拔之心。將見國家之元氣愈厚，而致治之德澤愈深，則天下謂某藩某科取士得人，而吾輩可以塞責矣。
廣東肇慶府儒學教授、安福劉秈謹序。
translation_en:
…at the imperial court. In lesser capacities, you will assist in service and support governance; in greater capacities, you will receive and promulgate imperial commands and assist in administration. Our hope is that you will not disappoint the authorities’ intentions in presenting worthy scholars, nor the chief examiners’ care in selecting you. We shall then see the vital strength of the state grow ever more robust, and the beneficent influence of good government deepen ever further. All under Heaven will say that this province, in this examination year, obtained worthy men through its selection of scholars, and we shall have discharged our responsibility.
Respectfully prefaced by Liu Xian 劉秈 of Anfu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhaoqing Prefecture, Guangdong.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
天地生物厚於人而賢則人之秀
者也自昔君臨天下克承
上天休命任人理物以保乂家邦未始
不由賢才衆多然後治功有成而
丕基永固也書曰天惟純佑命則
商實詩曰王國克生惟周之楨是
===
已仰惟
皇明統一寰區
聖聖御極歷百餘年多賢彙征布列中
外而庶績咸熈華夷綏服皆由
天眷純至錫賚賢俊而教養之有素選
舉之有法也乃成化丁酉值大比
興賢之秋浙江觀風臺憲暨藩臬
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序

天地生物，厚於人，而賢則人之秀者也。自昔君臨天下，克承上天休命，任人理物，以保乂家邦，未始不由賢才衆多，然後治功有成，而丕基永固也。《書》曰：「天惟純佑命，則商實。」《詩》曰：「王國克生，惟周之楨。」是已。

仰惟皇明統一寰區，聖聖御極，歷百餘年，多賢彙征，布列中外，而庶績咸熈，華夷綏服，皆由天眷純至，錫賚賢俊，而教養之有素，選舉之有法也。乃成化丁酉，值大比興賢之秋，浙江觀風臺憲暨藩臬
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In bringing forth living things, Heaven and Earth bestow particular favor upon humankind, and the worthy are the finest among human beings. From antiquity, rulers who have governed all under Heaven, successfully received august Heaven’s gracious mandate, appointed men and ordered affairs so as to preserve and govern their realms, have invariably depended upon an abundance of worthy talent. Only then could their work of government succeed and the great foundations of their rule remain secure forever. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven bestowed its wholehearted protection and mandate; thus Shang was filled with worthy men.” The Book of Odes says: “The royal kingdom could bring them forth; they were the pillars of Zhou.” This is precisely what these words mean.

We reverently consider how our august Ming unified the realm, and how sage sovereign after sage sovereign has occupied the throne for more than a hundred years. Many worthy men have advanced together into service, taking up posts both at court and in the provinces. Every undertaking has flourished, and Chinese and non-Chinese alike have been pacified and submitted. All this derives from Heaven’s wholehearted favor in bestowing worthy and outstanding men, together with longstanding provision for their education and nurture and established methods for their selection and appointment. Now, in the dingyou year of Chenghua [1477], when autumn brought the triennial great examination for raising worthy men to office, Zhejiang’s censorial officials charged with inspecting local conditions, together with its provincial administration and surveillance officials…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
重臣前期走幣聘教授劉祥為考
試官而華亦與焉學正胡淵教諭
楚綸何覲陳震單暠關銓訓導顧
宗義先楷為同考官主司文衡至期
合十一郡髦士抱藝操觚皷勇文
塲者二千有竒循例三試焉先其
未試也提督學校副使胡榮詢察
士之學行于庠序既而巡按監察
御史佀鍾復覈實之然後藩司具
名進諸棘院所以杜僥倖而禁奸
弊者嚴且密矣于時
欽差鎮守司設監太監李義巡塩監察
御史李介他若工部員外郎韓紳
亦有事於斯境相與勸勉振作以
punctuated: 重臣前期走幣聘教授劉祥為考試官，而華亦與焉。學正胡淵，教諭楚綸、何覲、陳震、單暠、關銓，訓導顧宗義、先楷為同考官，主司文衡。至期，合十一郡髦士抱藝操觚、皷勇文塲者二千有竒，循例三試焉。先其未試也，提督學校副使胡榮詢察士之學行于庠序；既而巡按監察御史佀鍾復覈實之，然後藩司具名進諸棘院。所以杜僥倖而禁奸弊者，嚴且密矣。于時，欽差鎮守司設監太監李義、巡塩監察御史李介，他若工部員外郎韓紳，亦有事於斯境，相與勸勉振作，以
translation_en:
…the high officials sent gifts in advance to invite Liu Xiang, a prefectural school instructor, to serve as Examiner, and I, Hua, also took part. Hu Yuan, a subprefectural school instructor; Chu Lun, He Jin, Chen Zhen, Shan Gao, and Guan Quan, county school instructors; and Gu Zongyi and Xian Kai, assistant instructors, served as Associate Examiners, jointly overseeing the assessment of literary merit. When the appointed time arrived, more than two thousand outstanding scholars from the eleven prefectures assembled, bringing their learning, taking up their writing tablets, and mustering their courage in the literary arena. In accordance with precedent, they underwent three examination sessions.

Before the examination, Hu Rong, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner serving as Superintendent of Schools, had investigated the candidates’ learning and conduct in their schools. Subsequently, Si Zhong, the Regional Inspecting Censor, verified these findings once more. Only then did the Provincial Administration Commission draw up the list of names and submit it to the examination compound. The measures for preventing unmerited success and prohibiting fraud and abuse were thus rigorous and thorough.

At this time, Li Yi, Grand Eunuch of the Directorate of Palace Accoutrements, imperially commissioned to serve as Regional Defender, and Li Jie, the Salt-inspecting Censor, as well as others such as Han Shen, Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, also had official business within this territory. Together they offered encouragement and spurred everyone to exert themselves, in order to…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
圖賛襄
當宁求賢盛典内而提調則右布政使
杜謙右叅議張敷華監試則按察使
戴珙僉事魏富外而綱維防範則
左叅政李田右叅政張寰李嗣副
使楊瑄端宏王齊左叅議盧雍右
叅議吳森僉事劉餘慶李瓛林僯吳
琠梁昉潘珪錢山以及凡百執事
靡不簡任得人恪恭厥職而御史
佀鍾寔監臨焉華等躬勤考校積
日逾旬披卷閱辭黜鄙倍抑恠詭
汰浮冗取其言之成文純雅中式
者九十名所以鑑別妍媸評品高
下者公且明矣故事列在院官屬
punctuated:
圖賛襄當宁求賢盛典。内而提調，則右布政使杜謙、右叅議張敷華；監試，則按察使戴珙、僉事魏富；外而綱維防範，則左叅政李田、右叅政張寰、李嗣，副使楊瑄、端宏、王齊，左叅議盧雍、右叅議吳森，僉事劉餘慶、李瓛、林僯、吳琠、梁昉、潘珪、錢山，以及凡百執事，靡不簡任得人，恪恭厥職。而御史佀鍾寔監臨焉。華等躬勤考校，積日逾旬，披卷閱辭，黜鄙倍，抑恠詭，汰浮冗，取其言之成文、純雅中式者九十名。所以鑑別妍媸、評品高下者，公且明矣。

故事，列在院官屬，
translation_en:
…to assist in the reigning Emperor’s grand undertaking of seeking worthy men. Within the examination compound, the Proctors were Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Du Qian and Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Fuhua; those overseeing the examination were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Dai Gong and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wei Fu. Outside, responsibility for maintaining order and taking precautions rested with Left Administration Vice Commissioner Li Tian; Right Administration Vice Commissioners Zhang Huan and Li Si; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Yang Xuan, Duan Hong, and Wang Qi; Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Lu Yong; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wu Sen; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Liu Yuqing, Li Huan, Lin Lin, Wu Tian, Liang Fang, Pan Gui, and Qian Shan. These and all the other functionaries were suitably selected for their appointments and performed their duties with reverent diligence. Censor Si Zhong served as Supervising Official.

Hua and his colleagues personally and diligently assessed the papers for more than ten days. They opened the scripts and examined their language, rejected the vulgar and perverse, disfavored the strange and outlandish, and eliminated the superficial and prolix. They selected ninety candidates whose writing formed coherent compositions, was pure and elegant, and met the prescribed standards. Their discrimination between fine and poor work and their assessment of relative merit were impartial and discerning.

According to established practice, the officials serving within the examination compound are listed…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第舉人氏名并刻文之粹者為小
錄以獻諸
御覽傳播四方焉華謹拜手稽首為
國家得賢賀用序諸首曰惟江浙東南
文物大藩湖山清峙海陸環衍士
生其間孕秀鍾靈接武賢科視他
邦尤勝茲逢
===
昭代亨嘉之運爾諸士子居養學校衣
冠絃誦服禮樂而泳詩書講明大
學之道固濟濟衆盛稱凡民之俊
秀矣一旦舒英吐秀刊名賢書觀
其典則條暢之為經義嚴整淵奧
之為表誥鋪張發越之為論䇿精
彩煥郁又言之秀而文者是以動
punctuated:
第舉人氏名，并刻文之粹者，為小錄以獻諸御覽，傳播四方焉。華謹拜手稽首，為國家得賢賀，用序諸首曰：
惟江浙，東南文物大藩，湖山清峙，海陸環衍。士生其間，孕秀鍾靈，接武賢科，視他邦尤勝。茲逢昭代亨嘉之運，爾諸士子居養學校，衣冠絃誦，服禮樂而泳詩書，講明大學之道，固濟濟衆盛，稱凡民之俊秀矣。一旦舒英吐秀，刊名賢書，觀其典則條暢之為經義，嚴整淵奧之為表誥，鋪張發越之為論䇿，精彩煥郁，又言之秀而文者，是以動
translation_en:
…arrange the names of the provincial graduates in order and have the finest of their compositions engraved for printing, making a brief record to submit for imperial inspection and circulate throughout the realm. I, Hua, reverently bow with clasped hands and knock my head to the ground, congratulating the state on obtaining worthy men. Accordingly, I place this preface at the beginning:
Jiangsu and Zhejiang constitute a great center of culture in the southeast, where lakes and mountains stand clear and lofty, and sea and land extend on every side. Scholars born here embody its beauty and concentrated spiritual vitality, following one another into the ranks of successful examination candidates in numbers surpassing those of other regions. Now, in this illustrious age of flourishing prosperity, you scholars have lived and been nurtured in the schools. Properly capped and robed, you have recited to the accompaniment of strings, practiced rites and music, immersed yourselves in the Odes and Documents, and studied and elucidated the Way of the Great Learning. Numerous and accomplished indeed, you merit the designation “the outstanding talents among the common people.” Once you display your gifts and reveal your excellence, your names are inscribed in the register of worthies. Consider your essays on the Classics, conforming to classical standards and lucidly ordered; your memorials and proclamations, rigorously structured and profound; and your discourses and policy essays, expansive and eloquent. Brilliant and richly expressive, these are also utterances of distinction and literary refinement. Thus they stir…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
人耳目振耀一時矣然秀而不實
聖師所歎行將會試禮闈進對
大廷荐躋祿位可不思所以充其實乎
必曰吾之進身敷奏以言耳言者
心之聲行之表言外也心内也言
末也行本也急於外而遺其内競
其末而棄其本豈務實乎盍反求
===
諸心主敬以存之寡欲以養之知
性以盡之使廣大高明廓然而大
公致謹其行非仁無為非義無行
非禮不動而動容周旋循蹈乎規
矩由是宅此心以明德則内能成
己推此心以新民則外能成物至
於調元賛化寅亮天工皆此心之
punctuated: 人耳目，振耀一時矣。然秀而不實，聖師所歎。行將會試禮闈，進對大廷，荐躋祿位，可不思所以充其實乎？必曰：「吾之進身敷奏，以言耳。」言者，心之聲，行之表。言外也，心内也；言末也，行本也。急於外而遺其内，競其末而棄其本，豈務實乎？盍反求諸心，主敬以存之，寡欲以養之，知性以盡之，使廣大高明，廓然而大公。致謹其行，非仁無為，非義無行，非禮不動，而動容周旋，循蹈乎規矩。由是宅此心以明德，則内能成己；推此心以新民，則外能成物。至於調元賛化，寅亮天工，皆此心之
translation_en:
…people’s eyes and ears, shining brilliantly in their day. Yet to flower without bearing fruit was something the Sage Teacher lamented. Soon you will take the Metropolitan Examination within the examination compound of the Ministry of Rites, advance to answer before the imperial court, and rise successively to salaried offices. Can you fail to consider how to give substance to your accomplishments? You will surely say: “It is through words alone that I advance into office and present my statements to the throne.” Words are the voice of the heart and the outward expression of conduct. Words are external; the heart is internal. Words are the branches; conduct is the root. If you press after the external and neglect the internal, compete over the branches and abandon the root, are you truly pursuing substance?

Why not turn back and seek it within your own hearts? Make reverent attentiveness your guiding principle to preserve the heart, diminish desires to nourish it, and understand your nature to realize it fully, making it broad and great, lofty and luminous, expansive and wholly impartial. Exercise the utmost care in your conduct: undertake nothing that is not humane, pursue nothing that is not righteous, and make no movement contrary to ritual propriety. In every bearing and movement, follow the proper standards. Thus, by grounding yourselves in this heart so as to manifest luminous virtue, you can inwardly perfect yourselves; by extending this heart so as to renew the people, you can outwardly bring others to fulfillment. As for harmonizing the primal forces and assisting the transforming work of creation, reverently aiding Heaven’s work—all these are this heart’s…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
實用行成乎邇則親和而家正行
孚乎遠則君正而國定民康乂而
天下平皆此行之實效天之厚我
以靈秀而同類蚩蚩同生芸芸皆
於我而使各遂其性實心普實行
順匪直虛言虛文而已秀之充實
有如是夫允哉其為有德之賢也
===
斯可無負上天生賢輔治之心
聖明養賢及民之意臺省諸臣舉賢報
國之忠而德業建于當時聲光垂于
永世
皇朝億萬年永保無疆佑命弼寧無疆
宗社亦將咸有賴焉名動一時奚足多
歟華忝預校文之末敢以是為諸
punctuated:
實用。行成乎邇，則親和而家正；行孚乎遠，則君正而國定，民康乂而天下平，皆此行之實效。天之厚我以靈秀，而同類蚩蚩，同生芸芸，皆於我而使各遂其性，實心普，實行順，匪直虛言虛文而已。秀之充實有如是夫！允哉，其為有德之賢也！
斯可無負上天生賢輔治之心、聖明養賢及民之意、臺省諸臣舉賢報國之忠，而德業建于當時，聲光垂于永世。皇朝億萬年永保無疆佑命，弼寧無疆宗社，亦將咸有賴焉。名動一時，奚足多歟？華忝預校文之末，敢以是為諸
translation_en:
…practical application. When conduct is perfected among those nearby, kin are harmonious and the family is properly ordered; when conduct wins trust among those far away, the ruler is upright and the state secure, the people enjoy well-being and good order, and all under Heaven is at peace. These are all the actual effects of such conduct. Heaven has generously endowed me with spiritual distinction; the untutored multitudes of my fellow humans and the teeming beings who share life with me all depend upon me [?] to enable each to fulfill its nature. A sincere heart extends universally, and genuine conduct accords with what is right—not merely empty words and empty compositions. Such is the fullness of cultivated excellence! Truly, such a person is a worthy possessed of virtue!
Only thus can one live up to Heaven’s purpose in bringing forth worthy men to assist in governance, the enlightened sovereign’s intention in nurturing worthy men so that benefits reach the people, and the loyalty of the officials of the Censorate and central administration in recommending worthy men to repay the state. Virtuous achievements will then be established in their own time, and their illustrious reputation will endure forever. The imperial dynasty’s perpetual preservation of Heaven’s boundless favor and mandate for countless millions of years, and the upholding and securing of its ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain for all time, will likewise depend upon this. What is so worthy of praise in a reputation that stirs only a single age? I, Hua, unworthily occupying a humble place among those evaluating the examination writings, venture to offer these words to the various…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄

賜進士江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教
諭莆田鄭華謹序
punctuated:
賢勸，循名責實，尚願有徵於茲云。
賜進士、江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭、莆田鄭華謹序。
translation_en:
…as encouragement to these worthy men. In holding them accountable for achievements commensurate with their reputations, I still hope to see this borne out in them.
Preface respectfully written by Zheng Hua of Putian, recipient of the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) degree and Instructor of the Confucian School of Luling County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi.
