title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
顏淵喟然歎曰仰之彌高鑽之彌堅瞻之
在前忽焉在後夫子循循然善誘人博
我以文約我以禮欲罷不能既竭吾才
如有所立卓爾雖欲從之末由也已
悠遠則博厚博厚則高明博厚所以載物
也高明所以覆物也悠久所以成物也
===
孔子聖之時者也孔子之謂集大成集大
成也者金聲而玉振之也金聲也者始
條理也玉振之也者終條理也始條理
者智之事也終條理者聖之事也智譬
則巧也聖譬則力也由射於百步之外
也其至爾力也其中非爾力也
易
聖人久於其道而天下化成
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

顏淵喟然歎曰：「仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅。瞻之在前，忽焉在後。夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮。欲罷不能，既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。雖欲從之，末由也已。」

悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。

孔子，聖之時者也。孔子之謂集大成。集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。金聲也者，始條理也；玉振之也者，終條理也。始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。

易

聖人久於其道，而天下化成。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: “The more I look up at it, the higher it rises; the more I bore into it, the harder it becomes. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind me. The Master skillfully guides people step by step. He broadens me through learning and restrains me through ritual. Even if I wished to stop, I could not. When I have exhausted my abilities, something seems to stand loftily before me. Though I wish to follow it, I have no way to do so.”

Enduring far into the distance brings breadth and depth; breadth and depth bring height and brilliance. Through breadth and depth, things are borne up; through height and brilliance, things are covered; through lasting endurance, things are brought to completion.

Confucius was the sage who acted according to the time. Confucius is said to have gathered together the great consummation. Gathering together the great consummation is like sounding the bronze bells and concluding with the jade chimes. The sounding of the bronze bells begins the ordered sequence; the sounding of the jade chimes completes it. Beginning the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; completing it is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength. It is like shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away: that the arrow reaches it is due to your strength; that it hits the mark is not due to your strength.

Book of Changes

The sage endures in his Way, and all under Heaven are transformed and brought to completion.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
父父子子兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正
正家而天下定矣象曰風自火出家人
君子以言有物而行有恒
是故蓍之德圓而神卦之德方以知六爻
之義易以貢聖人以此洗心退藏於密
吉凶與民同患神以知來知以藏往其
孰能與於此哉古之聰明叡知神武而
不殺者夫是以明於天之道而察於民
===
之故是興神物以前民用聖人以此齋
戒以神明其德夫是故闔戶謂之坤闢
戶謂之乾一闔一闢謂之變往來不窮
謂之通見乃謂之象形乃謂之器制而
用之謂之法利用出入民咸用之謂之
神
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖
人南面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此
punctuated:
父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、婦婦，而家道正；正家而天下定矣。象曰：「風自火出，家人；君子以言有物而行有恒。」

是故蓍之德圓而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明叡知、神武而不殺者夫！是以明於天之道，而察於民之故，是興神物以前民用。聖人以此齋戒，以神明其德夫！是故闔戶謂之坤，闢戶謂之乾，一闔一闢謂之變，往來不窮謂之通，見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此
translation_en:
When fathers act as fathers, sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, younger brothers as younger brothers, husbands as husbands, and wives as wives, the way of the family is properly ordered. Set the family in order, and all under Heaven will be settled. The Commentary on the Images says: “Wind issues from fire: this is Jiaren, the Family. Accordingly, the noble man gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.”

Thus the virtue of the milfoil stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and knowing; and the meanings of the six lines change to disclose their import. By these the sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into hidden depths, sharing the people’s concern over good and ill fortune. Through numinous insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores up what has passed. Who could attain to this? Surely those of antiquity who were perceptive, discerning, sagacious, and wise, whose martial power was numinous yet did not kill! Thus they understood the Way of Heaven and discerned the circumstances of the people, and so brought forth these numinous objects to guide the people’s undertakings. Through these the sage purifies himself and observes abstinence, thereby rendering his virtue numinous and luminous. Thus closing the door is called Kun, the Receptive; opening the door is called Qian, the Creative. One closing and one opening is called change; coming and going without end is called free passage. What becomes visible is called an image; what takes shape is called an implement. Fashioning things and putting them to use is called a method; making their use beneficial in coming and going, so that all the people employ them, is called numinous efficacy.

Li, the Clinging, means brightness. All things become visible to one another; it is the hexagram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven and turns toward the light to govern, evidently taking his model from this …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也坤也者地也萬物皆致養焉故曰致
役乎坤兌正秋也萬物之所說也故曰
說言乎兌
書
惟動丕應徯志
往盡乃心無康好逸豫乃其乂民
欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
予不允惟若茲誥予惟曰襄我二人汝有
===
合哉言曰在時二人天休滋至惟時二
人弗戡其汝克敬德明我俊民在讓後
人于丕時嗚呼篤棐時二人我式克至
于今日休我咸成文王功于不怠丕冒
海隅出日罔不率俾公曰君子不惠若
茲多誥予惟用閔于天越民
詩
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播□
punctuated:
也。坤也者，地也，萬物皆致養焉，故曰：「致役乎坤。」兌，正秋也，萬物之所說也，故曰：「說言乎兌。」

書
惟動丕應徯志。
往盡乃心，無康好逸豫，乃其乂民。
欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。
予不允惟若茲誥，予惟曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉！」言曰：「在時二人，天休滋至；惟時二人弗戡，其汝克敬德，明我俊民，在讓後人于丕時。嗚呼！篤棐時二人，我式克至于今日休。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。」公曰：「君子，不惠若茲多誥，予惟用閔于天越民。」

詩
晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯，亟其乘屋，其始播□
translation_en:
…indeed. Kun is earth: all things receive nourishment from it. Hence it is said, “They render service in Kun.” Dui is autumn at its height, when all things rejoice. Hence it is said, “They rejoice in Dui.”

Book of Documents
“Whenever you act, they will respond greatly, awaiting your intentions.”
“Go and devote your whole heart to your task. Do not settle into a love of ease and pleasure; then you will govern the people well.”
“We wish this to endure for ten thousand years: may the king’s sons and grandsons forever protect the people.”
“It is not merely to secure your trust that I admonish you thus [?]. I say only: ‘Let us two assist one another; will you join with me?’ I say: ‘While these two men remain, Heaven’s blessings will come in increasing abundance. Should these two men prove unequal to the task, may you reverently cultivate virtue, bring our men of outstanding ability to light, and pass on a great season of prosperity to those who follow. Ah! By faithfully assisting these two men, we have been able to attain the blessings of this day. Let us together complete King Wen’s work without flagging, extending its shelter to the shores of the sea and the place where the sun rises, so that none fail to follow and obey.’ The Duke said: ‘My lord, I take no pleasure in these many admonitions; I speak only out of concern for Heaven and the people.’”

Book of Odes
“By day you gather thatch; by night you twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roof, for you must begin sowing [illegible]…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
穀二之日鑿冰冲冲三之日納于凌陰
四之日其蚤獻羔祭韭
保兹天子生仲山甫仲山甫之德柔嘉維
則令儀令色小心翼翼古訓是式威儀
是力天子是若明命使賦王命仲山甫
式是百辟纘戎祖考王躬是保出納王
命王之喉舌賦政于外四方爰發
假以溢我我其收之駿惠我文王曾孫篤
===
之
有駜有駜駜彼乘黄夙夜在公在公明明
振振鷺鷺于下鼓咽咽醉言舞于胥樂
兮有駜有駜駜彼乘牡夙夜在公在公
飲酒振振鷺鷺于飛鼓咽咽醉言歸于
胥樂兮有駜有駜駜彼乘駽夙夜在公
在公載燕自今以始歲其有君子有穀
詒孫子于胥樂兮
punctuated:
穀。二之日，鑿冰冲冲；三之日，納于凌陰。四之日，其蚤獻羔祭韭。

保兹天子，生仲山甫。仲山甫之德，柔嘉維則；令儀令色，小心翼翼。古訓是式，威儀是力；天子是若，明命使賦。王命仲山甫：「式是百辟，纘戎祖考。王躬是保，出納王命。王之喉舌，賦政于外，四方爰發。」

假以溢我，我其收之。駿惠我文王，曾孫篤之。

有駜有駜，駜彼乘黄。夙夜在公，在公明明。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言舞，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘牡。夙夜在公，在公飲酒。振振鷺，鷺于飛。鼓咽咽，醉言歸，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘駽。夙夜在公，在公載燕。自今以始，歲其有。君子有穀，詒孫子，于胥樂兮！
translation_en:
…grain. In the second month, they hew the ice with resounding blows; in the third month, they place it in the icehouse. In the fourth month, early on, they offer a lamb and sacrifice with chives.

To protect this Son of Heaven, Heaven brought forth Zhong Shanfu. Zhong Shanfu’s virtue takes gentleness and goodness as its rule. His bearing is fine, his expression gracious; he is cautious and reverent. He models himself on ancient teachings and diligently maintains his dignified deportment. He obeys the Son of Heaven, whose clear commands charge him with distributing affairs of government. The king commands Zhong Shanfu: “Be a model for the many lords; carry on the work of your forefathers. Protect the king’s person; convey the king’s commands and report back to him. Be the king’s throat and tongue. Distribute the duties of government abroad, so that the four quarters are set in motion.”

Grant me abundance, and I shall receive it. Fully following our King Wen, may his great-grandson remain steadfast in his ways.

Strong and stout, strong and stout are those four yellow horses! Morning and night they attend at the duke’s court, attending there with tireless diligence. The egrets flock together; the egrets descend. The drums sound deep and full. Flushed with wine, they dance: together let us rejoice! Strong and stout, strong and stout are those four stallions! Morning and night they attend at the duke’s court, drinking wine at his court. The egrets flock together; the egrets fly. The drums sound deep and full. Flushed with wine, they return home: together let us rejoice! Strong and stout, strong and stout are those four dark horses flecked with white! Morning and night they attend at the duke’s court, feasting there. From this time onward, may each year bring a harvest! May the noble lord possess goodness and bequeath it to his descendants: together let us rejoice!

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛
侯曹伯伐鄭圍新城秋楚人圍許諸
侯遂救許〔僖公六年〕
諸侯會于扈〔文公十七年〕楚子鄭人侵陳遂侵宋
晉人宋人伐鄭〔並宣公元年〕宋華元帥師及
鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘晉人宋
人衛人陳人侵鄭〔並宣公二年〕晉侯使士匄
來聘杞伯來朝邾子來朝〔並成公十八年〕
公會單子晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯莒子邾
子齊世子光己未同盟于雞澤陳侯
使袁僑如會〔襄公三年〕
季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥
師會晉郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊
侯戰于鞌齊師敗績〔成公二年〕
陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮
punctuated:
春秋

盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕。夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。秋，楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許〔僖公六年〕。

諸侯會于扈〔文公十七年〕。楚子、鄭人侵陳，遂侵宋。晉人、宋人伐鄭〔並宣公元年〕。宋華元帥師及鄭公子歸生帥師戰于大棘。晉人、宋人、衛人、陳人侵鄭〔並宣公二年〕。晉侯使士匄來聘。杞伯來朝。邾子來朝〔並成公十八年〕。

公會單子、晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、莒子、邾子、齊世子光，己未，同盟于雞澤。陳侯使袁僑如會〔襄公三年〕。

季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌，齊師敗績〔成公二年〕。

陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕。鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮。
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

A covenant was concluded at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕 In summer, the Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng and besieging Xincheng. In autumn, the forces of Chu besieged Xu; the assembled lords thereupon went to Xu’s aid. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xi.〕

The lords met at Hu. 〔Seventeenth year of Duke Wen.〕 The Viscount of Chu and the forces of Zheng invaded Chen, then proceeded to invade Song. The forces of Jin and Song attacked Zheng. 〔Both entries: first year of Duke Xuan.〕 Hua Yuan of Song, commanding an army, fought at Daji against Prince Guisheng of Zheng, who also commanded an army. The forces of Jin, Song, Wei, and Chen invaded Zheng. 〔Both entries: second year of Duke Xuan.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a diplomatic visit to Lu. The Earl of Qi came to pay a court visit. The Viscount of Zhu came to pay a court visit. 〔All three entries: eighteenth year of Duke Cheng.〕

The Duke of Lu met with the Viscount of Shan, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi. On the jiwei day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Jize. The Marquis of Chen sent Yuan Qiao to attend the meeting. 〔Third year of Duke Xiang.〕

Jisun Xingfu, Zangsun Xu, Shusun Qiaoru, and Gongsun Yingqi commanded an army and joined Xi Ke of Jin, Sun Liangfu of Wei, and Prince Shou of Cao in fighting the Marquis of Qi at An. The army of Qi suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Second year of Duke Cheng.〕

The Marquis of Chen fled home. 〔Seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 The forces of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Prince Xie of Cai.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
〔襄公八年〕冬楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕晋侯
使士匄来聘〔襄公八年〕冬公會晋侯宋公
衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小
邾子齊世子光伐鄭十有二月己亥同
盟于戲〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥師伐吳〔昭公六年〕
秋公會劉子晋侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子
于平丘〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕齊侯
===
伐徐〔昭公十六年〕秋齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕
禮記
土工金工石工木工獸工草工典制六材
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢
而置之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因
地事地因名山升中于天因吉土以饗
帝于郊升中于天而鳳凰降龜龍假饗
帝于郊而風雨節寒暑時是故聖人南
punctuated:
〔襄公八年〕冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭。〔襄公八年〕晋侯使士匄来聘。〔襄公八年〕冬，公會晋侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥師伐吳。〔昭公六年〕秋，公會劉子、晋侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘。〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来。〔昭公十三年〕齊侯伐徐。〔昭公十六年〕秋，齊高發帥師伐莒。〔昭公十九年〕

《禮記》

土工、金工、石工、木工、獸工、草工，典制六材。

是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳凰降、龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節、寒暑時。是故聖人南
translation_en:
…〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In winter, Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng.〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a courtesy visit.〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 In winter, the duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi.〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 Wei Pi of Chu led an army to attack Wu.〔Sixth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, the duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu.〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 Wu destroyed Zhoulai.〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The Marquis of Qi attacked Xu.〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 In autumn, Gao Fa of Qi led an army to attack Ju.〔Nineteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

Workers in earth, metal, stone, wood, animal materials, and plant materials oversee the working of these six materials.

Thus, in antiquity, the former kings esteemed those possessing virtue, honored those possessing the Way, entrusted responsibilities to the capable, and selected worthy men and installed them in office. They assembled the multitude and solemnly charged them. Thus they relied on Heaven to serve Heaven, and on Earth to serve Earth. At renowned mountains they presented to Heaven an account of their accomplishments, and on auspicious ground they offered sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburban rite. When they presented their accomplishments to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they offered sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburban rite, wind and rain were duly regulated, and cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Thus the sage, facing south…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
面而立而天下大治
王者功成作樂治定制禮其功大者其樂
備其治辯者其禮具干戚之舞非備樂
也孰亨而祀非達禮也五帝殊時不相
沿樂三王異世不相襲禮樂極則憂禮
粗則偏矣及夫敦樂而無憂禮備而不
偏者其唯大聖乎
賓再拜受主人般還曰辟主人阼階上拜
===
送賓般還曰辟
第貳塲
論
明王以孝治天下
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表
punctuated:
面而立，而天下大治。
王者功成作樂，治定制禮。其功大者，其樂備；其治辯者，其禮具。干戚之舞，非備樂也；孰亨而祀，非達禮也。五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異世，不相襲禮。樂極則憂，禮粗則偏矣。及夫敦樂而無憂，禮備而不偏者，其唯大聖乎！
賓再拜受，主人般還曰辟。主人阼階上拜送，賓般還曰辟。
第貳塲
論
明王以孝治天下。
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢令郡國求遺賢詔。
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥。
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表。
translation_en:
… stands facing south, and all under Heaven is brought into good order.
When a king has accomplished his work, he creates music; when his government is established, he institutes rites. The greater his achievements, the more complete his music; the more differentiated his governance, the more fully furnished his rites. A dance with shields and battle-axes does not constitute the entirety of music; offering cooked food in sacrifice does not encompass the whole of ritual. The Five Emperors lived at different times and did not perpetuate one another’s music; the Three Kings belonged to different ages and did not copy one another’s rites. Music carried to excess brings sorrow; rites that are crude become one-sided. As for cultivating music without sorrow and making rites complete without one-sidedness, could anyone but a great sage accomplish this?
The guest bows twice and receives the offering. The host turns aside: this is called ‘making way.’ The host bows from the top of the eastern steps as he presents the offering; the guest turns aside: this is called ‘making way.’
Second Session
Discourse
The enlightened king governs all under Heaven through filial piety.
Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of a Han emperor ordering the commanderies and kingdoms to seek out worthy men who have been overlooked.
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Han Yu Vice Minister of Personnel.
Compose a memorial of thanks in which the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education leads the students in expressing gratitude for an increase in the bamboo and wooden offering vessels and the ranks of dancers used in sacrifices to Confucius.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
判語五條
隱匿費用稅粮課物
公差人貟欺陵長官
公使人等索借馬疋
監守自盜倉庫錢粮
有司官吏不住公廨
第叁場
策五道
問自古帝王之治天下必有洪謨大訓以
昭鑒萬世如我
太祖高皇帝之大誥
太宗文皇帝之為善陰騭以及
列聖垂統頒煥典章光同日月其與仲尼所纘
述易書詩春秋禮樂之言果有同歟否
歟夫讀典謨而潜思堯舜之聖德頌
制書而遠想
punctuated:
判語五條
隱匿費用稅粮課物。公差人貟欺陵長官。公使人等索借馬疋。監守自盜倉庫錢粮。有司官吏不住公廨。
第叁場
策五道
問：自古帝王之治天下，必有洪謨大訓，以昭鑒萬世。如我太祖高皇帝之《大誥》、太宗文皇帝之《為善陰騭》，以及列聖垂統，頒煥典章，光同日月，其與仲尼所纘述《易》《書》《詩》《春秋》《禮》《樂》之言，果有同歟？否歟？夫讀典謨而潜思堯舜之聖德，頌制書而遠想……
translation_en:
Five legal-judgment topics
Concealing or expending tax grain and goods collected as levies.
Personnel dispatched on official business bullying or insulting senior officials.
Persons on official missions demanding horses on loan.
Custodians themselves stealing money or grain from the storehouses under their charge.
Officials and clerks of local administrative offices failing to reside in their official quarters.

Third Session
Five policy questions
Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings governing All Under Heaven have invariably established grand plans and great instructions to serve as shining guides for all ages. Examples include the Grand Pronouncements of our Emperor Taizu Gao and Good Deeds and Hidden Blessings of Emperor Taizong Wen, as well as the successive sage emperors’ transmission of the imperial legacy and promulgation of splendid statutes and institutions, whose brilliance equals that of the sun and moon. Are these indeed in accord with the words of the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites, and Music that Zhongni compiled and transmitted, or are they not? Reading the Canons and Counsels, one reflects deeply upon the sagely virtue of Yao and Shun; reciting imperial decrees, one turns one’s thoughts back to …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之神功亦臣子之所當講也且如延曆數
所以紀年如漢如唐或遇災祥而輒改
今則紀一元而終始創廟宇所以祀神
如宋如元或加美號而過諂今則立木
主以正名至於前代宫室多施繪畫今
乃命侍臣以大學衍義書於兩廡者其
意果安在歟自古人君多好馳騁今乃
命畫工以經歷艱難繪於圖冊者其心
===
果何為歟他如定歷代名臣從祀帝王
廟庭所去者誰氏所增者何官俱可得
而詳言之歟爾諸士子沐浴
聖化亦有年矣今應賓興而来宜鋪張萬世之
宏規揚厲無前之偉績庶使後生晚學
有如親覩焉幸毋讓
問治道隆替風化醇漓係乎賢才之進退
而賢才之進其要在乎抑奔競獎恬退
punctuated:
祖宗之神功，亦臣子之所當講也。且如延曆數，所以紀年，如漢如唐，或遇災祥而輒改；今則紀一元而終始。創廟宇，所以祀神，如宋如元，或加美號而過諂；今則立木主以正名。至於前代宫室多施繪畫，今乃命侍臣以《大學衍義》書於兩廡者，其意果安在歟？自古人君多好馳騁，今乃命畫工以經歷艱難繪於圖冊者，其心果何為歟？他如定歷代名臣從祀帝王廟庭，所去者誰氏，所增者何官，俱可得而詳言之歟？爾諸士子沐浴聖化亦有年矣，今應賓興而来，宜鋪張萬世之宏規，揚厲無前之偉績，庶使後生晚學有如親覩焉。幸毋讓！

問：治道隆替，風化醇漓，係乎賢才之進退；而賢才之進，其要在乎抑奔競、獎恬退。
translation_en:
…the wondrous achievements of the imperial ancestors: these, too, are matters that subjects ought to study and discuss. Consider, for example, the continuation of calendrical reckoning [?], by which years are recorded. Under the Han and Tang, reign titles were sometimes changed whenever calamities or auspicious signs appeared; now a single reign title is used from beginning to end. Temples are established to offer sacrifices to the gods. Under the Song and Yuan, splendid titles were sometimes conferred upon them with excessive flattery; now wooden spirit tablets are erected to rectify their names. As for the palaces of preceding dynasties, these were extensively adorned with paintings; now attendant officials have instead been commanded to inscribe the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) in the two side galleries. What precisely is the intention behind this? From antiquity, rulers have often delighted in riding at full gallop; now painters have instead been commanded to depict experiences of hardship in illustrated albums. What precisely is the purpose behind this? Further, in determining which eminent ministers of successive dynasties should receive subsidiary sacrifices in the precincts of the Temple of Emperors, which men were removed, and what offices did those added hold? Can you explain all these matters in detail? You candidates have long been nurtured by the sage ruler’s transforming influence. Now that you have come in response to the summons for the selection of worthy men, you should expound the grand designs that will endure for ten thousand generations and extol achievements without precedent, so that younger scholars and later students may feel as though they had witnessed them in person. Do not hold back!

Question: The flourishing or decline of governance, and the integrity or corruption of customs, depend upon the advancement or dismissal of worthy and talented men. The key to advancing such men lies in curbing competitive pursuit of office and encouraging those who remain contentedly withdrawn…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而已考之於古若玉堂獻記不入翰苑
河平獻頌不留蘭臺兩及相門則却以
素定一謁大資則却以不求所以抑奔
競也然以名世大儒而甘有美新之作
後學山斗而三上宰相之書豈奔競不
足鄙歟不以私書至京師則擢之御史
不以私事干朝廷則處之諫諍有不就
廷試者遷除監學有不肯自陳者薦充
===
館職所以獎恬退也然以首陽逸民無
裨於邦家之治桐江高節有乖於君臣
之倫豈恬退不足尚歟方今
朝廷治理清明登用賢俊選舉有方考察有
法所以杜僥倖防請謁至矣盡矣然而
望塵奔趨者猶未息鎮靜恬退者或未
見不知其故安在茲欲使士大夫盡尚
廉耻甘事恬退絶夫奔競之跡藹然禮
punctuated: 而已。考之於古，若玉堂獻記，不入翰苑；河平獻頌，不留蘭臺；兩及相門，則却以素定；一謁大資，則却以不求：所以抑奔競也。然以名世大儒，而甘有美新之作；後學山斗，而三上宰相之書：豈奔競不足鄙歟？不以私書至京師，則擢之御史；不以私事干朝廷，則處之諫諍；有不就廷試者，遷除監學；有不肯自陳者，薦充館職：所以獎恬退也。然以首陽逸民，無裨於邦家之治；桐江高節，有乖於君臣之倫：豈恬退不足尚歟？方今朝廷治理清明，登用賢俊，選舉有方，考察有法，所以杜僥倖、防請謁，至矣，盡矣。然而望塵奔趨者猶未息，鎮靜恬退者或未見，不知其故安在？茲欲使士大夫盡尚廉耻，甘事恬退，絶夫奔競之跡，藹然禮
translation_en:
…and nothing more. Examining precedents from antiquity, we find that one who presented a record concerning the Jade Hall was not admitted to the Hanlin Academy, and one who presented a eulogy during the Heping era was not retained in the Orchid Terrace. One who twice visited a chief councillor’s gate was rebuffed on the grounds that the decision had already been settled; another who paid a single visit to a Grand Academician (dazi) was rebuffed on the grounds that office should not be sought. These were ways of curbing competitive pursuit of advancement. Yet an eminent Confucian scholar renowned in his age willingly composed In Praise of the Xin, while a man whom later scholars revered as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper submitted letters to the chief councillor three times. Could it be that competitive pursuit of advancement does not deserve contempt?

One who brought no private letters to the capital was promoted to censor; one who did not trouble the court with private affairs was appointed to a remonstrance post. Someone who declined to sit the court examination was promoted and appointed to supervise education; someone unwilling to put forward his own claims was recommended for an academy post. These were ways of rewarding quiet withdrawal. Yet the recluses of Shouyang contributed nothing to the governance of the realm, while the lofty integrity of the recluse of Tongjiang ran counter to the proper relationship between ruler and subject. Could it be that quiet withdrawal does not deserve esteem?

Today the court’s government is clear and enlightened. It advances the worthy and talented, follows proper procedures in selection, and has established rules for evaluating officials. Its measures to bar advancement through undeserved good fortune and prevent solicitation of favors are thorough and complete. Yet those who rush forward at the sight of the dust raised by the powerful have still not ceased, while those who remain composed and quietly withdraw are perhaps nowhere to be seen. Where does the cause lie? We now wish to have all scholar-officials esteem integrity and a sense of shame, willingly practice quiet withdrawal, and put an end to every trace of competitive pursuit of advancement, so that ritual propriety may flourish…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讓之風以驗
聖明治道之隆風化之醇不知何道而可爾諸
士子涵薰有年抱負而来必有其說願
著于篇
問自孔子刪詩三百篇之後即為楚辭視
風雅已一變矣又下而為漢魏之五言
則詩再變矣然三百篇經聖人所筆削
善惡昭彰以示勸懲楚辭則經朱子所
===
校錄亦取其發於性情為人臣子不得
於君父者讀之亦可以發其抑鬱無聊
之態厥後劉坦之輯選詩補註謂其可
以羽翼風雅焉夫楚辭作於屈原雖曰
南國宗之為辭賦之祖然其跌蕩怪神
怨懟激發醇儒莊士或羞稱之朱子果
何為之集註耶又欲掇經史韻語及文
選古詞附于詩楚辭之後果何旨耶其
punctuated:
讓之風，以驗聖明治道之隆、風化之醇，不知何道而可？爾諸士子涵薰有年，抱負而来，必有其說，願著于篇。
問：自孔子刪詩三百篇之後，即為楚辭，視風雅已一變矣。又下而為漢魏之五言，則詩再變矣。然三百篇經聖人所筆削，善惡昭彰，以示勸懲。楚辭則經朱子所校錄，亦取其發於性情，為人臣子不得於君父者，讀之亦可以發其抑鬱無聊之態。厥後劉坦之輯選詩補註，謂其可以羽翼風雅焉。夫楚辭作於屈原，雖曰南國宗之，為辭賦之祖，然其跌蕩怪神、怨懟激發，醇儒莊士或羞稱之。朱子果何為之集註耶？又欲掇經史韻語及文選古詞，附于詩、楚辭之後，果何旨耶？其
translation_en:
…a spirit of deference, thereby demonstrating the flourishing governance and pure moral influence of our sagely and enlightened ruler: by what means might this be achieved? You candidates have received this nurturing influence for years and come with learning and aspirations. You must have something to say; please set it down in writing.
Question: After Confucius edited the three hundred poems of the Book of Odes, there followed the Songs of Chu (Chu ci), already a transformation from the Airs and Elegantiae. Later still came the five-character poetry of the Han and Wei, marking a second transformation of poetry. Yet the three hundred poems underwent the Sage’s editing, clearly revealing good and evil to encourage virtue and warn against wrongdoing. The Songs of Chu were collated and recorded by Master Zhu, who likewise valued their expression of human nature and feelings. Those who, as subjects or sons, fail to find favor with their rulers or fathers can read them to give expression to their melancholy and desolation. Subsequently, Liu Tanzhi [?] compiled Supplementary Annotations to Selected Poems, saying that these poems could serve as a complement to the Airs and Elegantiae. Now, the Songs of Chu originated with Qu Yuan. Although it is said that the southern lands revered him as the progenitor of lyric poetry and rhapsody, his unrestrained flights, strange spirits, resentment, and vehement outbursts have made some orthodox Confucians and sober-minded scholars ashamed to speak of him. Why, then, did Master Zhu compile collected annotations to these works? Moreover, he wished to gather rhymed passages from the classics and histories, together with ancient verses from the Selections of Refined Literature (Wen xuan), and append them to the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu. What exactly was his intention? His…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
續楚辭也始之於成相終之以鞠歌擬
招其意何在至於補註也其立法之意
亦有得於朱子註詩及楚辭之意歟其
補遺也抑又有得於朱子抄經史韻語
文選古詩附于詩楚□之後之意歟他
如續編集之始終其與楚辭後語成相
擬招之意同歟否歟不學詩無以言聖
人之訓也爾多士必有能言之者幸明
===
以告我毋多讓焉
問兵凶器也聖人不得已而用之然有文
事者必有武備亦君子之所當講焉姑
舉一二已往者論其成敗且以見今日
之事亦有可憂者焉昔韓信之破趙而
李左車說陳餘曰信下井陘其勢粮食
必在後假竒兵三萬絶其輜重此取勝
之策也千載悔其謀之不用若然則拔
punctuated:
續楚辭也，始之於成相，終之以鞠歌、擬招，其意何在？至於補註也，其立法之意，亦有得於朱子註詩及楚辭之意歟？其補遺也，抑又有得於朱子抄經史韻語、文選古詩附于詩、楚□之後之意歟？他如續編集之始終，其與楚辭後語成相、擬招之意同歟否歟？「不學詩，無以言」，聖人之訓也。爾多士必有能言之者，幸明以告我，毋多讓焉。
問：兵，凶器也，聖人不得已而用之。然有文事者必有武備，亦君子之所當講焉。姑舉一二已往者，論其成敗，且以見今日之事亦有可憂者焉。昔韓信之破趙，而李左車說陳餘曰：「信下井陘，其勢粮食必在後，假竒兵三萬，絶其輜重。」此取勝之策也，千載悔其謀之不用。若然，則拔
translation_en:
…In continuing the Songs of Chu, what was his intention in beginning with “Cheng xiang” (Accompanying the Pestle) and ending with “Ju ge” (Song of the Ball) and “Ni zhao” (Imitation Summons)? As for the Supplementary Commentary, did the principles on which it was organized likewise reflect an understanding of Zhu Xi’s intentions in annotating the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu? In supplying omissions, did it also reflect an understanding of Zhu Xi’s intention in copying out rhymed passages from the classics and histories, together with ancient poems from the Selections of Refined Literature, and appending them to the Book of Odes and the Songs of Chu [one character illegible]? Again, did the choice of beginning and ending for the continuation embody the same intention as the placement of “Accompanying the Pestle” and “Imitation Summons” in the Later Words on the Songs of Chu, or not? “Unless you study the Odes, you will have no means of speaking”: this is the Sage’s instruction. Among you many scholars there must be those able to speak on this. Kindly explain it clearly to me, without excessive modesty.
Question: Weapons are instruments of ill omen; the sage uses them only when compelled. Yet those engaged in civil affairs must also maintain military preparedness. This too is something the gentleman ought to study. Let us take one or two instances from the past and discuss their successes and failures, thereby also revealing matters in our own day that warrant concern. When Han Xin defeated Zhao, Li Zuoche urged Chen Yu: “When Xin comes down through Jingxing, the circumstances dictate that his provisions must be behind him. Lend me thirty thousand troops for a surprise operation, and I shall cut off his baggage train.” This was a strategy for victory; for a thousand years people have regretted that his plan was not adopted. If so, then pulling out…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
赤幟於趙壁背綿水而為陣豈必賴井
陘而後可以成功耶是必有一說也諸
葛亮之伐魏而司馬懿謂諸將曰亮若
出武功依山而東誠為可憂若西止五
丈原諸將可以無事也當時信其說而
不疑若然則遺巾幗而必怒知食簡而
不喜豈必在出武功而後可以威敵耶
是必有一論也方今浙江東北沿海延
===
袤數千里海賊出没
朝廷深以為慮既設武臣以總督之又設憲
臣以監臨之然巡司弓兵僉自均徭守
倭軍士太半餘丁兼以邊海倉廒多半
空虚萬一有警敵之既無人守之又無
粮若何而可也爾諸士俱負窮經致用
之學可酌古準今條陳長治久安之策
以俟
punctuated: 赤幟於趙壁，背綿水而為陣，豈必賴井陘而後可以成功耶？是必有一說也。諸葛亮之伐魏，而司馬懿謂諸將曰：「亮若出武功，依山而東，誠為可憂；若西止五丈原，諸將可以無事也。」當時信其說而不疑。若然，則遺巾幗而必怒，知食簡而不喜，豈必在出武功而後可以威敵耶？是必有一論也。方今浙江東北沿海，延袤數千里，海賊出没，朝廷深以為慮。既設武臣以總督之，又設憲臣以監臨之。然巡司弓兵僉自均徭，守倭軍士太半餘丁，兼以邊海倉廒多半空虚。萬一有警，敵之既無人，守之又無粮，若何而可也？爾諸士俱負窮經致用之學，可酌古準今，條陳長治久安之策，以俟
translation_en:
…red banners at Zhao’s ramparts, and drawing up a battle formation with the Mian River at his back—did success necessarily depend upon Jingxing? There must be an explanation for this. When Zhuge Liang attacked Wei, Sima Yi told his generals: “If Liang advances through Wugong and moves east along the mountains, there will indeed be cause for concern. If he halts to the west at Wuzhangyuan, you generals will have nothing to trouble you.” At the time, his words were believed without question. If so, then sending women’s head coverings would surely provoke anger, while learning that his meals were meager brought no joy [?]. Did intimidating the enemy necessarily depend upon advancing through Wugong? There must be an argument to explain this.

Today, Zhejiang’s northeastern seaboard extends for several thousand li, and maritime bandits appear and disappear along it. The court is deeply concerned. It has appointed military officials to exercise overall command and censorial officials to supervise them. Yet the archers of the Police Offices are levied through the equalized corvée system, and more than half the soldiers defending against Japanese raiders are supernumerary males from military households. Moreover, most coastal granaries stand empty. Should an alarm arise, there would be neither men to resist the enemy nor grain to sustain the defense. How can this be acceptable? All you candidates possess learning devoted to thoroughly investigating the classics and putting them into practice. Consider ancient precedents in light of present circumstances, and set forth, point by point, policies for lasting order and enduring peace, to await…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上問而發焉
問旱澇之災雖堯湯之世所不免也說者
謂彼災自災耳於堯湯之民無損焉書
曰有備無患傳曰凡事豫則立此之謂
歟浙為東南大藩民素富庶地瀕江海
比年以来陰陽愆伏水旱相仍浹旬淫
雨海水泛溢而一河兩岸民居之壞於
蕩析者在在有之經月不雨旱魃為虐
而東疇西畞禾稼之傷於枯槁者比比皆
是將欲委諸氣化歟則所司坐視之咎
有所歸將欲變置壇壝歟則
朝廷擅易之禁無敢任於斯二者日展轉往
来於心思焉此救災禦患所宜講也矧
備災易救災難攷之成周有救荒之政
可詳其目歟亦有治水之制可悉其實
歟他如後世或發廩减直以濟貧或聽
punctuated:
上問而發焉。

問：旱澇之災，雖堯湯之世所不免也。說者謂彼災自災耳，於堯湯之民無損焉。《書》曰：「有備無患。」《傳》曰：「凡事豫則立。」此之謂歟？浙為東南大藩，民素富庶，地瀕江海。比年以来，陰陽愆伏，水旱相仍。浹旬淫雨，海水泛溢，而一河兩岸，民居之壞於蕩析者，在在有之；經月不雨，旱魃為虐，而東疇西畞，禾稼之傷於枯槁者，比比皆是。將欲委諸氣化歟？則所司坐視之咎有所歸。將欲變置壇壝歟？則朝廷擅易之禁，無敢任。於斯二者，日展轉往来於心思焉。此救災禦患所宜講也。矧備災易，救災難。攷之成周，有救荒之政，可詳其目歟？亦有治水之制，可悉其實歟？他如後世，或發廩减直以濟貧，或聽
translation_en:
…and set them forth when questioned by His Majesty.

Question: Disasters of drought and flooding could not be avoided even in the ages of Yao and Tang. Commentators say that those disasters were merely disasters and did no harm to the people of Yao and Tang. The Book of Documents says, “With preparation, there is no calamity.” The Record of Rites says, “In all things, preparation ensures success.” Is this what these sayings mean?

Zhejiang is a great province of the southeast. Its people have long been prosperous and numerous, and its lands border the rivers and the sea. In recent years, yin and yang have departed from their proper courses, and floods and droughts have followed one another. When relentless rain continues for ten days, seawater overflows, and everywhere along both banks of a river people's dwellings are swept away and destroyed. When no rain falls for a month, the drought demon wreaks havoc, and throughout the fields to east and west, crops wither and perish.

Should we attribute all this to the transformations of nature? Then responsibility for standing idly by would fall upon the officials in charge. Should we alter the arrangement of the ritual altars and their enclosures? Yet the court prohibits unauthorized alterations, and no one dares undertake them. Between these two alternatives, our thoughts turn back and forth each day. These are matters that must be discussed in considering disaster relief and protection against calamity. Moreover, preparing for disaster is easy; relieving it is difficult.

Examining the flourishing Zhou dynasty, we find policies for famine relief: can you explain their provisions in detail? There were also institutions for water control: can you give a full account of their actual operation? As for later ages, some opened granaries and reduced grain prices to aid the poor, while others permitted…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
民興造以取給均有惠於浙者參之古
果有合歟或作石堤以防江潮或浚二
河以免市淘均有功於杭者行於今抑
克濟歟夫事不師古無以善於今徒便
諸今無以合於古諸生齎所蘊而来其
參酌古今務宜民情以合土俗我將採
其可行者轉而語之所司
punctuated: 民興造以取給，均有惠於浙者，參之古，果有合歟？或作石堤以防江潮，或浚二河以免市淘，均有功於杭者，行於今，抑克濟歟？夫事不師古，無以善於今；徒便諸今，無以合於古。諸生齎所蘊而来，其參酌古今，務宜民情，以合土俗。我將採其可行者，轉而語之所司。
translation_en: …the people to undertake construction work to earn their livelihood—measures that all benefited Zhejiang: when compared with ancient practice, did they indeed accord with it? Some built stone embankments to hold back the river tides; others dredged the two canals to prevent the scouring of the city [?]. These measures all benefited Hangzhou, but if implemented today, could they prove effective? In undertaking affairs, without taking antiquity as our model, we cannot act well in the present; by seeking only present convenience, we cannot accord with antiquity. You candidates have come bearing the learning you have accumulated. Weigh ancient and present practices together, taking care to suit the circumstances of the people and accord with local customs. I shall select those proposals that can be implemented and convey them to the responsible officials.

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
四書
顏淵喟然嘆曰仰之彌高鑽之彌堅瞻之在前
忽焉在後夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約
我以禮欲罷不能既竭吾才如有所立卓爾
雖欲從之末由也已
潘温
同考試官教諭單批〔塲中作此題者多牽率一中字講甚不快人此篇發明顏子學聖人處不馳不驟有學有見佳作也〕
同考試官訓導顧批〔行文條暢命意光明一結尤見學力可取〕
===
考試官教授劉批〔說顏子歸功聖人處三復讀之作意煥然〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔此作周旋曲折殆繪畫然可謂善作者也〕
大賢嘆聖道之高妙必述其教之有序與學之所
至也蓋聖道高妙未易學也大賢因其教之有序
而學之有得是宜發嘆而歸功於聖人也歟昔顏
子學既有得無上事而喟然嘆曰我游夫子之門
學夫子之道以為高而可及耶則仰彌高而不可
及以為堅而可入耶則鑽彌堅而不可入何無窮
盡也從容以求之瞻之若在吾前勇猛以進之忽
punctuated:
四書

顏淵喟然嘆曰：「仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅，瞻之在前，忽焉在後。夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮，欲罷不能。既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。雖欲從之，末由也已。」

潘温

同考試官教諭單批〔塲中作此題者，多牽率一中字講，甚不快人。此篇發明顏子學聖人處，不馳不驟，有學有見，佳作也。〕

同考試官訓導顧批〔行文條暢，命意光明，一結尤見學力，可取。〕

考試官教授劉批〔說顏子歸功聖人處，三復讀之，作意煥然。〕

考試官教諭鄭批〔此作周旋曲折，殆繪畫然，可謂善作者也。〕

大賢嘆聖道之高妙，必述其教之有序與學之所至也。蓋聖道高妙，未易學也。大賢因其教之有序，而學之有得，是宜發嘆而歸功於聖人也歟！昔顏子學既有得，無上事，而喟然嘆曰：「我游夫子之門，學夫子之道，以為高而可及耶？則仰彌高而不可及；以為堅而可入耶？則鑽彌堅而不可入。何無窮盡也！從容以求之，瞻之若在吾前；勇猛以進之，忽
translation_en:
Four Books

Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: “The more I look up to it, the higher it becomes; the more I bore into it, the harder it becomes. I look for it ahead, and suddenly it is behind. The Master skillfully guides people step by step. He broadens me through learning and restrains me through ritual. Though I wish to stop, I cannot. Having exhausted my abilities, I seem to see something standing loftily before me. Though I wish to follow it, I have no means of doing so.”

Pan Wen

Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: 〔Many candidates writing on this topic in the examination hall strained to explain it through the single character zhong, “the mean” [?], which is most unsatisfying. This essay elucidates how Master Yan learned from the sage, neither rushing nor hurrying. It shows both learning and insight: an excellent composition.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: 〔The writing is orderly and fluent, and its conception clear and luminous. The conclusion especially reveals the strength of the author’s learning. It merits selection.〕

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: 〔In explaining how Master Yan credited the sage for his achievement, the author’s conception shines forth when one reads it repeatedly.〕

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔The turns and intricacies of this composition are almost like a painting. Its author may indeed be called an accomplished writer.〕

When the great worthy marveled at the loftiness and subtlety of the sage’s Way, he necessarily described both the ordered progression of the sage’s teaching and the point his own learning had reached. For the sage’s Way is lofty and subtle, and is not easily learned. Through the ordered progression of the sage’s teaching, the great worthy attained something in his learning. Was it not fitting, then, that he should sigh in admiration and credit the sage for his achievement?

Formerly, Master Yan, having attained something in his learning, had no higher undertaking [?], and sighed deeply, saying: “I have studied at the Master’s gate and learned the Master’s Way. Do I suppose it lofty yet attainable? The more I look up to it, the higher it becomes, beyond my reach. Do I suppose it hard yet penetrable? The more I bore into it, the harder it becomes, beyond my power to penetrate. How inexhaustible it is! When I seek it calmly, it seems to be before me; when I advance toward it with courage and vigor, suddenly …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
焉又在吾後何無方體也夫子之道雖曰高妙其
教人也循循善誘先博我以文使我致知而為入
道之門然後約我以禮使我力行以為進道之路
教之有序如此故我從事於斯悅之之深自不容
已而吾才之既竭味之之至自不能止而吾力之
已盡由是向之高堅者今則如有卓立於吾前向
之前後者今則如見卓爾於吾目然見之雖親造
之尤難欲致知以從之歟夫子生而知也博文之
功將安施乎欲力行以從之歟夫子安而行也約
===
禮之功將安用乎吁顏子學既有得述其先難之
故後得之由而歸功於聖人如此其可謂深知聖
人而善學之者矣大抵顏子之知鄰於生知顏子
之行幾於安行其未至於卓爾之地者守之也非
化之也假之以年則不日而化矣何卓爾之不可
造乎奈何賢哉之稱方興喪予之嘆即繼惜哉
悠遠則博厚博厚則高明博厚所以載物也高
明所以覆物也悠久所以成物也
劉湜
punctuated:
焉又在吾後，何無方體也！夫子之道雖曰高妙，其教人也循循善誘，先博我以文，使我致知而為入道之門，然後約我以禮，使我力行以為進道之路。教之有序如此，故我從事於斯，悅之之深，自不容已，而吾才之既竭；味之之至，自不能止，而吾力之已盡。由是向之高堅者，今則如有卓立於吾前；向之前後者，今則如見卓爾於吾目。然見之雖親，造之尤難。欲致知以從之歟？夫子生而知也，博文之功將安施乎？欲力行以從之歟？夫子安而行也，約禮之功將安用乎？吁！顏子學既有得，述其先難之故、後得之由，而歸功於聖人如此，其可謂深知聖人而善學之者矣。大抵顏子之知鄰於生知，顏子之行幾於安行，其未至於卓爾之地者，守之也，非化之也。假之以年，則不日而化矣，何卓爾之不可造乎？奈何「賢哉」之稱方興，「喪予」之嘆即繼，惜哉！

悠遠則博厚，博厚則高明。博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。

劉湜
translation_en:
…yet again it is behind me. How it eludes any fixed form! Though the Master's Way is lofty and subtle, in teaching others he skillfully guides them step by step. First he broadens me through cultural learning, enabling me to extend my knowledge as the gateway to entering the Way. Then he restrains me through ritual, enabling me to practice earnestly as the path to advancing in the Way. Such is the orderly sequence of his teaching. Thus, as I devote myself to this, my delight is so deep that I cannot desist, though I have exhausted my abilities; my savoring of it is so complete that I cannot stop, though I have spent all my strength. What formerly seemed lofty and hard now seems to stand towering before me; what formerly appeared now ahead, now behind, now seems to stand distinctly before my eyes. Yet although I see it intimately, attaining it is especially difficult. Shall I extend my knowledge to follow him? The Master was born knowing: where, then, could the effort of broadening my cultural learning be applied? Shall I practice earnestly to follow him? The Master acts with ease: what use, then, could there be for the effort of restraining myself through ritual?

Ah! Having gained something through learning, Master Yan explained the reasons for his earlier difficulties and the means of his subsequent attainment, attributing the achievement to the sage in this way. He may indeed be called one who deeply understood the sage and knew well how to learn from him. In general, Master Yan's knowledge approached innate knowledge, and his conduct came close to effortless practice. That he had not yet reached that towering height was because he still maintained his hold upon the Way, rather than having been transformed by it. Had he been granted more years, he would soon have undergone that transformation. Why should that towering height have been beyond his attainment? Alas, scarcely had the praise, “How worthy!” arisen when the lament, “Heaven has bereft me!” followed. What a pity!

“Extending far and long, it becomes broad and substantial; broad and substantial, it becomes lofty and luminous. Breadth and substantiality are what sustain all things; loftiness and luminosity are what cover all things; enduring constancy is what brings all things to completion.”

Liu Shi 劉湜

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導顧批此篇有銷叙有發明場中似此不多見焉
同考試官教諭楚批中庸一題場中作者多拘拘如鶴處雞
籠局促不舒此作其氣騫騰其文暢達高薦無疑
考試官教授劉批體認真確不疾不徐佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批此作能發明聖人功業與天地同用可取
中庸論聖人功業極其盛故能與天地同其用也
盖功業之盛實德之著見也向非積久而益盛何
能與天地同其用也哉中庸二十六章發明天道
如此謂夫有至誠無息之盛德斯發而為至誠無
===
息之功業自其功業之悠遠者言之蕩蕩乎寛大
無促迫也穆穆乎廣遠無終窮也惟悠遠故其積
也漸仁摩義施及中國廣博而深厚焉惟博厚故
其發也巍乎成功煥乎文章高大而光明焉此實
德之著見積久而益盛也如此故其博厚之積也
奠群生於教養之區與地之所以載萬物者同其
用高明之發也囿萬類於畢照之下與天之所以
覆萬物者同其功至其博厚而悠久也無一物之
被其澤豈
不得其所高明而悠久也無一物之不
punctuated:
同考試官訓導顧批：此篇有銷叙，有發明，場中似此不多見焉。
同考試官教諭楚批：中庸一題，場中作者多拘拘，如鶴處雞籠，局促不舒。此作其氣騫騰，其文暢達，高薦無疑。
考試官教授劉批：體認真確，不疾不徐，佳作也。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作能發明聖人功業與天地同用，可取。
《中庸》論聖人功業極其盛，故能與天地同其用也。盖功業之盛，實德之著見也。向非積久而益盛，何能與天地同其用也哉？《中庸》二十六章發明天道如此，謂夫有至誠無息之盛德，斯發而為至誠無息之功業。自其功業之悠遠者言之，蕩蕩乎寛大無促迫也，穆穆乎廣遠無終窮也。惟悠遠，故其積也，漸仁摩義，施及中國，廣博而深厚焉。惟博厚，故其發也，巍乎成功，煥乎文章，高大而光明焉。此實德之著見，積久而益盛也如此。故其博厚之積也，奠群生於教養之區，與地之所以載萬物者同其用；高明之發也，囿萬類於畢照之下，與天之所以覆萬物者同其功。至其博厚而悠久也，無一物之被其澤，豈不得其所？高明而悠久也，無一物之不
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor, comments: This essay offers exposition [?] and elucidation; few comparable works are to be found among the examination essays.
Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor, comments: On this topic from the Doctrine of the Mean, most candidates write constrainedly, like cranes confined in chicken coops, cramped and unable to stretch themselves. This essay's spirit soars, and its writing flows freely. I have no hesitation in recommending it highly.
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: Its understanding is sound and precise, its pace neither hurried nor slow. A fine essay.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: This essay elucidates how the sage's achievements perform the same function as Heaven and Earth. It merits acceptance.
The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the supreme flourishing of the sage's achievements, through which he can perform the same function as Heaven and Earth. The flourishing of these achievements is the visible manifestation of his genuine virtue. Unless they had accumulated over a long time and grown ever more abundant, how could they perform the same function as Heaven and Earth? Chapter Twenty-Six of the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the Way of Heaven in these terms: when there is abundant virtue of utmost sincerity that never ceases, it issues in achievements of utmost sincerity that never cease.
Speaking of the enduring and far-reaching character of these achievements, they are vast—expansive and free of constraint; they are majestic—extending far and wide without limit. Precisely because they endure and reach far, their accumulation imbues people with benevolence and shapes them through righteousness, extending throughout the Central Realm and becoming broad and deep. Precisely because they are broad and deep, their manifestation is lofty in accomplished deeds and brilliant in cultural forms, becoming high and luminous. Such is the visible manifestation of genuine virtue, accumulating over time and flourishing ever more abundantly.
Thus, in their broad and deep accumulation, they establish all living people within a realm of instruction and nurture, performing the same function as Earth in bearing the myriad things. In their lofty and luminous manifestation, they encompass all kinds of beings within an all-embracing illumination, accomplishing the same work as Heaven in covering the myriad things. When their breadth and depth also endure, there is not a single thing that receives their beneficence—could it fail to attain its proper place? [?] When their height and luminosity also endure, there is not a single thing that does not …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不與天地同一成物之妙乎是其本以悠遠致高
厚而高厚又悠久也聖人至誠功業何其盛哉大
抵誠之為道有以天而言者眞實無妄自然而然
也有以人而言者未能眞實無妄而欲其眞實無
妄者也此章之論正以推明前章天道之意其所
積而成者乃其實德著見功效氣象之謂非謂在
己之德亦待積而後成也故章末引文王之事以
證之夫豈積累漸次之謂哉學者詳之
孔子聖之時者也孔子之謂集大成集大成也
===
者金聲而玉振之也金聲也者始條理也玉
振之也者終條理也始條理者智之事也終
條理者聖之事也智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
由射於百步之外也其至爾力也其中非爾
力也
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批孟子一題場中俱能鋪叙求其能將樂之
始終射之巧力發明孔子聖之時中僅見此篇
同考試官教諭何批能以時字通貫一章深合題意
punctuated:
不與天地同一成物之妙乎？是其本以悠遠致高厚，而高厚又悠久也。聖人至誠功業何其盛哉！大抵誠之為道，有以天而言者，眞實無妄，自然而然也；有以人而言者，未能眞實無妄，而欲其眞實無妄者也。此章之論，正以推明前章天道之意。其所積而成者，乃其實德著見功效氣象之謂，非謂在己之德亦待積而後成也。故章末引文王之事以證之，夫豈積累漸次之謂哉？學者詳之。
孔子，聖之時者也。孔子之謂集大成。集大成也者，金聲而玉振之也。金聲也者，始條理也；玉振之也者，終條理也。始條理者，智之事也；終條理者，聖之事也。智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批：孟子一題，場中俱能鋪叙，求其能將樂之始終、射之巧力發明孔子聖之時中，僅見此篇。
同考試官教諭何批：能以時字通貫一章，深合題意。
translation_en:
…does it not share with Heaven and Earth the same wondrous capacity to bring things to fulfillment? Thus, through its enduring reach, its foundation attains height and depth; and this height and depth are themselves everlasting. How flourishing are the achievements of the sage’s utmost sincerity! Broadly speaking, sincerity as a Way may be discussed in terms of Heaven: it is genuine and without falsity, naturally so of itself. It may also be discussed in terms of human beings: they have not yet become genuine and without falsity, but seek to become so. The argument of this chapter serves precisely to elucidate the preceding chapter’s meaning concerning the Way of Heaven. What it describes as taking shape through accumulation is the efficacy and manifest character of the sage’s substantial virtue as it becomes evident; it does not mean that the virtue within him must likewise await accumulation before it is complete. Hence the chapter concludes by citing King Wen’s deeds as evidence. How could this refer to gradual, successive accumulation? Students should examine this carefully.
“Confucius was the sage who acted according to the time. Confucius may be said to have gathered together the great culmination. Gathering together the great culmination is like sounding the bronze bells and concluding with the jade chimes. Sounding the bronze bells begins the ordered sequence; sounding the jade chimes completes it. Beginning the ordered sequence is the work of wisdom; completing it is the work of sagehood. Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength. It is like shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away: reaching it is due to your strength; hitting the mark is not due to your strength.”
Shao Cheng.
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “On this question from the Mencius, all the candidates could give an exposition. But if one seeks an essay that uses the beginning and ending of music, and the skill and strength of archery, to illuminate how Confucius’s sagehood attained the mean appropriate to the time, this is the only one I have seen.”
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “It succeeds in using the word ‘time’ to unify the entire chapter and accords deeply with the meaning of the topic.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批融會傳註發明透徹真作手也
考試官教諭鄭批此作不窘滯不放肆可采
大賢論聖人具時中之道既即樂以見其聖智之
全復即射以明夫聖智之義蓋孔子之聖聖而時
中者也自非大賢即樂與射以著明之又何以見
其兼三子之聖而為一大聖也哉昔孟子之意謂
夫夷聖於清而不足於尹之任孔子可仕則仕可
止則止兼清與任而時出之焉尹聖於任而不足
於惠之和孔子可久則久可速則速兼任與和而
時出之焉夫孔子集三聖之事而為一大聖之事
如此不猶作樂者集衆音之小成而為一大成乎
集大成也者蓋於其樂之未作而先擊鎛鐘以宣
其聲俟其樂之既闋而後擊特磬以收其韻金以
宣之則八音翕然並奏而脉絡不紊此始條理也
玉以收之則八音詘然皆止而脉絡通貫此終條
理也始條理者猶孔子知無不盡非智之事乎終
條理者猶孔子德無不全非聖之事乎然聖智之
事如此而聖智之義何如是故以智言之譬則射
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：融會傳註，發明透徹，真作手也。
考試官教諭鄭批：此作不窘滯，不放肆，可采。
大賢論聖人具時中之道，既即樂以見其聖智之全，復即射以明夫聖智之義。蓋孔子之聖，聖而時中者也。自非大賢即樂與射以著明之，又何以見其兼三子之聖而為一大聖也哉？昔孟子之意謂：夫夷聖於清，而不足於尹之任；孔子可仕則仕，可止則止，兼清與任而時出之焉。尹聖於任，而不足於惠之和；孔子可久則久，可速則速，兼任與和而時出之焉。夫孔子集三聖之事而為一大聖之事如此，不猶作樂者集衆音之小成而為一大成乎？集大成也者，蓋於其樂之未作而先擊鎛鐘以宣其聲，俟其樂之既闋而後擊特磬以收其韻。金以宣之，則八音翕然並奏而脉絡不紊，此始條理也；玉以收之，則八音詘然皆止而脉絡通貫，此終條理也。始條理者，猶孔子知無不盡，非智之事乎？終條理者，猶孔子德無不全，非聖之事乎？然聖智之事如此，而聖智之義何如？是故以智言之，譬則射
translation_en:
Examiner Liu, Prefectural School Professor, comments: “He integrates the commentaries and elucidates their meaning thoroughly—a true master of composition.”

Examiner Zheng, County School Instructor, comments: “This composition is neither cramped and sluggish nor unrestrained. It merits acceptance.”

The great worthy, discussing how the sage possessed the Way of attaining the mean as circumstances require, first used music to reveal the completeness of his sageliness and wisdom, then used archery to clarify what sageliness and wisdom mean. For Confucius’s sageliness consisted in attaining the mean as circumstances required. Had the great worthy not made this clear through music and archery, how could we see that Confucius combined the sageliness of the three masters and thus became one great sage?

Mencius’s meaning was this: Boyi was sagely in purity but fell short of Yi Yin’s sense of responsibility. Confucius served when it was appropriate to serve and withdrew when it was appropriate to withdraw, combining purity and responsibility and manifesting each at the proper time. Yi Yin was sagely in responsibility but fell short of Liuxia Hui’s harmony. Confucius remained long when it was appropriate to remain long and departed swiftly when it was appropriate to depart swiftly, combining responsibility and harmony and manifesting each at the proper time. Confucius thus brought together the achievements of the three sages into the achievement of one great sage. Was this not like a musician bringing together the lesser completions of the various sounds into one grand completion?

To bring together a grand completion means first striking the great bell before the music begins, to sound its opening, and then, after the music has concluded, striking the single sounding stone to gather its resonance to a close. When the metal sounds the opening, the eight classes of instruments play together in concord, their interconnections remaining orderly: this is the beginning of ordered coherence. When the jade gathers the music to a close, the eight classes of instruments all cease together, their interconnections forming a continuous whole: this is the completion of ordered coherence. Beginning this ordered coherence is like Confucius’s knowledge, which left nothing unexplored—is this not the work of wisdom? Completing this ordered coherence is like Confucius’s virtue, which was complete in every respect—is this not the work of sageliness?

Such, then, are the workings of sageliness and wisdom; but what do sageliness and wisdom mean? Thus, to speak of wisdom, it may be compared to archery …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之巧也以聖言之譬則射之力也由射於百步之
外至其地者乃其力之所及非巧也中其的者乃
其巧之所致非力也由是觀之三子之力有餘而
巧不足孔子則巧力俱全聖智兼備此所以為聖
之時中也歟抑此章言三子之行各極其一偏孔
子之道兼全於眾理所以偏者由其蔽於始是以
缺於終所以全者由其知之至是以行之盡三子
猶春夏秋冬之各一其時孔子則太和元氣之流
行於四時也
===
易
父父子子兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正正家
而天下定矣象曰風自火出家人君子以言
有物而行有恒
邵誠
同考試官教諭陳批家人義求其簡明切當者僅見此篇
同考試官教諭何批此篇深得家人正倫理之義是宜錄出
考試官教授劉批易貴潔靜精微此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批發明家人之旨殆無餘蘊
punctuated:
之巧也。以聖言之，譬則射之力也。由射於百步之外，至其地者，乃其力之所及，非巧也；中其的者，乃其巧之所致，非力也。由是觀之，三子之力有餘而巧不足，孔子則巧力俱全，聖智兼備，此所以為聖之時中也歟！抑此章言三子之行，各極其一偏；孔子之道，兼全於眾理。所以偏者，由其蔽於始，是以缺於終；所以全者，由其知之至，是以行之盡。三子猶春夏秋冬之各一其時，孔子則太和元氣之流行於四時也。

易

父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正；正家，而天下定矣。象曰：「風自火出，家人；君子以言有物而行有恒。」

邵誠

同考試官教諭陳批：「家人義，求其簡明切當者，僅見此篇。」

同考試官教諭何批：「此篇深得家人正倫理之義，是宜錄出。」

考試官教授劉批：「易貴潔靜精微，此作得之。」

考試官教諭鄭批：「發明家人之旨，殆無餘蘊。」
translation_en:
…skill in archery. As for sagehood, it is comparable to strength in archery. When shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away, reaching that distance depends on strength, not skill; hitting the mark depends on skill, not strength. Viewed in this light, the three masters had strength in abundance but insufficient skill. Confucius, however, possessed both skill and strength in full, combining sagehood and wisdom. Is this not why he was the sage who attained the mean appropriate to the time? Furthermore, this chapter says that the conduct of each of the three masters reached the utmost in one particular aspect, whereas the Way of Confucius fully encompassed all principles. Their partiality arose from an initial limitation in understanding, which led to incompleteness in the end. His completeness arose from the utmost understanding, which enabled him to carry practice to its fullest extent. The three masters were like spring, summer, autumn, and winter, each confined to its own season; Confucius was like the primordial vital force of supreme harmony flowing through all four seasons.

Book of Changes

When the father acts as a father, the son as a son, the elder brother as an elder brother, the younger brother as a younger brother, the husband as a husband, and the wife as a wife, the way of the family is correct. Set the family right, and all under Heaven will be settled. The Commentary on the Images says: “Wind issues from fire: this is the hexagram Family. Thus the noble man gives substance to his words and constancy to his conduct.”

Shao Cheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Among interpretations of Family, this is the only essay I have found that meets the requirements of simplicity, clarity, precision, and aptness.”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “This essay deeply grasps the meaning of Family as the rectification of human relationships. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The Book of Changes prizes purity, stillness, precision, and subtlety. This composition achieves them.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “It elucidates the purport of Family, leaving virtually none of its underlying meaning unexplored.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
推卦畫以見正家之化因卦象以著正家之本盖
天下之本在於家而家之本則在於身也彖象聖
人互言以示人其意至矣昔吾夫子傳家人之彖
而推之卦畫謂夫上焉為父初焉為子則父子之
分嚴五焉為兄三焉為弟則兄弟之倫序五三夫
也夫正位乎外四二婦也婦正位乎内如此家道
其有不正乎家道既正殆見天下之大凡為父子
兄弟者莫不於焉是則是效各安其分焉四海之
廣凡為夫夫婦婦者莫不於焉是儀是刑各止其
===
所焉若然天下其有不定乎夫天下之定固本於
正家而家之正又本於脩身焉且家人之卦貞體
離也其象為火悔體巽也其象為風風自火出自
内及外有家人之象也君子體之言不虛言而言
皆切乎倫理則言為有物矣行非偽行而行必本
於倫理則行為有恒矣言行相顧則其身脩而家
豈有不治哉聖人以是傳家人之象厥旨微矣抑
論之言行者一身之樞機也一身之樞機一家之
規範也一家之規範天下之規範也能脩其身則
punctuated:
推卦畫以見正家之化，因卦象以著正家之本。盖天下之本在於家，而家之本則在於身也。彖象聖人互言以示人，其意至矣。昔吾夫子傳家人之彖，而推之卦畫，謂夫上焉為父，初焉為子，則父子之分嚴；五焉為兄，三焉為弟，則兄弟之倫序；五三夫也，夫正位乎外；四二婦也，婦正位乎内。如此，家道其有不正乎？家道既正，殆見天下之大，凡為父子兄弟者，莫不於焉是則是效，各安其分焉；四海之廣，凡為夫夫婦婦者，莫不於焉是儀是刑，各止其所焉。若然，天下其有不定乎？
夫天下之定固本於正家，而家之正又本於脩身焉。且家人之卦，貞體離也，其象為火；悔體巽也，其象為風。風自火出，自内及外，有家人之象也。君子體之，言不虛言，而言皆切乎倫理，則言為有物矣；行非偽行，而行必本於倫理，則行為有恒矣。言行相顧，則其身脩，而家豈有不治哉？聖人以是傳家人之象，厥旨微矣。抑論之，言行者，一身之樞機也；一身之樞機，一家之規範也；一家之規範，天下之規範也。能脩其身，則
translation_en:
By examining the hexagram’s lines, one sees the transforming influence of setting the family right; through the hexagram’s images, one makes clear the foundation of setting the family right. For the foundation of all under Heaven lies in the family, while the foundation of the family lies in the self. In the Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Image, the Sage presents these complementary teachings to instruct people. His meaning is most comprehensive.
In former times, our Master Confucius composed his commentary on the judgment of the Family hexagram, drawing out its meaning from the lines. The top line represents the father, and the first line the son: thus the distinction between father and son is strictly maintained. The fifth represents the elder brother, and the third the younger brother: thus the relationship between elder and younger brothers is properly ordered. The fifth and third represent husbands, and the husband occupies his correct position outside; the fourth and second represent wives, and the wife occupies her correct position inside. With things thus arranged, how could the way of the family fail to be correct? Once the way of the family is correct, throughout the vast realm all who are fathers and sons, elder and younger brothers, will surely take this as their rule and example, each resting content in his allotted role. Throughout the breadth of the Four Seas, all husbands and wives will take this as their pattern and model, each abiding in the proper place. If this is so, how could all under Heaven fail to be settled?
The settling of all under Heaven is indeed rooted in setting the family right, while setting the family right is in turn rooted in cultivating oneself. In the Family hexagram, the inner trigram is Li, whose image is fire; the outer trigram is Xun, whose image is wind. Wind issues from fire, proceeding from within to without: this presents the image of the family. The gentleman embodies this. His words are not empty words, but all accord closely with the ethical order of human relationships; thus his speech has substance. His actions are not sham actions, but are necessarily grounded in that ethical order; thus his conduct has constancy. When words and actions accord with one another, he cultivates his own person; how, then, could his family fail to be well governed? The Sage used this to explain the image of the Family hexagram, and its purport is subtle indeed.
To discuss this further: words and actions are the pivotal workings of the individual. The pivotal workings of the individual are the standard for the family; the standard for the family is the standard for all under Heaven. If one can cultivate oneself, then…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家豈有不齊國豈有不治天下豈有不平乎不然
大學何以曰欲治其國先齊其家欲齊其家先脩
其身
離也者明也萬物皆相見南方之卦也聖人南
面而聽天下嚮明而治蓋取諸此也坤也者
地也萬物皆致養焉故曰致役乎坤兌正秋
也萬物之所說也故曰說言乎兌
莫立之
同考試官教諭陳批本德位象時而兼以物隨帝出入為言說
===
卦之義於斯備矣易卷如子者指不多屈
同考試官教諭何批此篇以德位象時立說深得本旨
考試官教授劉批講析明白非熟於易者不能允宜高薦
考試官教諭鄭批易義如此作詳明者不多見
聖人說後天之卦有舉德位而推其義者有舉象
時而申其義者甚矣後天易卦之妙也自非聖人
舉其德位象時而互言之其義何自而見哉昔吾
夫子說卦論後天之易謂夫離之為卦其中虛之
體有明照之德故萬物之隨帝出乎震者莫不煥
punctuated:
家豈有不齊，國豈有不治，天下豈有不平乎？不然，《大學》何以曰：「欲治其國，先齊其家；欲齊其家，先脩其身。」

離也者，明也。萬物皆相見，南方之卦也。聖人南面而聽天下，嚮明而治，蓋取諸此也。坤也者，地也。萬物皆致養焉，故曰：「致役乎坤。」兌，正秋也，萬物之所說也，故曰：「說言乎兌。」

莫立之

同考試官教諭陳批：本德位象時，而兼以物隨帝出入為言，《說卦》之義於斯備矣。《易》卷如子者，指不多屈。

同考試官教諭何批：此篇以德位象時立說，深得本旨。

考試官教授劉批：講析明白，非熟於《易》者不能，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭鄭批：《易》義如此作詳明者，不多見。

聖人說後天之卦，有舉德位而推其義者，有舉象時而申其義者。甚矣，後天《易》卦之妙也！自非聖人舉其德位象時而互言之，其義何自而見哉？昔吾夫子說卦，論後天之《易》，謂夫離之為卦，其中虛之體，有明照之德，故萬物之隨帝出乎震者，莫不煥
translation_en:
…how could the family fail to be well ordered, the state fail to be well governed, or all under Heaven fail to be at peace? Otherwise, why would the Great Learning say: “Wishing to govern their states, they first ordered their families; wishing to order their families, they first cultivated themselves”?

“Li is brightness. All things become manifest to one another; it is the trigram of the south. The sage faces south to hear the affairs of all under Heaven and turns toward brightness to govern, taking his model from this. Kun is the earth. All things receive nourishment from it; hence the saying, ‘He brings service to completion in Kun.’ Dui is autumn at its height, in which all things rejoice; hence the saying, ‘He rejoices in Dui.’”

Mo Lizhi 莫立之

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Grounding the discussion in the trigrams’ attributes, positions, images, and seasons, and also speaking of how things follow the Lord on High in emerging and withdrawing, this essay fully encompasses the meaning of the Discussion of the Trigrams. One need bend few fingers to count examination papers on the Changes that equal yours.”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “This essay builds its interpretation upon attributes, positions, images, and seasons, and grasps the underlying purport profoundly.”

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “The exposition and analysis are clear. Only someone thoroughly familiar with the Changes could accomplish this. It certainly deserves recommendation for a high place.”

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “Essays elucidating the meaning of the Changes as fully and clearly as this are seldom seen.”

When the sage explains the trigrams of the Later Heaven arrangement, sometimes he adduces their attributes and positions to draw out their meaning, and sometimes he adduces their images and seasons to expound their meaning. How profound are the subtleties of the Later Heaven trigrams of the Changes! Had the sage not brought forward their attributes, positions, images, and seasons and discussed them in relation to one another, how could their meaning have become apparent? Formerly, our Master, explaining the trigrams and discussing the Changes in its Later Heaven arrangement, said that the trigram Li, with its form hollow in the center, possesses the attribute of luminous illumination. Thus all things that follow the Lord on High in coming forth in Zhen are without exception radiantly…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
然昭明于焉而相見乃為南方之卦焉萬物之隨
帝齊乎巽者靡不藹然暢茂于焉而嘉會位乎正
南之方焉是以聖人端冕凝旒面乎正南而聽天
下者非有取於此乎明目達聰嚮乎離明而治萬
民者又非取於是乎然物固隨帝以相見於離矣
而致養則在於坤焉蓋坤之為卦三畫皆陰有地
之象也物之相見於離者今皆委之於厚載之中
而各遂其長養之天物之嘉會于離者今悉致之
於含弘之內而各遂其發育之性故曰致役乎坤
===
者此也夫物既隨帝以致役於坤矣而和悅則又
在於兌焉蓋兌之為卦居乎正西之位適乎正秋
之時故向焉物之長養於坤者今則各正性命不
相假借而自足也昔焉物之發育於坤者今則保
合大和不相凌奪而自適也故曰說言乎兌者此
也是知離以德位言固足以明坤兌之德位坤兌
以象時言亦足以明離之象時也聖人以是說後
天之卦寧復有餘蘊哉抑考大傳上章明先天之
學以著其對待之體也此章論後天之學以明其
punctuated: 然昭明，于焉而相見，乃為南方之卦焉。萬物之隨帝齊乎巽者，靡不藹然暢茂，于焉而嘉會，位乎正南之方焉。是以聖人端冕凝旒，面乎正南而聽天下者，非有取於此乎？明目達聰，嚮乎離明而治萬民者，又非取於是乎？然物固隨帝以相見於離矣，而致養則在於坤焉。蓋坤之為卦，三畫皆陰，有地之象也。物之相見於離者，今皆委之於厚載之中，而各遂其長養之天；物之嘉會于離者，今悉致之於含弘之內，而各遂其發育之性。故曰「致役乎坤」者，此也。夫物既隨帝以致役於坤矣，而和悅則又在於兌焉。蓋兌之為卦，居乎正西之位，適乎正秋之時。故向焉物之長養於坤者，今則各正性命，不相假借而自足也；昔焉物之發育於坤者，今則保合大和，不相凌奪而自適也。故曰「說言乎兌」者，此也。是知離以德位言，固足以明坤兌之德位；坤兌以象時言，亦足以明離之象時也。聖人以是說後天之卦，寧復有餘蘊哉？抑考大傳，上章明先天之學，以著其對待之體也；此章論後天之學，以明其
translation_en:
…radiantly bright; here they become visible to one another. Thus Li is the trigram of the south. The myriad things that follow the Sovereign (Di) in attaining orderly completeness in Xun all flourish luxuriantly; here they gather in splendid union, in the position due south. Thus, when the sage, solemn in ceremonial robes and crown, with its pendants motionless, faces due south to hear the affairs of the realm, does he not take his model from this? When he makes his sight clear and his hearing receptive, turning toward the brightness of Li to govern the myriad people, does he not likewise take his model from this?

Yet although things follow the Sovereign in becoming visible to one another in Li, it is in Kun that they receive nourishment. For the trigram Kun has three lines, all yin, and possesses the image of earth. The things that became visible to one another in Li are now all entrusted to the earth’s ample sustaining capacity, each fulfilling its heaven-endowed potential for growth and nourishment. The things that gathered in splendid union in Li are now all committed to its capacious embrace, each fulfilling its nature through development. This is what is meant by “He brings service to fulfillment in Kun.”

Once things have followed the Sovereign in bringing service to fulfillment in Kun, their harmony and joy lie in Dui. For the trigram Dui occupies the position due west and corresponds to mid-autumn. Thus the things formerly grown and nourished in Kun now each find their proper nature and allotted destiny, sufficient in themselves without borrowing from one another. The things formerly developed in Kun now preserve and unite in supreme harmony, at ease in themselves without encroaching upon or taking from one another. This is what is meant by “He rejoices in Dui.”

From this we know that speaking of Li in terms of its virtue and position is indeed sufficient to elucidate the virtues and positions of Kun and Dui; speaking of Kun and Dui in terms of their images and seasons is likewise sufficient to elucidate the image and season of Li. When the sage explains the trigrams of the Later Heaven in this way, could any hidden meaning remain?
