title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
流行之用也至於下章則又合先天後天而言之
焉是則非先天無以為後天之體非後天無以為
先天之用此先天後天所以可相有而不可相無
者歟
書
欲至于萬年惟王子子孫孫永保民
戴豪
同考試官訓導顧批此題本難於描寫求其能說出有周大臣
祈君永命之意僅見此篇非究心於本領者不能高薦無疑
===
同考試官教諭單批人臣忠愛其君之意此作發明殆盡
考試官教授劉批理到詞充佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批能形容題意而又且質實不浮可取
歷年遠而世保其民此大臣祈君永命之意也盖
永天命而世保民不易致也大臣祈君永命而言
及乎此其忠愛無窮之心為何如哉吾想有周大
臣祈君之意若曰我向告王以明德而懷諸侯用
德而和迷民豈有他哉盖將有所祈也祈之何如
惟曰我周之有天下自今至于後日不徒百斯年
punctuated:
流行之用也。至於下章，則又合先天後天而言之焉。是則非先天無以為後天之體，非後天無以為先天之用。此先天後天所以可相有而不可相無者歟？

書
「欲至于萬年，惟王子子孫孫永保民。」
戴豪

同考試官訓導顧批：「此題本難於描寫，求其能說出有周大臣祈君永命之意，僅見此篇。非究心於本領者不能，高薦無疑。」
同考試官教諭單批：「人臣忠愛其君之意，此作發明殆盡。」
考試官教授劉批：「理到詞充，佳作也。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「能形容題意，而又且質實不浮，可取。」

歷年遠而世保其民，此大臣祈君永命之意也。盖永天命而世保民，不易致也。大臣祈君永命而言及乎此，其忠愛無窮之心為何如哉？吾想有周大臣祈君之意，若曰：「我向告王以明德而懷諸侯，用德而和迷民，豈有他哉？盖將有所祈也。祈之何如？惟曰我周之有天下，自今至于後日，不徒百斯年，
translation_en:
…the functioning of their ongoing circulation. In the following chapter, however, the Prior Heaven and Later Heaven arrangements are discussed together. Without Prior Heaven, there would be no underlying structure for Later Heaven; without Later Heaven, there would be no functioning of Prior Heaven. Is this why Prior Heaven and Later Heaven must coexist and cannot dispense with one another?

Book of Documents
“If you wish to reach ten thousand years, it is for you, O King, through your sons and grandsons, to protect the people forever.”
Dai Hao

Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This topic is inherently difficult to expound. In seeking an essay able to express the Zhou minister’s wish that his ruler’s mandate endure forever, I have found only this one. Such writing is impossible without careful attention to fundamentals. I recommend it highly without hesitation.”
Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor, comments: “This composition elucidates almost exhaustively a minister’s loyal love for his ruler.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “Its reasoning is sound and its expression ample: an excellent composition.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “It conveys the meaning of the topic while remaining substantial and grounded, free of superficiality. It merits acceptance.”

That the years should extend far into the future and that generation after generation should protect the people: this is what the great minister meant in wishing his ruler an enduring mandate. To perpetuate Heaven’s mandate and protect the people through successive generations is no easy achievement. When the great minister, wishing his ruler an enduring mandate, spoke of this, how boundless was the loyal love in his heart! I imagine the Zhou minister’s intention in expressing this wish for his ruler as though he were saying: “Earlier I told the king to make his virtue bright and thereby win the allegiance of the feudal lords, and to employ virtue and thereby bring the misguided people into harmony. Could I have had any other purpose? I had a wish to express. What was that wish? Simply this: that our Zhou’s possession of All under Heaven, from now into the future, should last not merely a hundred years…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而已雖千斯年未多也不徒千斯年而已欲至于
萬斯年而後可焉殆必繼王而為子者穆穆皇皇
宜君宜王皆以明德而永安斯民非特一世為然
而世世之為子者莫不以嗣以續於無窮所謂天
子萬年者在是矣繼子而為孫者本支百世君臨
萬邦皆用明德而承保萬民非惟一代為爾而代
代之為孫者莫不勿替引之於悠久所謂無疆惟
休者在是矣吁古人於進戒之餘而不忘乎祈禱
之誠祈禱之中而猶存乎勸戒之意忠君愛國之
===
心一何至哉嘗觀此章有周人臣之祈君既曰欲
至于萬年者所以歆動之也又曰惟王子子孫孫
永保民者又所以規戒之也告之未幾而戒之隨
至如此惜乎全書不可見而忠愛猶可想厥後周
家卜世三十歷年八百其大臣祈君永命之明驗
歟
予不允惟若茲誥予惟曰襄我二人汝有合哉
言曰在時二人天休滋至惟時二人弗戡其
汝克敬德明我俊民在讓後人于丕時嗚呼
punctuated:
而已，雖千斯年未多也。不徒千斯年而已，欲至于萬斯年而後可焉。殆必繼王而為子者，穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王，皆以明德而永安斯民，非特一世為然，而世世之為子者，莫不以嗣以續於無窮，所謂「天子萬年」者在是矣。繼子而為孫者，本支百世，君臨萬邦，皆用明德而承保萬民，非惟一代為爾，而代代之為孫者，莫不勿替引之於悠久，所謂「無疆惟休」者在是矣。吁！古人於進戒之餘，而不忘乎祈禱之誠；祈禱之中，而猶存乎勸戒之意，忠君愛國之心，一何至哉！嘗觀此章，有周人臣之祈君，既曰欲至于萬年者，所以歆動之也；又曰「惟王子子孫孫永保民」者，又所以規戒之也。告之未幾，而戒之隨至如此。惜乎全書不可見，而忠愛猶可想。厥後周家卜世三十，歷年八百，其大臣祈君永命之明驗歟？

予不允，惟若茲誥。予惟曰：「襄我二人，汝有合哉？」言曰：「在時二人，天休滋至。」惟時二人弗戡，其汝克敬德，明我俊民，在讓後人于丕時。嗚呼！
translation_en:
…and no more; even a thousand years would not be too many. Nor should it be merely a thousand years: only when it reaches ten thousand years will it suffice. Surely the sons who succeed the kings must be reverent and illustrious, fit to be rulers and kings, all employing manifest virtue to secure lasting peace for this people. This must hold not merely for one generation: successive generations of sons must continue the succession without end. Herein lies the meaning of “May the Son of Heaven endure for ten thousand years.” The grandsons who succeed those sons, with the main line and its branches enduring for a hundred generations and ruling over the myriad states, must all employ manifest virtue to preserve and protect the myriad people. This must hold not merely for one generation: successive generations of grandsons must carry it forward without allowing it to lapse, into the distant future. Herein lies the meaning of “May its blessings be without limit.” Ah! After offering admonitions, the ancients did not forget the sincerity of prayer; and within their prayers they still retained the intention to exhort and admonish. How profound was their devotion to their ruler and love for their state!

I have considered this chapter. When the minister of Zhou prayed for his ruler and first expressed the wish that his reign should extend to ten thousand years, he sought thereby to inspire him. When he further said, “May the king’s sons and grandsons forever protect the people,” he sought thereby to admonish him. Scarcely had he offered his counsel before admonition followed in this way. Alas, the complete document can no longer be seen, yet his loyalty and affection can still be imagined. Thereafter, the house of Zhou endured for thirty generations, as divined, and lasted eight hundred years. Was this not clear confirmation of its great minister’s prayer that his ruler’s mandate endure?

“You do not trust me when I admonish you thus [?]. I say only: ‘Let us two aid one another; will you join me?’ It is said: ‘Upon these two men, Heaven’s blessings came in abundance.’ Yet these two men could not fully bear them. You should reverently cultivate virtue and bring our outstanding men to light, bequeathing to later generations a time of greatness [?]. Ah! …”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
篤棐時二人我式克至于今日休我咸成文
王功于不怠丕冒海隅出日罔不率俾公曰
君子不惠若兹多誥予惟用閔于天越民
潘温
同考試官訓導顧批此篇以天命民心立說深合本旨
同考試官教諭單批此題頭緒頗多難於包括是篇文法簡
勁而理致炳如槩視初場無出其右矣
考試官教授劉批長題貴歛繁就實此作得之
考試官教諭鄭批寫出周公留召公之深意可佳
===
大臣之留同列也既原己之致誥而欲共念乎天
民復申己之詳誥而惟用憂乎天民盖大臣一身
天命民心所繫也苟於求去而不反覆致誥以留
之又何以終天命而安民心哉昔召公告老而去
周公留之若曰商周群臣之輔君文武受命之惟
艱我嘗為公告矣豈不信於人而若此告語乎予
惟曰王業之成在我二人汝聞我言而有合哉亦
曰在是二人但天命我周休嘉滋至惟我二人將
不堪勝汝若以盈滿為懼則當能自敬德益加寅
punctuated:
篤棐時二人，我式克至于今日休。我咸成文王功于不怠，丕冒海隅出日，罔不率俾。」公曰：「君子不惠若兹多誥，予惟用閔于天越民。」

潘温

同考試官訓導顧批：此篇以天命民心立說，深合本旨。
同考試官教諭單批：此題頭緒頗多，難於包括。是篇文法簡勁，而理致炳如，槩視初場，無出其右矣。
考試官教授劉批：長題貴歛繁就實，此作得之。
考試官教諭鄭批：寫出周公留召公之深意，可佳。

大臣之留同列也，既原己之致誥而欲共念乎天民，復申己之詳誥而惟用憂乎天民。盖大臣一身，天命民心所繫也。苟於求去而不反覆致誥以留之，又何以終天命而安民心哉？昔召公告老而去，周公留之，若曰：「商周群臣之輔君，文武受命之惟艱，我嘗為公告矣。豈不信於人而若此告語乎？予惟曰：王業之成，在我二人。汝聞我言而有合哉？亦曰：在是二人。但天命我周，休嘉滋至，惟我二人將不堪勝。汝若以盈滿為懼，則當能自敬德，益加寅
translation_en:
…Through the devoted assistance of these two men, we have thus been able to attain the blessings of this day. Let us together complete King Wen’s achievement without slackening, extending its shelter far and wide, to the coastal lands where the sun rises, so that none fail to obey.” The Duke said: “You, my lord, do not heed these many admonitions. I speak only out of concern for Heaven and the people.”

Pan Wen 潘温

Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor, comments: This essay grounds its argument in Heaven’s Mandate and the hearts of the people, closely conforming to the fundamental meaning of the passage.
Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor, comments: This topic has many strands, difficult to encompass. This essay’s composition is concise and forceful, and its reasoning shines clearly. Surveying the first-session essays as a whole, none surpasses it.
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: With a long topic, what matters is drawing its many strands together and reaching the substance. This essay achieves that.
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: It brings out the Duke of Zhou’s profound intention in retaining the Duke of Shao. Admirable.

When a great minister seeks to retain a fellow minister, he first explains why he has offered admonitions, wishing them both to keep Heaven and the people in mind; he then reiterates why his admonitions have been so detailed, solely out of concern for Heaven and the people. For Heaven’s Mandate and the hearts of the people are bound up with the person of a great minister. If, when such a minister seeks to leave, one does not repeatedly admonish him in order to retain him, how can one fulfill Heaven’s Mandate to the end and set the people’s hearts at ease?

In former times, when the Duke of Shao sought retirement on grounds of age and prepared to depart, the Duke of Zhou urged him to remain, saying in effect: “I have already spoken to you, my lord, about how the ministers of Shang and Zhou assisted their rulers, and how difficult it was for Kings Wen and Wu to receive the Mandate. Is it because I lack confidence in you that I speak in this way? I say only that the completion of the royal undertaking rests with us two. Having heard my words, do you agree? You too say that it rests with these two men. Yet Heaven has bestowed its Mandate upon our Zhou, and blessings come in ever greater abundance; we two may prove unable to bear them. If you fear the fullness of prosperity, you should yourself attend reverently to virtue and become still more reverent…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
畏明揚俊民布列庶位以盡大臣之職業以答滋
至之天休他日推遜後人於盛大之時而去可也
今天休未答豈汝辭位之時乎夫天休固所當答
而民心尤所當圖故又嘆息而告之以為惟我二
人左右之功既篤于前時故政教之美式隆於今
日然未可以是自足也尤當并力一心共成文王
未終之功而罔敢或怠仁覆天下使海隅日出之
地無不臣服可也今遠人未俾豈汝求退之時乎
然周公之言雖切恐召公之意未信於是又稱君
===
以尊之而申其意謂夫共答天命咸服民心我今
為公告矣豈不順于理而若茲多誥耶誠以乘茲
大命公之責也今而遽去則乘載無所托而天命
不終矣此我所為憂焉命作民極公之任也今而
不留則作極無其人而斯民無賴矣此我所為閔
焉吁始言若茲誥終言若茲多誥周公之告召公
其言語之際亦可悲矣大抵成功不居大臣之道
故洛邑既成周公告歸成王親政召公退休雖然
忠君憂國之心未嘗已也是以迪將之言一出而
punctuated:
畏，明揚俊民，布列庶位，以盡大臣之職業，以答滋至之天休。他日推遜後人，於盛大之時而去，可也。今天休未答，豈汝辭位之時乎？夫天休固所當答，而民心尤所當圖。故又嘆息而告之，以為惟我二人左右之功既篤于前時，故政教之美式隆於今日。然未可以是自足也，尤當并力一心，共成文王未終之功，而罔敢或怠，仁覆天下，使海隅日出之地無不臣服，可也。今遠人未俾，豈汝求退之時乎？然周公之言雖切，恐召公之意未信，於是又稱君以尊之，而申其意，謂夫共答天命，咸服民心，我今為公告矣。豈不順于理而若茲多誥耶？誠以乘茲大命，公之責也。今而遽去，則乘載無所托，而天命不終矣，此我所為憂焉。命作民極，公之任也。今而不留，則作極無其人，而斯民無賴矣，此我所為閔焉。
吁！始言若茲誥，終言若茲多誥，周公之告召公，其言語之際亦可悲矣。大抵成功不居，大臣之道。故洛邑既成，周公告歸；成王親政，召公退休。雖然，忠君憂國之心未嘗已也。是以迪將之言一出而
translation_en:
…in reverent fear, openly promote outstanding men and appoint them throughout the offices, thereby fulfilling the duties of a great minister and requiting Heaven’s ever-increasing blessings. On some future day, you may yield to those who come after you and depart when prosperity has reached its height. But now, while Heaven’s blessings remain unrequited, can this be the time for you to resign your position? Heaven’s blessings must indeed be requited, but the people’s allegiance demands still greater consideration. Thus he sighed again and told him: “Because the two of us rendered substantial service in assisting the ruler in earlier days, the excellence of government and instruction has flourished today. Yet we must not rest content with this. Above all, we should unite our strength and purpose to complete King Wen’s unfinished work, never daring to slacken. Our benevolence should shelter all under Heaven, so that none, even at the sea’s edge where the sun rises, fail to submit as subjects. Now that the distant peoples have not yet been brought into submission, can this be the time for you to seek retirement?”
Yet although the Duke of Zhou’s words were earnest, he feared that the Duke of Shao was still not persuaded. He therefore addressed him again as “lord” to honor him and reiterated his meaning: “I have now explained to you, my lord, how we must together requite Heaven’s mandate and win the allegiance of all the people. Would I offer so many admonitions if they did not accord with principle? Truly, bearing this great mandate is your responsibility. If you abruptly depart now, there will be no one to whom its burden can be entrusted, and Heaven’s mandate will not be carried through to its completion. This is what worries me. Having been charged to serve as the people’s highest exemplar, you bear this duty. If you do not remain now, there will be no one to serve as that exemplar, and these people will have no one on whom to rely. This is what grieves me.”
Alas! At the outset he spoke of “admonishing thus,” and at the close of “offering so many admonitions.” In the Duke of Zhou’s admonitions to the Duke of Shao, even his manner of speaking was deeply moving. In general, to accomplish one’s work without clinging to one’s position is the way of a great minister. Thus, once Luoyi was completed, the Duke of Zhou requested leave to return home; when King Cheng took personal charge of government, the Duke of Shao retired. Nevertheless, their devotion to the ruler and concern for the state never ceased. Hence, once the words urging guidance and support were uttered, …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事畢矣居室之治其可緩乎彼茅所以補屋也則
晝往取茅以為覆蓋之需索所以編茅也則夜而
絞索以為束縛之用于以亟乘其屋而葺理之惟
勤于以急升其居而營繕之不懈所以然者豈好
勞哉盖以來歲將至吾民欲播穀於南畝而不暇
於此也來春將及吾民欲有事於西疇而不遑於
斯也夫農事固不可忘而君事尤所當備彼二陽
之月固陰冱寒冰可取也吾則趨事赴工而鑿之
冲冲焉三陽之月風未解凍水可藏也吾則併力
===
齊心而納于冰室焉所以然者豈惡逸哉盖以四
陽司令蚤朝屆期吾君將獻彼羔羊而司寒是祀
以行乎啟冰之禮矣可不及時而為之藏乎將取
彼新韭而司寒是祭以舉乎開冰之儀矣可不先
時而為之備乎邠民不待督責而自相勸戒如此
非先公風化之厚能若是哉大抵七月之詩一言
以蔽之曰豫而已大寒在冬而備之於秋收成在
秋而圖之於春蠶績未成而曰為公子裘嘉蔬以養老朋酒以獻君拳拳
舉而曰為公子裳狩獵未
punctuated: 事畢矣，居室之治，其可緩乎？彼茅所以補屋也，則晝往取茅，以為覆蓋之需；索所以編茅也，則夜而絞索，以為束縛之用。于以亟乘其屋，而葺理之惟勤；于以急升其居，而營繕之不懈。所以然者，豈好勞哉？盖以來歲將至，吾民欲播穀於南畝，而不暇於此也；來春將及，吾民欲有事於西疇，而不遑於斯也。夫農事固不可忘，而君事尤所當備。彼二陽之月，固陰冱寒，冰可取也，吾則趨事赴工，而鑿之冲冲焉；三陽之月，風未解凍，水可藏也，吾則併力齊心，而納于冰室焉。所以然者，豈惡逸哉？盖以四陽司令，蚤朝屆期，吾君將獻彼羔羊，而司寒是祀，以行乎啟冰之禮矣，可不及時而為之藏乎？將取彼新韭，而司寒是祭，以舉乎開冰之儀矣，可不先時而為之備乎？邠民不待督責，而自相勸戒如此，非先公風化之厚，能若是哉？大抵《七月》之詩，一言以蔽之，曰豫而已。大寒在冬，而備之於秋；收成在秋，而圖之於春。蠶績未成，而曰「為公子裘」；嘉蔬以養老，朋酒以獻君，拳拳舉而曰「為公子裳」；狩獵未
translation_en:
…the work is finished. Can repairs to the dwelling then be delayed? Thatch is what repairs the roof, so by day they go to gather it to supply the roofing material. Rope is what binds the thatch, so by night they twist ropes for fastening it. They promptly climb onto their roofs and diligently mend them; they hasten up onto their dwellings and repair them without slackening. Do they do this because they enjoy toil? It is because the coming year is approaching: our people will wish to sow grain in the southern fields and will have no leisure for these tasks. The coming spring is drawing near: our people will wish to work in the western fields and will have no time for these matters.

Agricultural work certainly must not be neglected, but service to the lord especially requires preparation. In the month of the second yang, the yin cold is firmly established and bitter, and ice can be harvested. We therefore hurry to the task and set to work, hewing it with resounding blows. In the month of the third yang, the wind has not yet thawed the ice, and frozen water can be stored. We therefore unite our strength and purpose and bring it into the icehouse. Do we do this because we dislike ease? It is because, when the fourth yang governs the season and the appointed early morning arrives [?], our lord will offer a lamb in sacrifice to the spirit presiding over cold, performing the rite of opening the icehouse. Can we fail to store the ice in good time for him? He will take fresh chives and sacrifice to the spirit presiding over cold, carrying out the ceremony of opening the icehouse. Can we fail to prepare for him beforehand?

The people of Bin encourage and admonish one another in this way without waiting to be supervised or reproached. Could they be like this without the profound transforming influence of their former lords? In general, the poem “The Seventh Month” can be summed up in a single word: preparedness. The severe cold comes in winter, but they prepare for it in autumn; the harvest comes in autumn, but they plan for it in spring. Before silkworm raising and textile work are finished, they say, “Make a fur robe for the lord’s son” [?]. Fine vegetables nourish the aged, and paired vessels of wine are offered to the lord. With earnest devotion they raise it and say, “Make lower garments for the lord’s son” [?]; the hunt has not yet …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎憂勤之意惓惓乎忠愛之心邠俗之厚如是周
公舉以為成王告得無意乎
有駜有駜駜彼乘黃夙夜在公在公明明振振
鷺鷺于下鼓咽咽醉言舞于胥樂兮有駜有
駜駜彼乘牡夙夜在公在公飲酒振振鷺鷺
于下鼓咽咽醉言歸于胥樂兮有駜有駜駜
彼乘駰夙夜在公在公載燕自今以始歲其
有君子有穀詒孫子于胥樂兮
陳邦直
===
同考試官訓導先批形容當時燕飲頌禱之意有餘味焉
同考試官教諭楚批題合三章欲觀士子講貫作者類
多失此得彼冗繁可厭是篇詞簡意盡故錄之
同考試官學正胡批詞氣舂容筆力老健宜置高選
考試官教授劉批詞不冗費理甚明白
考試官教諭鄭批頌義宜簡古此作得之
詩人屢託所乘以興君臣燕飲而頌禱以相樂也
夫君臣相樂治世之休詩人屢托興而歌頌其事
不亦宜乎此燕飲而頌禱之辭想其託興之意若
punctuated:
乎憂勤之意，惓惓乎忠愛之心。邠俗之厚如是，周公舉以為成王告，得無意乎？

有駜有駜，駜彼乘黃。夙夜在公，在公明明。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言舞，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘牡。夙夜在公，在公飲酒。振振鷺，鷺于下。鼓咽咽，醉言歸，于胥樂兮！有駜有駜，駜彼乘駰。夙夜在公，在公載燕。自今以始，歲其有，君子有穀，詒孫子，于胥樂兮！

陳邦直

同考試官訓導先批：形容當時燕飲頌禱之意，有餘味焉。
同考試官教諭楚批：題合三章，欲觀士子講貫。作者類多失此得彼，冗繁可厭。是篇詞簡意盡，故錄之。
同考試官學正胡批：詞氣舂容，筆力老健，宜置高選。
考試官教授劉批：詞不冗費，理甚明白。
考試官教諭鄭批：頌義宜簡古，此作得之。

詩人屢託所乘以興君臣燕飲，而頌禱以相樂也。夫君臣相樂，治世之休，詩人屢托興而歌頌其事，不亦宜乎？此燕飲而頌禱之辭，想其託興之意，若
translation_en:
…in their concern and diligence, and so earnest in their loyal affection. Such was the generosity of Bin’s customs. Could the Duke of Zhou have had no purpose in citing them to admonish King Cheng?

“Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four yellow horses! Morning and night at the duke’s court, at court diligent and discerning. The egrets flock together; the egrets descend. The drums resound. Drunk, we dance, all rejoicing together! Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four stallions! Morning and night at the duke’s court, at court drinking wine. The egrets flock together; the egrets descend. The drums resound. Drunk, we return home, all rejoicing together! Stout and strong, stout and strong—stout are those four dark-dappled horses! Morning and night at the duke’s court, at court holding a feast. From this time onward, may each year bring abundance; may the noble lord possess goodness and pass it down to his descendants, all rejoicing together!”

Chen Bangzhi

Associate Examiner Xian, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The portrayal of the spirit of feasting, praise, and prayer on that occasion leaves a lingering savor.”
Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor, comments: “The topic combines three stanzas to test the candidates’ integrated understanding. Most writers capture one aspect while missing another, becoming tediously verbose. This essay is concise in expression and complete in meaning; hence its inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Hu, School Instructor, comments: “The language and tenor are ample and unhurried, and the writing mature and vigorous. It deserves a high ranking.”
Examiner Liu, Professor, comments: “The language is economical, and the principles are very clearly expressed.”
Examiner Zheng, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of a hymn should be conveyed with antique simplicity. This composition achieves that.”

The poet repeatedly draws upon the horses they ride as evocative openings for the feasting of ruler and ministers, offering praise and prayers that contribute to their shared enjoyment. The shared enjoyment of ruler and ministers is a blessing of an age of good government. Is it not fitting that the poet repeatedly uses evocative imagery to sing its praises? These are words of praise and prayer at a feast. If we imagine the intention behind this imagery, it is as though…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰有駜然而肥強者四馬皆黃矣我魯君臣夙夜
在公相與辨治豈無燕樂乎燕必有舞則或坐或
伏振振然如鷺之下也燕必有鼓則或疾或徐咽
咽然其聲之長也斯時也君臣胥慶勢位兩忘醉
而起舞以相樂焉詩人之意無窮託興之詞必再
又謂有駜然而肥強者四馬皆牡矣我魯君臣夙
夜在公相與燕飲豈無樂舞乎蹲蹲舞我則既抑
且揚振振然如鷺之飛也坎坎鼓我則既和且平
咽咽然其聲之遠也斯時也上下相懽情意交契
===
醉而言歸以相樂焉詩人之意未巳託興之詞必
三又謂有駜有駜則駜彼乘駽矣夙夜在公則在
公載燕矣君燕其臣臣媚其君惟願自今以始樂
嵗相仍以一人之慶而為千萬人之慶也君子有
榖詒厥孫子以一巳之善而為千萬世之善也豈
不足以相樂乎吁罄懽洽於燕飲之餘竭忠愛於
頌禱之頃魯之君臣何相得之深哉大抵君臣之
分以嚴為主朝廷之禮以敬為主然一於嚴敬則
情或不通而無以盡其忠告之益故先王制為燕
punctuated: 曰：「有駜然而肥強者，四馬皆黃矣。我魯君臣夙夜在公，相與辨治，豈無燕樂乎？燕必有舞，則或坐或伏，振振然如鷺之下也；燕必有鼓，則或疾或徐，咽咽然其聲之長也。斯時也，君臣胥慶，勢位兩忘，醉而起舞以相樂焉。」詩人之意無窮，託興之詞必再，又謂：「有駜然而肥強者，四馬皆牡矣。我魯君臣夙夜在公，相與燕飲，豈無樂舞乎？蹲蹲舞我，則既抑且揚，振振然如鷺之飛也；坎坎鼓我，則既和且平，咽咽然其聲之遠也。斯時也，上下相懽，情意交契，醉而言歸以相樂焉。」詩人之意未巳，託興之詞必三，又謂：「有駜有駜，則駜彼乘駽矣；夙夜在公，則在公載燕矣。君燕其臣，臣媚其君，惟願自今以始，樂嵗相仍，以一人之慶而為千萬人之慶也；君子有榖，詒厥孫子，以一巳之善而為千萬世之善也。豈不足以相樂乎？」吁！罄懽洽於燕飲之餘，竭忠愛於頌禱之頃，魯之君臣何相得之深哉！大抵君臣之分以嚴為主，朝廷之禮以敬為主，然一於嚴敬，則情或不通，而無以盡其忠告之益。故先王制為燕
translation_en:
…saying: “Stout and strong, all four horses are yellow. We, the ruler and ministers of Lu, attend to public duties morning and night, together conducting government: should we not also enjoy a banquet? A banquet must have dancing: now sitting, now bowing low, the dancers move their wings like egrets descending. A banquet must have drumming: now quick, now slow, its resonant sound lingers. At this moment, ruler and ministers rejoice together, both forgetting power and rank; warmed by wine, they rise and dance for their mutual enjoyment.” The poet’s meaning is inexhaustible, so his evocative imagery must appear a second time. He says again: “Stout and strong, all four horses are stallions. We, the ruler and ministers of Lu, attend to public duties morning and night and drink together at the banquet: should we not have music and dancing? They dance rhythmically for us, now lowering themselves, now rising, moving their wings like egrets in flight. They beat the drums for us, harmonious and measured, their resonant sound carrying far. At this moment, superiors and subordinates delight in one another, their feelings meeting in accord; having drunk their fill, they speak of returning home, sharing their enjoyment.”

The poet’s meaning is not yet exhausted, so his evocative imagery must appear a third time. He says again: “‘Stout, stout’—stout indeed is that team of four dark-grey horses. ‘Morning and night at the lord’s court’—there at court they hold a banquet. The ruler feasts his ministers, and the ministers show affection for their ruler. They wish only that, from this time onward, years of plenty may follow one another, making the blessing of one man the blessing of countless people. May the lord possess goodness and bequeath it to his descendants, making the goodness of one person the goodness of countless generations. Is this not sufficient for their mutual enjoyment?”

Ah! They express their joy and fellowship to the full in the course of banqueting, and pour out their loyalty and affection in their praises and prayers. How profound was the mutual understanding between the ruler and ministers of Lu! In general, the distinction between ruler and minister rests chiefly on strictness, and court ritual rests chiefly on reverence. Yet if strictness and reverence alone prevail, feelings may fail to pass between them, leaving no way to obtain the full benefit of loyal counsel. Thus the former kings instituted the rites of banqueting…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
飲之禮以通上下之情今魯之羣臣宴于公所願
其年穀常登為庶民之慮切矣願其子孫為善為
後世之慮深矣亦可謂善頌善禱而盡忠告之益
者歟
春秋
盟于召陵僖公四年夏公會齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯曹
伯伐鄭圍新城秋楚人圍許諸侯遂救許
僖公六年
劉湜
===
考試官教授劉批此篇析理詳明措辭簡捷足可以破場
中之失體認而尚浮詞以求勝者允宜高薦
考試官教諭鄭批有斷制有發揮賢能薦書舍子其誰
伯功既成而能節其力以討罪竭其力以恤患此
見齊桓召陵服楚之後而伐鄭救許又得討罪恤
患之義也時而春秋荆楚天下莫強焉齊桓主伯
勢不兩立一旦爰整八國仗義南征屈完服辜盟
于召陵不血一刃而楚自却不遺一矢而敵自沮
□齊之功烈盛矣然齊自召陵之後兵服四夷威
punctuated:
飲之禮，以通上下之情。今魯之羣臣宴于公所，願其年穀常登，為庶民之慮切矣；願其子孫為善，為後世之慮深矣。亦可謂善頌善禱，而盡忠告之益者歟！
春秋
盟于召陵，僖公四年。夏，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯伐鄭，圍新城。秋，楚人圍許，諸侯遂救許。僖公六年。
劉湜
考試官教授劉批：此篇析理詳明，措辭簡捷，足可以破場中之失體認而尚浮詞以求勝者，允宜高薦。
考試官教諭鄭批：有斷制，有發揮，賢能薦書，舍子其誰！
伯功既成，而能節其力以討罪，竭其力以恤患，此見齊桓召陵服楚之後，而伐鄭救許，又得討罪恤患之義也。時而春秋，荆楚天下莫強焉。齊桓主伯，勢不兩立。一旦爰整八國，仗義南征，屈完服辜，盟于召陵，不血一刃而楚自却，不遺一矢而敵自沮。□齊之功烈盛矣！然齊自召陵之後，兵服四夷，威
translation_en:
…the rites of banqueting, to allow the feelings of superiors and subordinates to flow between them. Now, as the assembled ministers of Lu feast at their lord’s residence, they wish that his grain harvests may always be abundant: their concern for the common people is earnest indeed. They wish that his descendants may do good: their concern for later generations is profound indeed. May they not be said to excel in praise and prayer, and to realize fully the benefits of loyal counsel?
Spring and Autumn Annals
“They made a covenant at Shaoling.” Fourth year of Duke Xi.
“In summer, the duke joined the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao in attacking Zheng; they besieged Xincheng. In autumn, the men of Chu besieged Xu. The assembled lords thereupon relieved Xu.” Sixth year of Duke Xi.
Liu Shi
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: This essay analyzes principles thoroughly and clearly, and its wording is concise and direct. It is fully capable of refuting those in the examination hall who lack substantive understanding yet prize empty phrasing in their pursuit of success. It certainly deserves a high recommendation.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: There is decisive judgment; there is development of the underlying meaning. In the recommendation of the worthy and capable, whom should we choose but you!
Once his achievements as hegemon were established, he could restrain his strength in punishing wrongdoing and expend it fully in relieving distress. This is evident in Duke Huan of Qi’s conduct after he had brought Chu to submission at Shaoling: in attacking Zheng and relieving Xu, he again fulfilled the proper principles of punishing wrongdoing and relieving distress. At that time, in the Spring and Autumn period, no power under Heaven was stronger than Jing-Chu. Duke Huan of Qi held the hegemony; the circumstances did not allow the two powers to stand together. Then he marshaled eight states and, upholding righteousness, campaigned southward. Qu Wan acknowledged guilt, and they made a covenant at Shaoling. Without a single blade being bloodied, Chu withdrew of its own accord; without a single arrow being discharged, the enemy’s resolve collapsed. title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
動諸夏今而大合列辟問罪懿親之鄭環攻新造
之邑然以六國而伐鄭兵車雲集宜若振槁然而
公乃圍而不舉者意豈不曰好攻戰樂殺人者於
罪為大於是惟整兵以示之而不狃於速克惟寬
容以來之而不急於圖勝豈非伯主節其力以討
罪乎繼而楚欲救鄭廼攻大岳之裔計解鄭人之
圍然以強楚而陵弱許勢力弗敵不啻拉朽然而
公即移師以赴之者意豈不曰救患分災於禮為
急於是寧釋有罪之鄭亟拯無辜之許寧隳垂成
===
之功速慰引領之望又非伯主盡其力以恤患乎
吁討罪猶理亂繩不可急也救患猶解倒懸不可
緩也桓知其然故於召陵之後伐鄭救許寬猛適
宜如此春秋得不備書以美之歟抑又論之陳不
可陵猶鄭不可虐也桓公前乎伐鄭責陳甚備何
慈於鄭而忍於陳乎徐不可棄猶許不可忘也桓
公後乎救許緩徐不力何勤於許而怠於徐乎先
儒謂其功過相半信矣
陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕鄭人侵蔡獲蔡公子燮〔襄公八年〕
punctuated:
動諸夏。今而大合列辟，問罪懿親之鄭，環攻新造之邑。然以六國而伐鄭，兵車雲集，宜若振槁。然而公乃圍而不舉者，意豈不曰：「好攻戰、樂殺人者，於罪為大。」於是惟整兵以示之，而不狃於速克；惟寬容以來之，而不急於圖勝。豈非伯主節其力以討罪乎？繼而楚欲救鄭，廼攻大岳之裔，計解鄭人之圍。然以強楚而陵弱許，勢力弗敵，不啻拉朽。然而公即移師以赴之者，意豈不曰：「救患分災，於禮為急。」於是寧釋有罪之鄭，亟拯無辜之許；寧隳垂成之功，速慰引領之望。又非伯主盡其力以恤患乎？吁！討罪猶理亂繩，不可急也；救患猶解倒懸，不可緩也。桓知其然，故於召陵之後，伐鄭救許，寬猛適宜如此。《春秋》得不備書以美之歟？抑又論之，陳不可陵，猶鄭不可虐也。桓公前乎伐鄭，責陳甚備，何慈於鄭而忍於陳乎？徐不可棄，猶許不可忘也。桓公後乎救許，緩徐不力，何勤於許而怠於徐乎？先儒謂其功過相半，信矣。

陳侯逃歸〔襄公七年〕。鄭人侵蔡，獲蔡公子燮〔襄公八年〕。
translation_en:
…shook the central states. Now he assembled the rulers in great numbers to call Zheng, a state closely related to the royal house, to account, and surrounded its newly built city. With six states attacking Zheng and war chariots gathering like clouds, taking it should have been as easy as shaking down withered leaves. Yet the duke besieged it without capturing it. Was his intention not this: “To delight in warfare and take pleasure in killing is among the gravest offenses”? Thus he merely marshaled his troops to make a display, without becoming bent on a swift conquest; he showed forbearance to induce submission, without hastening to secure victory. Was this not a hegemon restraining his strength in punishing wrongdoing?

Then Chu, wishing to rescue Zheng, attacked the descendants of Da Yue—that is, Xu—planning thereby to lift the siege of Zheng. With mighty Chu assailing weak Xu, their strength was so unequal that overcoming Xu would have been as easy as breaking rotten wood. Yet the duke immediately moved his army to its aid. Was his intention not this: “Relieving distress and sharing the burden of calamity are urgent duties under ritual propriety”? Thus he preferred to release guilty Zheng in order to rescue innocent Xu at once, and to abandon an achievement nearly completed in order swiftly to satisfy those craning their necks in hope. Was this not also a hegemon exerting his strength to the utmost to relieve distress?

Ah! Punishing wrongdoing is like untangling knotted cords: it must not be hurried. Relieving distress is like releasing someone hanging upside down: it must not be delayed. Duke Huan understood this. Hence, after Shaoling, in attacking Zheng and rescuing Xu, he balanced leniency and severity so appropriately. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to record these events fully in praise of him? Yet let us consider further. Chen should not have been oppressed, just as Zheng should not have been abused. Before attacking Zheng, Duke Huan had been exceedingly exacting in his demands upon Chen. Why was he merciful toward Zheng but cruel toward Chen? The state of Xu 徐 should not have been abandoned, just as Xu 許 should not have been forgotten. After rescuing Xu 許, Duke Huan was slow and ineffectual in aiding Xu 徐. Why was he diligent toward Xu 許 but negligent toward Xu 徐? Earlier Confucian scholars said that his achievements and faults stood in equal measure. How true!

The Marquis of Chen fled and returned home. 〔Seventh year of Duke Xiang〕 Men of Zheng invaded Cai and captured Xie, a son of the ruler of Cai. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang〕

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
冬楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕晉侯使士匄
来聘〔襄公八年〕冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭
十有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕楚薳罷帥
師伐吳〔昭公六年〕秋公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕齊侯伐
徐〔昭公十六年〕秋齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕
朱顯
===
考試官教授劉批場中作此題紛紛無定見惟此義寫出二
公之賢否宛在目前所謂過屠門大嚼其知肉味者乎
考試官教諭鄭批此作詞嚴義正得春秋之旨宜錄出
勢有難為而伯主得善勝之道時有可為而伯嗣
無自強之志此晉悼所以克復舊業而齊景所以
終於無成也比事以觀賢否昭然矣且夫春秋之
中晉悼嗣伯去文襄之時未遠其餘澤猶有存者
若何而見其勢之難為耶是時陳嘗與晉同事者
也今則不思輔晉而棄于鄬之會鄭亦與晉同志
punctuated:
冬，楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕。晉侯使士匄来聘〔襄公八年〕。冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕。楚薳罷帥師伐吳〔昭公六年〕。秋，公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。吳滅州来〔昭公十三年〕。齊侯伐徐〔昭公十六年〕。秋，齊高發帥師伐莒〔昭公十九年〕。
朱顯
考試官教授劉批：場中作此題，紛紛無定見，惟此義寫出二公之賢否，宛在目前。所謂過屠門大嚼，其知肉味者乎？
考試官教諭鄭批：此作詞嚴義正，得春秋之旨，宜錄出。
勢有難為，而伯主得善勝之道；時有可為，而伯嗣無自強之志。此晉悼所以克復舊業，而齊景所以終於無成也。比事以觀，賢否昭然矣。且夫春秋之中，晉悼嗣伯，去文襄之時未遠，其餘澤猶有存者，若何而見其勢之難為耶？是時，陳嘗與晉同事者也，今則不思輔晉，而棄于鄬之會；鄭亦與晉同志
translation_en:
In winter, Prince Zhen of Chu led an army against Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang〕 The Marquis of Jin sent Shi Gai on a courtesy mission to our court. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang〕 In winter, the Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly concluded a covenant at Xi. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xiang〕 Wei Pi of Chu led an army against Wu. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhao〕 In autumn, the Duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquises of Jin and Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earls of Zheng and Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao〕 Wu destroyed Zhoulai. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao〕 The Marquis of Qi attacked Xu. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Zhao〕 In autumn, Gao Fa of Qi led an army against Ju. 〔Nineteenth year of Duke Zhao〕

Zhu Xian

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: Those answering this question in the examination hall offered a welter of views without any firm judgment. This essay alone portrays the worthiness and unworthiness of the two dukes as vividly as if they stood before our eyes. As the saying goes, one passes a butcher’s doorway and chews heartily: might this be someone who knows the taste of meat?

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: This composition is rigorous in expression and correct in interpretation. It grasps the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals and merits inclusion in the record.

The circumstances were difficult, yet the hegemon found the way to prevail through skill; the times offered opportunities, yet the heir to hegemonic power lacked the resolve to strengthen himself. This is why Duke Dao of Jin could restore his predecessors’ achievements, whereas Duke Jing of Qi ultimately accomplished nothing. Compare the events, and their worthiness and unworthiness become clear.

Now, during the Spring and Autumn period, when Duke Dao of Jin succeeded to the hegemony, the age of Dukes Wen and Xiang was not far past, and some of their beneficent legacy still remained. How, then, can we see that his circumstances were difficult? At that time, Chen had formerly acted in concert with Jin. Now, however, it gave no thought to supporting Jin, but abandoned it at the meeting at Wei. Zheng, too, had shared Jin’s aims…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者也今則無故侵蔡而召子囊之伐晋方失陳國
中之勢未振鄭又侵蔡楚人之詞稍直巳而士匄
聘魯告將用師于鄭焉則諸侯皆不欲戰而人心
亦必有疑怠矣以勢而觀誠難為也使悼公一以
戰伐為威兵力為武思復先君之業不亦難乎幸
而違荀偃戰楚之言聽武子救楚之策雖合列國
而興伐鄭之兵卒許鄭成而結于戲之盟脩德息
師竟收成功悼公得善勝之道如此非賢而能之
乎春秋所□善之也若夫春秋之季齊景代興去
===
桓公之時巳遠其餘澤亦巳斬矣若何而見其時
之易為耶于時楚實中國勍敵也今而欲雪舊忿
命薳罷以伐吳晋乃諸夏盟主也今而欲服列國
會平丘以示威楚方攻吳則無睥睨之計晋惟示
威則無駕馭之畧巳而吳併州来又出楚之不意
焉則吳之爭雄亦不在於中國矣以時而論實易
為也使景公誠能尊事王室輯寧中夏桓公之業
獨不可復乎奈何不以德義懷人惟以威力脅人
今年既躬親甲胄以伐徐明年復爰整師旅以伐
punctuated: 者也，今則無故侵蔡，而召子囊之伐。晋方失陳，國中之勢未振；鄭又侵蔡，楚人之詞稍直。巳而士匄聘魯，告將用師于鄭焉，則諸侯皆不欲戰，而人心亦必有疑怠矣。以勢而觀，誠難為也。使悼公一以戰伐為威、兵力為武，思復先君之業，不亦難乎？幸而違荀偃戰楚之言，聽武子救楚之策，雖合列國而興伐鄭之兵，卒許鄭成而結于戲之盟，脩德息師，竟收成功。悼公得善勝之道如此，非賢而能之乎？春秋所□善之也。若夫春秋之季，齊景代興，去桓公之時巳遠，其餘澤亦巳斬矣。若何而見其時之易為耶？于時，楚實中國勍敵也，今而欲雪舊忿，命薳罷以伐吳；晋乃諸夏盟主也，今而欲服列國，會平丘以示威。楚方攻吳，則無睥睨之計；晋惟示威，則無駕馭之畧。巳而吳併州来，又出楚之不意焉，則吳之爭雄亦不在於中國矣。以時而論，實易為也。使景公誠能尊事王室，輯寧中夏，桓公之業獨不可復乎？奈何不以德義懷人，惟以威力脅人？今年既躬親甲胄以伐徐，明年復爰整師旅以伐
translation_en: … had likewise shared Jin’s aims. Now, however, Zheng attacked Cai without cause, provoking an expedition by Zinang. Jin had just lost Chen’s allegiance, and its strength at home had not recovered; Zheng’s further attack on Cai gave Chu a somewhat stronger justification. Subsequently, Shi Gai went on a diplomatic visit to Lu and announced that troops would be deployed against Zheng. Yet the regional lords all wished to avoid battle, and people must also have harbored doubts and grown dispirited. Judging by these circumstances, action was indeed difficult. If Duke Dao had relied entirely on warfare to establish his authority and on armed strength to demonstrate martial prowess, would it not have been difficult to restore his predecessor’s achievements? Fortunately, he rejected Xun Yan’s proposal to fight Chu and accepted Wuzi’s plan to aid Chu [?]. Although he assembled the states and raised troops against Zheng, he ultimately granted Zheng peace and concluded the covenant at Xi. By cultivating virtue and resting his troops, he finally achieved success. Such was Duke Dao’s mastery of the way to win well: could anyone without worthiness have accomplished this? This is what the Spring and Autumn Annals praises in him [one character illegible]. As for Duke Jing of Qi, who rose to power late in the Spring and Autumn period, Duke Huan’s time was already distant, and the lingering benefits of his rule had also come to an end. How, then, can we see that the times made action easy? At that time, Chu was a formidable enemy of the central states. Now, wishing to avenge an old grievance, it ordered Wei Pi to attack Wu. Jin was the covenant leader of the various Xia states; now, wishing to bring the states into submission, it convened the assembly at Pingqiu to display its might. With Chu occupied in attacking Wu, it had no designs on the central states; with Jin merely displaying its might, it had no strategy for controlling them. Subsequently, Wu annexed Zhoulai, again taking Chu by surprise. Thus Wu’s contest for supremacy was likewise not directed toward the central states. Judging by the times, action was truly easy. Had Duke Jing sincerely honored and served the royal house and brought concord and peace to the central Xia states, could Duke Huan’s achievements really not have been restored? Why did he fail to win people over through virtue and righteousness, seeking only to intimidate them through force? One year he personally donned armor and helmet to attack Xu; the next year he again mustered his troops to attack…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
莒其心既私其志亦卑景公失圖伯之策如此而
謂賢者為之乎春秋所以惜之也雖然悼公之復
伯固賢矣亦由用武子之策而然也景公之失伯
固庸矣亦由不用晏子之謀而爾也噫賢才之用
舍係乎政事之得失政事之得失關乎國家之盛
衰有國者不用賢才奚可哉
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德尊有道任有能舉賢而置
之聚衆而誓之是故因天事天因地事地因
===
名山升中于天因吉土以饗帝于郊升中于
天而鳳凰降龜龍假饗帝于郊而風雨節寒
暑時是故聖人南面而立而天下大治
孫昪
同考試官教諭闕批此題雖長實易場中作者多強辭
求其講貫精切運筆雄健無如此篇也是宜錄出
考試官教授劉批其文達其氣昌窮理者固如是乎
考試官教諭鄭批據理遣詞明白通暢有識之士也
聖王擇人示戒而舉祀獲其應此所以享無為之
punctuated:
莒。其心既私，其志亦卑。景公失圖伯之策如此，而謂賢者為之乎？春秋所以惜之也。雖然，悼公之復伯固賢矣，亦由用武子之策而然也；景公之失伯固庸矣，亦由不用晏子之謀而爾也。噫！賢才之用舍係乎政事之得失，政事之得失關乎國家之盛衰。有國者不用賢才，奚可哉？
禮記
是故昔先王尚有德，尊有道，任有能，舉賢而置之，聚衆而誓之。是故因天事天，因地事地，因名山升中于天，因吉土以饗帝于郊。升中于天而鳳凰降，龜龍假；饗帝于郊而風雨節，寒暑時。是故聖人南面而立，而天下大治。
孫昪
同考試官教諭闕批：此題雖長，實易。場中作者多強辭，求其講貫精切、運筆雄健，無如此篇也。是宜錄出。
考試官教授劉批：其文達，其氣昌，窮理者固如是乎？
考試官教諭鄭批：據理遣詞，明白通暢，有識之士也。
聖王擇人示戒而舉祀，獲其應，此所以享無為之
translation_en:
…Ju. His heart was selfish, and his aspirations were low. Duke Jing’s failure in planning to attain hegemony was such as this: could one call it the work of a worthy ruler? This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals expresses regret over him. Nevertheless, although Duke Dao’s restoration of hegemony certainly showed his worthiness, it also resulted from his adoption of Wuzi’s strategy. Although Duke Jing’s failure to attain hegemony certainly showed his mediocrity, it also resulted from his failure to adopt Yanzi’s counsel. Alas! Whether worthy and talented men are employed or set aside determines success or failure in government; success or failure in government bears upon the flourishing or decline of the state. How can those who rule states fail to employ worthy and talented men?
Record of Rites
“Thus, in antiquity, the former kings esteemed those possessed of virtue, honored those possessed of the Way, entrusted responsibilities to the capable, and promoted worthy men and installed them in office. They assembled the multitude and admonished them under oath. Thus they used what belonged to Heaven to serve Heaven, and what belonged to Earth to serve Earth. They used renowned mountains to present reports of accomplishment to Heaven, and auspicious ground to offer sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburban sacrifice. When they presented reports of accomplishment to Heaven, phoenixes descended and tortoises and dragons arrived; when they offered sacrifice to the Supreme Lord in the suburbs, wind and rain were regulated, and cold and heat came in their proper seasons. Thus the sage stood facing south, and all under Heaven was brought to great order.”
Sun Bian 孫昪
Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: “Although this topic is long, it is actually easy. Many candidates in the examination strained their language. For precise and penetrating exposition and a vigorous command of the brush, none equals this essay. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: “His writing is lucid, and its vital force abundant. Is this indeed what one who investigates principle to the utmost is like?”
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: “He chooses his words on the basis of principle, expressing himself clearly and fluently. He is a man of discernment.”
The sage king selected men, issued admonitions, and performed sacrifices, receiving the corresponding responses. This was how he enjoyed …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
治也盖祀禮有關於治化也大矣自非聖王克謹
祀禮而獲休瑞之應其何以能享無為之治哉記
禮器者謂夫昔聖王之有天下也知天地生成之
功而報本之禮不可以不舉但不能自任其事故
必擇人以任之焉是故德有諸己者則貴尚之而
不敢忽道積厥躬者則尊崇之而不敢慢才能可
使者又任用之而無疑焉于以舉衆賢而置於位
則小大之官莫不具其職于以聚衆賢而誓其心
則小大之官莫不謹其職由是因天之尊而制為
===
事天之禮郊以祀天于圓丘因地之卑而制為事
地之禮社以祭地于方澤因巡狩而至於方岳則
進此方諸侯治功平成之事以告于天因王都而
兆於南郊則於每歲冬至一陽始生之時以饗於
帝夫告平成之事于天則誠格乎天而天饗之故
鳳凰以降龜龍以假而瑞物臻焉饗郊祀之禮于
帝則誠格乎帝而帝饗之故風雨以節寒暑以時
而休徵應焉聖王於此夫何為哉但見正離位而
履至尊嚮離明而臨大寶端冕凝旒而已耳萬邦
punctuated: 治也。盖祀禮有關於治化也大矣！自非聖王克謹祀禮而獲休瑞之應，其何以能享無為之治哉？記《禮器》者謂夫昔聖王之有天下也，知天地生成之功，而報本之禮不可以不舉，但不能自任其事，故必擇人以任之焉。是故德有諸己者，則貴尚之而不敢忽；道積厥躬者，則尊崇之而不敢慢；才能可使者，又任用之而無疑焉。于以舉衆賢而置於位，則小大之官莫不具其職；于以聚衆賢而誓其心，則小大之官莫不謹其職。由是因天之尊而制為事天之禮，郊以祀天于圓丘；因地之卑而制為事地之禮，社以祭地于方澤。因巡狩而至於方岳，則進此方諸侯治功平成之事以告于天；因王都而兆於南郊，則於每歲冬至一陽始生之時以饗於帝。夫告平成之事于天，則誠格乎天而天饗之，故鳳凰以降，龜龍以假，而瑞物臻焉；饗郊祀之禮于帝，則誠格乎帝而帝饗之，故風雨以節，寒暑以時，而休徵應焉。聖王於此，夫何為哉？但見正離位而履至尊，嚮離明而臨大寶，端冕凝旒而已耳。萬邦
translation_en:
…order. Indeed, sacrificial rites have an immense bearing on governance and moral transformation! Unless a sage king could conscientiously observe these rites and obtain a response in auspicious portents, how could he enjoy order achieved through nonaction? The author of “Ritual Vessels” (Liqi) says that when the sage kings of old possessed all under Heaven, they understood Heaven and Earth’s achievement in generating and nurturing living things, and knew that rites repaying these origins could not be neglected. Yet they could not undertake these affairs alone, so they necessarily selected men to entrust with them. Thus, those who possessed virtue within themselves were esteemed and honored, never disregarded; those who had accumulated the Way in their persons were revered and exalted, never slighted; and those whose talents could be put to use were employed without misgivings. By raising up the assembled worthy men and placing them in office, they ensured that officials both great and small were fully equipped to discharge their duties. By gathering these worthy men and binding their hearts through an oath, they ensured that officials both great and small attended conscientiously to their duties.

Accordingly, in recognition of Heaven’s exalted position, they instituted rites for serving Heaven, performing the suburban sacrifice to Heaven at the Circular Mound. In recognition of Earth’s lowly position, they instituted rites for serving Earth, performing the soil-altar sacrifice to Earth at the Square Marsh. When their inspection tours brought them to the sacred mountain of a region, they presented to Heaven an account of the regional lords’ achievements in bringing order and peace. At the royal capital, they marked out a sacrificial precinct in the southern suburb and offered sacrifice to the Lord on High each year at the winter solstice, when the first yang force began to arise. When they reported their achievements in bringing order and peace to Heaven, their sincerity reached Heaven and Heaven accepted their offerings. Thus phoenixes descended, tortoises and dragons arrived, and auspicious creatures appeared. When they presented the suburban sacrificial rites to the Lord on High, their sincerity reached him and he accepted their offerings. Thus wind and rain came in due measure, cold and heat arrived in their proper seasons, and favorable signs responded.

What, then, did the sage king have to do? One saw only that he took his proper place in the southern position of the trigram Li and occupied the most exalted station, faced the brightness of Li and presided over the imperial throne, wearing his ceremonial robes and crown, its pendants hanging motionless. The myriad states…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
自爾其協和也垂紳正笏而已耳四方自爾其風
動也至誠格天之效有如此夫抑嘗因是而考之
書曰黍稷非馨明德惟馨鬼神無常享享于克誠
然先王既合上下之誠而奉天帝之祭故瑞物之
臻休徵之應亦幽明感通自然之理也彼後世不
脩誠敬以格神徒事封禪以希福者何其謬哉
王者功成作樂治定制禮其功大者其樂備其
治辯者其禮具干戚之舞非備樂也孰亨而
祀非達禮也五帝殊時不相沿樂三王異世
===
不相襲禮樂極則憂禮粗則偏矣及夫敦樂
而無憂禮備而不偏者其唯大聖乎
丁養浩
同考試官教諭闕批題本冠冕作者缺記問之功漫不知所主間
有得者而文又不足以發之此篇如大匠運斤而尺度自合佳作也
考試官教授劉批詞簡理明允宜高捷
考試官教諭鄭批文理渾融宜錄為學禮者式
禮樂本治功而帝王不相述禮樂有偏弊而聖人
為獨全盖禮樂所以象功飾治也帝王隨時世而
punctuated:
自爾其協和也。垂紳正笏而已耳，四方自爾其風動也。至誠格天之效有如此夫！抑嘗因是而考之，《書》曰：「黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。鬼神無常享，享于克誠。」然先王既合上下之誠而奉天帝之祭，故瑞物之臻、休徵之應，亦幽明感通自然之理也。彼後世不脩誠敬以格神，徒事封禪以希福者，何其謬哉！
王者功成作樂，治定制禮。其功大者，其樂備；其治辯者，其禮具。干戚之舞，非備樂也；孰亨而祀，非達禮也。五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異世，不相襲禮。樂極則憂，禮粗則偏矣。及夫敦樂而無憂、禮備而不偏者，其唯大聖乎！
丁養浩
同考試官教諭闕批：題本冠冕，作者缺記問之功，漫不知所主；間有得者，而文又不足以發之。此篇如大匠運斤，而尺度自合，佳作也。
考試官教授劉批：詞簡理明，允宜高捷。
考試官教諭鄭批：文理渾融，宜錄為學禮者式。
禮樂本治功，而帝王不相述；禮樂有偏弊，而聖人為獨全。盖禮樂所以象功飾治也，帝王隨時世而
translation_en:
…of themselves come into harmony. He need only let his sash hang down and hold his audience tablet upright, and the four quarters respond as grass bends before the wind. Such is the efficacy of utmost sincerity in reaching Heaven! I have also examined this in light of the Documents, which says: “Millet is not fragrant; luminous virtue alone is fragrant.” And: “Spirits do not always accept offerings; they accept those of the truly sincere.” Since the former kings brought together the sincerity of those above and below in offering sacrifices to Heaven and the Supreme Lord, the arrival of auspicious creatures and the response of favorable signs likewise followed the natural principle of sympathetic communication between the unseen and visible realms. How mistaken were those of later ages who failed to cultivate sincerity and reverence to reach the spirits, and merely undertook the feng and shan sacrifices in hopes of blessings!
When a king’s achievements are complete, he creates music; when his governance is settled, he establishes rites. Those whose achievements are great have music that is complete; those whose governance is comprehensive have rites that are fully furnished. Dances with shields and axes do not constitute music in its completeness; cooking offerings and sacrificing them does not constitute a full understanding of rites. The Five Emperors lived at different times and did not continue one another’s music; the Three Kings lived in different ages and did not copy one another’s rites. Music carried to excess produces sorrow; rites that are crude become one-sided. As for those whose music is rich without producing sorrow, and whose rites are complete without becoming one-sided—surely only the great sages achieve this!
Ding Yanghao
Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: The topic itself is imposing, but writers lack the grounding that comes from memorization and inquiry and have little notion of its central point. Occasionally someone grasps something of it, yet his writing is inadequate to express it. This essay is like a master carpenter wielding his axe: the dimensions fall naturally into place. An excellent composition.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: Concise in expression and clear in principle; it truly deserves success at a high rank.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: The writing and its reasoning form a seamless whole. It should be recorded as a model for students of the rites.
Rites and music are rooted in governance and achievement, yet emperors and kings did not simply follow one another. Rites and music are subject to one-sidedness and defects, yet the sage alone achieves completeness. For rites and music serve to represent achievements and adorn governance; emperors and kings, according to their times and ages, …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
制作固有異矣然非聖人孰能用之而無弊哉樂
記載以示人宜矣且王者受天明命為天下君彼
功成於天下而必作樂以象其功治定於天下而
必制禮以飾其治惟樂以象功其功之成者巍巍
而無外則所作之樂亦無不備惟禮以飾治其治
之定者蕩蕩而無遺則所制之禮亦無不具總持
干戚而舞不如韶樂之盡善盡美以征伐之功異
於揖遜故耳豈得為備樂哉孰烹牲體而薦不如
血腥之得乎禮意以後世之治異於隆古故耳豈
===
得為達禮哉故少皥顓頊帝嚳堯舜五帝之時殊
矣然各因其功而作樂不相沿焉禹湯文武三王
之世異矣然各因其治而制禮不相襲焉夫禮樂
本治功而制作如此若奏樂而欲極其聲音之娛
樂則樂極悲来矣能無憂乎行禮而不能詳審於
節文則偏失不舉矣能無偏乎及夫敦厚於樂而
無樂極悲来之憂禮儀備具而無偏粗不舉之失
者其惟備道德之全建中和之極功大而樂備治
辯而禮具之大聖能然耳是豈常人所能及哉禮
punctuated: 制作固有異矣，然非聖人，孰能用之而無弊哉？《樂記》載以示人，宜矣。且王者受天明命，為天下君，彼功成於天下而必作樂以象其功，治定於天下而必制禮以飾其治。惟樂以象功，其功之成者巍巍而無外，則所作之樂亦無不備；惟禮以飾治，其治之定者蕩蕩而無遺，則所制之禮亦無不具。總持干戚而舞，不如韶樂之盡善盡美，以征伐之功異於揖遜故耳，豈得為備樂哉？孰烹牲體而薦，不如血腥之得乎禮意，以後世之治異於隆古故耳，豈得為達禮哉？故少皥、顓頊、帝嚳、堯、舜，五帝之時殊矣，然各因其功而作樂，不相沿焉；禹、湯、文、武，三王之世異矣，然各因其治而制禮，不相襲焉。夫禮樂本治功，而制作如此。若奏樂而欲極其聲音之娛樂，則樂極悲来矣，能無憂乎？行禮而不能詳審於節文，則偏失不舉矣，能無偏乎？及夫敦厚於樂而無樂極悲来之憂，禮儀備具而無偏粗不舉之失者，其惟備道德之全、建中和之極、功大而樂備、治辯而禮具之大聖能然耳。是豈常人所能及哉？禮
translation_en:
…their institutions certainly differed. Yet who but a sage could employ them without harmful consequences? It is fitting that the Record of Music records this to instruct people. A true king receives Heaven’s luminous mandate and becomes lord of all under Heaven. When his achievements throughout the realm are complete, he must create music to represent them; when his governance of the realm is firmly established, he must institute rites to embellish it. Since music represents achievement, if his completed achievements are lofty and all-embracing, the music he creates will likewise lack nothing. Since rites embellish governance, if his established governance is broad and leaves nothing unattended, the rites he institutes will likewise be fully furnished. Dancing while grasping shields and battle-axes falls short of the Shao music’s perfect goodness and perfect beauty, simply because achievement through punitive conquest differs from achievement through deferential abdication. How could this count as complete music? Cooking the bodies of sacrificial animals and presenting them falls short of the use of blood and raw flesh in capturing the meaning of ritual, simply because the governance of later ages differs from that of high antiquity. How could this count as a full understanding of rites?

Thus the Five Emperors—Shaohao, Zhuanxu, Diku, Yao, and Shun—lived at different times, and each created music according to his achievements, without simply following his predecessor. The ages of the Three Kings—Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—differed, and each instituted rites according to his governance, without simply copying his predecessor. Rites and music are rooted in governance and achievement, and their institution proceeds in this way. If, in performing music, one seeks to exhaust the pleasures of its sounds, pleasure carried to excess will bring sorrow. Can there then be no cause for concern? If, in practicing rites, one cannot scrutinize their measured forms carefully, there will be one-sided errors and neglected observances. Can there then be no partiality? As for being earnest and substantial in music, without the worry that excessive pleasure will bring sorrow, and possessing the full array of ritual observances, without the faults of partiality, crudity, or neglect—only a great sage can accomplish this: one who possesses the fullness of the Way and virtue, establishes the highest standard of equilibrium and harmony, whose achievements are great and whose music is complete, whose governance is well ordered and whose rites are fully furnished. How could an ordinary person attain this? Rites…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
樂本治功而制作信然矣抑論聖人之制禮樂不
特象功飾治盖將資之以賛造化扶世教焉經曰
禮樂明備天地官矣是造化有資於禮樂也既曰
樂也者聖人之所樂也而可以善民心又曰安上
治民莫善於禮非世教有資於禮樂乎吁禮樂所
關甚大如此非有道德之盛而致治功之隆者烏
能當制作之柄哉
論
明王以孝治天下
===
劉湜
同考試官訓導顧批作論貴乎抑揚反覆通暢厥旨場中
好高者失之險好奇者失之怪此作深得作論之旨可敬可敬
同考試官教諭楚批事有證據文有鋪叙歆羨歆羨
考試官教授劉批有源流有發揮允宜高薦
考試官教諭鄭批沿經遣辭而文豐贍當是作手
論曰聖人有至德以履天位必有要道以順
天下盖聖人之德純乎天性而孝為天之經
德之本聖人之道順乎民心而孝為民之行
punctuated:
樂本治功而制作，信然矣。抑論聖人之制禮樂，不特象功飾治，盖將資之以賛造化、扶世教焉。經曰：「禮樂明備，天地官矣。」是造化有資於禮樂也。既曰：「樂也者，聖人之所樂也，而可以善民心。」又曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」非世教有資於禮樂乎？吁！禮樂所關甚大如此，非有道德之盛而致治功之隆者，烏能當制作之柄哉？

論
明王以孝治天下
劉湜

同考試官訓導顧批：作論貴乎抑揚反覆，通暢厥旨。場中好高者失之險，好奇者失之怪。此作深得作論之旨，可敬可敬！

同考試官教諭楚批：事有證據，文有鋪叙，歆羨歆羨！

考試官教授劉批：有源流，有發揮，允宜高薦。

考試官教諭鄭批：沿經遣辭，而文豐贍，當是作手。

論曰：聖人有至德以履天位，必有要道以順天下。盖聖人之德純乎天性，而孝為天之經、德之本；聖人之道順乎民心，而孝為民之行
translation_en:
…music are indeed created on the basis of good government and achievement. Yet, considering the sage’s institution of rites and music, these do more than represent achievement and embellish good government: he also employs them to assist the transforming processes of Heaven and Earth and sustain moral instruction in society. The classic says: “When rites and music are manifest and complete, Heaven and Earth perform their offices.” Thus those transforming processes depend upon rites and music. It says: “Music is what the sage delights in, and it can make the people’s hearts good.” It also says: “For securing those above and governing the people, nothing excels rites.” Does this not show that moral instruction in society depends upon rites and music? Ah! So momentous are the concerns of rites and music! Unless one possesses abundant moral virtue and achieves the highest accomplishments in government, how could one wield the authority to institute them?

Discourse
“The Enlightened King Governs All under Heaven through Filial Piety”
By Liu Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Gu, Assistant Instructor: In composing a discourse, what matters is modulating the argument and examining it repeatedly from different sides, thereby bringing out its meaning fully and clearly. In the examination hall, those who strive for loftiness err toward precarious expression; those who strive for novelty err toward the bizarre. This composition thoroughly grasps the principles of discourse writing. Admirable, admirable!

Comment by Associate Examiner Chu, Instructor: Its factual claims have supporting evidence, and its prose develops its exposition fully. Enviable, enviable!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: It has foundations and a clear line of development, together with elaboration of its meaning. It certainly deserves recommendation at a high rank.

Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its wording follows the classics, while its prose is rich and ample. This must be an accomplished writer.

The discourse states: A sage who possesses consummate virtue and occupies the heavenly throne must have an essential Way by which to bring all under Heaven into accord. For the sage’s virtue is pure in its Heaven-endowed nature, and filial piety is Heaven’s constant principle and the root of virtue; the sage’s Way accords with the people’s hearts, and filial piety is the people’s proper conduct…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
教之始明王以孝治天下所謂至德要道而
民用和睦上下無怨也歟宜孔子以是為教
而曽子述以為經也愚請敷暢其旨天高地
下萬物散殊而聖人則代天理物乾父坤母
民胞物與而大君則父母宗子古昔明王備
聖人之德居大君之位知天地之化則善述
其事窮天地之神則善繼其志固以事親之
孝盡事天之道矣然神化雖妙不可使民知
也立政以張為治之具制刑以為輔治之法
===
道民以政而不從又有刑以一之矣然刑政
雖善不能使民從也惟其首出庶物知生物
之本於父母者無二本卓冠羣倫知人倫之
先於父子者同一性而愛親之孝人之良知
也孝親之道人之本性也聖人因其良知而
導之因其本性而教之何不知不化之有彼
有國而為諸侯有家而為卿大夫列爵分職
如目隨綱皆王臣也林生而族處同類而異
形面内環觀如星拱極皆天民也明王以孝
punctuated: 教之始。明王以孝治天下，所謂至德要道，而民用和睦，上下無怨也歟？宜孔子以是為教，而曽子述以為經也。愚請敷暢其旨。天高地下，萬物散殊，而聖人則代天理物；乾父坤母，民胞物與，而大君則父母宗子。古昔明王備聖人之德，居大君之位，知天地之化，則善述其事；窮天地之神，則善繼其志。固以事親之孝，盡事天之道矣。然神化雖妙，不可使民知也。立政以張為治之具，制刑以為輔治之法，道民以政而不從，又有刑以一之矣。然刑政雖善，不能使民從也。惟其首出庶物，知生物之本於父母者無二本；卓冠羣倫，知人倫之先於父子者同一性。而愛親之孝，人之良知也；孝親之道，人之本性也。聖人因其良知而導之，因其本性而教之，何不知不化之有？彼有國而為諸侯，有家而為卿大夫，列爵分職，如目隨綱，皆王臣也。林生而族處，同類而異形，面内環觀，如星拱極，皆天民也。明王以孝
translation_en:
…the beginning of instruction. When enlightened kings governed All under Heaven through filial piety, was this not what is meant by supreme virtue and the essential Way, through which the people lived in harmony and neither superiors nor inferiors bore resentment? It was fitting that Confucius made this his teaching and that Zengzi expounded it as a classic. I venture to elaborate its meaning.

Heaven is high and earth below; the myriad things are dispersed and distinct, while the sage orders them on Heaven’s behalf. Qian is the father and Kun the mother; the people are siblings and all things companions, while the great ruler serves as parent and head of the lineage. The enlightened kings of antiquity possessed the virtue of sages and occupied the position of great rulers. Understanding the transformations of Heaven and Earth, they ably carried forward their work; fathoming the spiritual efficacy of Heaven and Earth, they ably continued their purpose. Thus, through the filial devotion with which they served their parents, they fully realized the Way of serving Heaven. Yet, wondrous though these spiritual transformations were, they could not make the people understand them. They established government to deploy the instruments of rule and instituted punishments as a means of supporting governance. If the people would not follow when guided through government, punishments were also available to bring them into conformity. Yet, good though punishments and government might be, they could not make the people obedient.

Standing foremost among all beings, the sage knew that living beings have their root in their parents and have no second root. Towering above all humankind, he knew that all share the same nature, in which the relationship between father and son comes first among human relationships. The filial devotion of loving one’s parents is people’s innate moral knowledge; the Way of filial service to one’s parents is their original nature. The sage guides them through this innate knowledge and teaches them through this original nature. How could any fail to understand or to be transformed?

Those who possess states and serve as regional lords, and those who possess domains and serve as ministers and grand masters, are arrayed in ranks and assigned their duties like the meshes of a net following its main cord: all are the king’s subjects. Those who live in multitudes and dwell in kin groups, alike in kind but different in form, turn inward and look toward the center, like the stars gathering around the pole: all are Heaven’s people. The enlightened kings, through filial piety…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而率臣內焉隆是孝以篤於親則祗載共職
之是敬問安視膳之唯謹外焉舉斯心以加
諸彼則不敢遺小國之臣而尤懷諸侯有畏
以孝而化民則上老老而民興孝上有好而
下必甚教以六行則孝為首糾以八刑則不
孝為先制田里教樹畜使民遂養老之願立
學校明禮義使民知愛敬之道制禮以節是
孝則生事葬祭隆殺有等而敬親之禮通上
下而均行作樂以和是孝則八音克諧神人
===
以和而和親之樂合幽明而咸格親親而仁
民仁民而愛物推孝之序有順而無逆家齊
而國治國治而天下平成孝之教由近以及
遠殆見天下之臣雖萬國也萬國之心靡不
欣欣然歡洽天下之民雖萬姓也萬姓之心
罔不熈熈然和睦於焉繼志述事踐先王之
位而無愧禴祠烝嘗嚴先王之祀而無斁諸
侯法之以治國恭儉愛民不敢侮鰥寡故得
百姓之懽心以事其先君卿大夫效之以治
punctuated:
而率臣，內焉隆是孝以篤於親，則祗載共職之是敬，問安視膳之唯謹；外焉舉斯心以加諸彼，則不敢遺小國之臣，而尤懷諸侯有畏。以孝而化民，則上老老而民興孝，上有好而下必甚。教以六行，則孝為首；糾以八刑，則不孝為先。制田里，教樹畜，使民遂養老之願；立學校，明禮義，使民知愛敬之道。制禮以節是孝，則生事葬祭，隆殺有等，而敬親之禮通上下而均行；作樂以和是孝，則八音克諧，神人以和，而和親之樂合幽明而咸格。

親親而仁民，仁民而愛物，推孝之序有順而無逆；家齊而國治，國治而天下平，成孝之教由近以及遠。殆見天下之臣，雖萬國也，萬國之心靡不欣欣然歡洽；天下之民，雖萬姓也，萬姓之心罔不熈熈然和睦。於焉繼志述事，踐先王之位而無愧；禴祠烝嘗，嚴先王之祀而無斁。諸侯法之以治國，恭儉愛民，不敢侮鰥寡，故得百姓之懽心以事其先君；卿大夫效之以治
translation_en:
…and thereby leads his ministers. Within, he exalts this filial devotion to deepen his attachment to his parents, reverently fulfilling his duties and scrupulously attending to their well-being and meals. Without, he extends this same heart to others: he dares not neglect even the minister of a small state, and especially cherishes the feudal lords with awe [?]. When he transforms the people through filial devotion, those above honor the aged, and the people are stirred to filial conduct; whatever those above favor, those below will pursue still more ardently. In instruction through the six forms of conduct, filial devotion comes first; in correction through the eight punishments, unfilial conduct is the foremost offense. He regulates fields and residential holdings and teaches planting and animal husbandry, enabling the people to fulfill their wish to support their elders. He establishes schools and elucidates ritual propriety and righteousness, enabling the people to understand the way of love and reverence. He establishes rites to regulate this filial devotion: service to parents in life, burial, and sacrifice each have their graded degrees of elaboration and simplicity, while the rites for honoring parents extend through all ranks and are practiced alike. He creates music to harmonize this filial devotion: the eight classes of musical instruments sound in accord, spirits and human beings are brought into harmony, and the music that brings harmony among kin unites the unseen and visible realms, reaching them all.

From loving one’s kin one proceeds to benevolence toward the people, and from benevolence toward the people to care for all things: the order in which filial devotion is extended follows its proper course without reversal. When the family is ordered, the state is well governed; when the state is well governed, all under Heaven is at peace: the teaching that brings filial devotion to fulfillment proceeds from what is near to what is distant. Thus one may see that, although the ministers under Heaven belong to myriad states, the hearts of all those states are filled with joy and concord; although the people under Heaven comprise myriad families, the hearts of all those families are filled with gladness and harmony. Thereupon, he carries on the intentions and undertakings of the former kings, occupying their throne without shame. In the seasonal sacrifices—yue, ci, zheng, and chang—he solemnly maintains their worship without weariness. The feudal lords take him as their model in governing their states: reverent and frugal, they love the people and dare not mistreat widowers and widows. Thus they win the joyful allegiance of the common people with which to serve their former rulers. Ministers and grand masters emulate him in governing …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
家刑于寡妻至於兄弟故得人之懽心以事
其親由是達諸天下人皆順其自然之性通
乎四海人皆遵乎脩道之教庶政惟和由有
孝以為根本五刑不用由有孝以為教化陰
陽和風雨時一至德之感也羣生和萬物遂
一要道之洽也論至於是則知明王之治雖
萬目畢張必能孝而後綱舉以父子人倫之
綱也雖庶事咸治必克孝而後本立以事親
事之本也稽之於古若親睦九族而黎民於
===
變瞽瞍厎豫而天下化堯舜之治以孝而成
也為人子止於孝而萬民咸和善繼人之志
善述人之事而四方訓之文武之治亦以孝
而成也方今
聖人在上德堯舜之德道文武之道以天下養而
慈闈安其孝嚴
郊廟祀而鬼神享其祭是以百司庶府是矜是式
皆移孝為忠用遂顯揚之志群黎百姓是訓
是行皆謹身節用欲致孝養之誠和氣充乎
punctuated:
家，刑于寡妻，至於兄弟，故得人之懽心以事其親。由是達諸天下，人皆順其自然之性；通乎四海，人皆遵乎脩道之教。庶政惟和，由有孝以為根本；五刑不用，由有孝以為教化。陰陽和，風雨時，一至德之感也；羣生和，萬物遂，一要道之洽也。論至於是，則知明王之治，雖萬目畢張，必能孝而後綱舉，以父子人倫之綱也；雖庶事咸治，必克孝而後本立，以事親事之本也。

稽之於古，若親睦九族而黎民於變，瞽瞍厎豫而天下化，堯舜之治以孝而成也。為人子止於孝而萬民咸和，善繼人之志，善述人之事而四方訓之，文武之治亦以孝而成也。

方今聖人在上，德堯舜之德，道文武之道，以天下養而慈闈安其孝，嚴郊廟祀而鬼神享其祭。是以百司庶府，是矜是式，皆移孝為忠，用遂顯揚之志；群黎百姓，是訓是行，皆謹身節用，欲致孝養之誠。和氣充乎
translation_en:
…their households, setting an example for their wives and extending it to their brothers, and thus winning others’ affection with which to serve their parents. From this, its influence reaches throughout the realm, and all follow their natural dispositions; it extends throughout the Four Seas, and all abide by the teaching that cultivates the Way. The many affairs of government are harmonious because filial piety provides their foundation; the five punishments go unused because filial piety provides moral instruction. The harmony of yin and yang and the seasonableness of wind and rain are entirely the response elicited by this consummate virtue; the harmony of living creatures and the flourishing of all things are entirely the pervasive effect of this essential Way. Having carried the discussion this far, we know that, in an enlightened king’s government, although all the myriad meshes of the net are spread, its main cord can be raised only through his practice of filial piety, for the father–son relationship is the main cord of human relationships. Although the many affairs are all put in order, their foundation can be established only through his fulfillment of filial piety, for serving one’s parents is the foundation of all service.

Examining antiquity, we find that Yao brought the nine degrees of kinship into affectionate harmony, and the common people were transformed; Shun brought Gusou to contentment, and all under Heaven were morally transformed. The governance of Yao and Shun was perfected through filial piety. As a son, King Wen rested in filial piety, and the myriad people were all harmonious; by skillfully carrying forward their predecessors’ intentions and accomplishments, Kings Wen and Wu became models for the four quarters. Their governance, too, was perfected through filial piety.

Today the sage occupies the throne, embodying the virtue of Yao and Shun and following the Way of Kings Wen and Wu. He uses the resources of all under Heaven to provide for his mother, who rests secure in the maternal palace through his filial devotion; he solemnly conducts the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices, and the spirits accept his offerings. Thus the hundred offices and the various government bureaus revere and emulate him: all turn filial piety into loyalty, thereby fulfilling their aspiration to bring honor to their parents. The common people all follow his teaching and put it into practice: all are careful in their conduct and frugal in their expenditures, seeking to express their sincerity in filial support. Harmonious vital energy fills…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
兩間休徵應乎五事唐虞成周之治復見於
今日矣愚何幸躬逢其盛
孫昇
同考試官教諭闕批初讀此論可驚可駭深潜涵泳如走下坂
車如縛白額虎不可以科場文字視之也置居前列允恊輿情
同考試官教諭單批不險不惟有趣有味議論至此宜當起敬
考試官教授劉批此論意深辭古如不施控勒而騎生馬者
豈穉筆所能及耶允宜録出以範後學
考試官教諭鄭批命意淵深行文蒼古真有學之士也
===
土積而成山山之為山草木生焉禽獸居焉
是山之性也水積而成川川之為川萍藻出
焉魚鱉遊焉是川之性也以山而植萍藻置
魚鱉是反其山之性而所謂萍藻所謂魚鱉
者皆失其所焉以川而植草木養禽獸是反
其川之性而所謂草木所謂禽獸者亦失其
所焉故體物而不遺者天也雲行雨施品物
流形化化而無窮天何容心哉随物而厚生
者地也飛潜動植大造普施形形而不已地
punctuated:
兩間，休徵應乎五事，唐虞成周之治復見於今日矣。愚何幸躬逢其盛！
孫昇。
同考試官教諭闕批：初讀此論，可驚可駭；深潜涵泳，如走下坂車，如縛白額虎，不可以科場文字視之也。置居前列，允恊輿情。
同考試官教諭單批：不險不惟，有趣有味，議論至此，宜當起敬。
考試官教授劉批：此論意深辭古，如不施控勒而騎生馬者，豈穉筆所能及耶？允宜録出，以範後學。
考試官教諭鄭批：命意淵深，行文蒼古，真有學之士也。
土積而成山，山之為山，草木生焉，禽獸居焉，是山之性也。水積而成川，川之為川，萍藻出焉，魚鱉遊焉，是川之性也。以山而植萍藻、置魚鱉，是反其山之性，而所謂萍藻、所謂魚鱉者皆失其所焉。以川而植草木、養禽獸，是反其川之性，而所謂草木、所謂禽獸者亦失其所焉。故體物而不遺者，天也。雲行雨施，品物流形，化化而無窮，天何容心哉？随物而厚生者，地也。飛潜動植，大造普施，形形而不已，地
translation_en:
…between Heaven and Earth, auspicious signs respond to the Five Activities, and the good governance of Tang, Yu, and Chengzhou is seen again today. How fortunate I, in my humble station, am to witness this flourishing age in person!
Sun Sheng.
Comment by Associate Examiner Que, Instructor: On first reading, this discourse astonishes and startles. Upon deeply immersing oneself in it, it is like driving a carriage downhill or binding a white-browed tiger. It cannot be regarded as merely an examination composition. Placing it among the foremost entries truly accords with the general judgment.
Comment by Associate Examiner Shan, Instructor: Neither strained nor [unclear: 惟][?], it has interest and savor. Argument of this caliber rightly commands respect.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Professor: This discourse has profound meaning and antique diction. It is like riding an unbroken horse without applying the reins. How could an immature writer achieve this? It certainly deserves to be transcribed as a model for later students.
Comment by Examiner Zheng, Instructor: Its conception is profound, and its prose has an antique vigor. This is truly a man of learning.
Earth accumulates to form a mountain. What makes a mountain a mountain is that plants and trees grow there and birds and beasts dwell there: this is the nature of a mountain. Water accumulates to form a river. What makes a river a river is that duckweed and aquatic plants emerge there and fish and turtles swim there: this is the nature of a river. To plant duckweed and aquatic plants on a mountain and put fish and turtles there is to act contrary to the mountain’s nature; those duckweed and aquatic plants, those fish and turtles, all lose their proper place. To plant grasses and trees in a river and rear birds and beasts there is to act contrary to the river’s nature; those grasses and trees, those birds and beasts, likewise lose their proper place. Thus it is Heaven that embodies all things without omission. Clouds move and rain falls; the myriad things flow into form, transformation following transformation without end. What deliberate intention could Heaven have? It is Earth that enriches life in accordance with each thing. Flying and submerged creatures, animals and plants—all receive the universal bounty of creation, form following form without cease. Earth…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何容心哉故明王之以孝治天下乃因人之
所固有者而開導之即天之體物而不遺因
民之所自然者而誘引之即地之隨物以厚
生所謂不立異以求名不反道而敗德如山
也必植草木必居禽獸焉如川也必生萍藻
必遊魚鼈焉其性也如此人或有疑之者曰
富國強兵人君治天下之要道所以制侵陵
厚邦本如秦如漢當時陳之者莫先行之者
恐後求賢取士安天下之良法所以充庶位
===
理繁劇如唐如宋當時告之者諄諄用之者
亟亟而仲尼謂明王以孝治天下抑有說歟
盖孝者天之經地之義民之行也明王乃則
天之經因地之義順民之行焉故愛敬盡於
事親德教刑於四海將見治國者不敢侮鰥
寡治家者不敢侮臣妾無有不得其懽心者
焉又豈止於如此而已哉大寶之位祖宗之
所授也不敢以富貴而驕天下四海之衆祖
宗之所遺也不敢以天下而奉一人于以保
punctuated:
何容心哉？故明王之以孝治天下，乃因人之所固有者而開導之，即天之體物而不遺；因民之所自然者而誘引之，即地之隨物以厚生。所謂不立異以求名，不反道而敗德。如山也，必植草木，必居禽獸焉；如川也，必生萍藻，必遊魚鼈焉。其性也如此。
人或有疑之者曰：「富國強兵，人君治天下之要道，所以制侵陵、厚邦本。如秦如漢，當時陳之者莫先，行之者恐後。求賢取士，安天下之良法，所以充庶位、理繁劇。如唐如宋，當時告之者諄諄，用之者亟亟。而仲尼謂明王以孝治天下，抑有說歟？」
盖孝者，天之經，地之義，民之行也。明王乃則天之經，因地之義，順民之行焉。故愛敬盡於事親，德教刑於四海。將見治國者不敢侮鰥寡，治家者不敢侮臣妾，無有不得其懽心者焉。又豈止於如此而已哉？大寶之位，祖宗之所授也，不敢以富貴而驕天下；四海之衆，祖宗之所遺也，不敢以天下而奉一人。于以保
translation_en:
… how could Earth act with deliberate intent? Thus, when an enlightened king governs all under Heaven through filial piety, he guides people by drawing upon what they inherently possess, just as Heaven gives substance to all things without omitting any. He leads the people by drawing upon what comes naturally to them, just as Earth follows the nature of each thing to nourish its life. This is what is meant by neither pursuing distinction to gain fame nor contravening the Way to ruin virtue. A mountain must grow grasses and trees and shelter birds and beasts; a river must produce duckweed and algae and have fish and turtles swimming in it. Such are their natures.
Someone who doubts this might say: “Enriching the state and strengthening its armies are essential means by which a ruler governs all under Heaven, restraining aggression and strengthening the foundations of the state. Under the Qin and Han, those who advocated these measures strove to be foremost, and those who implemented them feared falling behind. Seeking worthy men and selecting men of ability are sound methods for bringing peace to all under Heaven, filling the various offices and handling complex and demanding affairs. Under the Tang and Song, those who urged these methods did so earnestly, and those who employed them did so urgently. Yet Zhongni said that enlightened kings governed all under Heaven through filial piety. Is there an explanation for this?”
Filial piety is the constant principle of Heaven, the proper order of Earth, and the conduct of the people. The enlightened king therefore models himself on Heaven’s constant principle, accords with Earth’s proper order, and follows the conduct natural to the people. Thus, love and reverence find their fullest expression in serving one’s parents, and moral instruction becomes a model throughout the Four Seas. We shall then see those who govern states not daring to mistreat widowers and widows, and those who govern households not daring to mistreat male and female servants: there will be none whose goodwill they do not gain. Yet how could the effects stop here? The throne, that great treasure, was bestowed by the ancestors; the ruler therefore dares not use his wealth and rank to lord it over all under Heaven. The multitudes within the Four Seas were bequeathed by the ancestors; he therefore dares not use all under Heaven to serve a single person. By these means he preserves …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
社稷於靈長于以措斯民於樂業亦何莫而
非明王之以孝治天下也耶是以天下和平
而四靈畢至禍亂不作而萬國休寧矣古亦
有是君歟若虞舜之事瞽瞍夔夔齊慄乃以
身先天下而四方有風動之休武王之事文
王善繼善述亦以身先天下而四海有永清
之化則孝之根於人心之固有者可知也已
真如山之養草木禽獸川之蓄萍藻魚鱉有
不期然而然者焉或又疑之曰在人有上智
===
與下愚為政有刑驅與勢迫離母而居見罪
於孟軻怨親之詩乃形於小弁若曰明王以
孝治天下恐四海之廣億兆之衆亦有離母
而怨親者焉似未可深信也於乎有是我人
君以仁感天下天下以仁應之者堯舜是也
人君以義感天下天下以義應之者湯武是
也矧至愚而神者民心也至明而顯者孝道
也人君能以孝而自處則天下之人必曰是
吾君能孝也吾亦有親焉有親而不事吾亦
punctuated:
社稷於靈長，于以措斯民於樂業，亦何莫而非明王之以孝治天下也耶？是以天下和平，而四靈畢至；禍亂不作，而萬國休寧矣。古亦有是君歟？若虞舜之事瞽瞍，夔夔齊慄，乃以身先天下，而四方有風動之休；武王之事文王，善繼善述，亦以身先天下，而四海有永清之化。則孝之根於人心之固有者，可知也已。真如山之養草木禽獸，川之蓄萍藻魚鱉，有不期然而然者焉。

或又疑之曰：「在人有上智與下愚，為政有刑驅與勢迫。離母而居，見罪於孟軻；怨親之詩，乃形於《小弁》。若曰明王以孝治天下，恐四海之廣、億兆之衆，亦有離母而怨親者焉，似未可深信也。」於乎！有是我？人君以仁感天下，天下以仁應之者，堯舜是也；人君以義感天下，天下以義應之者，湯武是也。矧至愚而神者，民心也；至明而顯者，孝道也。人君能以孝而自處，則天下之人必曰：「是吾君能孝也，吾亦有親焉。有親而不事，吾亦
translation_en:
…the altars of soil and grain in enduring security, and thereby settle the people in contented pursuit of their livelihoods: how could any of this fail to exemplify an enlightened king’s governing all under Heaven through filial piety? Thus all under Heaven enjoy peace and harmony, and the four auspicious creatures all appear; calamities and disorder do not arise, and the myriad states enjoy tranquility. Were there such rulers in antiquity? Yu Shun served Gusou with reverent awe and vigilant care, setting an example in his own person for all under Heaven, so that the four quarters enjoyed the blessing of being stirred by his influence as by the wind. King Wu served King Wen by ably carrying on his purposes and continuing his undertakings, likewise setting an example in his own person for all under Heaven, so that all within the four seas were transformed toward lasting peace. We may thus understand that filial piety is rooted in what the human heart inherently possesses. It is truly like mountains nourishing grasses, trees, birds, and beasts, or rivers sustaining duckweed, water plants, fish, and turtles: these things come about without being deliberately sought.

Someone might nevertheless raise a doubt, saying: “Among people there are both the supremely wise and the utterly foolish; in governing, there are those driven by punishments and compelled by force. Living apart from one’s mother drew condemnation from Meng Ke; resentment toward a parent found poetic expression in ‘The Lesser Cap’ (Xiao Bian). If one says that enlightened kings govern all under Heaven through filial piety, I fear that, across the vast expanse of the four seas and among its countless multitudes, there will still be those who leave their mothers and resent their parents. It seems that this claim cannot yet be fully trusted.” Ah! Can this be so [?]? When rulers moved all under Heaven through benevolence, and all under Heaven responded with benevolence, these were Yao and Shun. When rulers moved all under Heaven through righteousness, and all under Heaven responded with righteousness, these were Tang and Wu. Moreover, the people’s hearts, though seemingly most uncomprehending, are wondrously responsive; the way of filial piety is supremely clear and manifest. If a ruler can conduct himself with filial piety, then the people throughout the realm will surely say: “Our ruler here can practice filial piety. I too have parents. If I have parents yet do not serve them, I too…”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有子焉不欲子之不順於我則不敢以此事
吾親不樂子之不孝於我則不敢以此奉吾
親相師相法於治教休明之日相率相引於
仁義道德之塲仲尼所謂得萬國之懽心以
事其先君而明王以孝治天下至此瞭然矣
復民之性導民之善更豈有過於此哉是即
草木鳥獸生養於山萍藻魚鼈浮遊於水各
奠其位各適其性也而明王以孝治天下之
功化又當與天之體物不遺地之隨物厚生
===
相參列而不相背馳也如此夫求諸今日
聖天子奉
聖母以孝治天下則其感化之效又與帝舜文王
同驅而並列也仲尼之言幾二千載而始驗
矣愚何幸身親見之謹論
表
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞國子祭酒率諸生謝表
孫昪
同考試官教諭闕批表佳
punctuated:
有子焉。不欲子之不順於我，則不敢以此事吾親；不樂子之不孝於我，則不敢以此奉吾親。相師相法於治教休明之日，相率相引於仁義道德之塲。仲尼所謂得萬國之懽心，以事其先君，而明王以孝治天下，至此瞭然矣。復民之性，導民之善，更豈有過於此哉？是即草木鳥獸生養於山，萍藻魚鼈浮遊於水，各奠其位，各適其性也。而明王以孝治天下之功化，又當與天之體物不遺、地之隨物厚生，相參列而不相背馳也。如此夫！求諸今日，聖天子奉聖母，以孝治天下，則其感化之效，又與帝舜、文王同驅而並列也。仲尼之言幾二千載而始驗矣。愚何幸身親見之！謹論。
表
擬增孔子籩豆佾舞，國子祭酒率諸生謝表。
孫昪
同考試官教諭闕批：表佳。
translation_en:
…have children as well. If I do not want my children to disobey me, I dare not behave that way in serving my parents; if I take no pleasure in my children’s being unfilial toward me, I dare not treat my own parents in that manner. People teach and emulate one another in an age of flourishing government and moral instruction, leading and guiding one another in the realm of benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue. This is what Zhongni meant by winning the joyful allegiance of the myriad states in order to serve one’s departed rulers. How an enlightened king governs all under Heaven through filial piety thus becomes perfectly clear. Could anything surpass this in restoring the people’s inherent nature and guiding their goodness? It is just like plants, trees, birds, and beasts growing and flourishing in the mountains, and duckweed, algae, fish, and turtles floating and swimming in the waters: each is settled in its proper place, and each finds fulfillment in its own nature. The achievements and transforming influence of an enlightened king’s government through filial piety should likewise stand alongside Heaven’s embodiment of all things without omission and Earth’s generous nourishment of each according to its nature, working together without running counter to them. Such indeed is the case!
Looking to the present day, our sagely Son of Heaven reverently serves his sagely mother and governs all under Heaven through filial piety. The effects of his inspiring and transforming influence keep pace with, and stand alongside, those of Emperor Shun and King Wen. Only now, nearly two thousand years later, have Zhongni’s words been borne out. How fortunate I am, ignorant though I be, to witness this in person! Respectfully submitted as a discourse.
Memorial
Draft memorial of thanks, on the occasion of an increase in the bamboo and wooden sacrificial vessels and the ranks of ritual dancers honoring Kongzi, presented by the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education at the head of the students.
Sun Bian 孫昪
Associate Examiner Que, Instructor, comments: “A fine memorial.”

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭何批氣象寬洪可取
考試官教授劉批有典有則佳作也
考試官教諭鄭批得體
伏以先孔子而聖者非孔子無以明後孔子
而聖者非孔子無以法道冠古今刪六經而
垂訓德侔天地配大化以施功宰我有賢於
堯舜之稱曽參有潔於江漢之喻故過魯一
祀開漢家四百年之帝業入廟再拜啓唐室
三百載之王基聞之者喜見之者榮陳綱立
===
紀伊誰之功著德立言是誰之力邇者尊崇
盛禮闡
昭代之宏規增制鴻休恢太平之盛典景行實
超於前哲報功垂法於後人士類歡騰儒風
益振茲盖伏遇
〇〇〇〇
默運乾綱布道義以臨天下
靜含坤造廣仁恕以賴萬方
智本生知
punctuated:
同考試官教諭何批：氣象寬洪，可取。
考試官教授劉批：有典有則，佳作也。
考試官教諭鄭批：得體。

伏以先孔子而聖者，非孔子無以明；後孔子而聖者，非孔子無以法。道冠古今，刪六經而垂訓；德侔天地，配大化以施功。宰我有賢於堯舜之稱，曽參有潔於江漢之喻。故過魯一祀，開漢家四百年之帝業；入廟再拜，啓唐室三百載之王基。聞之者喜，見之者榮。陳綱立紀，伊誰之功？著德立言，是誰之力？邇者尊崇盛禮，闡昭代之宏規；增制鴻休，恢太平之盛典。景行實超於前哲，報功垂法於後人。士類歡騰，儒風益振。茲盖伏遇〇〇〇〇，默運乾綱，布道義以臨天下；靜含坤造，廣仁恕以賴萬方。智本生知，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner He, an Instructor, comments: “Broad and generous in spirit; worthy of acceptance.”
Examiner Liu, a Professor, comments: “Grounded in classical precedent and conforming to proper standards: an excellent composition.”
Examiner Zheng, an Instructor, comments: “Appropriate to its form.”

We humbly submit: without Confucius, the sages who preceded him could not have been made clearly known; without Confucius, those who became sages after him would have had no model to follow. His Way surpasses all others, ancient and modern; he edited the Six Classics to transmit instruction to posterity. His virtue equals Heaven and Earth; he cooperates with the great transforming process to accomplish his work. Zai Wo praised him as worthier than Yao and Shun; Zeng Shen compared his purity to the waters of the Jiang and Han rivers. Thus, a single sacrifice when passing through Lu opened the Han dynasty’s four hundred years of imperial rule; two bows upon entering his temple inaugurated the Tang house’s three hundred years of kingship. Those who hear of these acts rejoice; those who witness them feel honored. Whose achievement was it to set forth the guiding principles and establish order? Whose exertion was it to manifest virtue and leave enduring teachings?

Recently, magnificent rites honoring Confucius have displayed the grand designs of this illustrious age; expanded ceremonial provisions and great blessings have enlarged the splendid observances of an age of peace. These lofty deeds truly surpass those of former worthies, repaying his achievements and transmitting a model to later generations. Scholars rejoice, and the Confucian tradition flourishes all the more. This is because we have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇 [imperial designation unclear], who silently wields Heaven’s governing authority, spreading the Way and righteousness to rule all under Heaven; who serenely embodies Earth’s creative power, extending benevolence and forbearance to benefit every region. Your wisdom rests upon knowledge possessed from birth…

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖由天縱
盛名兼配於三王丕績纘承乎
列聖崇儒重道制度考文籩豆加飾增高夫子
之門墻佾舞展容用饗天王之禮樂于以格
聖靈而厚風化于以補缺典而重彞倫春秋
祀事於廟庭中外頒行於庠序郁郁斯文於
今為盛巍巍洪制振古罕聞臣某等職忝司成
位登胄監目靚曠世所無之禮身親百代所
吝之儀謹率六館之書生敬望
===
九重而稽首趨蹌舞蹈惟思感激之深進退周
旋莫罄揄揚之妙伏願
宗社奠安世道與吾道而俱泰
皇圖鞏固
聖壽與
國壽以無疆臣某等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉表稱
謝以
punctuated: 聖由天縱，盛名兼配於三王，丕績纘承乎列聖。崇儒重道，制度考文，籩豆加飾，增高夫子之門墻；佾舞展容，用饗天王之禮樂。于以格聖靈而厚風化，于以補缺典而重彞倫。春秋祀事於廟庭，中外頒行於庠序。郁郁斯文，於今為盛；巍巍洪制，振古罕聞。臣某等職忝司成，位登胄監，目靚曠世所無之禮，身親百代所吝之儀。謹率六館之書生，敬望九重而稽首，趨蹌舞蹈，惟思感激之深；進退周旋，莫罄揄揚之妙。伏願宗社奠安，世道與吾道而俱泰；皇圖鞏固，聖壽與國壽以無疆。臣某等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以
translation_en: …Your sageliness is Heaven-bestowed. Your illustrious renown matches that of the Three Kings, and your great achievements carry forward those of the successive sage emperors. You honor Confucian learning and esteem the Way, establish institutions and examine cultural forms. By further adorning the bamboo and wooden sacrificial vessels, you have heightened the walls and gates of the Master's school; by displaying the ordered ranks of ritual dancers, you offer him the rites and music of the Son of Heaven. Thus you draw near the sage's spirit and deepen moral transformation; thus you supply what was lacking in the ritual statutes and give weight to the enduring human relationships. Spring and autumn sacrifices are performed in the temple courtyard, and these provisions are promulgated for observance in schools both at the capital and throughout the realm. This flourishing culture now reaches its fullness; such lofty and magnificent institutions have seldom been heard of since antiquity. We, your servants, So-and-so and the others, unworthily charged with directing education and holding office in the Directorate of Education, have beheld [?] rites unprecedented across the ages and personally participated in ceremonies rarely granted in a hundred generations. We respectfully lead the students of the Six Colleges, gaze reverently toward the Ninefold Palace, and bow our heads to the ground. Advancing with measured steps and dancing in homage, we think only of our profound gratitude; advancing, withdrawing, and turning according to ritual, we cannot exhaust the wonders deserving praise. We humbly wish that the imperial ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain may be securely established, and that the order of the age and our Way may flourish together; that the imperial enterprise may stand firm, and that Your Majesty's longevity and the dynasty's longevity may alike be boundless. We, your servants, So-and-so and the others, look up toward Heaven and revere Your Sagely Majesty, overwhelmed by intense emotion and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and thereby …

title: 成化十三年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聞
